docs.title: Vertex AI documentation
docs.text: Vertex AI is a machine learning (ML) platform that lets you train and deploy ML models and AI applications. Vertex AI combines data engineering, data science, and ML engineering workflows, enabling team collaboration using a common toolset. Learn more.

docs.text:
• Gemini

    Use Gemini, Google's multimodal generative AI model, to process images, videos, and text.

  • Generative AI

    Access Google's generative AI models to test, tune, and deploy them for use in your AI-powered applications.

  • Model Garden

    Use Model Garden to discover, test, customize, and deploy Google proprietary and select OSS generative AI models and LLMs.

docs.title: Overview of Generative AI on Vertex AI
docs.text:
Build production-ready generative AI agents and applications on Vertex AI using Google's advanced models and open, enterprise-grade infrastructure.

  • Build, deploy, and connect agents: Build agents with an open approach and deploy them with enterprise-grade controls. Connect agents across your enterprise ecosystem.
  • Enterprise ready: Deploy your generative AI agents and applications at scale with enterprise-grade security, data residency and privacy, access transparency, and low latency.
  • State-of-the-art features: Expand the capabilities of your applications by using the 2 million token context window that Gemini supports, and the built-in multimodality and thinking capabilities from Gemini 1.5 models.
  • Open and flexible platform: Vertex AI Model Garden provides a library of over 200 enterprise-ready models and Vertex AI Model Builder helps you test, customize, deploy, and monitor Google proprietary and select third-party models, including Anthropic's Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Meta's Llama 3, and Mistral AI's Mixtral 8x7B.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Agent: An AI system that can understand a user's goal and dynamically work to achieve it by interacting with users, tools, and external systems.
  • Multimodality: The ability of a model to process and understand information from multiple types of data, such as images, text, and audio, simultaneously.
  • Grounding: The process of connecting a model's responses to verifiable sources of information to improve accuracy and reduce hallucinations.
  • Embeddings: Numerical representations of text, images, or other data, used to capture semantic meaning and enable tasks like search and classification.
  • Tuning: The process of adapting a pre-trained model to perform better on a specific task by training it on a smaller, task-specific dataset.

docs.text:

  • Browse the Vertex AI Studio Prompt Gallery: Test out prompts with no setup required.
  • Generate images and verify watermarks using Imagen: Create a watermarked image using Imagen on Vertex AI.

docs.title: Featured capabilities
docs.text:
• Agent Builder: A suite of features for building and deploying AI agents.
  • Live API: Use the Live API to provide your end users with the experience of natural, human-like voice conversations.
  • Thinking: Solve complex requests and show the model's thought process behind its response using Gemini's built-in reasoning capabilities.
  • Grounding: Ground your responses using Google Search, Maps, or even your own data.
  • Generate embeddings: Generate embeddings to perform tasks such as search, classification, clustering, and outlier detection.
  • Tuning: Adapt your model to perform specific tasks with greater precision and accuracy.
  • Image generation: Build next-generation AI products that transform your user's imagination into high quality visual assets using AI generation in seconds.
  • Video generation: Use Veo on Vertex AI to generate new videos from a text prompt or an image prompt.
  • Generative AI evaluation service: Vertex AI lets you evaluate any generative model or application and benchmark the evaluation results against your own judgment, using your own evaluation criteria.

docs.title: Cost of building and deploying AI models in Vertex AI
docs.text:
This document details the pricing for Generative AI services on Vertex AI. Prices are listed in US Dollars (USD). If you pay in a currency other than USD, the prices listed in your currency on Cloud Platform SKUs apply.

You are charged only for requests that return a 200 OK response code. Requests that result in other response codes, such as 4xx or 5xx, do not incur charges for input or output.

For all other Vertex AI pricing, including ML Platform and MLOps services, see the Vertex AI pricing page.

Model Availability

Starting April 29, 2025, Gemini 1.5 Pro and Gemini 1.5 Flash models are not available in projects that have no prior usage of these models, including new projects. For details, see Model versions and lifecycle.

Concepts
  • Token: The basic unit of text processed by a large language model; approximately 4 characters of English text equals one token.
  • Grounded Prompt: A request submitted to a model that includes one or more queries to an external data source like Google Search to provide more factual and up-to-date responses.
  • Provisioned Throughput: A service that provides a reserved amount of model processing capacity for a fixed price, ensuring consistent performance and throughput.
  • Generative AI Scale Unit (GSU): The unit of measure for purchasing provisioned throughput.
  • Context Caching: A feature that stores parts of your input (context) to reduce costs and latency on subsequent requests with similar context.

docs.title: Grounding
docs.text:
Grounding enhances model responses by connecting them to external data sources. Gemini model usage fees apply separately.

  • Grounding with Google Search:

    • Gemini 2.0 Flash, 2.5 Flash, and 2.5 Flash-Lite: Includes a combined 1,500 grounded prompts per day at no additional charge.
    • Gemini 2.5 Pro: Includes 10,000 grounded prompts per day at no additional charge.
    • Overage: Prompts exceeding the daily free limit are billed at $35 per 1,000 grounded prompts.
    • Billing: Charged only when a prompt successfully returns web results.

  • Web Grounding for enterprise:

    • Price: $45 per 1,000 grounded prompts.
    • Billing: Charged only when a prompt successfully returns web results.

  • Grounding with your data:

    • Price: $2.50 per 1,000 requests (starting June 16, 2025).

For usage exceeding 1 million grounded prompts per day, please contact your account team.

docs.title: Provisioned Throughput
docs.text:
Provisioned throughput guarantees a set amount of throughput for your generative AI workloads, transacted via generative AI scale units (GSUs). You can learn more about GSU throughput here and use our online estimator.

Duration Price per GSU Per 1 week commit $1,200 Week 1 month commit $2,700 Month 3 month commit $2,400 Month 1 year commit $2,000 Month

docs.title: Example cost calculation
docs.text:
A user needs to support 10 queries per second (QPS) for a query with 1,000 input text tokens, 500 input audio tokens, and 300 output text tokens using gemini-2.0-flash.

  1. Calculate Burndown-Adjusted Tokens per Query: Using the throughput and burndown rate table, we find the rates for gemini-2.0-flash:

    • Input text burndown rate: 1 token
    • Input audio burndown rate: 7 tokens

    • Output text burndown rate: 4 tokens

    • Input tokens: (1,000 text tokens * 1) + (500 audio tokens * 7) = 4,500 burndown-adjusted tokens

    • Output tokens: 300 text tokens * 4 = 1,200 burndown-adjusted tokens
    • Total per query: 4,500 + 1,200 = 5,700 total tokens

  2. Calculate Total Tokens per Second:

    • 5,700 tokens/query * 10 QPS = 57,000 total tokens per second.

  3. Calculate Required GSUs:

    • 57,000 tokens/sec ÷ 3,360 per-second throughput/GSU = 16.96 GSUs.
    • Since the minimum purchase increment is 1, the user needs 17 GSUs.

  4. Calculate Cost:

    • 1 week: 17 GSUs * $1,200/GSU = $20,400
    • 1 month: 17 GSUs * $2,700/GSU = $45,900
    • 3 months: 17 GSUs * $2,400/GSU = $40,800 per month
    • 1 year: 17 GSUs * $2,000/GSU = $34,000 per month

docs.title: Gemini Online Inference on Vertex AI Service Level Agreement (SLA)
docs.text:
During the Term of the agreement under which Google has agreed to provide Google Cloud Platform to Customer (as applicable, the "Agreement"), the Covered Service will provide a Monthly Uptime Percentage to Customer (the "Service Level Objective" or "SLO") as follows:

Covered Service Monthly Uptime Percentage generateContent and streamGenerateContent methods of Gemini Online Inference on Vertex AI 99.5%

If Google does not meet the SLO, and if Customer meets its obligations under this SLA, Customer will be eligible to receive the Financial Credits described below. Monthly Uptime Percentage and Financial Credit are determined on a calendar month basis per Project. This SLA states Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for any failure by Google to meet the SLO. Capitalized terms used in this SLA, but not defined in this SLA, have the meaning set forth in the Agreement. If the Agreement authorizes the resale or supply of Google Cloud Platform under a Google Cloud partner or reseller program, then all references to Customer in this SLA mean Partner or Reseller (as applicable), and any Financial Credit(s) will only apply for impacted Partner or Reseller order(s) under the Agreement.

docs.title: Definitions
docs.text:
The following definitions apply to the SLA:

  • "Covered Service" means the generateContent and streamGenerateContent methods of Gemini Online Inference API on Vertex AI.
  • "Downtime" means more than a five percent Error Rate and is measured based on server side Error Rate.
  • "Downtime Period" means a period of five or more consecutive minutes of Downtime. Partial minutes or intermittent Downtime for a period of less than five minutes will not count towards any Downtime Periods.
  • "Error Rate" means the number of Valid Requests that result in an error code response with HTTP Status 5XX divided by the total number of Valid Requests during the Downtime Period.
  • "Financial Credit" means the following:
Monthly Uptime Percentage Percentage of monthly bill for the Covered Service that does not meet SLO that will be credited to Customer's future monthly bills 99.0% - < 99.5% 10% 95.0% - < 99.0% 25% < 95.0% 50%
  • "Monthly Uptime Percentage" means total number of minutes in a month, minus the number of minutes of Downtime suffered from all Downtime Periods in a month, divided by the total number of minutes in a month.
  • "Valid Requests" are requests that conform to the Documentation, and that would normally result in a non-error response.

docs.title: Customer must request Financial Credit
docs.text: In order to receive any of the Financial Credits described above, Customer must notify Google technical support within 30 days from the time Customer becomes eligible to receive a Financial Credit. Customer must also provide Google with log files showing Downtime Periods and the date and time they occurred. If Customer does not comply with these requirements, Customer will forfeit its right to receive a Financial Credit. Further, Customer must be in good standing under the Agreement in order to receive a Financial Credit.

docs.title: Maximum Financial Credit
docs.text: The maximum aggregate number of Financial Credits issued by Google to Customer for all Downtime Periods in a single billing month will not exceed 50% of the amount due from Customer for the Covered Service that did not meet SLO for the applicable month. Financial Credits will be in the form of a monetary credit applied to future use of the Covered Service and will be applied within 60 days after the Financial Credit was agreed to by Google.

docs.title: SLA exclusions
docs.text:
The SLA does not apply to any (a) features or services designated pre-general availability (unless otherwise set forth in the associated Documentation); (b) features or services excluded from the SLA (in the associated Documentation), including requests made using Grounding with Google Search; or (c) errors (i) caused by factors outside of Google's reasonable control; (ii) that resulted from Customer's software or hardware or third party software or hardware, or both; (iii) that resulted from abuses or other behaviors that violate the Agreement; or (iv) that resulted from quotas applied by the system or listed in the Documentation or Admin Console.

Last modified July 30, 2024

docs.title: Access control
docs.text:
To use the generative AI features on Vertex AI, principals (for example, users, groups, and service accounts) in your project must be granted the appropriate Identity and Access Management (IAM) role. You can grant predefined roles for common use cases or create custom roles for least-privilege access.

This page describes the predefined roles available for generative AI features and lists the specific permissions you can use to create custom roles.

Concepts
  • Principal: An identity that can be granted access to a Google Cloud resource. A principal can be a Google Account (for an end user), a service account (for an application or compute workload), a Google group, or a Google Workspace account or Cloud Identity domain that can access the resource.
  • IAM Role: A collection of permissions that defines what actions are allowed on a resource. When you grant a role to a principal, you grant all the permissions that the role contains.
  • Permission: Determines what operations are allowed on a resource. Permissions are represented in the format service.resource.verb, such as aiplatform.endpoints.predict.

docs.title: Predefined roles
docs.text:
IAM provides predefined roles that grant access to specific resources and prevent unauthorized access to other resources. If a predefined role meets your needs, you can grant it to a principal instead of creating a custom role.

The following table compares the most common predefined roles for users of Vertex AI generative AI features:

Role Description Key Use Case Vertex AI Administrator (roles/aiplatform.admin) Provides full access to all Vertex AI resources, including the ability to manage models, endpoints, and jobs. For principals who need to manage the entire Vertex AI environment, including creating, deleting, and modifying all resources. Vertex AI User (roles/aiplatform.user) Provides permissions to use Vertex AI resources, such as running prediction jobs and managing datasets, but not to create or delete certain resources like endpoints. For developers, data scientists, and applications that need to use generative AI models and other Vertex AI features without having full administrative control.

To learn more about all available Vertex AI IAM roles, see Vertex AI access control with IAM.

docs.title: Granular permissions and custom roles
docs.text:
If the predefined roles don't meet your specific business requirements, you can create a custom role with permissions that you define.

The following table maps generative AI API methods to the permissions required for each operation. You can use this table to determine the permissions to include in a custom role.

Operation Permissions needed Make prompt requests aiplatform.endpoints.predict Save, view, update, and delete prompts in Vertex AI Studio aiplatform.datasets.createaiplatform.datasets.updateaiplatform.datasets.deleteaiplatform.datasets.listaiplatform.datasets.get Model tuning aiplatform.pipelineJobs.*aiplatform.customJobs.*aiplatform.datasets.exportaiplatform.datasets.getaiplatform.models.uploadaiplatform.models.getaiplatform.endpoints.createaiplatform.endpoints.getaiplatform.endpoints.deployaiplatform.metadataStores.getstorage.objects.createstorage.objects.updatestorage.objects.getstorage.objects.list

To see a complete list of Vertex AI IAM permissions, see IAM permissions.

docs.title: Bounding box detection
docs.text:
Preview

This feature is experimental and is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

The Gemini API can perform object detection and localization within images and video. By identifying and delineating objects with bounding boxes, you can build a wide range of applications.

Key benefits include:

  • Simple integration: Easily add object detection capabilities to your applications, regardless of your computer vision expertise.
  • Customizable detection: Generate bounding boxes based on custom text instructions (e.g., "I want to see bounding boxes of all the green objects in this image") without needing to train a custom model.

To see a complete, runnable example of bounding box detection, you can open the "Spatial understanding with Gemini" notebook in your preferred environment.

Open in Colab Open in Colab Enterprise Open in Vertex AI Workbench View on GitHub

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Bounding Box: A rectangular box used to identify the location of an object in an image or video frame.
  • Object Detection: The process of identifying and locating objects within an image or video.
  • Localization: The task of predicting the precise location of an object, typically represented by a bounding box.
  • Normalized Coordinates: A system where coordinates are scaled to a common range (e.g., 0 to 1000), making them independent of the original image's dimensions.
Set up your environment

Install the SDK

To get started, install the Generative AI SDK for Python.

pip install --upgrade google-genai

To learn more, see the SDK reference documentation.

Set environment variables

Set environment variables to use the Generative AI SDK with Vertex AI.

# Replace the `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` values
# with appropriate values for your project.
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global
export GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=True

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Detect objects with bounding boxes
docs.text:
The following workflow outlines the steps to detect objects and draw bounding boxes using the Python SDK.

flowchart TD
    A[Set up environment] --> B[Define helper functions]
    B --> C[Configure the model]
    C --> D[Generate content and visualize]

click A "#setup-environment"
click B "#define-helper-functions"
click C "#configure-the-model"
click D "#generate-content-and-visualize"
Python SDK

1. Import libraries and define helper functions

First, import the necessary libraries. The following helper code includes a pydantic class to represent a bounding box and a function to draw the boxes on an image using PIL. The model returns bounding boxes in the [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max] format, with coordinate values normalized to 1000.

View the helper code 
import requests
from google import genai
from google.genai.types import (
    GenerateContentConfig,
    HarmBlockThreshold,
    HarmCategory,
    HttpOptions,
    Part,
    SafetySetting,
)
from PIL import Image, ImageColor, ImageDraw
from pydantic import BaseModel

# Helper class to represent a bounding box
class BoundingBox(BaseModel):
    """
    Represents a bounding box with its 2D coordinates and associated label.

    Attributes:
        box_2d (list[int]): A list of integers representing the 2D coordinates of the bounding box,
                            typically in the format [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max].
        label (str): A string representing the label or class associated with the object within the bounding box.
    """

    box_2d: list[int]
    label: str

# Helper function to plot bounding boxes on an image
def plot_bounding_boxes(image_uri: str, bounding_boxes: list[BoundingBox]) -> None:
    """
    Plots bounding boxes on an image with labels, using PIL and normalized coordinates.

    Args:
        image_uri: The URI of the image file.
        bounding_boxes: A list of BoundingBox objects. Each box's coordinates are in
                        normalized [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max] format.
    """
    with Image.open(requests.get(image_uri, stream=True, timeout=10).raw) as im:
        width, height = im.size
        draw = ImageDraw.Draw(im)

        colors = list(ImageColor.colormap.keys())

        for i, bbox in enumerate(bounding_boxes):
            # Scale normalized coordinates to image dimensions
            abs_y_min = int(bbox.box_2d[0] / 1000 * height)
            abs_x_min = int(bbox.box_2d[1] / 1000 * width)
            abs_y_max = int(bbox.box_2d[2] / 1000 * height)
            abs_x_max = int(bbox.box_2d[3] / 1000 * width)

            color = colors[i % len(colors)]

            # Draw the rectangle using the correct (x, y) pairs
            draw.rectangle(
                ((abs_x_min, abs_y_min), (abs_x_max, abs_y_max)),
                outline=color,
                width=4,
            )
            if bbox.label:
                # Position the text at the top-left corner of the box
                draw.text((abs_x_min + 8, abs_y_min + 6), bbox.label, fill=color)

        im.show()

2. Configure the model

Next, configure the model by providing system instructions, generation parameters, and a response schema. By setting response_mime_type to application/json and providing a response_schema, you instruct the model to return a JSON object that conforms to the structure of the BoundingBox class.

client = genai.Client(http_options=HttpOptions(api_version="v1"))

config = GenerateContentConfig(
    system_instruction="""
    Return bounding boxes as an array with labels.
    Never return masks. Limit to 25 objects.
    If an object is present multiple times, give each object a unique label
    according to its distinct characteristics (colors, size, position, etc..).
    """,
    temperature=0.5,
    safety_settings=[
        SafetySetting(
            category=HarmCategory.HARM_CATEGORY_DANGEROUS_CONTENT,
            threshold=HarmBlockThreshold.BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH,
        ),
    ],
    response_mime_type="application/json",
    response_schema=list[BoundingBox],
)

3. Generate content and visualize

Finally, call the model with an image and a text prompt. The response will contain the parsed bounding box data, which you can then visualize using the helper function.

image_uri = "https://storage.googleapis.com/generativeai-downloads/images/socks.jpg"

response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents=[
        Part.from_uri(
            file_uri=image_uri,
            mime_type="image/jpeg",
        ),
        "Output the positions of the socks with a face. Label according to position in the image.",
    ],
    config=config,
)
print(response.text)
plot_bounding_boxes(image_uri, response.parsed)

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Example response:

The response.text will contain a JSON string similar to the following:

[
    {"box_2d": [6, 246, 386, 526], "label": "top-left light blue sock with cat face"},
    {"box_2d": [234, 649, 650, 863], "label": "top-right light blue sock with cat face"}
]

docs.title: Control access to Model Garden models
docs.text:
The Model Garden organization policy lets you centrally control which models your users can access and what actions they can take. By default, any principal with permissions to use Vertex AI can use Model Garden to discover, customize, and deploy a wide variety of Google and third-party models.

You can define a policy at the organization, folder, or project level to ensure that your users can only access an approved set of models. For example, you might set a policy to restrict usage to a specific list of Google and third-party models for production environments. A policy applies to all principals within its scope and is not configured on a per-user basis.

For more information, see Introduction to the Organization Policy Service.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Before you begin

Concepts

Concepts
  • Organization Policy: A service for centrally controlling your organization's cloud resources.
  • Model Garden: A curated platform in Vertex AI for discovering, testing, and deploying foundation models.
  • Model ID: The unique identifier for a model in Model Garden, formatted as publishers/PUBLISHER/models/MODEL_NAME.
  • Constraint: A specific type of restriction applied to a Google Cloud service or a list of services.
  • Resource Hierarchy: The organization of Google Cloud resources in a tree-like structure, consisting of an organization, folders, and projects.

Policy evaluation

When a policy is evaluated, all policies that apply to a particular resource are merged. Any explicit deny value takes precedence over any explicit allow value.

For example, if a folder policy denies a specific model and a project policy within that folder allows the same model, access to the model is denied at the project level. The explicit deny at the folder level overrides the allow at the project level. However, if you configure the project policy to override all parent policies, access to the model is allowed.

For more information, see Understanding hierarchy evaluation in the Resource Manager documentation.

Considerations

  • The Model Garden organization policy only applies to models in Model Garden. It does not apply to models registered in the Vertex AI Model Registry.
  • An organization policy can't exceed 500 total allowed and denied values.
  • For a custom policy, you must specify each model and action individually. You cannot allow or deny a group of models with a single rule (for example, denying all third-party models).

docs.title: How Model Garden access control works
docs.text:
This section describes the workflow for controlling access to Model Garden models.

flowchart TD
    A[Understand policy options] --> B[Identify model IDs and actions]
    B --> C[Set the organization policy]
    C --> D[Verify policy enforcement]

click A "#understand-policy-options"
click B "#identify-model-ids-and-actions"
click C "#set-an-organization-policy-for-model-garden"
click D "#verify-the-policy"

docs.title: Understand policy options
docs.text:
When you set a policy, you choose one of the following enforcement approaches. By default, if no policy is set or inherited, all models and actions are allowed.

Policy Option Definition and Use Case Allow all models This is the default behavior. All models and actions in Model Garden are accessible. Use this if you do not need to restrict model access. Deny all models All models and actions in Model Garden are blocked. Use this to completely disable access to Model Garden within a specific organization, folder, or project. Custom allow policy Explicitly lists the models and actions that are permitted. All other models and actions are implicitly denied. Use this for a "deny by default" security posture, where you only want to grant access to a pre-approved list of models. Custom deny policy Explicitly lists the models and actions that are denied. All other models and actions are implicitly allowed. Use this for an "allow by default" posture, where you want to permit access to most models but block a few specific ones.

docs.title: Specify models and actions in a policy
docs.text:
To specify models in a custom policy, use the following format, which combines the model ID and a specific action:

publishers/PUBLISHER/models/MODEL_NAME:ACTION

Replace the following:

  • PUBLISHER: The name of the publisher who owns the model.
  • MODEL_NAME: The name of the model to allow or deny.
  • ACTION: The model action to allow or deny.

For example, to define a policy rule for predictions with the Gemini 1.0 Pro model, you would specify publishers/google/models/gemini-1.0-pro:predict.

The fully qualified ID (publishers/PUBLISHER/models/MODEL_NAME) is also known as the model ID. To find the model ID for a model, go to its model card in Model Garden. For links to model cards, see the list of models in Explore AI models in Model Garden.

Model actions

For each model, you can allow or deny the following actions:

  • predict: Specifies whether users can make online and batch predictions with a model's managed API (model as a service).
  • deploy: For models without a managed API, specifies whether users can deploy models on Google Cloud (for example, using one-click deployment in the Google Cloud console).
  • tune: Specifies whether users can tune models.

docs.title: Set an organization policy for Model Garden
docs.text:
You can set a policy for Model Garden using the Google Cloud console or the Google Cloud CLI. The name of the constraint to use is vertexai.allowedModels.

Google Cloud consoleGoogle Cloud CLI

You can create and manage organization policies directly in the Google Cloud console. When editing the policy, you can select a customization option and add conditional rules to specify the allowed or denied models and actions.

For detailed instructions, see Creating and managing organization policies.

To set a policy with the gcloud CLI, you first create a YAML file that defines your policy rules. Then, you apply the policy to your desired organization, folder, or project.

For detailed instructions, see Using constraints.

docs.title: Policy examples
docs.text:
The following examples are in the YAML format used when setting a policy with the gcloud CLI.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Example: Deny a set of models

The following policy denies specific actions on a list of models and implicitly allows all other models and actions.

name: organizations/ORGANIZATION_ID/policies/vertexai.allowedModels
spec:
  rules:
    - values:
        deniedValues:
        - publishers/meta/models/llama3:deploy
        - publishers/google/models/gemini-1.5-flash-001:tune
        - publishers/hf-google/models/gemma-2b:deploy

Replace ORGANIZATION_ID with the ID of your Google Cloud organization. For more information, see Getting an organization resource.

Example: Allow a set of models

The following policy allows specific actions on a list of models and implicitly denies all other models and actions.

name: organizations/ORGANIZATION_ID/policies/vertexai.allowedModels
spec:
  rules:
    - values:
        allowedValues:
        - publishers/meta/models/llama3:deploy
        - publishers/google/models/gemini-1.5-flash-001:tune
        - publishers/hf-google/models/gemma-2b:deploy

docs.title: Verify the policy
docs.text: After you set and apply the policy, its effects are enforced in the associated organization, folder, or project. Users will only be able to see and use the models and actions permitted by the effective policy in the Model Garden UI and through the API. For example, if a model's deploy action is denied, the Deploy button will be disabled on its model card in the Google Cloud console.

docs.text: • Learn about Model Garden and its offerings.

docs.title: Generative AI and zero data retention
docs.text:
Google was the first in the industry to publish an AI/ML Privacy Commitment, which outlines our belief that customers should have the highest level of security and control over their data that is stored in the cloud. That commitment extends to Google Cloud's generative AI products. Google ensures that its teams are following these commitments through robust data governance practices, which include reviews of the data that Google Cloud uses in the development of its products. More details about how Google processes data can also be found in Google's Cloud Data Processing Addendum (CDPA).

Concepts
  • Zero Data Retention: A state where a service does not store or retain any customer data after a request is processed.
  • Data Caching: Temporarily storing user inputs and model outputs to reduce latency for subsequent, similar prompts.
  • Prompt Logging: Recording prompts for the purpose of monitoring and preventing service abuse.
  • Grounding: Using external, verifiable data sources, like Google Search, to improve the factual accuracy of a model's response.
  • Session Resumption: An optional feature that stores session data to allow a user to reconnect to a previous API session.

docs.title: Training restriction
docs.text: As outlined in Section 17 "Training Restriction" in the Service Terms section of Service Specific Terms, Google won't use your data to train or fine-tune any AI/ML models without your prior permission or instruction. This applies to all managed models on Vertex AI, including GA and pre-GA models.

docs.title: Customer data retention and achieving zero data retention
docs.text:
To achieve zero data retention, customers must take specific actions to disable features where customer data is retained for limited periods. The following table outlines these scenarios and the required actions.

Scenario Data Stored Retention Period Action for Zero Retention Data Caching User inputs and model outputs. Up to 24 hours. Disable data caching at the project level. Prompt Logging for Abuse Monitoring Prompts from non-invoiced accounts. Up to 30 days. Request an exception for abuse monitoring. See Abuse monitoring. Grounding with Google Search Prompts, contextual information, and generated output. Up to 30 days. Do not use the Grounding with Google Search feature. Session Resumption for Gemini Live API Text, video, and audio prompt data and model outputs. Up to 24 hours. Do not enable this optional feature in the API request. See Live API.

This applies to all managed models on Vertex AI, including GA and pre-GA models.

docs.title: Enabling and disabling data caching
docs.text:
You can manage data caching for your Google Cloud project by using the following curl commands. To grant the permissions required to manage caching, see Vertex AI access control with IAM.

The following diagram shows the workflow for managing data caching settings.

flowchart TD
    A[Get current cache status] --> B["Disable caching (if enabled)"]
    A --> C["Enable caching (if disabled)"]

click A "#get-current-cache-setting"
click B "#disable-caching"
click C "#enable-caching"

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Get current cache settingDisable cachingEnable caching

Run the following command to determine if caching is enabled or disabled for a project. To run this command, a user must be granted one of the following roles: roles/aiplatform.viewer, roles/aiplatform.user, or roles/aiplatform.admin.

PROJECT_ID=PROJECT_ID
# Setup project_id
$ gcloud config set project PROJECT_ID

# GetCacheConfig
$ curl -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/cacheConfig

# Response if caching is enabled (caching is enabled by default).
{
  "name": "projects/PROJECT_ID/cacheConfig"
}

# Response if caching is disabled.
{
  "name": "projects/PROJECT_ID/cacheConfig"
  "disableCache": true
}

Run the following curl command to disable caching for a Google Cloud project. To run this command, a user must be granted the Vertex AI Administrator role, roles/aiplatform.admin.

PROJECT_ID=PROJECT_ID
# Setup project_id
$ gcloud config set project PROJECT_ID

# Opt-out of caching.
$ curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/cacheConfig -d '{
  "name": "projects/PROJECT_ID/cacheConfig",
  "disableCache": true
}'

# Response.
{
  "name": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/projects/PROJECT_ID/cacheConfig/operations/${OPERATION_ID}",
  "done": true,
  "response": {
    "@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.protobuf.Empty"
  }
}

If you disabled caching for a Google Cloud project and want to re-enable it, run the following curl command. To run this command, a user must be granted the Vertex AI Administrator role, roles/aiplatform.admin.

PROJECT_ID=PROJECT_ID
# Setup project_id
$ gcloud config set project PROJECT_ID

# Opt in to caching.
$ curl -X PATCH     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/cacheConfig -d '{
  "name": "projects/PROJECT_ID/cacheConfig",
  "disableCache": false
}'

# Response.
{
  "name": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/projects/PROJECT_ID/cacheConfig/operations/${OPERATION_NUMBER}",
  "done": true,
  "response": {
    "@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.protobuf.Empty"
  }
}

docs.title: Dynamic shared quota (DSQ)
docs.text:
Dynamic Shared Quota (DSQ) serves your pay-as-you-go (PayGo) requests with greater flexibility to adapt to your workload needs without requiring you to manage quotas or submit quota increase requests (QIR). With DSQ, there are no predefined quota limits on your usage. Instead, DSQ provides access to a large, shared pool of resources that are dynamically allocated based on real-time availability and demand across all customers using a specific model.

When more customers are active, each customer might experience lower throughput. Conversely, when fewer customers are active, each customer might achieve higher throughput.

Concepts
  • Dynamic Shared Quota (DSQ): A flexible, pay-as-you-go quota model that provides access to a large, shared pool of resources allocated dynamically based on real-time demand.
  • Provisioned Throughput: A service that reserves a specific amount of model processing capacity exclusively for your use, ensuring consistent performance and availability for a fixed cost.

docs.title: When to use Dynamic Shared Quota
docs.text:
Vertex AI offers two primary ways to manage throughput for generative AI models: Dynamic Shared Quota (DSQ) and Provisioned Throughput. DSQ is ideal for applications with variable traffic, while Provisioned Throughput is designed for applications requiring stable, predictable performance.

The following table compares DSQ and Provisioned Throughput:

Feature Dynamic Shared Quota (DSQ) Provisioned Throughput Best for Applications with variable or unpredictable traffic, development, and testing. Production applications requiring high, stable throughput and guaranteed availability. Cost Model Pay-as-you-go (PayGo) based on usage. Fixed hourly cost for reserved capacity, with a one-hour minimum commitment. Performance Throughput is dynamic and depends on shared resource availability and overall system demand. Guaranteed, stable, and predictable throughput based on the reserved capacity. Quota Management No predefined limits; access to a large, shared resource pool. Capacity is reserved exclusively for your project.

For workloads that demand high availability and predictable service levels, see Provisioned Throughput.

docs.title: Supported models
docs.text:
The following Gemini models and their supervised fine-tuned versions support DSQ:

Preview

  • Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash with Live API
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash with image generation
  • Gemini 2.5 Pro
  • Gemini 2.5 Flash
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite

The following legacy Gemini models also support DSQ:

  • Gemini 1.5 Pro
  • Gemini 1.5 Flash

docs.title: How DSQ works
docs.text:
DSQ adapts to your traffic patterns by providing access to a large, shared resource pool. Your project's access to this pool is not capped by a predefined limit but is determined by the overall capacity and the collective real-time demand from all customers. This model offers significant flexibility, allowing your workloads to burst and consume more resources when they are available.

To ensure a fair and stable experience, DSQ uses a dynamic prioritization approach to manage requests, especially during periods of high demand. This means that while the system accommodates bursts, unusually large and rapid spikes in traffic from a single source might be handled with a different priority than more consistent traffic. This management approach protects overall system stability and ensures equitable access for all users.

Gemini requests with multi-modal inputs are subject to the corresponding system rate limits for image, audio, video, and document processing.

docs.title: Handling 429 Resource Exhausted errors
docs.text:
With DSQ, a 429 Resource Exhausted error does not mean you have hit a fixed quota limit on your project. Instead, it indicates that the shared resource pool for a specific model in a region is temporarily experiencing demand that exceeds the available capacity. This is a temporary state of contention for resources, not a permanent block on your project.

Think of it like trying to board a popular train during peak rush hour. There isn't a ticket limit specifically for you, but the train itself might be momentarily full.

Because availability in this dynamic environment can change quickly, we recommend implementing exponential backoff and retry mechanisms in your application to handle these errors. For more tactics, see A guide to handling 429 errors.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Enable Data Access audit logs
docs.text:
To monitor the usage of your model endpoints, you can enable Data Access audit logs for Vertex AI. These logs help you track who did what, where, and when. Data Access audit logs include "admin read" operations that read metadata or configuration, and "data read" and "data write" operations that read or write user-provided data.

Before you begin Concepts

Audit Logs: Chronological records of activities that have occurred within a system, which are used for security, compliance, and operational troubleshooting. Data Access audit logs: A type of audit log that records API calls that read, write, or modify user data.

Grant permissions

To view the data_access log stream in the Google Cloud console after enabling the logs, you need the Private Logs Viewer (roles/logging.privateLogViewer) IAM role.

To resolve this, you can migrate to a supported model. The following table outlines your options.

After updating, test all critical features to ensure your application works as expected before deploying the changes.

docs.title: How do the Gemini 2 models compare to the 1.5 generation?
docs.text:
The Gemini 2 models offer several improvements over the 1.5 generation:

  • Improved multilingual capabilities: Gemini 2 models show strong advancements in multilingual understanding, with increased scores in the Global MMLU (Lite) benchmark.
  • Significant gains in reasoning and knowledge factuality: Gemini 2.5 Pro shows substantial improvements in GPQA (domain expert reasoning) and SimpleQA (world knowledge factuality), indicating an enhanced ability to understand and provide accurate information.
  • Enhanced mathematical problem-solving: Both Gemini 2.0 Flash and Gemini 2.5 Pro demonstrate notable progress in handling complex mathematical problems, as evidenced by the MATH and HiddenMath benchmarks.

The following table compares the Gemini 2 models:

Model name Description Upgrade path for... Gemini 2.5 Pro Strongest model quality (especially for code and world knowledge), with a 1M token-long context window. Gemini 1.5 Pro users who want better quality or are invested in long context and code. Gemini 2.0 Flash Workhorse model for daily tasks, featuring enhanced performance and a real-time Live API. - Gemini 1.5 Flash users who want significantly better quality with a slight increase in latency.- Gemini 1.5 Pro users who want slightly better quality and real-time latency. Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite Our most cost-effective offering to support high throughput. - Gemini 1.5 Flash users who want better quality for the same price and speed.- Customers looking for the fastest model in the Gemini 2 family.

To see all benchmark capabilities for Gemini 2, visit the Google DeepMind documentation.

Generally Available. Key Features Basic image generation. High-quality images, low latency, and flexible editing options.

For more details, see the Imagen 3 overview.

  • Gemini 2.5 Pro: This is an experimental model and has a 10 queries per minute (QPM) limit.

docs.title: Why does my quota usage show as 0% on the API dashboard when I'm sending requests?
docs.text:
Gemini models on Vertex AI use a Dynamic Shared Quota (DSQ) system. This approach automatically manages capacity across all users in a region, ensuring optimal performance without the need for manual quota adjustments. As a result, you won't see traditional quota usage displayed in the Quotas & System Limits tab. Your project automatically receives the necessary resources based on real-time availability.

To monitor your usage, use the Vertex AI Model Garden monitoring dashboard.

Go to the Monitoring Dashboard

Troubleshooting

docs.title: When should I use Provisioned Throughput?
docs.text:
Use the following table to decide between Provisioned Throughput (PT) and the default pay-as-you-go (PAYG) model.

Consideration Provisioned Throughput (PT) Pay-as-you-go (PAYG) Workload Production applications requiring consistent, high throughput and low latency. Development, testing, or applications with variable or unpredictable traffic. Cost Structure Deterministic weekly or monthly costs, enabling predictable budget planning. Billed based on actual usage (per character). Performance Guaranteed capacity ensures a predictable and stable user experience. Performance is subject to shared resource availability.

For more information, see the Provisioned Throughput overview.

docs.title: What models are supported for Provisioned Throughput?
docs.text:
• Google models: The list of supported Google models, including throughput, purchase increment, and burndown rate, is available on our Supported models page.
  • Partner models: To purchase Provisioned Throughput for partner models (such as Anthropic's Claude models), you must contact Google. You cannot order these through the Google Cloud console. For more information, see Partner models.

docs.title: How can I monitor my Provisioned Throughput usage?
docs.text:
You can measure your Provisioned Throughput usage in three ways:

  • Use the Model Garden monitoring dashboard.
  • Use the built-in monitoring metrics.
  • Use the HTTP response headers.

When using the built-in monitoring metrics or HTTP response headers, you can create a chart in the Metrics Explorer to monitor usage.

docs.title: What permissions are required to purchase and use Provisioned Throughput?
docs.text:
To buy and manage Provisioned Throughput, follow the instructions in the Permissions section. The same permissions for pay-as-you-go apply for Provisioned Throughput usage.

If you still have issues placing an order, you might need to add one of the following IAM roles:

  • Vertex AI Administrator
  • Vertex AI Platform Provisioned Throughput Admin

docs.title: What is a GSU?
docs.text: A generative AI scale unit (GSU) is an abstract measure of capacity for throughput provisioning. A GSU's price and capacity are fixed, but the throughput it delivers varies between models because different models require different amounts of capacity to achieve the same throughput.

docs.title: How can I estimate my GSU needs for Provisioned Throughput?
docs.text:
You can estimate your Provisioned Throughput needs by following these steps:

  1. Gather your requirements: Determine your expected inputs per query, outputs per query, and queries per second (QPS).
  2. Calculate your throughput: 
    Throughput per sec = (Inputs per query in chars + Outputs per query in chars) * QPS
  3. Calculate your GSUs: Use the estimation tool in the purchasing console to calculate the number of GSUs needed to cover your usage for the given model.

Go to the Estimation Tool

For a detailed walkthrough, see the example of estimating your Provisioned Throughput needs.

docs.title: How often am I billed for Provisioned Throughput?
docs.text: You are invoiced at the end of each month for any charges you incur for Provisioned Throughput usage during that month.

docs.title: How long does it take to activate my Provisioned Throughput order?
docs.text:
• Small orders or incremental increases: The order is typically auto-approved and ready within minutes if capacity is available.
  • Large orders or increases: These may take longer and might require direct communication to prepare capacity. We aim to provide a decision (approved or denied) within one week of submission.

docs.title: Can I test Provisioned Throughput before placing an order?
docs.text:
While a direct test environment is not available, you can place a one-week order with a limited number of GSUs. This provides a cost-effective way to experience its benefits and assess its suitability for your requirements.

For more information, see Purchase Provisioned Throughput.
