docs.title: Controlled generation
docs.text:
Controlled generation guides model output to adhere to specific constraints, such as a JSON schema.

PythonJavaJavaScriptGo

Before

_RESPONSE_SCHEMA_STRUCT = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "location": {
            "type": "string",
        },
    },
    "required": ["location"],
}

response = model.generate_content(
    contents="Why is sky blue? Respond in JSON Format.",
    generation_config=generative_models.GenerationConfig(
        ...
        response_schema=_RESPONSE_SCHEMA_STRUCT,
    ),
)

After

response_schema = {
  "type": "ARRAY",
  "items": {
    "type": "OBJECT",
    "properties": {
      "recipe_name": {"type": "STRING"},
      "ingredients": {"type": "ARRAY", "items": {"type": "STRING"}},
    },
    "required": ["recipe_name", "ingredients"],
  },
}

prompt = """
  List a few popular cookie recipes.
"""

response = client.models.generate_content(
  model="gemini-2.5-flash",
  contents=prompt,
  config={
    "response_mime_type": "application/json",
    "response_schema": response_schema,
  },
)

Before

import com.google.cloud.vertexai.api.Schema;
import com.google.cloud.vertexai.api.Type;
import com.google.cloud.vertexai.generativeai.ContentMaker;
import com.google.cloud.vertexai.generativeai.PartMaker;

GenerationConfig generationConfig = GenerationConfig.newBuilder()
  .setResponseMimeType("application/json")
  .setResponseSchema(Schema.newBuilder()
    .setType(Type.ARRAY)
    .setItems(Schema.newBuilder()
      .setType(Type.OBJECT)
      .putProperties("object", Schema.newBuilder().setType(Type.STRING).build())
      .build())
    .build())
  .build();

GenerativeModel model = new GenerativeModel(modelName, vertexAI)
  .withGenerationConfig(generationConfig);

GenerateContentResponse response = model.generateContent(
  ContentMaker.fromMultiModalData(
    PartMaker.fromMimeTypeAndData("image/jpeg",
      "gs://cloud-samples-data/generative-ai/image/office-desk.jpeg"),
    PartMaker.fromMimeTypeAndData("image/jpeg",
      "gs://cloud-samples-data/generative-ai/image/gardening-tools.jpeg"),
    "Generate a list of objects in the images."

);

After

Import the Schema and Type modules:

import com.google.genai.types.Schema;
import com.google.genai.types.Type;

Create the response schema:

Schema schema =
  Schema.builder()
    .type(Type.Known.ARRAY)
    .items(
      Schema.builder()
        .type(Type.Known.OBJECT)
        .properties(
          ImmutableMap.of(
            "recipe_name",
            Schema.builder().type(Type.Known.STRING).build(),
            "ingredients",
            Schema.builder()
              .type(Type.Known.ARRAY)
              .items(Schema.builder().type(Type.Known.STRING))
              .build()))
        .required("recipe_name", "ingredients"))
    .build();

Add the schema to the content config:

GenerateContentConfig config =
  GenerateContentConfig.builder()
    .responseMimeType("application/json")
    .candidateCount(1)
    .responseSchema(schema)
    .build();

Generate responses with the config:

GenerateContentResponse response =
client.models.generateContent(
    "gemini-2.5-flash", "List a few popular cookie recipes.", config);

For the full implementation, see GenerateContentWithResponseSchema.java.

docs.title: Count tokens
docs.text:
Tokens are the fundamental units of text that models process. You can count or compute tokens in a request.

PythonJavaJavaScriptGo

Before

content = ["Why is sky blue?", "Explain it like I'm 5."]

response = model.count_tokens(content)

After

Count Tokens

response = client.models.count_tokens(
    model='gemini-2.5-flash',
    contents='why is the sky blue?',
)
print(response)

Compute tokens

response = client.models.compute_tokens(
    model='gemini-2.5-flash',
    contents='why is the sky blue?',
)
print(response)

Before

import com.google.cloud.vertexai.api.CountTokensResponse;

CountTokensResponse response = model.countTokens(textPrompt);

int promptTokenCount = response.getTotalTokens();
int promptCharCount = response.getTotalBillableCharacters();

GenerateContentResponse contentResponse = model.generateContent(textPrompt);

int tokenCount = contentResponse.getUsageMetadata().getPromptTokenCount();
int candidateTokenCount = contentResponse.getUsageMetadata().getCandidatesTokenCount();
int totalTokenCount = contentResponse.getUsageMetadata().getTotalTokenCount();

After

Import the CountTokensResponse and ComputeTokensResponse modules:

import com.google.genai.types.CountTokensResponse;
import com.google.genai.types.ComputeTokensResponse;

Use countTokens to count the number of tokens used for a prompt:

CountTokensResponse response =
  client.models.countTokens("gemini-2.5-flash", "What is your name?", null);

Use computeTokens for a more granular analysis of how the prompt is tokenized:

ComputeTokensResponse response =
  client.models.computeTokens("gemini-2.5-flash", "What is your name?", null);

For the full implementation, see CountTokens.java.

Before

const request = {
    contents: [{role: 'user', parts: [{text: 'How are you doing today?'}]}],
  };
const response = await generativeModel.countTokens(request);
console.log('count tokens response: ', JSON.stringify(response));

After

const response = await ai.models.countTokens({
  model: 'gemini-2.5-flash',
  contents: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.',
});

Before

package tokencount

import (
  "context"
  "fmt"
  "cloud.google.com/go/vertexai/genai"
)

resp, err := model.CountTokens(ctx, prompt)

fmt.Fprintf(w, "Number of tokens for the prompt: %d\n", resp.TotalTokens)

resp2, err := model.GenerateContent(ctx, prompt)

fmt.Fprintf(w, "Number of tokens for the prompt: %d\n", resp2.UsageMetadata.PromptTokenCount)
fmt.Fprintf(w, "Number of tokens for the candidates: %d\n", resp2.UsageMetadata.CandidatesTokenCount)
fmt.Fprintf(w, "Total number of tokens: %d\n", resp2.UsageMetadata.TotalTokenCount)

After

  "context"

client, err := genai.NewClient(ctx, &genai.ClientConfig{Backend: genai.BackendVertexAI})

countTokensResult, err := client.Models.CountTokens(ctx, *model, genai.Text("What is your name?"), nil)

fmt.Println(countTokensResult.TotalTokens)

docs.title: Model deprecations (MaaS)
docs.text:
After a period of time, MaaS models are deprecated and typically replaced with newer model versions. To provide you with time to test and migrate to newer models, this page lists all models that are deprecated along with their shutdown date.

Concepts
  • Models as a Service (MaaS): Provides access to third-party generative AI models on Vertex AI without needing to manage the underlying infrastructure.
  • Queries Per Minute (QPM): The maximum number of requests your project can send to a model every minute.
  • Tokens Per Minute (TPM): The total number of input and output tokens your project can process every minute.
  • Context Length: The maximum number of tokens (including both input and output) that a model can process in a single request.
Mistral Nemo

Mistral Nemo is deprecated as of June 30, 2025 and will be shutdown on August 20, 2025. Mistral Nemo is available to existing customers only.

Mistral Nemo is Mistral AI's most cost efficient proprietary model. Use Mistral Nemo for low-latency workloads and basic tasks that can be done in bulk, such as classification, customer support, and text generation.

docs.title: Get batch text embeddings predictions
docs.text: Batch prediction is a way to efficiently send a large number of non-latency-sensitive embedding requests. Unlike online predictions, where you are limited to one input request at a time, you can send up to 30,000 prompts in a single batch request. You specify an output location, provide your input source, and the embedding predictions are asynchronously populated in your output location.

docs.title: Supported models
docs.text:
All stable versions of text embedding models support batch predictions. Stable versions are models that are no longer in preview and are fully supported for production environments.

To see the full list of supported embedding models, see Embedding model and versions.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Set up your environment Concepts
  • Batch prediction: A process for sending a large number of prediction requests in a single job for offline processing, rather than one at a time.
  • JSONL (JSON Lines): A text format for storing structured data where each line is a separate JSON object.
  • BigQuery: A serverless, highly scalable data warehouse that lets you run SQL queries over vast amounts of data.
  • REST API: A standardized way for applications to communicate over HTTP, allowing you to make requests to Vertex AI services directly.

Set up your project

  1. In the Google Cloud console, on the project selector page, select or create a Google Cloud project.
  2. Make sure that billing is enabled for your Google Cloud project.
  3. Enable the Vertex AI API.
  4. Set up authentication.

Authenticate

To use the REST API or the Python SDK, you need to authenticate. The examples on this page assume you are using gcloud for authentication.

  1. Install the Google Cloud CLI.
  2. To initialize the gcloud CLI, run the following command: 
    gcloud init
  3. To authenticate your Google Account to the gcloud CLI, run the following command: 
    gcloud auth login

This tutorial shows you how to get batch predictions for text embeddings. The following diagram shows the workflow.

flowchart TD
    A[Prepare inputs] --> B[Request a batch response]
    B --> C[Retrieve batch output]

click A "#prepare-inputs"
click B "#request-a-batch-response"
click C "#retrieve-batch-output"
Tutorial: Get batch text embeddings

Prepare your inputs

The input for batch requests is a list of prompts stored in either a BigQuery table or a JSON Lines (JSONL) file in Cloud Storage. Choose the format that best suits your data source and workflow.

Format Description Use Case JSONL A text file in Cloud Storage where each line is a JSON object containing a content field. Ideal for unstructured or file-based data pipelines. Simple to create and manage for smaller datasets. BigQuery A table in BigQuery with a column that contains the prompt text. Best for large-scale, structured datasets already stored in BigQuery. Enables seamless integration with other data analytics workflows.

JSONL

View JSONL input and output examples

Input Example

Each line in the file must be a valid JSON object with a content key.

{"content":"Give a short description of a machine learning model:"}
{"content":"Best recipe for banana bread:"}

Output Example

The output file contains one JSON object per line, corresponding to each input request.

{"instance":{"content":"Give..."},"predictions": [{"embeddings":{"statistics":{"token_count":8,"truncated":false},"values":[0.2,....]}}],"status":""}
{"instance":{"content":"Best..."},"predictions": [{"embeddings":{"statistics":{"token_count":3,"truncated":false},"values":[0.1,....]}}],"status":""}

BigQuery

View BigQuery input and output examples

Input Example

The input table should contain at least one column with the prompt text. The column name can be anything.

content "Give a short description of a machine learning model:" "Best recipe for banana bread:"

Output Example

The output table includes the original input content, a predictions column with the embeddings, and a status column.

content predictions status "Give a short description of a machine learning model:" '[{"embeddings": { "statistics":{"token_count":8,"truncated":false}, "Values":[0.1,....] } }]' "Best recipe for banana bread:" '[{"embeddings": { "statistics":{"token_count":3,"truncated":false}, "Values":[0.2,....] } }]'

Request a batch response

You can request a batch response using the Vertex AI REST API or the Gen AI SDK for Python. Depending on the number of input items, the task can take some time to complete.

Method Description Use Case REST API Send an HTTP POST request directly to the Vertex AI API endpoint. Useful for integration with any programming language or for environments where installing a client library is not feasible. Python SDK Use the google-genai library to create and manage batch jobs programmatically. Recommended for Python-based applications, providing a higher-level, more convenient interface. REST APIPython SDK

To request a batch prediction, send a POST request to the publisher model endpoint.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: The ID of your Google Cloud project.
  • BP_JOB_NAME: A unique name for your batch prediction job.
  • INPUT_URI: The URI of your input source. For BigQuery, use the format bq://PROJECT_ID.DATASET_ID.TABLE_ID. For JSONL, use the Cloud Storage URI gs://BUCKET_NAME/FILENAME.jsonl.
  • OUTPUT_URI: The URI of your output destination. For BigQuery, use bq://PROJECT_ID.DATASET_ID. For Cloud Storage, use gs://BUCKET_NAME/PREFIX/.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/batchPredictionJobs

Request JSON body:

The following example uses a BigQuery input source. To use a JSONL file, change instancesFormat to jsonl and bigquerySource to gcsSource.

{
    "name": "BP_JOB_NAME",
    "displayName": "BP_JOB_NAME",
    "model": "publishers/google/models/textembedding-gecko",
    "inputConfig": {
      "instancesFormat":"bigquery",
      "bigquerySource":{
        "inputUri" : "INPUT_URI"
      }
    },
    "outputConfig": {
      "predictionsFormat":"bigquery",
      "bigqueryDestination":{
        "outputUri": "OUTPUT_URI"
    }
  }
}

To send your request, choose one of these options:

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

curl

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \  
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \  
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \  
     -d @request.json \  
     "https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/batchPredictionJobs"

PowerShell

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token  
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }  

Invoke-WebRequest `  
    -Method POST `  
    -Headers $headers `  
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `  
    -InFile request.json `  
    -Uri "https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/batchPredictionJobs" | Select-Object -Expand Content

You should receive a JSON response similar to the following, which includes the name of the job containing its unique ID.

{
  "name": "projects/123456789012/locations/us-central1/batchPredictionJobs/1234567890123456789",
  "displayName": "BP_sample_publisher_BQ_20230712_134650",
  "model": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/models/textembedding-gecko",
  "inputConfig": {
    "instancesFormat": "bigquery",
    "bigquerySource": {
      "inputUri": "bq://project_name.dataset_name.text_input"
    }
  },
  "modelParameters": {},
  "outputConfig": {
    "predictionsFormat": "bigquery",
    "bigqueryDestination": {
      "outputUri": "bq://project_name.llm_dataset.embedding_out_BP_sample_publisher_BQ_20230712_134650"
    }
  },
  "state": "JOB_STATE_PENDING",
  "createTime": "2023-07-12T20:46:52.148717Z",
  "updateTime": "2023-07-12T20:46:52.148717Z",
  "labels": {
    "owner": "sample_owner",
    "product": "llm"
  },
  "modelVersionId": "1",
  "modelMonitoringStatus": {}
}

You can poll for the status of the batch job using the job ID (BATCH_JOB_ID) until the job state is JOB_STATE_SUCCEEDED.

curl \
  -X GET \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/batchPredictionJobs/BATCH_JOB_ID

Note: You can run only one batch response job at a time. Custom Service accounts, live progress, CMEK, and VPC-SC reports aren't supported at this time.

Install the SDK

pip install --upgrade google-genai

To learn more, see the SDK reference documentation.

Run the code

Set environment variables and run the Python script to create and monitor a batch job.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

# Replace the `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` values
# with appropriate values for your project.
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=us-central1
export GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=True


import time

from google import genai
from google.genai.types import CreateBatchJobConfig, JobState, HttpOptions

client = genai.Client(http_options=HttpOptions(api_version="v1"))
# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below line
# output_uri = "gs://your-bucket/your-prefix"

# See the documentation: https://googleapis.github.io/python-genai/genai.html#genai.batches.Batches.create
job = client.batches.create(
    model="text-embedding-005",
    # Source link: https://storage.cloud.google.com/cloud-samples-data/generative-ai/embeddings/embeddings_input.jsonl
    src="gs://cloud-samples-data/generative-ai/embeddings/embeddings_input.jsonl",
    config=CreateBatchJobConfig(dest=output_uri),
)
print(f"Job name: {job.name}")
print(f"Job state: {job.state}")
# Example response:
# Job name: projects/%PROJECT_ID%/locations/us-central1/batchPredictionJobs/9876453210000000000
# Job state: JOB_STATE_PENDING

# See the documentation: https://googleapis.github.io/python-genai/genai.html#genai.types.BatchJob
completed_states = {
    JobState.JOB_STATE_SUCCEEDED,
    JobState.JOB_STATE_FAILED,
    JobState.JOB_STATE_CANCELLED,
    JobState.JOB_STATE_PAUSED,
}

while job.state not in completed_states:
    time.sleep(30)
    job = client.batches.get(name=job.name)
    print(f"Job state: {job.state}")
    if job.state == JobState.JOB_STATE_FAILED:
        print(f"Error: {job.error}")
        break

# Example response:
# Job state: JOB_STATE_PENDING
# Job state: JOB_STATE_RUNNING
# Job state: JOB_STATE_RUNNING
# ...
# Job state: JOB_STATE_SUCCEEDED

Retrieve batch output

When a batch prediction task is complete, the output is stored in the Cloud Storage bucket or BigQuery table that you specified in your request. You can then access the files in Cloud Storage or query the table in BigQuery to retrieve your embeddings.

docs.title: Get multimodal embeddings
docs.text:
To see an example of multimodal embeddings, you can run the "Intro to multimodal embeddings" Jupyter notebook in one of the following environments:

Open in Colab Open in Colab Enterprise Open in Vertex AI Workbench View on GitHub

The multimodal embeddings model generates 1408-dimension numerical representations (vectors) based on the input you provide, which can include a combination of image, text, and video data. These embedding vectors can then be used for subsequent tasks like image classification, video content moderation, or multimodal search.

Because the image, text, and video embedding vectors exist in the same semantic space and have the same dimensionality, they can be used interchangeably for various use cases, such as searching for images using text or searching for videos using an image.

For text-only embedding use cases, we recommend using the Vertex AI text embeddings API instead. The text-embeddings API is often better suited for tasks like text-based semantic search, clustering, and long-form document analysis. For more information, see Get text embeddings.

docs.title: Supported models
docs.text:
You can get multimodal embeddings by using the following model:

  • multimodalembedding

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
Consider the following input aspects when using the multimodal embeddings model:

  • Text in images: The model can distinguish text within images, similar to optical character recognition (OCR). If you need to differentiate between a description of the image content and the text appearing in an image, use prompt engineering to be specific. For example, use "picture of a cat" versus "the text 'cat'".

    Input Text Image the text 'cat' picture of a cat Image credit: Manja Vitolic on Unsplash.

  • Embedding similarities: The dot product of embeddings is a similarity metric, not a calibrated probability. Its score distribution can vary across different use cases. Avoid using a fixed value threshold to measure quality. Instead, use ranking approaches for retrieval or a sigmoid function for classification tasks.

docs.title: API limits
docs.text:
The following limits apply when you use the multimodalembedding model.

Limit Value and description Text and image data Maximum API requests per minute per project 120-600, depending on the region. Maximum text length 32 tokens (~32 words). Inputs exceeding this length are internally truncated. Language English Image formats BMP, GIF, JPG, PNG Image size Base64-encoded images: 20 MB (when transcoded to PNG). Cloud Storage images: 20 MB (original file format). The model resizes images to 512x512 pixels, so higher-resolution images are not necessary. To reduce latency, use smaller images. Video data Audio supported N/A - The model does not consider audio content when generating video embeddings. Video formats AVI, FLV, MKV, MOV, MP4, MPEG, MPG, WEBM, and WMV. Maximum video length (Cloud Storage) No limit. However, only 2 minutes of content can be analyzed at a time per request.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Embeddings: Numerical vector representations of data (like text or images) that capture semantic meaning, allowing machines to understand relationships and similarity between different pieces of data.
  • Multimodal: Refers to a system's ability to process and understand information from multiple types of data, such as text, images, and video, simultaneously.
  • Semantic Space: A high-dimensional space where embeddings are plotted, such that items with similar meanings are located closer to each other.
  • Tokens: The basic units of text that a model processes, which can be words, subwords, or characters.
  • Base64: An encoding scheme that converts binary data (like images) into a text string, allowing it to be easily transmitted over systems that are designed to handle text.
Prerequisites

  1. Sign in to your Google Cloud account. If you're new to Google Cloud, create an account to evaluate how our products perform in real-world scenarios. New customers also get $300 in free credits to run, test, and deploy workloads.

docs.title: Get embeddings for image and text
docs.text:
Use the following code samples to send an embedding request with image and text data. You can send a request with both data types or with an individual data type.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

RESTPythonNode.jsJavaGo

For more information about multimodalembedding model requests, see the multimodalembedding model API reference.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • LOCATION: Your project's region. For example, us-central1, europe-west2, or asia-northeast3.
  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • TEXT: The target text to get embeddings for. For example, a cat.
  • B64_ENCODED_IMG: The target image to get embeddings for, specified as a base64-encoded byte string.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/multimodalembedding@001:predict

Request JSON body:

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "text": "TEXT",
      "image": {
        "bytesBase64Encoded": "B64_ENCODED_IMG"
      }
    }
  ]
}

To send your request, choose one of these options:

curl

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d @request.json \
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/multimodalembedding@001:predict"
PowerShell

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method POST `
    -Headers $headers `
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `
    -InFile request.json `
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/multimodalembedding@001:predict" | Select-Object -Expand Content
View sample response

The embedding the model returns is a 1408-dimension float vector. The following sample response is shortened for space.

{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "textEmbedding": [
        0.010477379,
        -0.00399621,
        0.00576670747,
        [...]
        -0.00823613815,
        -0.0169572588,
        -0.00472954148
      ],
      "imageEmbedding": [
        0.00262696808,
        -0.00198890246,
        0.0152047109,
        -0.0103145819,
        [...]
        0.0324628279,
        0.0284924973,
        0.011650892,
        -0.00452344026
      ]
    }
  ],
  "deployedModelId": "DEPLOYED_MODEL_ID"
}

To learn how to install or update the Vertex AI SDK for Python, see Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python. For more information, see the Vertex AI SDK for Python API reference documentation.

import vertexai
from vertexai.vision_models import Image, MultiModalEmbeddingModel

# TODO(developer): Update & uncomment line below

model = MultiModalEmbeddingModel.from_pretrained("multimodalembedding@001")
image = Image.load_from_file(
    "gs://cloud-samples-data/vertex-ai/llm/prompts/landmark1.png"
)

embeddings = model.get_embeddings(
    image=image,
    contextual_text="Colosseum",
    dimension=1408,
)
print(f"Image Embedding: {embeddings.image_embedding}")
print(f"Text Embedding: {embeddings.text_embedding}")
# Example response:
# Image Embedding: [-0.0123147098, 0.0727171078, ...]
# Text Embedding: [0.00230263756, 0.0278981831, ...]

Before trying this sample, follow the Node.js setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Node.js API reference documentation.

/**
 * TODO(developer): Uncomment these variables before running the sample.\
 * (Not necessary if passing values as arguments)

// const project = 'YOUR_PROJECT_ID';
// const location = 'YOUR_PROJECT_LOCATION';
// const baseImagePath = 'YOUR_BASE_IMAGE_PATH';
// const textPrompt = 'YOUR_TEXT_PROMPT';
const aiplatform = require('@google-cloud/aiplatform');

// Imports the Google Cloud Prediction service client
const {PredictionServiceClient} = aiplatform.v1;

// Import the helper module for converting arbitrary protobuf.Value objects.
const {helpers} = aiplatform;

// Specifies the location of the api endpoint
const clientOptions = {
  apiEndpoint: 'us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com',
};
const publisher = 'google';
const model = 'multimodalembedding@001';

// Instantiates a client
const predictionServiceClient = new PredictionServiceClient(clientOptions);

async function predictImageFromImageAndText() {
  // Configure the parent resource
  const endpoint = `projects/${project}/locations/${location}/publishers/${publisher}/models/${model}`;

  const fs = require('fs');
  const imageFile = fs.readFileSync(baseImagePath);

  // Convert the image data to a Buffer and base64 encode it.
  const encodedImage = Buffer.from(imageFile).toString('base64');

  const prompt = {
    text: textPrompt,
    image: {
      bytesBase64Encoded: encodedImage,
    },
  };
  const instanceValue = helpers.toValue(prompt);
  const instances = [instanceValue];

  const parameter = {
    sampleCount: 1,
  };
  const parameters = helpers.toValue(parameter);

  const request = {
    endpoint,
    instances,
    parameters,
  };

  // Predict request
  const [response] = await predictionServiceClient.predict(request);
  console.log('Get image embedding response');
  const predictions = response.predictions;
  console.log('\tPredictions :');
  for (const prediction of predictions) {
    console.log(`\t\tPrediction : ${JSON.stringify(prediction)}`);
  }
}

await predictImageFromImageAndText();

Before trying this sample, follow the Java setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Java API reference documentation.

import com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.EndpointName;
import com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.PredictResponse;
import com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.PredictionServiceClient;
import com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.PredictionServiceSettings;
import com.google.gson.Gson;
import com.google.gson.JsonObject;
import com.google.protobuf.InvalidProtocolBufferException;
import com.google.protobuf.Value;
import com.google.protobuf.util.JsonFormat;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Paths;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Base64;
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

public class PredictImageFromImageAndTextSample {

  public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
    // TODO(developer): Replace this variable before running the sample.
    String project = "YOUR_PROJECT_ID";
    String textPrompt = "YOUR_TEXT_PROMPT";
    String baseImagePath = "YOUR_BASE_IMAGE_PATH";

    // Learn how to use text prompts to update an image:
    // https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/generative-ai/image/edit-images
    Map<String, Object> parameters = new HashMap<String, Object>();
    parameters.put("sampleCount", 1);

    String location = "us-central1";
    String publisher = "google";
    String model = "multimodalembedding@001";

    predictImageFromImageAndText(
        project, location, publisher, model, textPrompt, baseImagePath, parameters);
  }

  // Update images using text prompts
  public static void predictImageFromImageAndText(
      String project,
      String location,
      String publisher,
      String model,
      String textPrompt,
      String baseImagePath,
      Map<String, Object> parameters)
      throws IOException {
    final String endpoint = String.format("%s-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443", location);
    final PredictionServiceSettings predictionServiceSettings =
        PredictionServiceSettings.newBuilder().setEndpoint(endpoint).build();

    // Initialize client that will be used to send requests. This client only needs to be created
    // once, and can be reused for multiple requests.
    try (PredictionServiceClient predictionServiceClient =
        PredictionServiceClient.create(predictionServiceSettings)) {
      final EndpointName endpointName =
          EndpointName.ofProjectLocationPublisherModelName(project, location, publisher, model);

      // Convert the image to Base64
      byte[] imageData = Base64.getEncoder().encode(Files.readAllBytes(Paths.get(baseImagePath)));
      String encodedImage = new String(imageData, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);

      JsonObject jsonInstance = new JsonObject();
      jsonInstance.addProperty("text", textPrompt);
      JsonObject jsonImage = new JsonObject();
      jsonImage.addProperty("bytesBase64Encoded", encodedImage);
      jsonInstance.add("image", jsonImage);

      Value instanceValue = stringToValue(jsonInstance.toString());
      List<Value> instances = new ArrayList<>();
      instances.add(instanceValue);

      Gson gson = new Gson();
      String gsonString = gson.toJson(parameters);
      Value parameterValue = stringToValue(gsonString);

      PredictResponse predictResponse =
          predictionServiceClient.predict(endpointName, instances, parameterValue);
      System.out.println("Predict Response");
      System.out.println(predictResponse);
      for (Value prediction : predictResponse.getPredictionsList()) {
        System.out.format("\tPrediction: %s\n", prediction);
      }
    }
  }

  // Convert a Json string to a protobuf.Value
  static Value stringToValue(String value) throws InvalidProtocolBufferException {
    Value.Builder builder = Value.newBuilder();
    JsonFormat.parser().merge(value, builder);
    return builder.build();
  }
}

import (
    "context"
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"
    "io"

    aiplatform "cloud.google.com/go/aiplatform/apiv1beta1"
    aiplatformpb "cloud.google.com/go/aiplatform/apiv1beta1/aiplatformpb"
    "google.golang.org/api/option"
    "google.golang.org/protobuf/encoding/protojson"
    "google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/structpb"
)

// generateForTextAndImage shows how to use the multimodal model to generate embeddings for
// text and image inputs.
func generateForTextAndImage(w io.Writer, project, location string) error {
    // location = "us-central1"
    ctx := context.Background()
    apiEndpoint := fmt.Sprintf("%s-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443", location)
    client, err := aiplatform.NewPredictionClient(ctx, option.WithEndpoint(apiEndpoint))
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to construct API client: %w", err)
    }
    defer client.Close()

    model := "multimodalembedding@001"
    endpoint := fmt.Sprintf("projects/%s/locations/%s/publishers/google/models/%s", project, location, model)

    // This is the input to the model's prediction call. For schema, see:
    // https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/model-reference/multimodal-embeddings-api#request_body
    instance, err := structpb.NewValue(map[string]any{
        "image": map[string]any{
            // Image input can be provided either as a Google Cloud Storage URI or as
            // base64-encoded bytes using the "bytesBase64Encoded" field.
            "gcsUri": "gs://cloud-samples-data/vertex-ai/llm/prompts/landmark1.png",
        },
        "text": "Colosseum",
    })
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to construct request payload: %w", err)
    }

    req := &aiplatformpb.PredictRequest{
        Endpoint: endpoint,
        // The model supports only 1 instance per request.
        Instances: []*structpb.Value{instance},
    }

    resp, err := client.Predict(ctx, req)
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate embeddings: %w", err)
    }

    instanceEmbeddingsJson, err := protojson.Marshal(resp.GetPredictions()[0])
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to convert protobuf value to JSON: %w", err)
    }
    // For response schema, see:
    // https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/model-reference/multimodal-embeddings-api#response-body
    var instanceEmbeddings struct {
        ImageEmbeddings []float32 `json:"imageEmbedding"`
        TextEmbeddings  []float32 `json:"textEmbedding"`
    }
    if err := json.Unmarshal(instanceEmbeddingsJson, &instanceEmbeddings); err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to unmarshal JSON: %w", err)
    }

    imageEmbedding := instanceEmbeddings.ImageEmbeddings
    textEmbedding := instanceEmbeddings.TextEmbeddings

    fmt.Fprintf(w, "Text embedding (length=%d): %v\n", len(textEmbedding), textEmbedding)
    fmt.Fprintf(w, "Image embedding (length=%d): %v\n", len(imageEmbedding), imageEmbedding)
    // Example response:
    // Text embedding (length=1408): [0.0023026613 0.027898183 -0.011858357 ... ]
    // Image embedding (length=1408): [-0.012314269 0.07271844 0.00020170923 ... ]

    return nil
}

docs.title: Specify lower-dimension embeddings
docs.text:
By default, an embedding request returns a 1408-dimension float vector. You can also specify lower-dimension embeddings for text and image data to optimize for latency and storage versus quality.

Dimension Benefit 128, 256, 512 Lower latency and smaller storage footprint for subsequent tasks like search or recommendation. 1408 (default) Higher accuracy and quality for the same tasks. RESTPythonGo

To request a lower dimension, add the parameters.dimension field to your request body. The parameter accepts one of the following values: 128, 256, 512, or 1408.

Request JSON body:

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "image": {
        "gcsUri": "IMAGE_URI"
      },
      "text": "TEXT"
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "dimension": EMBEDDING_DIMENSION
  }
}
View sample response (128 dimensions) 
{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "imageEmbedding": [
        0.0279239565,
        [...128 dimension vector...]
        0.00403284049
      ],
      "textEmbedding": [
        0.202921599,
        [...128 dimension vector...]
        -0.0365431122
      ]
    }
  ],
  "deployedModelId": "DEPLOYED_MODEL_ID"
}
View sample response (256 dimensions) 
{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "imageEmbedding": [
        0.248620048,
        [...256 dimension vector...]
        -0.0646447465
      ],
      "textEmbedding": [
        0.0757875815,
        [...256 dimension vector...]
        -0.02749932
      ]
    }
  ],

docs.title: Get embeddings for video
docs.text: You can request embeddings for a video alone, or in combination with image and text data.

docs.title: Video embedding modes
docs.text:
There are three modes for video embeddings, which correspond to the density of embeddings generated. You specify the mode by setting the intervalSec in your request. An embedding is generated for each video interval of intervalSec length. The minimal interval is 4 seconds, and intervals greater than 120 seconds might reduce embedding quality. Pricing depends on the mode you use.

Mode Max embeddings per minute Video embedding interval (intervalSec) Essential 4 intervalSec >= 15 Standard 8 8 <= intervalSec < 15 Plus 15 4 <= intervalSec < 8

docs.title: Video embeddings best practices
docs.text:
• Single embedding for a video: To generate a single embedding for the first two minutes of a video, set intervalSec to 120.
  • Videos longer than two minutes: To process a video longer than two minutes, send multiple requests, specifying the startOffsetSec and endOffsetSec for each two-minute segment.

docs.title: Get video-only embeddings
docs.text:
Use the following samples to get embeddings for video content.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

RESTPythonGo

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • LOCATION: Your project's region.
  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • VIDEO_URI: The Cloud Storage URI of the target video (e.g., gs://my-bucket/embeddings/supermarket-video.mp4). You can also provide the video as a base64-encoded byte string using bytesBase64Encoded.
  • videoSegmentConfig: (Optional) Specify the video segments in seconds. If omitted, the default is {"startOffsetSec": 0, "endOffsetSec": 120, "intervalSec": 16}, which falls into the Essential pricing tier.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/multimodalembedding@001:predict

Request JSON body:

  "instances": [

import (
    "context"
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"
    "io"
    "time"

    aiplatform "cloud.google.com/go/aiplatform/apiv1beta1"
    aiplatformpb "cloud.google.com/go/aiplatform/apiv1beta1/aiplatformpb"
    "google.golang.org/api/option"
    "google.golang.org/protobuf/encoding/protojson"
    "google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/structpb"
)

// generateForVideo shows how to use the multimodal model to generate embeddings for video input.
func generateForVideo(w io.Writer, project, location string) error {
    // location = "us-central1"

    // The default context timeout may be not enough to process a video input.
    ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)
    defer cancel()

    apiEndpoint := fmt.Sprintf("%s-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443", location)
    client, err := aiplatform.NewPredictionClient(ctx, option.WithEndpoint(apiEndpoint))
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to construct API client: %w", err)
    }
    defer client.Close()

    model := "multimodalembedding@001"
    endpoint := fmt.Sprintf("projects/%s/locations/%s/publishers/google/models/%s", project, location, model)

    // This is the input to the model's prediction call. For schema, see:
    // https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/model-reference/multimodal-embeddings-api#request_body
    instances, err := structpb.NewValue(map[string]any{
        "video": map[string]any{
            // Video input can be provided either as a Google Cloud Storage URI or as base64-encoded
            // bytes using the "bytesBase64Encoded" field.
            "gcsUri": "gs://cloud-samples-data/vertex-ai-vision/highway_vehicles.mp4",
            "videoSegmentConfig": map[string]any{
                "startOffsetSec": 1,
                "endOffsetSec":   5,
            },
        },
    })
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to construct request payload: %w", err)
    }

    req := &aiplatformpb.PredictRequest{
        Endpoint: endpoint,
        // The model supports only 1 instance per request.
        Instances: []*structpb.Value{instances},
    }
    resp, err := client.Predict(ctx, req)
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate embeddings: %w", err)
    }

    instanceEmbeddingsJson, err := protojson.Marshal(resp.GetPredictions()[0])
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to convert protobuf value to JSON: %w", err)
    }
    // For response schema, see:
    // https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/model-reference/multimodal-embeddings-api#response-body
    var instanceEmbeddings struct {
        VideoEmbeddings []struct {
            Embedding      []float32 `json:"embedding"`
            StartOffsetSec float64   `json:"startOffsetSec"`
            EndOffsetSec   float64   `json:"endOffsetSec"`
        } `json:"videoEmbeddings"`
    }
    if err := json.Unmarshal(instanceEmbeddingsJson, &instanceEmbeddings); err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to unmarshal json: %w", err)
    }
    // Get the embedding for our single video segment (`.videoEmbeddings` object has one entry per
    // each processed segment).
    videoEmbedding := instanceEmbeddings.VideoEmbeddings[0]

    fmt.Fprintf(w, "Video embedding (seconds: %.f-%.f; length=%d): %v\n",
        videoEmbedding.StartOffsetSec,
        videoEmbedding.EndOffsetSec,
        len(videoEmbedding.Embedding),
        videoEmbedding.Embedding,
    )
    // Example response:
    // Video embedding (seconds: 1-5; length=1408): [-0.016427778 0.032878537 -0.030755188 ... ]

    return nil
}

import (
    "context"
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"
    "io"
    "time"

    aiplatform "cloud.google.com/go/aiplatform/apiv1beta1"
    aiplatformpb "cloud.google.com/go/aiplatform/apiv1beta1/aiplatformpb"
    "google.golang.org/api/option"

    "google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/structpb"
)

// generateForImageTextAndVideo shows how to use the multimodal model to generate embeddings for
// image, text and video data.
func generateForImageTextAndVideo(w io.Writer, project, location string) error {
    // location = "us-central1"

    // The default context timeout may be not enough to process a video input.
    ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)
    defer cancel()

    apiEndpoint := fmt.Sprintf("%s-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443", location)
    client, err := aiplatform.NewPredictionClient(ctx, option.WithEndpoint(apiEndpoint))
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to construct API client: %w", err)
    }
    defer client.Close()

    model := "multimodalembedding@001"
    endpoint := fmt.Sprintf("projects/%s/locations/%s/publishers/google/models/%s", project, location, model)

    // This is the input to the model's prediction call. For schema, see:
    // https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/model-reference/multimodal-embeddings-api#request_body
    instance, err := structpb.NewValue(map[string]any{
        "text": "Domestic cats in natural conditions",
        "image": map[string]any{
            // Image and video inputs can be provided either as a Google Cloud Storage URI or as
            // base64-encoded bytes using the "bytesBase64Encoded" field.
            "gcsUri": "gs://cloud-samples-data/generative-ai/image/320px-Felis_catus-cat_on_snow.jpg",
        },
        "video": map[string]any{
            "gcsUri": "gs://cloud-samples-data/video/cat.mp4",
        },
    })
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to construct request payload: %w", err)
    }

    req := &aiplatformpb.PredictRequest{
        Endpoint: endpoint,
        // The model supports only 1 instance per request.
        Instances: []*structpb.Value{instance},
    }

    resp, err := client.Predict(ctx, req)
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate embeddings: %w", err)
    }

    instanceEmbeddingsJson, err := protojson.Marshal(resp.GetPredictions()[0])
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to convert protobuf value to JSON: %w", err)
    }
    // For response schema, see:
    // https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/model-reference/multimodal-embeddings-api#response-body
    var instanceEmbeddings struct {
        ImageEmbeddings []float32 `json:"imageEmbedding"`
        TextEmbeddings  []float32 `json:"textEmbedding"`
        VideoEmbeddings []struct {
            Embedding      []float32 `json:"embedding"`
            StartOffsetSec float64   `json:"startOffsetSec"`
            EndOffsetSec   float64   `json:"endOffsetSec"`
        } `json:"videoEmbeddings"`
    }
    if err := json.Unmarshal(instanceEmbeddingsJson, &instanceEmbeddings); err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to unmarshal JSON: %w", err)
    }

    imageEmbedding := instanceEmbeddings.ImageEmbeddings
    textEmbedding := instanceEmbeddings.TextEmbeddings
    // Get the embedding for our single video segment (`.videoEmbeddings` object has one entry per
    // each processed segment).
    videoEmbedding := instanceEmbeddings.VideoEmbeddings[0].Embedding

    fmt.Fprintf(w, "Image embedding (length=%d): %v\n", len(imageEmbedding), imageEmbedding)
    fmt.Fprintf(w, "Text embedding (length=%d): %v\n", len(textEmbedding), textEmbedding)
    fmt.Fprintf(w, "Video embedding (length=%d): %v\n", len(videoEmbedding), videoEmbedding)
    // Example response:
    // Image embedding (length=1408): [-0.01558477 0.0258355 0.016342038 ... ]
    // Text embedding (length=1408): [-0.005894961 0.008349559 0.015355394 ... ]
    // Video embedding (length=1408): [-0.018867437 0.013997682 0.0012682161 ... ]

    return nil
}

docs.title: Get text embeddings
docs.text:
This document describes how to create a text embedding using the Vertex AI Text embeddings API.

Text embeddings are dense vector representations of text. For example, the gemini-embedding-001 model generates 3072-dimensional vectors for a given piece of text. These dense vector embeddings are created using deep-learning methods similar to those used by large language models.

Unlike sparse vectors that map words to numbers, dense vectors are designed to represent the semantic meaning of text. The primary benefit of using dense vector embeddings is the ability to perform semantic search. Instead of searching for direct word or syntax matches, you can search for text passages that align with the meaning of your query, even if the passages don't use the same phrasing.

The embedding vectors are normalized, so you can use cosine similarity, dot product, or Euclidean distance to get the same similarity rankings.

  • To learn more about embeddings, see the Embeddings for generative AI overview.
  • To learn about text embedding models, see Text embedding models.
  • For information about which languages each embeddings model supports, see Supported text languages.

To see an example of getting text embeddings, run the "Getting Started with Text Embeddings + Vertex AI Vector Search" Jupyter notebook in one of the following environments:

Open in Colab Open in Colab Enterprise Open in Vertex AI Workbench View on GitHub

This document follows the workflow shown in the following diagram:

flowchart TD
    A[Before you begin] --> B(Supported models)
    B --> C(Get text embeddings for a snippet of text)
    C --> D(Add an embedding to a vector database)

    click A "#before-you-begin"
    click B "#supported-models"
    click C "#get-text-embeddings-for-a-snippet-of-text"
    click D "#add-an-embedding-to-a-vector-database"

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Text embeddings: Numerical vector representations of text that capture semantic meaning.
  • Dense vector: A vector where most of the elements are non-zero, used to represent complex relationships in data like text.
  • Semantic search: A search technique that understands the intent and contextual meaning of words in a query, rather than just matching keywords.
  • Cosine similarity: A metric used to measure the cosine of the angle between two non-zero vectors, often used to determine similarity between text documents.
  • Vector database: A database designed to store and query high-dimensional vectors, such as those generated by embedding models.
Prerequisites

  1. Sign in to your Google Cloud account. If you're new to Google Cloud, create an account to evaluate how our products perform in real-world scenarios. New customers also get $300 in free credits to run, test, and deploy workloads.

  2. Create or select a Google Cloud project. In the Google Cloud console, on the project selector page, select or create a Google Cloud project.

    Note: If you don't plan to keep the resources that you create in this procedure, create a project instead of selecting an existing project. After you finish these steps, you can delete the project, removing all resources associated with the project.

    Go to project selector

  3. Enable the Vertex AI API.

docs.title: Supported models
docs.text:
You can get text embeddings by using the following models:

Model name Description Output Dimensions Max sequence length Supported text languages gemini-embedding-001 State-of-the-art performance across English, multilingual and code tasks. It unifies the previously specialized models like text-embedding-005 and text-multilingual-embedding-002 and achieves better performance in their respective domains. Read our Tech Report for more detail. up to 3072 2048 tokens Supported text languages text-embedding-005 Specialized in English and code tasks. up to 768 2048 tokens English text-multilingual-embedding-002 Specialized in multilingual tasks. up to 768 2048 tokens Supported text languages

For superior embedding quality, gemini-embedding-001 is our large model designed to provide the highest performance. Note that gemini-embedding-001 supports one instance per request.

Note: Only use the models as listed in the supported models table. Don't specify a model without the @version suffix or @latest. These model names are not considered valid.

docs.title: Get text embeddings for a snippet of text
docs.text: You can get text embeddings for a snippet of text by using the Vertex AI API or an SDK.

docs.title: API limits
docs.text:
For each request, you're limited to 250 input texts for non-Gemini models, and a single input text for Gemini Embedding models. The API has a maximum input token limit of 20,000. Inputs exceeding this limit result in a 400 error. Each individual input text is further limited to 2048 tokens; any excess is silently truncated. You can also disable silent truncation by setting autoTruncate to false.

For more information, see Text embedding limits.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
When you generate embeddings, you can configure the following parameters:

  • Task type: Specify the downstream application for the embeddings to achieve the best performance. For more details, see Choose a task type.
  • Embedding dimension: All models produce a full-length embedding vector by default (3072 for gemini-embedding-001 and 768 for other models). You can use the output_dimensionality parameter to reduce the vector size, which can save storage and improve computational efficiency with a small trade-off in quality.

The following examples use the gemini-embedding-001 model.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

cURLVertex AI SDK for PythonGen AI SDK for Python

-X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \

"https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/gemini-embedding-001:predict" -d \
$'{
  "instances": [
    {
      "content": "How do I get a driver\'s license/learner\'s permit?",
      "task_type": "RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT",
      "title": "Driver\'s License"
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "outputDimensionality": 3072
  }
}'

from vertexai.language_models import TextEmbeddingModel

docs.title: Choose an embeddings task type
docs.text: Vertex AI embeddings models can generate optimized embeddings for various task types, such as document retrieval, question answering, and fact verification. Task types are labels that optimize the embeddings that the model generates based on your intended use case. This document describes how to choose the optimal task type for your embeddings.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Embeddings: Numerical vector representations of text, images, or other data, where similar items have vectors that are close to each other in the vector space.
  • Task Type: A parameter that optimizes the generated embeddings for a specific downstream application, such as retrieval, classification, or clustering.
  • Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG): A technique that enhances the responses of Large Language Models (LLMs) by retrieving relevant information from an external knowledge base and providing it as context.
  • Vector Search: A method for finding the most similar items to a given query in a high-dimensional vector space, commonly used with embeddings.
  • Symmetric vs. Asymmetric Search:
    • Symmetric: Use cases where the query and the documents are of similar length and structure (e.g., finding similar sentences). The SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY task type is symmetric.
    • Asymmetric: Use cases where the query is typically short and the documents are long (e.g., searching a database of articles with a keyword query). Retrieval-focused task types are asymmetric.

docs.title: Supported models
docs.text:
Task types are supported by the following models:

  • text-embedding-005
  • text-multilingual-embedding-002
  • gemini-embedding-001

Preview

The following limitations apply when using these models:

  • Don't use these preview models on mission critical or production systems.
  • These models are available in us-central1 only.
  • Batch predictions are not supported.
  • Customization is not supported.

docs.title: Benefits of using task types
docs.text:
Task types can improve the quality of embeddings generated by an embeddings model.

For example, when building Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, a common design is to use text embeddings and Vector Search to perform a similarity search. This can sometimes lead to poor search quality because questions and their answers are not always semantically similar. A question like "Why is the sky blue?" and its answer "The scattering of sunlight causes the blue color" have different meanings as standalone statements. Without task types, a RAG system might not recognize their relationship.

Figure 1. Questions and their answers aren't semantically similar, which means that embeddings won't automatically show their relation.

To overcome this, a developer might need to fine-tune a model to learn the relationship between queries and answers or use advanced techniques like LLM-based query expansion or HyDE, which can add latency and cost.

Task types solve this problem by generating optimized embeddings that place the query and its corresponding answer closer together in the embedding space. This saves the time and cost of developing custom task-specific embeddings and leads to improved similarity search results in RAG systems and other applications like classification, clustering, and fact verification.

Figure 2. Task types optimize embeddings for specific tasks. In this case, questions and answers are brought closer together in the embeddings space.

docs.title: How to choose a task type
docs.text:
The best task type depends on your specific use case. The following workflow helps you determine which task type to select. If your use case doesn't align with a documented use case, use the RETRIEVAL_QUERY task type by default.

flowchart TD
    A[Start: Determine your use case] --> B{What is your primary goal?};
    B --> C[Retrieve information from a text corpus?];
    B --> D[Classify text into predefined categories?];
    B --> E[Group similar texts together?];
    B --> F[Assess similarity between two texts?];

    C --> G["<b>Use Asymmetric Task Types:</b><br/>- RETRIEVAL_QUERY (for queries)<br/>- RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT (for corpus)<br/>- QUESTION_ANSWERING<br/>- FACT_VERIFICATION<br/>- CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY"];
    D --> H["<b>Use Symmetric Task Type:</b><br/>- CLASSIFICATION"];
    E --> I["<b>Use Symmetric Task Type:</b><br/>- CLUSTERING"];
    F --> J["<b>Use Symmetric Task Type:</b><br/>- SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY"];

    click G "#information-retrieval"
    click H "#classification"
    click I "#clustering"
    click J "#semantic-similarity"

The following table provides a summary of the available task types.

Task Type Description Use Case Type RETRIEVAL_QUERY Generates embeddings for a short query to search a large corpus of documents. Asymmetric RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT Generates embeddings for the documents in a corpus that will be searched over. Asymmetric QUESTION_ANSWERING Generates embeddings for a query that is phrased as a question. Asymmetric FACT_VERIFICATION Generates embeddings for a query to retrieve documents that support or refute a factual claim. Asymmetric CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY Generates embeddings for a natural language query to retrieve relevant code blocks. Asymmetric CLASSIFICATION Generates embeddings optimized to classify texts according to preset labels. Symmetric CLUSTERING Generates embeddings optimized to cluster texts based on their similarities. Symmetric SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY Generates embeddings optimized to assess the semantic similarity between two texts. Not for retrieval. Symmetric

docs.title: Task type use cases and examples
docs.text:
Information Retrieval

When building a search or retrieval system, you work with two types of text: a corpus (the collection of documents to search over) and a query (the user's search input). For the best performance, you must use different task types for the corpus and the queries.

1. Embed your document corpus: First, generate embeddings for your entire collection of documents using the RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT task type. You typically perform this step once to index your corpus and store the resulting embeddings in a vector database.

2. Embed user queries: Next, when a user submits a search, generate an embedding for their query in real time using a task type that matches their intent. The system uses this query embedding to find the most similar document embeddings in your vector database.

The following task types are used for queries:

  • RETRIEVAL_QUERY: Use for standard search queries to find relevant documents.
  • QUESTION_ANSWERING: Use when queries are expected to be questions (e.g., "How do I tie my shoelaces?").
  • FACT_VERIFICATION: Use to retrieve a document that proves or disproves a statement (e.g., "apples grow underground").
  • CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY: Use to retrieve a code block based on a natural language query (e.g., "sort an array"). Code blocks in the corpus should be embedded using RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT.

Key Point: To get embeddings for information retrieval, use RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT for your documents and a corresponding query task type (like RETRIEVAL_QUERY) for user queries.

Classification

If you want to use embeddings to classify texts according to preset labels, use the CLASSIFICATION task type. This task type generates embeddings in a space that is optimized for classification.

For example, to classify the sentiment of social media posts as positive, negative, or neutral, you would embed a post like "I don't like traveling on airplanes" using the CLASSIFICATION task type. The resulting embedding would be suitable for a model to classify its sentiment as negative.

Key Point: To get embeddings that are optimized to classify text using predefined labels, use the CLASSIFICATION task type.

Clustering

If you want to use embeddings to cluster texts based on their similarities, use the CLUSTERING task type. This task type generates embeddings that are optimized for being grouped based on similarity.

For example, you can generate embeddings for news articles to show users articles that are topically related to ones they have previously read. After the embeddings are generated and clustered, you can suggest additional sports-related articles to users who read a lot about sports.

Additional use cases for clustering include:

  • Customer segmentation: Group customers with similar profiles for targeted marketing.
  • Product segmentation: Cluster products based on titles, descriptions, or reviews for segment analysis.
  • Market research: Cluster survey responses or social media data to reveal hidden patterns and trends.
  • Healthcare: Cluster patients based on medical data to identify groups with similar conditions or treatment responses.
  • Customer feedback trends: Cluster feedback from surveys, social media, and support tickets to identify common pain points and feature requests.

Key Point: To get embeddings that are optimized for clustering based on similarities, use the CLUSTERING task type.

Semantic Similarity

If you want to use embeddings to assess the similarity between two texts, use the SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY task type. This task type is optimized for generating similarity scores.

For example, to compare the similarity of "The cat is sleeping" and "The feline is napping," you would generate embeddings for both texts. A similarity score calculated from these embeddings would be high because both texts have nearly the same meaning.

A real-world scenario is a recommendation system that identifies items (products, articles, movies) that are semantically similar to a user's preferred items to provide personalized recommendations.

Key Point: To get embeddings that are optimized to assess text similarity, use the SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY task type.

Note: SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY is not intended for retrieval use cases like document search. For retrieval, use RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT, RETRIEVAL_QUERY, QUESTION_ANSWERING, or FACT_VERIFICATION.

docs.title: Code examples
docs.text:
The following examples demonstrate how to generate an embedding for a code retrieval query.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

RESTPython 
PROJECT_ID=PROJECT_ID

curl \
-X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/text-embedding-005:predict -d \
$'{
  "instances": [
    {
      "task_type": "CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY",
      "content": "Function to add two numbers"
    }
  ],
}'

To learn how to install or update the Vertex AI SDK for Python, see Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python. For more information, see the Vertex AI SDK for Python API reference documentation.

from vertexai.language_models import TextEmbeddingInput, TextEmbeddingModel

MODEL_NAME = "gemini-embedding-001"
DIMENSIONALITY = 3072


def embed_text(
    texts: list[str] = ["Retrieve a function that adds two numbers"],
    task: str = "CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY",
    model_name: str = "gemini-embedding-001",
    dimensionality: int | None = 3072,
) -> list[list[float]]:
    """Embeds texts with a pre-trained, foundational model."""
    model = TextEmbeddingModel.from_pretrained(model_name)
    kwargs = dict(output_dimensionality=dimensionality) if dimensionality else {}

    embeddings = []
    # gemini-embedding-001 takes one input at a time
    for text in texts:
        text_input = TextEmbeddingInput(text, task)
        embedding = model.get_embeddings([text_input], **kwargs)
        print(embedding)
        # Example response:
        # [[0.006135190837085247, -0.01462465338408947, 0.004978656303137541, ...]]
        embeddings.append(embedding[0].values)

    return embeddings


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Embeds code retrieval query with a pre-trained, foundational model.
    # Using this function to calculate the embedding for the query.
    texts = ["Retrieve a function that adds two numbers"]
    task = "CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY"
    code_query_embeddings = embed_text(
        texts=texts, task=task, model_name=MODEL_NAME, dimensionality=DIMENSIONALITY
    )

    # Embeds code blocks with a pre-trained, foundational model.
    # Using this function to calculate the embedding for the corpus.
    texts = [
        "def func(a, b): return a + b",
        "def func(a, b): return a - b",
        "def func(a, b): return (a ** 2 + b ** 2) ** 0.5",
    ]
    task = "RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT"
    code_block_embeddings = embed_text(
        texts=texts, task=task, model_name=MODEL_NAME, dimensionality=DIMENSIONALITY
    )

docs.title: Ground responses using RAG
docs.text:
Grounding is a technique that helps produce model responses that are more trustworthy and factual by connecting them to verifiable sources of information. The recommended best practice for implementing grounding is retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). RAG retrieves relevant data from an indexed knowledge base and provides it to the generative model as context for its response.

Vertex AI provides multiple ways to implement a RAG solution, from a fully integrated experience to a custom, mix-and-match approach using individual components.

docs.title: Approaches to RAG in Vertex AI
docs.text:
Vertex AI offers both a managed, end-to-end RAG solution and individual APIs that you can use to build your own custom RAG pipeline. The following table compares these two approaches.

Approach Description Best for Key Components Vertex AI RAG Engine (Integrated) A fully managed, end-to-end RAG solution that handles document ingestion, parsing, indexing, retrieval, and generation. Users who want a quick and easy way to ground models on their own data without building a custom pipeline. An integrated service that abstracts away the underlying components. Custom RAG with Vertex AI Components A flexible approach where you build your own RAG pipeline using individual, swappable Vertex AI and Document AI components. Users who need full control and customization over their RAG workflow, such as using a custom retriever or a different vector database.
  • Document layout parser
  • Vertex AI Vector Search
  • Grounding generation API
  • Check grounding API

This document focuses on the integrated approach using the Vertex AI RAG Engine.

docs.title: Ground responses using the Vertex AI RAG Engine
docs.text: You can ground a model on your data directly in the Vertex AI Studio by connecting your prompt to a RAG Engine corpus.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Grounding: The process of connecting a generative model's output to verifiable sources of information to enhance its factuality and trustworthiness.
  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): A technique where a model retrieves relevant information from a data source before generating a response, allowing it to answer questions based on knowledge outside of its training data.
  • Corpus: A collection of documents that you provide to the RAG Engine to serve as the knowledge base for grounding.
  • Vertex AI RAG Engine: A managed Vertex AI service that ingests your data, indexes it for retrieval, and performs the RAG process to ground model responses.

Before you can ground a prompt, you must have a corpus of data created and ingested by the RAG Engine.

docs.title: Use Google Search suggestions
docs.text:
When you use grounding with Google Search, you must display any Search suggestions returned in the model's response within your application.

For more information on grounding with Google Search, see Grounding with Google Search.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Grounding: The process of connecting a large language model's (LLM) response to verifiable sources of information, such as Google Search, to improve accuracy and reduce hallucinations.
  • Search suggestions: Search query terms, provided in the API response, that you must display alongside the grounded LLM response to allow users to explore the topic further on Google Search.

docs.title: Understanding the API response
docs.text:
When you make a grounded request, the API response includes the LLM-generated content and the search queries that you must display as Search suggestions. The key fields are:

  • "content": The LLM-generated response.
  • "webSearchQueries": A list of search query strings to be used for the Search suggestions.

For example, the following JSON snippet shows a grounded response to a prompt about a tropical plant.

"predictions": [
  {
    "content": "Monstera is a type of vine that thrives in bright indirect light…",
    "groundingMetadata": {
      "webSearchQueries": ["What's a monstera?"],
    }
  }
]

You must take the webSearchQueries from this output and display them as Search suggestions in your application according to the following requirements.

docs.title: Usage requirements
docs.text:
• Display the Search suggestion exactly as it is provided in the API response, without any modifications.
  • When a user interacts with a Search suggestion, they must be taken directly to the Google Search results page (SRP).
  • Do not include any intermediate screens or additional steps between the user's tap and the display of the SRP.
  • Do not display any other search results or suggestions next to the Search suggestion or its associated grounded LLM response.

docs.title: Display requirements
docs.text:
• Visual Fidelity: Display the Search suggestion exactly as provided, without modifying colors, fonts, or appearance. The suggestion must render as specified in the following light and dark mode mockups.

    Example of Search suggestion chips in light and dark modes.

  • Visibility: The corresponding Search suggestion must remain visible whenever a grounded response is shown.

  • Branding: You must strictly follow Google's guidelines for third-party use of Google brand features, available at the Brand Resource Center.
  • Layout: The field containing the Search suggestion chips must be the same width as the grounded response from the LLM.

docs.title: User interaction
docs.text:
When a user taps a Search suggestion chip, they are taken directly to an SRP for the search term displayed in the chip. The SRP can open either within your application's browser or in a separate browser application. Do not minimize, remove, or obstruct the SRP's display in any way.

The following animation illustrates the required tap-to-SRP interaction.

Animation showing the user flow from tapping a suggestion to viewing the SRP.

docs.title: Implementation using the API response
docs.text:
When you use the API to ground a response with Google Search, the model response provides compliant HTML and CSS styling in the renderedContent field. You can implement this field directly to display the Search suggestions in your application.

For a complete example of the API response containing the renderedContent field, see the response section in Grounding with Google Search.

Note: The HTML and CSS provided in the API response automatically adapt to the user's device settings, displaying in either light or dark mode based on the prefers-color-scheme media feature.

docs.title: Grounding with Elasticsearch
docs.text:
This page explains how to use your Elasticsearch instance to ground large language model (LLM) responses on your private data.

Grounding enhances LLM responses by providing factual context from specified data sources. By grounding with Elasticsearch, you can leverage your existing Elasticsearch indexes to improve the quality and reliability of Gemini's output. This helps reduce hallucinations and ensures responses are relevant to your data.

This capability allows you to build powerful Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) applications, such as:

  • Generative search summaries
  • Question-and-answer chatbots using enterprise data
  • Agents grounded in your proprietary data

You can ground a model on up to 10 data sources at once. For comprehensive results, you can combine grounding with Elasticsearch with Grounding with Google Search to connect the model to public information from the internet.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Grounding: The process of connecting a large language model (LLM) to external data sources to provide factual, up-to-date context for its responses.
  • RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation): An AI framework that retrieves facts from an external knowledge base to ground LLMs before they generate a response.
  • Elasticsearch Index: A collection of related documents in Elasticsearch that are stored and indexed together for fast searching.
  • Search Template: A predefined search request in Elasticsearch that can be executed with different parameters, simplifying complex queries.
  • kNN (k-Nearest Neighbors) Search: A method for finding the 'k' most similar items in a dataset to a query, commonly used for semantic search with vector embeddings.
Prerequisites

Before you can ground LLM responses with Elasticsearch, complete the following:

  1. Enable the Vertex AI API: Ensure the Vertex AI API is enabled for your Google Cloud project.
  2. Install the gcloud CLI: Install and initialize the Google Cloud command-line tool.
  3. Set up Elasticsearch: You need an existing Elasticsearch cluster and index. Gather the following information:
    • Endpoint: The URL of your Elasticsearch cluster.
    • Index Name: The name of the index you want to search (e.g., my-data-index).
    • API Key: An API key that grants access to your Elasticsearch cluster. The key must have the prefix ApiKey.
  4. Create an Elasticsearch search template: Create a search template that returns result data for grounding. For more information, see the next section.

docs.text:

ConsoleREST API

To ground a model with Elasticsearch in the Google Cloud console, follow these steps:

  1. Go to the Vertex AI Studio Create prompt page.

    Go to Create prompt

  2. In the Settings panel, click the Grounding: Your data toggle to enable it.

  3. In the Customize Grounding pane, select Elasticsearch.
  4. Enter your Elasticsearch endpoint.
  5. Enter your Elasticsearch API Key.
  6. Enter your Elasticsearch index.
  7. Enter your Elasticsearch search template.
  8. Adjust the Number of hits slider to set the number of results to retrieve.
  9. Click Save.
  10. Enter your prompt in the prompt input field.
  11. Click Submit to generate the grounded response.

This section shows how to use the Vertex AI API to ground a model with your Elasticsearch data source.

Prepare a grounded generation request

To send a text prompt and ground it with Elasticsearch, send a POST request to the Vertex AI API. In the request body, replace the following placeholders:

  • QUERY: The text prompt to ground.
  • ELASTIC_SEARCH_ENDPOINT: The absolute endpoint path for the Elasticsearch resource.
  • ELASTIC_SEARCH_API_KEY: The API key for the Elasticsearch data endpoint.
  • INDEX_NAME: The name of the Elasticsearch index to use for grounding.
  • SEARCH_TEMPLATE_NAME: The Elasticsearch search template to use for grounding.
  • NUM_HITS: The number of results to return from the Elasticsearch data source.

Request JSON body:

{
  "contents": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "parts": [
        {
          "text": "QUERY"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "tools": [{
    "retrieval": {
      "externalApi": {
        "api_spec": "ELASTIC_SEARCH",
        "endpoint": "ELASTIC_SEARCH_ENDPOINT",
        "apiAuth": {
          "apiKeyConfig": {
            "apiKeyString": "ApiKey ELASTIC_SEARCH_API_KEY"
          }
        },
        "elasticSearchParams": {
          "index": "INDEX_NAME",
          "searchTemplate": "SEARCH_TEMPLATE_NAME",
          "numHits": "NUM_HITS",
        }
      }
    }
  }]
}

For more information on other API fields, such as system instructions and multi-turn chats, see the Generative AI beginner's guide.

Send the API request

Save the request body in a file named request.json. Then, execute the following curl command. Replace the following placeholders:

  • LOCATION: The region to process the request. For available locations, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.
  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID. For more information, see Creating and managing projects.
  • MODEL_ID: The ID of the multimodal model you are using.
curl -X POST \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
    -d @request.json \
"https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:generateContent"
