docs.title: Style customization
docs.text:
Preview

This product or feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Google Cloud Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA products and features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

Deprecation Notice

Starting on June 24, 2025, Imagen versions 1 and 2 are deprecated. Imagen models imagegeneration@002, imagegeneration@005, and imagegeneration@006 will be removed on September 24, 2025. For more information about migrating to Imagen 3, see Migrate to Imagen 3.

Imagen 3 style customization helps you generate new images that adhere to the style of reference images you provide. By supplying one or more reference images along with a text prompt, you can guide the model to create new visuals that adopt the specified artistic style.

Note: For more information about imagen-3.0-capability-001 model requests, see the imagen-3.0-capability-001 model API reference.

docs.title: Use cases
docs.text:
Imagen 3 offers free-style prompting, which can give the impression that it can do more than it is trained to do. The following sections describe intended use cases for Imagen 3 style customization and provide non-exhaustive examples of unintended use cases.

We recommend using Imagen 3 for the intended use cases, as we've trained the model on those scenarios and expect good results. Conversely, while you can push the model to do things outside of the intended use cases, we don't expect good results.

docs.title: Intended use cases
docs.text:
The following are use cases intended for Imagen 3 style customization:

  • Generate an image from text input that follows the specific style provided by a reference image.
  • Alter a photo of a person.
  • Alter a photo of a person and preserve their facial expression.

docs.title: Examples of unintended use cases
docs.text:
The following is a non-exhaustive list of use cases that Imagen 3 isn't trained to do and for which it might produce poor results:

  • Generate an image from text and a reference image with the intent to control the composition of the generated image from the reference image.
  • Generate an image of a person from a reference image that has a person with a particular facial expression.
  • Place two people in a different scene, preserve their identities, and specify the style of the output image (such as an oil painting) using a reference image.
  • Stylize a photo of a pet and turn it into a drawing while preserving or specifying the composition of the image.
  • Place a product, such as a cookie or a couch, into different scenes with different product angles while following a specific image style (such as photorealistic with specific colors, lighting, or animation).

docs.title: Style customization example
docs.text:
The following example demonstrates how style customization works with a reference image and a text prompt.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Style Customization: A feature that allows you to generate images in a specific artistic style by providing reference images.
  • Reference Image: An image you provide to the model to define the target style for the new image generation.
  • Text Prompt: A description of the desired content for the generated image, which can include references to the style images.
  • base64: An encoding scheme that converts binary data (like images) into a text string, allowing it to be easily included in JSON or XML data formats.
  • referenceId: A unique identifier you assign to a reference image so you can refer to it within your text prompt (e.g., [1]).
Prerequisites

  1. Sign in to your Google Cloud account. If you're new to Google Cloud, create an account to evaluate how our products perform in real-world scenarios. New customers also get $300 in free credits to run, test, and deploy workloads.

  2. Select or create a Google Cloud project. In the Google Cloud console, on the project selector page, select or create a Google Cloud project.

    Note: If you don't plan to keep the resources that you create in this procedure, create a project instead of selecting an existing project. After you finish these steps, you can delete the project, removing all resources associated with the project.

    Go to project selector

  3. Enable billing for your project. Make sure that billing is enabled for your Google Cloud project.

  4. Enable the Vertex AI API.

    Enable the API

  5. Set up authentication. Select the tab for how you plan to use the samples on this page:

    ConsoleREST

    When you use the Google Cloud console to access Google Cloud services and APIs, you don't need to set up authentication.

    To use the REST API samples on this page in a local development environment, you use the credentials you provide to the gcloud CLI.

    After installing the Google Cloud CLI, initialize it by running the following command:

    gcloud init

    If you're using an external identity provider (IdP), you must first sign in to the gcloud CLI with your federated identity.

    For more information, see Authenticate for using REST in the Google Cloud authentication documentation.

docs.title: Customize a style
docs.text:
To see an example of Imagen 3 Customization, you can run the "Imagen 3 Customized Images" Jupyter notebook in one of the following environments:

Open in Colab Open in Colab Enterprise Open in Vertex AI Workbench View on GitHub

Alternatively, follow the instructions below to send a request using the REST API or the Python SDK.

RESTPython

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • LOCATION: Your project's region (for example, us-central1). For a list of available regions, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.
  • TEXT_PROMPT: The text prompt that guides what images the model generates. To use style customization, include the referenceId of the reference image(s) in the format [referenceId]. For example: Generate an image in glowing style [1] based on the following caption: A church in the mountain.
  • BASE64_REFERENCE_IMAGE: A reference image to guide image generation. The image must be specified as a base64-encoded byte string.
  • STYLE_DESCRIPTION: (Optional) A text description of the reference image you can then use in the prompt field.
  • IMAGE_COUNT: The number of generated images. Accepted integer values: 1-4. Default value: 4.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagen-3.0-capability-001:predict

Request JSON body:

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "TEXT_PROMPT",
      "referenceImages": [
        {
          "referenceType": "REFERENCE_TYPE_STYLE",
          "referenceId": 1,
          "referenceImage": {
            "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_REFERENCE_IMAGE"
          },
          "styleImageConfig": {
            "styleDescription": "STYLE_DESCRIPTION"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "sampleCount": IMAGE_COUNT
  }
}

To send your request, choose one of these options:

cURLPowerShell

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d @request.json \
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagen-3.0-capability-001:predict"

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method POST `
    -Headers $headers `
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `
    -InFile request.json `
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagen-3.0-capability-001:predict" | Select-Object -Expand Content

The following sample response is for a request with "sampleCount": 2. The response returns two prediction objects, with the generated image bytes base64-encoded.

{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES",
      "mimeType": "image/png"
    },
    {
      "mimeType": "image/png",
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES"
    }
  ]
}

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

from google import genai
from google.genai.types import EditImageConfig, Image, StyleReferenceConfig, StyleReferenceImage

client = genai.Client()

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below line
# output_gcs_uri = "gs://your-bucket/your-prefix"

# Create a style reference image of a neon sign stored in Google Cloud Storage
# using https://storage.googleapis.com/cloud-samples-data/generative-ai/image/neon.png
style_reference_image = StyleReferenceImage(
    reference_id=1,
    reference_image=Image(gcs_uri="gs://cloud-samples-data/generative-ai/image/neon.png"),
    config=StyleReferenceConfig(style_description="neon sign"),
)

image = client.models.edit_image(
    model="imagen-3.0-capability-001",
    prompt="generate an image of a neon sign [1] with the words: have a great day",
    reference_images=[style_reference_image],
    config=EditImageConfig(
        edit_mode="EDIT_MODE_DEFAULT",
        number_of_images=1,
        seed=1,
        safety_filter_level="BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE",
        person_generation="ALLOW_ADULT",
        output_gcs_uri=output_gcs_uri,
    ),
)

# Example response:
# gs://your-bucket/your-prefix
print(image.generated_images[0].image.gcs_uri)

docs.text:
Caution: Starting on June 24, 2025, Imagen versions 1 and 2 are deprecated. Imagen models imagegeneration@002, imagegeneration@005, and imagegeneration@006 will be removed on September 24, 2025 . For more information about migrating to Imagen 3, see Migrate to Imagen 3.

Imagen 3 Customization's subject customization helps you generate new images from a text prompt and a reference image that you provide. The reference image that you provide helps guide new image generation.

Note: For more information about imagen-3.0-capability-001 model requests, see the imagen-3.0-capability-001 model API reference.

docs.title: Use cases
docs.text:
Imagen 3 Customization offers free-style prompting, which can give the impression that it can do more than it is trained to do. The following sections describe intended use cases for Imagen 3 Customization, and non-exhaustive examples of unintended use cases.

We recommend using Imagen 3 Customization for the intended use cases, as we've trained the model on those use cases and expect good results for them. Conversely, while you can push the model to do things outside of the intended use cases, we don't expect good results.

docs.title: Intended use cases
docs.text:
The following are use cases intended for Imagen 3 Customization subject customization:

  • Stylize a photo of a person, with the option to preserve their facial expressions.
  • Place a product, such as a couch or a cookie, into different scenes with different product angles (with low success).
  • Generate variations of a product that doesn't preserve exact details.

docs.title: Examples of unintended use cases
docs.text:
The following is a non-exhaustive list of use cases that Imagen 3 Customization isn't trained to do and produces poor results for:

  • Place two or more people in different scenes while preserving their identities.
  • Place two or more people in different scenes while preserving their identities and specifying the style of the output image using an example image as input for the style.
  • Stylize a photo of two or more people while preserving their identities.
  • Place a pet into different scenes while preserving its identity.
  • Stylize a photo of a pet and turn it into a drawing.
  • Stylize a photo of a pet and turn it into a drawing, while preserving or specifying the style of the image (such as watercolor).
  • Place a pet and a person into a different scene, preserving the identities of both.
  • Stylize a photo of a pet and one or more people and turn it into a drawing.
  • Place two products into different scenes with different product angles.
  • Place a product, such as a cookie or a couch, into different scenes with different product angles, and following a specific image style (such as photorealistic with specific colors, lighting styles, or animation).
  • Place a product into a different scene, while preserving the specific composition of the scene as specified by a control image.
  • Place two products into different scenes with different product angles, using a specific image as input (such as photorealistic with specific colors, lighting styles, or animation).
  • Place two products into different scenes, while preserving the specific composition of the scene as specified by a control image.

Concepts

Subject Customization: Generating new images from a text prompt and a reference image of a subject. Reference Image: An image you provide to guide the model on the appearance of a subject. Text Prompt: A description of the desired output image, which can reference the subject in the reference image. Face Mesh: A 3D map of facial landmarks used as a control image to preserve facial structure and expression. Few-shot prompting: Providing a few examples (in this case, reference images) to the model to guide its output.

Set up your project and environment
  1. Sign in to your Google Cloud account. If you're new to Google Cloud, create an account to evaluate how our products perform in real-world scenarios. New customers also get $300 in free credits to run, test, and deploy workloads.

  4. Enable the Vertex AI API.

This workflow guides you through the process of generating customized images with Imagen 3.

To see an example of Imagen 3 Customization, run the "Imagen 3 Customized Images" Jupyter notebook in one of the following environments:

Open in Colab Open in Colab Enterprise Open in Vertex AI Workbench View on GitHub

You can provide reference images of subject types when you use Imagen 3 Customization. Specifically, few-shot prompting with Imagen 3 Customization supports the following subjects: product, person, and animal companion. The subject you choose affects how you form your generation request.

The prompt you use with Imagen 3 Customization might affect the quality of your generated images. The following sections describe recommended prompt templates and samples to send customization requests.

docs.text:

The person should be looking straight ahead with a neutral expression. The background should be a ... Person image stylization without face mesh input Subject image (1-4) Create an image about SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION [1] to match the description: a portrait of SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION [1] ${PROMPT} Create an image about a woman with short hair[1] to match the description: a portrait of a woman with short hair[1] in 3d-cartoon style with blurred background. A cute and lovely character, smile face, looking at the camera, pastel color tone, high quality, 4k, masterpiece, super details, skin texture, texture mapping, soft shadows, soft realistic lighting, vibrant colors Person image stylization without face mesh input Subject image (1-4) Create a STYLE_DESCRIPTION [2] image about SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION [1] to match the description: a portrait of SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION [1] STYLE_PROMPT Create a 3d-cartoon style [2] image about a woman with short hair [1] to match the description: a portrait of a woman with short hair [1] in 3d-cartoon style with blur background. A Cute and lovely character, smile face. see the camera, pastel color tone, high quality, 4k, masterpiece, super details, skin texture, texture mapping, Soft shadows, soft realistic lighting, vibrant colors Person image stylization with face mesh input Subject image (1-3)*Facemesh control image (1) Create an image about SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION [1] in the pose of the CONTROL_IMAGE [2] to match the description: a portrait of SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION [1] ${PROMPT} Create an image about a woman with short hair [1] in the pose of the control image [2] to match the description: a portrait of a woman with short hair [1] in 3d-cartoon style with blur background. A Cute and lovely character, smile face. See the camera, pastel color tone, high quality, 4k, masterpiece, super details, skin texture, texture mapping, Soft shadows, soft realistic lighting, vibrant colors Person image stylization with face mesh input Subject image (1-3)*Facemesh control image (1) Create a STYLE_DESCRIPTION [3] image about SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION [1] in the pose of the CONTROL_IMAGE [2] to match the description: a portrait of SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION [1] ${PROMPT} Create a 3d-cartoon style [3] image about a woman with short hair [1] in the pose of the control image [2] to match the description: a portrait of a woman with short hair [1] in 3d-cartoon style with blur background. A Cute and lovely character, smile face. See the camera, pastel color tone, high quality, 4k, masterpiece, super details, skin texture, texture mapping, Soft shadows, soft realistic lighting, vibrant colors

We recommend that the face in your reference image has the following properties:

  • Is centered and occupies at least half of the whole image
  • Is rotated in frontal view in all directions (roll, pitch, and yaw)
  • Isn't occluded by objects, such as sunglasses or masks

Use the following samples to send a customization request with person reference images used to guide image generation. You can send this type of request with or without a face mesh control image to further guide image generation.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

RESTPython

For more information about imagen-3.0-capability-001 model requests, see the imagen-3.0-capability-001 model API reference.

This sample shows you how to specify a face mesh control area to guide generation, but you can also omit the control reference object ("referenceType": "REFERENCE_TYPE_CONTROL") and Imagen will automatically detect a face mesh control area.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • LOCATION: Your project's region. For example, us-central1, europe-west2, or asia-northeast3. For a list of available regions, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.
  • TEXT_PROMPT: The text prompt guides what images the model generates. To use Imagen 3 Customization, include the referenceId of the reference image or images you provide in the format [referenceId]. For example:
    • The following text prompt is for a request that has two reference images with "referenceId": 1. Both images have an optional description of "subjectDescription": "man with short hair". Additionally, there is a control face mesh image specified with "referenceId": 2: Create an image about a man with short hair [1] in the pose of control image [2] to match the description: A pencil style sketch of a full-body portrait of a man with short hair [1] with hatch-cross drawing, hatch drawing of portrait with 6B and graphite pencils, white background, pencil drawing, high quality, pencil stroke, looking at camera, natural human eyes
  • "referenceId": The ID of the reference image, or the ID for a series of reference images that correspond to the same subject or style. In this example the two reference images are of the same person, so they share the same referenceId (1) and the control face mesh image has a distinct referenceId (2). The generated image will follow the face structure of the face mesh extracted from the reference image and will improve the face appearance following. Only one face mesh control is supported.
  • BASE64_REFERENCE_IMAGE: A reference image to guide image generation. The image must be specified as a base64-encoded byte string.

  • SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION: Optional. A text description of the reference image you can then use in the prompt field. For example:

    "prompt": "_a full-body portrait of a man with short hair [1] with hatch-cross drawing_",
[...],
"subjectDescription": "man with short hair"

  • IMAGE_COUNT: The number of generated images. Accepted integer values: 1-4. Default value: 4.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagen-3.0-capability-001:predict

Request JSON body:

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "TEXT_PROMPT",
      "referenceImages": [

        {
          "referenceType": "REFERENCE_TYPE_SUBJECT",
          "referenceId": 1,
          "referenceImage": {
            "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_REFERENCE_IMAGE"
          },
          "subjectImageConfig": {
            "subjectDescription": "SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION",
            "subjectType": "SUBJECT_TYPE_PERSON"
          }
        },
        {
          "referenceType": "REFERENCE_TYPE_SUBJECT",
          "referenceId": 1,
          "referenceImage": {
            "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_REFERENCE_IMAGE"
          },
          "subjectImageConfig": {
            "subjectDescription": "SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION",
            "subjectType": "SUBJECT_TYPE_PERSON"
          }
        },{
          "referenceType": "REFERENCE_TYPE_CONTROL",
          "referenceId": 2,
          "referenceImage": {
            "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_REFERENCE_IMAGE"
          },
          "controlImageConfig": {
            "controlType": "CONTROL_TYPE_FACE_MESH",
            "enableControlImageComputation": true
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "sampleCount": IMAGE_COUNT
  }
}

curl

     -d @request.json \

The following sample response is for a request with "sampleCount": 2. The response returns two prediction objects, with the generated image bytes base64-encoded.

    {
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES",

from google import genai
from google.genai.types import (
    ControlReferenceConfig,
    ControlReferenceImage,
    EditImageConfig,
    Image,
    SubjectReferenceConfig,
    SubjectReferenceImage
)

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below line

docs.title: Product customization
docs.text:
The following table describes prompt templates that we recommend as a starting point when writing product customization prompts:

Reference images Prompt template Example Subject image (1-4) Create an image about SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION [1] to match the description: ${PROMPT} Create an image about Luxe Elixir hair oil, golden liquid in glass bottle [1] to match the description: A close-up, high-key image of a woman's hand holding Luxe Elixir hair oil, golden liquid in glass bottle [1] against a pure white background. The woman's hand is well-lit and the focus is sharp on the bottle, with a shallow depth of field blurring the background and emphasizing the product. The lighting is soft and diffused, creating a subtle glow around the bottle and hand. The overall composition is simple and elegant, highlighting the product's luxurious appeal. Subject image (1-4) Generate an image of a SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION but ${PROMPT} Generate an image of a Seiko watch [1] but in blue.

Use the following samples to send a customization request with product reference images used to guide image generation.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

ConsoleREST

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI > Media Studio page.

    Go to Media Studio

  2. In the Model section of the Parameters pane, select Imagen 3 if not already selected.

  3. Optional. Choose an Aspect ratio other than 1:1 (default).
  4. Optional. Change the Number of results.
  5. Optional. Provide a Negative prompt to guide the model on what to avoid generating.
  6. Optional. Change any Advanced options.
    1. In the Add reference pane, choose the Reference type: Subject - product.
    2. In the Reference images section, click Upload.
    3. Choose a locally-stored image and click Open.
    4. Optional. Provide a Description for the reference image.
    5. Click Done.
    6. Optional. To add more reference images, click Add an image and upload another image.
    7. After you add all your reference images, click Add reference.

    In the text prompt field (Write your prompt...), click Add reference.

    All the reference images you add in that pane have the same reference number. Use this reference number when you add the text prompt.

  8. In the text prompt field (Write your prompt...), add a text prompt that includes the reference number or numbers for the reference images. For example:

    1. bright white room, the product [1] on a glass table
    2. the animal [1] standing on a wide open field with a forest in the distance
    3. a black and white portrait of the person [1] on a city street in film noir style [2]

For more information about imagen-3.0-capability-001 model requests, see the imagen-3.0-capability-001 model API reference.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • LOCATION: Your project's region. For example, us-central1, europe-west2, or asia-northeast3. For a list of available regions, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.
  • TEXT_PROMPT: The text prompt guides what images the model generates. To use Imagen 3 Customization, include the referenceId of the reference image or images you provide in the format [referenceId]. For example:
    • Create an image about Luxe Elixir hair oil, golden liquid in glass bottle [1] to match the description: A close-up, high-key image of a woman's hand holding Luxe Elixir hair oil, golden liquid in glass bottle [1] against a pure white background. The woman's hand is well-lit and the focus is sharp on the bottle, with a shallow depth of field blurring the background and emphasizing the product.
  • "referenceId": The ID of the reference image, or the ID for a series of reference images that correspond to the same subject or style. In this example the two reference images are of the same product, so they share the same referenceId (1).
  • BASE64_REFERENCE_IMAGE: A reference image to guide image generation. The image must be specified as a base64-encoded byte string.

  • SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION: Optional. A text description of the reference image you can then use in the prompt field. For example:

    "prompt": "Luxe Elixir hair oil, golden liquid in glass bottle [1] _against a pure white background._ ",
[...],
"subjectDescription": "Luxe Elixir hair oil, golden liquid in glass bottle"

  • IMAGE_COUNT: The number of generated images. Accepted integer values: 1-4. Default value: 4.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagen-3.0-capability-001:predict

Request JSON body:

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "TEXT_PROMPT",
      "referenceImages": [
        {
          "referenceType": "REFERENCE_TYPE_SUBJECT",
          "referenceId": 1,
          "referenceImage": {
            "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_REFERENCE_IMAGE"
          },
          "subjectImageConfig": {
            "subjectType": "SUBJECT_TYPE_PRODUCT",
            "subjectDescription": "SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION"
          }
        },
        {
          "referenceType": "REFERENCE_TYPE_SUBJECT",
          "referenceId": 1,
          "referenceImage": {
            "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_REFERENCE_IMAGE"
          },
          "subjectImageConfig": {
            "subjectType": "SUBJECT_TYPE_PRODUCT",
            "subjectDescription": "SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "sampleCount": IMAGE_COUNT
  }
}

To send your request, choose one of these options:

curl

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login , or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI . You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d @request.json \
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagen-3.0-capability-001:predict"

PowerShell

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login . You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method POST `
    -Headers $headers `
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `
    -InFile request.json `
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagen-3.0-capability-001:predict" | Select-Object -Expand Content

The following sample response is for a request with "sampleCount": 2. The response returns two prediction objects, with the generated image bytes base64-encoded.

{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES",
      "mimeType": "image/png"
    },
    {
      "mimeType": "image/png",
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Upscale a generated, edited, or existing image
docs.text: You can use the image upscaling feature of Imagen on Vertex AI to increase the resolution of an image by 2x or 4x without a significant loss in quality. This is useful for improving the detail of generated, edited, or existing images.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • REST API: A REST API (Representational State Transfer Application Programming Interface) is a way for different software applications to communicate with each other over the internet using standard HTTP methods.
  • base64 encoding: A method of converting binary data (like an image) into a text string, allowing it to be easily transmitted in text-based formats like JSON.
  • Cloud Storage URI: A unique identifier for an object stored in Google Cloud Storage, formatted as gs://BUCKET_NAME/OBJECT_NAME.

docs.title: Model availability
docs.text:
Upscaling availability is based on the model version.

Feature imagegeneration@002 imagegeneration@005 imagegeneration@006 Upscaling ✔ Not supported Not supported

docs.title: Ways to upscale an image
docs.text:
You can upscale an image using the Google Cloud console for quick tasks or the REST API for automation and integration.

Method Use Case Google Cloud console Best for quick, one-off tasks and visual confirmation of results. REST API Best for automating upscaling tasks and integrating into applications. Google Cloud consoleREST API

The following workflow outlines the steps to upscale an image using the Google Cloud console.

flowchart TD
    A["Generate or select an image"] --> B["Configure upscaling"]
    B --> C["Export the image"]

click A "#generate-or-select-an-image"
click B "#configure-upscaling"
click C "#export-the-image"
Upscale an image using the Google Cloud console

1. Generate or select an image

  • Follow the generate image with text instructions to generate new images.
  • In the gallery, select the generated or an existing image that you want to upscale.

2. Configure upscaling

  • Click download Upscale/export.
  • Select Upscale images.
  • Choose a value from the Scale factor menu (2x or 4x).

3. Export the image

  • Click download Export to save the upscaled image to your local machine.

Use the following instructions to upscale an image by sending a POST request to the imagegeneration@002 model endpoint.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Before sending the request, replace the following placeholders with your own values:

  • LOCATION: Your project's region. For example, us-central1, europe-west2, or asia-northeast3. For a list of available regions, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.
  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • B64_BASE_IMAGE: The base image to upscale, specified as a base64-encoded byte string. The size limit is 10 MB.
  • IMAGE_SOURCE: The Cloud Storage URI of the image you want to upscale. For example: gs://output-bucket/source-photos/photo.png.
  • UPSCALE_FACTOR: The factor by which the image is upscaled. Available values are x2 or x4.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Make an upscale request
docs.text:
Send a POST request to the model. In the request body, specify "mode": "upscale" and include the upscaleConfig object.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagegeneration@002:predict

Request JSON body:

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "",
      "image": {
        // use one of the following to specify the image to upscale
        "bytesBase64Encoded": "B64_BASE_IMAGE"
        "gcsUri": "IMAGE_SOURCE"
        // end of base image input options
      },
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "sampleCount": 1,
    "mode": "upscale",
    "upscaleConfig": {
      "upscaleFactor": "UPSCALE_FACTOR"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Send the request
docs.text:

==== "curl" Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login , or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI . You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

```bash

```

==== "PowerShell" Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login . You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named `request.json`, and execute the following command:

```powershell
$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method POST `
    -Headers $headers `
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `

    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagegeneration@002:predict" | Select-Object -Expand Content
```

docs.title: Use prompt rewriter
docs.text:
Caution: Starting on June 24, 2025, Imagen versions 1 and 2 are deprecated. Imagen models imagegeneration@002, imagegeneration@005, and imagegeneration@006 will be removed on September 24, 2025. For more information about migrating to Imagen 3, see Migrate to Imagen 3.

Imagen on Vertex AI offers an LLM-based prompt rewriting tool, also known as a prompt rewriter. The prompt rewriter helps you obtain higher-quality output images by adding more detail to your prompt. If you disable the prompt rewriter, the quality of the images and how well the output resembles the prompt that you supplied might be impacted.

This feature is enabled by default for the following model versions:

  • imagen-4.0-generate-preview-06-06 (Preview)
  • imagen-4.0-fast-generate-preview-06-06 (Preview)
  • imagen-4.0-ultra-generate-preview-06-06 (Preview)
  • imagen-3.0-generate-002

The rewritten prompt is delivered in the API response only if the original prompt is fewer than 30 words long.

Try image generation (Vertex AI Studio) Try Imagen in a Colab

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Prompt Rewriter: An LLM-based tool that enhances a short, simple user prompt by adding more detail and descriptive language to generate higher-quality images.
  • Imagen: A family of text-to-image diffusion models developed by Google that generate photorealistic images from natural language text prompts.
  • LLM (Large Language Model): A type of artificial intelligence model trained on vast amounts of text data to understand and generate human-like language.
  • REST API: A standardized way for computer systems to communicate over the internet, allowing you to send requests and receive responses to interact with services like Vertex AI.

docs.title: Use the prompt rewriter
docs.text:
You can use the prompt rewriter through the Google Cloud console or by making a REST API request.

ConsoleREST API

The following workflow outlines the steps to use the prompt rewriter in the Google Cloud console.

flowchart TD

    B --> C["Enhance the prompt"]
    C --> D["Generate the image"]

click A "#navigate-to-imagen"
click B "#configure-generation-settings"
click C "#enhance-the-prompt"
click D "#generate-the-image"
Steps to use the prompt rewriter in the console

1. Navigate to Imagen in Media Studio

  • In the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI > Media Studio page.

    Go to Media Studio

  • Click Imagen. The Imagen Media Studio image generation page is displayed.

2. Configure generation settings

In the Settings panel, adjust the following options:

  • Model: Choose a model from the available options. For more information, see Imagen models.
  • Number of results: Adjust the slider or enter a value between 1 and 4.
  • Negative prompt: In the box, enter a prompt that describes what you don't want generated in the image.

3. Enhance the prompt

  • In the Write your prompt box, click Help me write. The Enhance my prompt window is displayed.
  • In the Current prompt box, write your prompt, and then click Enhance. The rewritten prompt is displayed in the Enhanced prompt box. You can edit the enhanced prompt or use it as displayed.
  • Click Insert to use the displayed prompt. The prompt is inserted into the Write your prompt box.

4. Generate the image

  • Click send Generate.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • MODEL_VERSION: The image generation model version to use. For more information, see model versions.
  • LOCATION: Your project's region. For example, us-central1, europe-west2, or asia-northeast3. For a list of available regions, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.
  • TEXT_PROMPT: The text prompt that guides what images the model generates. Before images are generated, this base prompt is enhanced with more detail using the prompt rewriter.
  • IMAGE_COUNT: The number of generated images. Accepted integer values: 1-4. Default value: 4.

To enable the prompt rewriter, set the enhancePrompt parameter to true in your request.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_VERSION:predict

Request JSON body:

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "TEXT_PROMPT"
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "sampleCount": IMAGE_COUNT,
    "enhancePrompt": true
  }
}

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

curlPowerShell

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d @request.json \
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_VERSION:predict"

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

    -Method POST `

    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `
    -InFile request.json `
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_VERSION:predict" | Select-Object -Expand Content

With prompt enhancement enabled, the response includes an additional prompt field that shows the enhanced prompt for each associated generated image:

  {
    "predictions": [
      {
        "mimeType": "MIME_TYPE",
        "prompt": "ENHANCED_PROMPT_1",
        "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES_1"
      },
      {
        "mimeType": "MIME_TYPE",
        "prompt": "ENHANCED_PROMPT_2",
        "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES_2"
      }
    ]
  }

For example, the following sample response is for a request with "sampleCount": 2 and "prompt": "A raccoon wearing formal clothes, wearing a top hat. Oil painting in the style of Vincent Van Gogh.". The response returns two prediction objects, each with their enhanced prompt and the generated image bytes base64-encoded.

{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "mimeType": "image/png",
      "prompt": " An oil painting in the style of Vincent van Gogh, depicting a raccoon adorned in a finely tailored tuxedo, complete with a crisp white shirt and a bow tie. The raccoon also sports a classic top hat, perched jauntily on its head. The painting uses thick, swirling brushstrokes characteristic of van Gogh, with vibrant hues of blue, yellow, and green in the background, contrasting with the dark tones of the raccoon's attire. The light source is subtly placed, casting a dramatic shadow of the raccoon's attire onto the surface it sits upon, further enhancing the depth and dimensionality of the composition. The overall impression is one of a whimsical and sophisticated character, a raccoon elevated to a higher class through its formal attire, rendered in van Gogh's iconic style.",
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES"
    },
    {
      "mimeType": "image/png",
      "prompt": " An oil painting in the style of Vincent van Gogh featuring a raccoon in a dapper suit, complete with a black jacket, crisp white shirt, and a black bow tie. The raccoon is wearing a black top hat, adding a touch of elegance to its ensemble. The painting is rendered with characteristic van Gogh brushwork, utilizing thick, impasto strokes of color. The background is a swirl of blues, greens, and yellows, creating a vibrant yet slightly chaotic atmosphere that contrasts with the raccoon's formal attire. The lighting is dramatic, casting sharp shadows and highlighting the textures of the fabric and the raccoon's fur, enhancing the sense of realism within the fantastical scene. The composition focuses on the raccoon's proud posture, highlighting the whimsical contrast of a wild animal dressed in formal attire, captured in the unique artistic language of van Gogh. ",

docs.title: Verify an image watermark
docs.text:
Caution: Starting on June 24, 2025, Imagen versions 1 and 2 are deprecated. Imagen models imagegeneration@002, imagegeneration@005, and imagegeneration@006 will be removed on September 24, 2025 . For more information about migrating to Imagen 3, see Migrate to Imagen 3.

This page describes how to verify if an image generated by Imagen on Vertex AI contains a digital watermark.

By default, Imagen on Vertex AI adds a digital watermark to any images generated by a model version that supports this feature. When you generate an image with a watermark, Imagen adds a non-visible digital watermark, called a SynthID, to the image file. You can then check if an image contains this digital watermark.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Imagen: A text-to-image diffusion model that lets you generate and edit high-quality, photorealistic images from natural language prompts.
  • SynthID: A technology that adds a non-visible digital watermark directly into the pixels of an image, making it detectable for identification without compromising image quality.

docs.title: Use Visual Question Answering (VQA) to get image information
docs.text:
Caution: Starting on June 24, 2025, Imagen versions 1 and 2 are deprecated. Imagen models imagegeneration@002, imagegeneration@005, and imagegeneration@006 will be removed on September 24, 2025 . For more information about migrating to Imagen 3, see Migrate to Imagen 3.

Visual Question Answering (VQA) lets you provide an image to a model and ask a question about its contents. In response, you receive one or more natural language answers.

Image source: Sharon Pittaway on Unsplash.Prompt question: What objects are in the image?Answer 1: marblesAnswer 2: glass marbles

docs.title: VQA model options
docs.text:
Vertex AI offers multiple models for performing VQA tasks. This page describes how to use the imagetext model (part of Imagen). The Gemini API can also perform VQA tasks, particularly for multimodal inputs.

The following table provides a high-level comparison to help you choose the best model for your use case.

Feature Gemini API Imagen (imagetext model) Input Multiple images, video, and text A single image Task Type Multimodal reasoning and conversation Short-form Q&A and captioning Best for Complex questions requiring context from multiple sources. Straightforward questions about a single image's contents.

Note: The Gemini API can answer questions based on multiple image inputs, while Imagen can process one image in each input. For more information, see the Gemini API documentation.

docs.title: Get VQA responses using the imagetext model
docs.text:
This section shows you how to get VQA responses for an image using the imagetext model.

The following workflow outlines the steps to get VQA responses.

flowchart TD
    A["Before you begin"] --> B["Prepare image and prompt"]
    B --> C["Send a VQA request"]
    C --> D["Interpret the VQA response"]

    click A "#before-you-begin"
    click B "#prepare-your-image-and-prompt"
    click C "#send-a-vqa-request"
    click D "#interpret-the-vqa-response"
Get VQA responses for an image

Before you begin

Concepts
  • Visual Question Answering (VQA): A task where a model answers natural language questions about an image.
  • imagetext model: A foundational model in Vertex AI for understanding images, capable of tasks like VQA and image captioning.
  • Token: The basic unit of text (e.g., a word or subword) that a language model processes.
  • Base64 encoding: A method to convert binary data like an image into a text string for use in text-based formats like JSON.

Before sending a request, complete the following setup:

  • Set up your Google Cloud project and authentication.
  • Enable the Vertex AI API.
  • Identify your PROJECT_ID and LOCATION. For a list of available regions, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.
  • To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

Prepare your image and prompt

To make a VQA request, you need the following:

  • An image: The image must be specified as a base64-encoded byte string. The size limit is 10 MB.
  • A prompt: The question you want to ask about your image. For example:
    • What color is this shoe?
    • What type of sleeves are on the shirt?
  • Response count (optional): The number of answers you want to generate. Accepted integer values are 1-3.

Send a VQA request

Use the following samples to ask a question and get an answer about an image.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

RESTPythonNode.js

For more information about imagetext model requests, see the imagetext model API reference.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • LOCATION: Your project's region (e.g., us-central1).
  • VQA_PROMPT: The question you want to ask about your image.
  • B64_IMAGE: The base64-encoded byte string of your image.
  • RESPONSE_COUNT: The number of answers to generate (1-3).

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagetext:predict

Request JSON body:

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "VQA_PROMPT",
      "image": {
          "bytesBase64Encoded": "B64_IMAGE"
      }
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "sampleCount": RESPONSE_COUNT
  }
}

To send your request, choose one of these options:

curl

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d @request.json \
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagetext:predict"

PowerShell

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method POST `
    -Headers $headers `
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `
    -InFile request.json `
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagetext:predict" | Select-Object -Expand Content

Before trying this sample, follow the Python setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Python API reference documentation.

In this sample, you use the load_from_file method to load a local image and the ask_question method to get answers.

import vertexai
from vertexai.preview.vision_models import Image, ImageTextModel

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# input_file = "input-image.png"
# question = "" # The question about the contents of the image.

vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

model = ImageTextModel.from_pretrained("imagetext@001")
source_img = Image.load_from_file(location=input_file)

answers = model.ask_question(
    image=source_img,
    question=question,
    # Optional parameters
    number_of_results=1,
)

print(answers)
# Example response:
# ['tabby']

Before trying this sample, follow the Node.js setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Node.js API reference documentation.

In this sample, you call the predict method on a PredictionServiceClient to get answers for the provided question.

/**
 * TODO(developer): Update these variables before running the sample.
 */
const projectId = process.env.CAIP_PROJECT_ID;
const location = 'us-central1';
const inputFile = 'resources/cat.png';
// The question about the contents of the image.
const prompt = 'What breed of cat is this a picture of?';

const aiplatform = require('@google-cloud/aiplatform');

// Imports the Google Cloud Prediction Service Client library
const {PredictionServiceClient} = aiplatform.v1;

// Import the helper module for converting arbitrary protobuf.Value objects
const {helpers} = aiplatform;

// Specifies the location of the api endpoint
const clientOptions = {
  apiEndpoint: `${location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com`,
};

// Instantiates a client
const predictionServiceClient = new PredictionServiceClient(clientOptions);

async function getShortFormImageResponses() {
  const fs = require('fs');
  // Configure the parent resource
  const endpoint = `projects/${projectId}/locations/${location}/publishers/google/models/imagetext@001`;

  const imageFile = fs.readFileSync(inputFile);
  // Convert the image data to a Buffer and base64 encode it.
  const encodedImage = Buffer.from(imageFile).toString('base64');

  const instance = {
    prompt: prompt,
    image: {
      bytesBase64Encoded: encodedImage,
    },
  };
  const instanceValue = helpers.toValue(instance);
  const instances = [instanceValue];

  const parameter = {
    // Optional parameters
    sampleCount: 2,
  };
  const parameters = helpers.toValue(parameter);

  const request = {
    endpoint,
    instances,
    parameters,
  };

  // Predict request
  const [response] = await predictionServiceClient.predict(request);
  const predictions = response.predictions;
  if (predictions.length === 0) {
    console.log(
      'No responses were generated. Check the request parameters and image.'
    );
  } else {
    predictions.forEach(prediction => {
      console.log(prediction.stringValue);
    });
  }
}
await getShortFormImageResponses();

Interpret the VQA response

The following sample response is for a request with "sampleCount": 2 and "prompt": "What is this?". The response returns two prediction string answers.

{
  "predictions": [
    "cappuccino",
    "coffee"
  ]
}

docs.title: VQA parameters
docs.text:
When you request VQA responses, you can set several parameters to control the output.

  • Number of results: Use this parameter to limit the number of answers returned for each request. For more information, see the imagetext (VQA) model API reference.
  • Seed number: A number you can add to a request to make the generated responses deterministic. Adding a seed number helps ensure that you get the same predictions each time, though the answers are not necessarily returned in the same order. For more information, see the imagetext (VQA) model API reference.

docs.title: Responsible AI safety filtering
docs.text:
The VQA feature model doesn't support user-configurable safety filters. However, the overall Imagen safety filtering occurs on the following data:

  • User input
  • Model output

As a result, your output may differ from the sample output if Imagen applies these safety filters. Consider the following examples.

Filtered input

If the input is filtered, the response is similar to the following:

{
  "error": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Media reasoning failed with the following error: The response is blocked, as it may violate our policies. If you believe this is an error, please send feedback to your account team. Error Code: 63429089, 72817394",
    "status": "INVALID_ARGUMENT",
    "details": [
      {
        "@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.DebugInfo",
        "detail": "[ORIGINAL ERROR] generic::invalid_argument: Media reasoning failed with the following error: The response is blocked, as it may violate our policies. If you believe this is an error, please send feedback to your account team. Error Code: 63429089, 72817394 [google.rpc.error_details_ext] { message: \"Media reasoning failed with the following error: The response is blocked, as it may violate our policies. If you believe this is an error, please send feedback to your account team. Error Code: 63429089, 72817394\" }"
      }
    ]
  }
}

Filtered output

If the number of responses returned is less than the sample count you specify, the missing responses were filtered by Responsible AI. For example, the following is a response to a request with "sampleCount": 2, but one of the responses is filtered out:

{
  "predictions": [
    "cappuccino"
  ]
}

If all the output is filtered, the response is an empty object similar to the following:

{}

docs.title: Abuse monitoring
docs.text: As outlined in Section 4.3 "Generative AI Safety and Abuse" of the Google Cloud Platform Terms of Service, Google uses the following process to detect potential abuse and violations of its Acceptable Use Policy and Prohibited Use Policy as part of providing Generative AI Services to customers.

docs.title: How abuse monitoring works
docs.text:
The abuse monitoring process involves several stages:

  • Automated detection: Google uses automated safety classifiers to detect potential abuse and violations. For technical details on how safety classifiers work, see Configure safety filters.

  • Prompt logging: If automated safety classifiers detect suspicious activity that requires further investigation, Google may log customer prompts solely to determine if a violation of the AUP or Prohibited Use Policy has occurred. This data is not used to train or fine-tune any AI/ML models. The data is stored securely for up to 30 days in the region selected by the customer and adheres to Google Cloud assurances like Data Residency, Access Transparency, and VPC Service Controls.

  • Action: Authorized Google employees may assess the flagged prompts and contact the customer for clarification. Failure to address the behavior—or in cases of recurring or severe abuse—may result in the suspension or termination of the customer's access to Vertex AI or Google Cloud services.

docs.title: Scope of abuse monitoring
docs.text:
The scope of abuse monitoring is defined by the services and customers involved:

  • Services in scope: This process applies to the Vertex AI API when used with Google's large language models.

  • Customers in scope: Prompt logging for abuse monitoring applies only to customers whose use of Google Cloud is governed by the Google Cloud Platform Terms of Service and who do not have an invoiced (offline) Cloud Billing account.

docs.title: Opt out of abuse monitoring
docs.text:
Customers may request an exception to opt out of prompt logging for abuse monitoring.

To request an exception, fill out this form. If your request is approved, Google will not store any prompts associated with the approved Google Cloud account for abuse monitoring purposes.

docs.title: Deployments and endpoints
docs.text:
Generative AI models and features on Vertex AI are accessible through regional endpoints and a global endpoint. Choosing the right endpoint depends on your requirements for availability, latency, and data residency.

Concepts
  • Endpoint: A specific URL where you send API requests to access and interact with an AI model.
  • Global Endpoint: A single, worldwide endpoint that automatically routes requests to available regions, designed for high availability and reliability.
  • Regional Endpoint: An endpoint located in a specific geographic region (e.g., us-central1), which ensures that data is processed within that location.
  • Data Residency: The requirement that data is stored and processed within a specific geographic boundary, often for regulatory or compliance reasons.

To help you decide which endpoint type to use, the following table compares their key features.

Feature Global Endpoint Regional Endpoints Availability Higher; automatically routes traffic away from outages. Limited to the health of a single region. Data Residency Not guaranteed; requests can be processed in any region. Guaranteed; data is processed in the specified region. Supported Features Limited. Does not support features like model tuning, batch prediction, or context caching. Full support for all applicable Vertex AI features. Use Case Ideal for applications requiring maximum uptime where data location is not a constraint. Best for applications with strict data residency requirements or those needing features not available on the global endpoint.

Note that model endpoints don't guarantee region availability or in-region ML processing. For information about data residency, see Data residency.

Global endpointRegional endpoints

Selecting a global endpoint for your requests can improve overall availability and reduce 429 (resource exhausted) errors. Do not use the global endpoint if you have ML processing requirements, because you cannot control which region your requests are sent to for processing.

Supported models

The global endpoint is supported for the following Google models:

  • Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite
  • Gemini 2.5 Pro
  • Gemini 2.5 Flash
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite

For information about partner models, see Google Cloud partner model endpoint locations.

Use the global endpoint

To use the global endpoint, exclude the location from the endpoint name and configure the resource location to global. For example, the following is a global endpoint URL:

https://**aiplatform.googleapis.com** /v1/projects/test-project/locations/**global** /publishers/google/models/gemini-2.0-flash-001:generateContent

For the Google Gen AI SDK, create a client that uses the global location:

client = genai.Client(
    vertexai=True, project='PROJECT_ID', location='global'
)

For the Vertex AI SDK for Python, initialize the SDK using the global location:

import vertexai
from vertexai.generative_models import GenerativeModel

vertexai.init(project='PROJECT_ID', location='global')

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Limitations

The following capabilities are not available when using the global endpoint:

  • Tuning
  • Batch prediction
  • Context caching
  • Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) corpus (RAG requests are supported)

Usage of the global endpoint with Provisioned Throughput is available only for the following models:

Model Latest supported model version Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite (preview) gemini-2.5-flash-lite-preview-06-17 Gemini 2.5 Pro gemini-2.5-pro Gemini 2.5 Flash gemini-2.5-flash Gemini 2.0 Flash gemini-2.0-flash-001 Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite gemini-2.0-flash-lite-001

Regional endpoints are located in specific geographic locations and guarantee data residency.

docs.title: Model monitoring metrics
docs.text:
Generative AI on Vertex AI provides a prebuilt model observability dashboard to help you view the behavior, health, and performance of fully-managed models. Fully-managed models, also known as Model as a Service (MaaS), are provided by Google and include Google's Gemini models and partner models with managed endpoints.

Generative AI automatically collects and reports activity from MaaS models, helping you monitor capacity and troubleshoot latency issues. Metrics from self-hosted models are not included in this dashboard.

Figure 1. An example of the model observability dashboard.

docs.title: How model observability works
docs.text: The model observability dashboard displays a subset of metrics collected by Cloud Monitoring, such as model requests per second (QPS), token throughput, and first-token latencies.

docs.title: Use cases
docs.text:
As an application developer, you can use the dashboard to understand how users interact with your models. For example, you can track trends in model usage (requests per second) and the compute intensity of user prompts (invocation latencies) over time. These metrics can also help you estimate costs for running each model.

When an issue arises, you can use the dashboard to quickly troubleshoot. By viewing API error rates, first-token latencies, and token throughput, you can verify that your models are responding reliably and in a timely manner.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: Vertex AI captures dashboard metrics only for API calls made to a model's endpoint. Usage from the Google Cloud console, such as metrics from Vertex AI Studio, is not included in the dashboard.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Model as a Service (MaaS): Refers to fully-managed models, such as Gemini, that are hosted and provided by Google.
  • Queries per second (QPS): The rate of requests sent to a model, indicating its usage level.
  • Token throughput: The rate at which a model processes and generates tokens, measuring its processing speed.
  • First token latency: The time it takes for the model to generate the first token in a response after receiving a prompt.
  • The observability dashboard is only available if you or another user has made at least one API call to a MaaS model in your project.

docs.title: Model versions and lifecycle
docs.text: This document defines key terms related to the lifecycle of Gemini and embedding models on Vertex AI. It also provides recommended upgrade paths and guidance on migrating to the latest model versions.

docs.title: Before you begin

Concepts
  • Model Version: A specific iteration of a model, identified by a unique ID and release date.
  • Stable Model: A model version that is publicly released and supported for production use until its retirement date.
  • Retired Model: A model version that is past its retirement date and no longer available for use.
  • Model Alias: A pointer that automatically references the latest stable version of a model, simplifying upgrades.

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

  2. Test all mission-critical features to verify everything works as expected.
  3. Deploy the updates following your standard procedures.

docs.title: Generative AI beginner's guide
docs.text:
This beginner's guide introduces you to the core technologies of generative AI and explains how they fit together to power chatbots and applications. Generative AI (also known as genAI or gen AI) is a field of machine learning (ML) that develops and uses ML models for generating new content.

Generative AI models are often called large language models (LLMs) because of their large size and ability to understand and generate natural language. However, depending on the data that the models are trained on, these models can understand and generate content from multiple modalities, including text, images, videos, and audio. Models that work with multiple modalities of data are called multimodal models.

Google provides the Gemini family of generative AI models designed for multimodal use cases, capable of processing information from multiple modalities, including images, videos, and text.

Concepts
  • Generative AI: A field of machine learning that develops and uses ML models for generating new content.
  • Large Language Model (LLM): A type of large generative AI model trained on vast amounts of text data to understand and generate natural language.
  • Multimodal model: A model capable of processing and generating content from multiple data types, such as text, images, and video.
  • Model tuning: The process of customizing a foundation model to perform specific tasks more effectively for a particular use case.
  • Grounding: The process of connecting a model's responses to verifiable sources of information to improve accuracy and reduce hallucinations.

docs.title: How generative AI creates content
docs.text:
For generative AI models to create useful content in real-world applications, they follow a workflow that enables them to perform new tasks, access external information, and block harmful content.

The following diagram shows how these different capabilities work together to generate a response from a user's prompt.

The generative AI content generation workflow.

docs.title: Prompt
docs.text:
The generative AI workflow starts with a prompt. A prompt is a natural language request sent to a generative AI model to elicit a response. Depending on the model, a prompt can contain text, images, videos, audio, documents, or a combination of modalities (multimodal).

Creating a prompt to get the desired response from the model is a practice called prompt design. While prompt design is a process of trial and error, there are principles and strategies you can use to guide the model to behave in the desired way. Vertex AI Studio offers a prompt management tool to help you manage your prompts.

docs.title: Foundation models
docs.text:
Prompts are sent to a generative AI model for response generation. Vertex AI provides access to a variety of generative AI foundation models through a managed API. You can explore Google models, as well as open models and models from Google partners, in Model Garden.

The following table provides a high-level overview of Google's foundation model APIs:

API Primary Use Case Gemini API Advanced reasoning, multi-turn chat, code generation, and multimodal tasks. Imagen API High-quality image generation, editing, and visual captioning. MedLM Medical question answering and summarization. (Deprecated)

docs.title: Model customization
docs.text:
You can customize the default behavior of Google's foundation models so that they consistently generate desired results without requiring complex prompts. This customization process is called model tuning. Model tuning helps you reduce the cost and latency of your requests by allowing you to simplify your prompts.

Vertex AI also offers model evaluation tools to help you evaluate the performance of your tuned model. After your tuned model is production-ready, you can deploy it to an endpoint and monitor its performance, similar to standard MLOps workflows.

docs.title: Access external information
docs.text:
Vertex AI offers multiple ways to give a model access to external APIs and real-time information. This helps the model provide more accurate and relevant responses by connecting it to information outside of its original training data.

Method Description Best For Grounding Connects model responses to a source of truth (your data or web search) to reduce hallucinations and improve factual accuracy. Answering questions based on specific documents or websites. RAG A specific architecture (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) that connects models to external knowledge sources like documents and databases. Building sophisticated Q&A systems over large, private knowledge bases. Function calling Allows the model to interact with external APIs to get real-time information or perform actions. Integrating with other services, like booking systems, weather APIs, or internal company tools.

docs.title: Citation check
docs.text: After the response is generated, Vertex AI checks whether citations need to be included. If a significant amount of the text in the response comes from a particular source, that source is added to the citation metadata in the response.

docs.title: Responsible AI and safety
docs.text: The final check that the prompt and response go through is the safety filters. Vertex AI checks both the prompt and the response against a list of safety attributes. If the content exceeds the safety threshold for one or more categories, the response is blocked, and Vertex AI returns a fallback response.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: If the prompt and response pass all safety checks, the response is returned to the user. Typically, the response is returned all at once. However, with Vertex AI you can also receive responses progressively as they are generated by enabling streaming.

docs.title: Get started
docs.text:
Try one of these quickstarts to get started with generative AI on Vertex AI.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

  • Generate text using the Vertex AI Gemini API: Use the SDK to send requests to the Vertex AI Gemini API.
  • Send prompts to Gemini using the Vertex AI Studio Prompt Gallery: Test prompts with no setup required.
  • Generate an image and verify its watermark using Imagen: Create a watermarked image using Imagen on Vertex AI.

docs.title: Best practices for Large Language Models (LLMs)
docs.text:
This document outlines best practices for working with Large Language Models (LLMs) on Vertex AI. Following these guidelines can help you improve response quality, reduce latency, and effectively use different prompt modalities.

Concepts
  • Latency: The time it takes for a model to process an input prompt and generate a response.
  • Time to first token (TTFT): The time it takes for the model to produce the first token of the response after receiving the prompt, which is a key metric for streaming applications.
  • Time to last token (TTLT): The total time taken by the model to process the prompt and generate the entire response.
  • Streaming: A technique where the model sends the response token by token as it's generated, rather than waiting for the full output.

docs.title: Reduce response latency
docs.text: When you build interactive applications, response time, also known as latency, plays a crucial role in the user experience. This section explores the concept of latency in the context of Vertex AI LLM APIs and provides actionable strategies to minimize it.

docs.title: Understanding latency metrics
docs.text:
When examining latency with a model, consider the following metrics:

  • Time to first token (TTFT) is the time that it takes for the model to produce the first token of the response after receiving the prompt. TTFT is particularly relevant for applications that use streaming, where providing immediate feedback is crucial.

  • Time to last token (TTLT) measures the overall time taken by the model to process the prompt and generate the complete response.

docs.title: Strategies to reduce latency
docs.text:
You can use several strategies with Vertex AI to minimize latency and enhance the responsiveness of your applications:

  • Choose the right model for your use case: Vertex AI provides a diverse range of models with varying capabilities and performance characteristics. Carefully evaluate your requirements for speed and output quality to choose the model that best aligns with your use case. For a list of available models, see Explore all models.

  • Optimize prompt and output size: The number of tokens in both your input prompt and expected output directly impacts processing time. Minimize your token count to reduce latency.

    • Craft clear and concise prompts that effectively convey your intent without unnecessary details. Shorter prompts reduce your time to first token. For example:
      • Verbose prompt: Could you please provide me with a summary of the main points from the attached article about renewable energy, but don't go into too much detail? Just the key takeaways would be great.
      • Concise prompt: Summarize the key takeaways of the attached article on renewable energy.
    • Use system instructions to control the length of the response. Instruct the model to provide concise answers or limit the output to a specific number of sentences or paragraphs. This strategy can reduce your time to last token.
    • Adjust the temperature. Experiment with the temperature parameter to control the randomness of the output. Lower temperature values can lead to shorter, more focused responses, while higher values can result in more diverse, but potentially longer, outputs.
    • Restrict output by setting a limit. Use the max_output_tokens parameter to set a maximum limit on the length of the generated response, preventing overly long output. However, be cautious as this might cut off responses mid-sentence.

  • Use streaming responses: With streaming, the model starts sending its response before it generates the complete output. This enables real-time processing of the output, and you can immediately update your user interface and perform other concurrent tasks. Streaming enhances perceived responsiveness and creates a more interactive user experience.
