docs.title: Get details of a tuning job
docs.text:
You can retrieve the details of a specific tuning job by its ID.

REST APIPython SDK

To get details of a model tuning job, send a GET request using the tuningJobs.get method and specify the TUNING_JOB_ID.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your project ID.
  • TUNING_JOB_REGION: The region where the tuning job is located.
  • TUNING_JOB_ID: The ID of the tuning job.

HTTP method and URL:

GET https://TUNING_JOB_REGION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/TUNING_JOB_REGION/tuningJobs/TUNING_JOB_ID

To send your request, choose one of these options:

curl

curl -X GET \  
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \  
     "https://TUNING_JOB_REGION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/TUNING_JOB_REGION/tuningJobs/TUNING_JOB_ID"

PowerShell

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token  
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }  

Invoke-WebRequest `  
    -Method GET `  
    -Headers $headers `  
    -Uri "https://TUNING_JOB_REGION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/TUNING_JOB_REGION/tuningJobs/TUNING_JOB_ID" | Select-Object -Expand Content

Response

You should receive a JSON response with the details of the tuning job.

{
  "name": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/TUNING_JOB_REGION/tuningJobs/TUNING_JOB_ID",
  "tunedModelDisplayName": "TUNED_MODEL_DISPLAYNAME",
  "createTime": CREATE_TIME,
  "endTime": END_TIME,
  "tunedModel": {
      "model": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/TUNING_JOB_REGION/models/MODEL_ID",
      "endpoint": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/TUNING_JOB_REGION/endpoints/ENDPOINT_ID"
  },
  "experiment": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/TUNING_JOB_REGION/metadataStores/default/contexts/EXPERIMENT_ID",
  "tuningDataStatistics": {
      "supervisedTuningDataStats": {
          "tuningDatasetExampleCount": "TUNING_DATASET_EXAMPLE_COUNT",

docs.title: Cancel a tuning job
docs.text:
You can cancel a tuning job that is currently in progress.

REST APIPython SDK

To cancel a model tuning job, send a POST request using the tuningJobs.cancel method and specify the TUNING_JOB_ID.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your project ID.
  • TUNING_JOB_REGION: The region where the tuning job is located.
  • TUNING_JOB_ID: The ID of the tuning job to cancel.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://TUNING_JOB_REGION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/TUNING_JOB_REGION/tuningJobs/TUNING_JOB_ID:cancel

To send your request, choose one of these options:

curl

curl -X POST \  
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \  
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \  
     -d "" \  
     "https://TUNING_JOB_REGION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/TUNING_JOB_REGION/tuningJobs/TUNING_JOB_ID:cancel"

PowerShell

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token  
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }  

Invoke-WebRequest `  
    -Method POST `  
    -Headers $headers `  
    -Uri "https://TUNING_JOB_REGION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/TUNING_JOB_REGION/tuningJobs/TUNING_JOB_ID:cancel" | Select-Object -Expand Content

Response

You should receive an empty JSON response upon successful cancellation.

docs.title: Veo on Vertex AI API
docs.text:
Preview

Some features in this document, such as the veo-3.0-generate-preview model, are in Preview.

Veo is a video generation model that creates a high-definition video from a text prompt, an image prompt, or both.

To explore this model in the console, see the Video Generation model card in the Model Garden.

Try Veo on Vertex AI (Vertex AI Studio) Try Veo in a Colab Request access: Advanced features & Veo waitlist

Concepts
  • Prompt: A text string that provides instructions to the model on what to generate in the video.
  • Long-running operation: An asynchronous API call that runs in the background, allowing you to check its status without waiting for it to complete.
  • Seed: A number used to initialize the generation process, which helps in producing deterministic (reproducible) results.
  • Negative prompt: A text string that specifies what you want the model to avoid generating.
  • MIME type: A standard that indicates the nature and format of a document, file, or assortment of bytes (e.g., image/jpeg).

docs.title: Generate a video
docs.text:
To generate a video, send a predictLongRunning POST request to the publisher model endpoint. You can generate a video from a text prompt or an image prompt.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Text-to-videoImage-to-video

Before using the request data, replace the following variables:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • MODEL_ID: The model ID to use. For example, veo-2.0-generate-001.
  • TEXT_PROMPT: The text prompt to guide video generation.
  • OUTPUT_STORAGE_URI: (Optional) The Cloud Storage bucket to store the output videos (e.g., gs://video-bucket/output/). If not provided, video bytes are returned in the response.
  • RESPONSE_COUNT: The number of videos to generate (1-4).

Request JSON body:

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "TEXT_PROMPT"
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "storageUri": "OUTPUT_STORAGE_URI",
    "sampleCount": RESPONSE_COUNT
  }
}

To send your request, choose one of the following options:

curlPowerShell

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \

     -d @request.json \

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login.

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method POST `

    -Uri "https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:predictLongRunning" | Select-Object -Expand Content

This request returns a full operation name with a unique operation ID.

Sample response: 

{
  "name": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID/operations/a1b07c8e-7b5a-4aba-bb34-3e1ccb8afcc8"
}

  • TEXT_PROMPT: The text prompt to guide video generation.
  • INPUT_IMAGE: A Base64-encoded string of the input image. For best results, use an image that is 720p or higher with a 16:9 or 9:16 aspect ratio.
  • MIME_TYPE: The MIME type of the input image (image/jpeg or image/png).

docs.title: Check the status of the video generation job
docs.text:
After submitting a generation request, you receive an operation name. Use this name to poll the status of the job by sending a fetchPredictOperation POST request.

Before using the request data, replace the following variables:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • MODEL_ID: The model ID used in the original request.
  • OPERATION_ID: The unique operation ID returned from the predictLongRunning request.

Request JSON body:

{
  "operationName": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID/operations/OPERATION_ID"
}

To send your request, choose one of the following options:

curlPowerShell

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d @request.json \
     "https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:fetchPredictOperation"

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method POST `
    -Headers $headers `
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `

    -Uri "https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:fetchPredictOperation" | Select-Object -Expand Content

When the done field in the response is true, the operation is complete, and the response object contains the URIs of the generated videos.

Sample response (when complete):

{
  "name": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID/operations/OPERATION_ID",
  "done": true,
  "response": {
    "@type": "type.googleapis.com/cloud.ai.large_models.vision.GenerateVideoResponse",
    "videos": [
      {
        "gcsUri":"gs://BUCKET_NAME/TIMESTAMPED_FOLDER/sample_0.mp4",
        "mimeType": "video/mp4"
      }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: This section provides detailed descriptions of the request and response bodies for the Veo API.

docs.title: predictLongRunning request body
docs.text:
{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": string,
      "image": {
        // Union field can be only one of the following:
        "bytesBase64Encoded": string,
        "gcsUri": string
      },
      "lastFrame": {
        // Union field can be only one of the following:
        "bytesBase64Encoded": string,
        "gcsUri": string
      },
      "video": {
        // Union field can be only one of the following:
        "bytesBase64Encoded": string,
        "gcsUri": string
      }
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "aspectRatio": string,
    "durationSeconds": integer,
    "enhancePrompt": boolean,
    "generateAudio": boolean,
    "negativePrompt": string,
    "personGeneration": string,
    "sampleCount": integer,
    "seed": uint32,
    "storageUri": string
  }
}

Instances

Field Type Description prompt string Required for text-to-video. A text string to guide video generation. Examples:
  • A fast-tracking shot through a bustling dystopian sprawl with bright neon signs, flying cars and mist, night, lens flare, volumetric lighting
  • Timelapse of the northern lights dancing across the Arctic sky, stars twinkling, snow-covered landscape
image object Optional. An image to guide video generation. Can be either bytesBase64Encoded or gcsUri. lastFrame object Optional. An image of the last frame to guide video generation. Supported by veo-2.0-generate-001 only. video object Optional. A Veo-generated video to extend in length. Supported by veo-2.0-generate-001 only. bytesBase64Encoded string A Base64-encoded string of an image or video file. gcsUri string A Cloud Storage URI to an image or video file. mimeType string Required for image, video, and lastFrame objects. Supported image types: image/jpeg, image/png. Supported video type: video/mp4.

Parameters

Field Type Description aspectRatio string Optional. The aspect ratio of the generated video. Accepted values: 16:9 (default), 9:16. durationSeconds integer Required. The length of the video in seconds.
  • veo-2.0-generate-001: 5-8 (default 8).
  • veo-3.0-generate-preview: 8.
enhancePrompt boolean Optional. If true (default), Gemini is used to enhance your prompt. generateAudio boolean Optional. If true, generates audio for the video. Required for veo-3.0-generate-preview. Not supported by veo-2.0-generate-001. negativePrompt string Optional. A text string describing what the model should avoid generating. personGeneration string Optional. Safety setting for people generation.
  • allow_adult (default): Allows generation of adults.
  • dont_allow: Disallows generation of people/faces.
sampleCount integer Optional. The number of videos to generate. Accepted values: 1-4. seed uint32 Optional. A number (0-4294967295) to make video generation deterministic. storageUri string Optional. A Cloud Storage URI (gs://BUCKET_NAME/SUBDIRECTORY) to store the output video. If not provided, base64-encoded video bytes are returned.

docs.text:
The response from polling the long-running operation.

{
   "name": string,
   "done": boolean,
   "response":{
      "@type":"type.googleapis.com/cloud.ai.large_models.vision.GenerateVideoResponse",
      "videos":[
         {
           "gcsUri": string,
           "mimeType": string
         }
      ]
   }
}
Field Description name The full operation name of the video generation job. done A boolean that is true when the operation is complete. response The response body, which contains the generated video details when the operation is done. videos An array of generated video objects. gcsUri The Cloud Storage URI of the generated video. mimeType The MIME type of the generated video (e.g., video/mp4).

docs.title: Vertex AI Model Optimizer
docs.text:
Preview

This feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

To see an example of using Vertex AI Model Optimizer, run the "Getting Started with Model Optimizer" Jupyter notebook in one of the following environments:

Open in Colab Open in Colab Enterprise Open in Vertex AI Workbench View on GitHub

Vertex AI Model Optimizer is a service that simplifies model selection by automatically routing your requests to the most suitable Gemini model. Instead of targeting a specific model version, you can send prompts to a single endpoint, and the service intelligently selects the best model (such as Gemini 1.5 Pro or Gemini 1.5 Flash) based on your cost and quality preferences.

For more information on Model Optimizer pricing, see Generative AI on Vertex AI pricing.

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
Model Optimizer lets you:

  • Simplify model selection: Avoid choosing and managing different models for each application.
  • Optimize for cost and quality: Balance performance and budget according to your needs.
  • Integrate seamlessly: Use the optimizer with existing Gemini APIs and SDKs.
  • Track usage: Monitor performance and identify opportunities for cost savings.
  • Handle text tasks efficiently: Automate endpoint selection for text-based use cases.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
When you send a request to the Model Optimizer, you specify a FeatureSelectionPreference to guide the model selection process. The service then routes your prompt to the appropriate underlying Gemini model that aligns with your preference.

The following table explains the available preferences:

Preference Description Best for PRIORITIZE_QUALITY Selects the highest-quality model (e.g., Gemini 1.5 Pro) for the best possible response. Tasks where accuracy, detail, and reasoning are critical. BALANCED Automatically balances cost and quality to provide a good trade-off. This is the default setting. General-purpose tasks where you want a mix of performance and efficiency. PRIORITIZE_COST Selects the most cost-effective model (e.g., Gemini 1.5 Flash) to minimize expense. High-volume or simple tasks where speed and low cost are the main priorities.

docs.title: Supported models
docs.text:
• Gemini 1.5 Flash
  • Gemini 1.5 Pro

docs.title: Language support
docs.text: Model Optimizer supports all languages that are also supported by the underlying Gemini models. For more information, see Gemini language support.

docs.title: Modality
docs.text:
Model Optimizer is designed for text-only use cases, including:

  • Coding, including function calling and code execution
  • Summarization
  • Single and multi-turn chat
  • Question and answering

docs.title: Handling unsupported features
docs.text:
Model Optimizer only supports text input and output. Requests containing unsupported data or tools will result in an error.

  • Multimodal requests: Requests that include prompts with multimodal data, such as video, images, or audio, will return an INVALID_ARGUMENT error.
  • Unsupported tools: Model Optimizer only supports function calling declarations. If a request contains other tool types, such as google_search or retrieval, an INVALID_ARGUMENT error is returned.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Vertex AI Model Optimizer: A service that acts as a single endpoint to automatically route generative AI requests to the best Gemini model based on user-defined preferences for cost and quality.
  • Gemini 1.5 Pro: A powerful, multimodal model that excels at complex, multi-turn reasoning tasks across text, images, audio, and video.
  • Gemini 1.5 Flash: A lighter-weight, cost-effective model optimized for high-volume, fast-response text-based tasks.

This guide shows you how to send requests to the Model Optimizer using the Generative AI SDK for Python.

The following workflow provides a high-level overview of the steps.

flowchart TD
    A[Set up your environment] --> B[Send a request to the Model Optimizer]
    B --> C[Receive an optimized response]

    click A "#set-up-your-environment"
    click B "#send-a-request-to-the-model-optimizer"
    click C "#send-a-request-to-the-model-optimizer"
Use the Model Optimizer with the Python SDK

1. Set up your environment

Install the latest version of the Generative AI SDK for Python.

pip install --upgrade google-genai

To learn more, see the Python SDK reference documentation.

2. Send a request to the Model Optimizer

Set the required environment variables and use the following code to send a prompt. You can change the feature_selection_preference to PRIORITIZE_QUALITY, BALANCED, or PRIORITIZE_COST.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

# Set environment variables to use the Gen AI SDK with Vertex AI
# Replace the `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` values
# with appropriate values for your project.
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global
export GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=True


from google import genai
from google.genai.types import (
    FeatureSelectionPreference,
    GenerateContentConfig,
    HttpOptions,
    ModelSelectionConfig
)

client = genai.Client(http_options=HttpOptions(api_version="v1beta1"))
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="model-optimizer-exp-04-09",
    contents="How does AI work?",
    config=GenerateContentConfig(
        model_selection_config=ModelSelectionConfig(
            feature_selection_preference=FeatureSelectionPreference.BALANCED  # Options: PRIORITIZE_QUALITY, BALANCED, PRIORITIZE_COST
        ),
    ),
)
print(response.text)
# Example response:
# Okay, let's break down how AI works. It's a broad field, so I'll focus on the ...
#
# Here's a simplified overview:
# ...

docs.title: Visual question and answering (VQA)
docs.text:
The imagetext model lets you perform visual question and answering (VQA) tasks. You can provide an image and a question, and the model returns one or more answers about the content of the image.

To explore this model in the console, see the imagetext model card in the Model Garden.

View the imagetext model card

Concepts
  • Visual Question Answering (VQA): A task where a model analyzes an image and provides a natural language answer to a question about that image.
  • Prompt: The question you ask the model about the image.

docs.title: Use cases
docs.text:
Common use cases for visual question and answering include the following:

  • Empower users to engage with visual content through a Q&A interface.
  • Enable customers to ask questions about product images on retail apps and websites.
  • Provide accessibility options for visually impaired users by describing image contents.

docs.title: HTTP method and URL
docs.text: POST https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/imagetext:predict

docs.title: Request body
docs.text:
{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": string,
      "image": {
        // Union field can be only one of the following:
        "bytesBase64Encoded": string,
        "gcsUri": string
        // End of list of possible types for union field.
      }
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "sampleCount": integer,
    "seed": integer
  }
}

docs.title: Request parameters
docs.text:
You can specify the image for your prompt in one of two ways:

Image Source Description bytesBase64Encoded Use for local images. The image file is converted to a Base64-encoded string and included directly in the JSON request body. gcsUri Use for images stored in a Cloud Storage bucket. The request includes the URI of the image file. This method is useful for larger images or when integrating with other Google Cloud services.

The following table describes the parameters for the imagetext model:

Parameter Description Acceptable values instances An array containing the prompt and image object. Only one image object is allowed per request. array prompt The question you want answered about your image. string (80 tokens max) bytesBase64Encoded The image to get information about, encoded as a Base64 string. Cannot be used with gcsUri. Base64-encoded string (PNG or JPEG, 20 MB max) gcsUri The Cloud Storage URI of the image to get information about. Cannot be used with bytesBase64Encoded. string (PNG or JPEG, 20 MB max) sampleCount The number of answers to generate for the question. integer (1-3) seed An optional integer to control the randomness of the output. Requests with the same seed and inputs will produce the same results. integer

docs.title: Sample request
docs.text:
Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • LOCATION: The region for your project. For a list of available regions, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.
  • VQA_PROMPT: The question you want to ask about the image (for example, "What color is this shoe?" or "What type of sleeves are on the shirt?").
  • B64_IMAGE: The Base64-encoded byte string of your image file. For more information, see Base64 encoding images.
  • RESPONSE_COUNT: The number of answers you want to generate (1-3).

The following examples show how to send a request using a local image file.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

curlPowerShell

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell.

  1. Save the request body in a file named request.json:

    {
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "VQA_PROMPT",
      "image": {
          "bytesBase64Encoded": "B64_IMAGE"
      }
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "sampleCount": RESPONSE_COUNT
  }
}

  2. Execute the following command in your terminal:

    curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d @request.json \
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagetext:predict"

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login.

docs.title: Run a computation-based evaluation pipeline
docs.text:
Note: For the most updated computation-based evaluation features, see Define your metrics.

You can evaluate the performance of foundation models and your tuned generative AI models on Vertex AI. The models are evaluated using a set of metrics against an evaluation dataset that you provide. This page explains how computation-based model evaluation through the evaluation pipeline service works, how to create and format the evaluation dataset, and how to perform the evaluation using the Google Cloud console, Vertex AI API, or the Vertex AI SDK for Python.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Before you begin Concepts
  • JSON Lines (JSONL): A text format for storing structured data where each line is a valid JSON object.
  • ROUGE-L (Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation - Longest Common Subsequence): A metric that measures the quality of a summary by comparing it to a reference summary based on the longest common subsequence of words.
  • BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy): A metric for evaluating the quality of machine-translated text by measuring the correspondence between a machine's output and that of a human.
  • F1-score: A measure of a model's accuracy on a dataset, calculated as the harmonic mean of precision and recall.

Required permissions

To perform this task, you must grant Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles to each of the following service accounts:

Service account Default principal Description Roles Vertex AI Service Agent service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount.com The Vertex AI Service Agent is automatically provisioned for your project and granted a predefined role. However, if an org policy modifies the default permissions of the Vertex AI Service Agent, you must manually grant the role to the service agent. Vertex AI Service Agent ('roles/aiplatform.serviceAgent') Vertex AI Pipelines Service Account PROJECT_NUMBER-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com The service account that runs the pipeline. The default service account used is the Compute Engine default service account. Optionally, you can use a custom service account instead of the default service account.
  • Vertex AI User ('roles/aiplatform.user')
  • Storage Object User ('roles/storage.objectUser')

Depending on your input and output data sources, you may also need to grant the Vertex AI Pipelines Service Account additional roles:

Data source Role Where to grant the role Standard BigQuery table BigQuery Data Editor Project that runs the pipeline BigQuery Data Viewer Project that the table belongs to BigQuery view of a standard BigQuery table BigQuery Data Editor Project that runs the pipeline BigQuery Data Viewer Project that the view belongs to BigQuery Data Viewer Project that the table belongs to BigQuery external table that has a source Cloud Storage file BigQuery Data Editor Project that runs the pipeline BigQuery Data Viewer Project that the external table belongs to Storage Object Viewer Project that the source file belongs to BigQuery view of a BigQuery external table that has a source Cloud Storage file BigQuery Data Editor Project that runs the pipeline BigQuery Data Viewer Project that the view belongs to BigQuery Data Viewer Project that the external table belongs to Storage Object Viewer Project that the source file belongs to Cloud Storage file BigQuery Data Viewer Project that runs the pipeline

docs.title: Overall workflow
docs.text:
This document guides you through the following workflow to run a computation-based evaluation.

flowchart LR
    A[Prepare evaluation dataset] --> B[Perform model evaluation] --> C[View evaluation results]

click A "#prepare-evaluation-dataset"
click B "#perform-model-evaluation"
click C "#view-evaluation-results"

docs.title: How computation-based model evaluation works
docs.text:
To evaluate the performance of a model, you first create an evaluation dataset that contains prompt and ground truth pairs. For each pair, the prompt is the input that you want to evaluate, and the ground truth is the ideal response for that prompt. During evaluation, the prompt in each pair of the evaluation dataset is passed to the model to produce an output. The output generated by the model and the ground truth from the evaluation dataset are used to compute the evaluation metrics.

The type of metrics used for evaluation depends on the task that you are evaluating. The following table shows the supported tasks and the metrics used to evaluate each task:

Task Metric Classification Micro-F1, Macro-F1, Per class F1 Summarization ROUGE-L Question answering Exact Match Text generation BLEU, ROUGE-L

docs.title: Supported models
docs.text:
Model evaluation is supported for the following models:

  • text-bison: Base and tuned versions.
  • Gemini: All tasks except classification.

docs.title: Prepare evaluation dataset
docs.text: The evaluation dataset that's used for model evaluation includes prompt and ground truth pairs that align with the task that you want to evaluate. Your dataset must include a minimum of 1 prompt and ground truth pair and at least 10 pairs for meaningful metrics. The more examples you provide, the more meaningful the results.

docs.title: Dataset format
docs.text:
Your evaluation dataset must be in JSON Lines (JSONL) format where each line contains a single prompt and ground truth pair specified in the input_text and output_text fields, respectively. The input_text field contains the prompt that you want to evaluate, and the output_text field contains the ideal response for the prompt.

The maximum token length for input_text is 8,192, and the maximum token length for output_text is 1,024.

Example JSONL dataset line:

{"input_text": "Provide a summary of the following article: [Article text]", "output_text": "This is the ideal summary of the article."}

docs.title: Upload evaluation dataset to Cloud Storage
docs.text: You must upload your evaluation dataset file to a Cloud Storage bucket. You can either create a new Cloud Storage bucket or use an existing one to store your dataset file. The bucket must be in the same region where you run the model evaluation job.

docs.title: Perform model evaluation
docs.text:
You can evaluate models using the Google Cloud console for a UI-driven approach, the REST API for integration with other services, or the Vertex AI SDK for Python for programmatic control within your workflows.

Method Best for Google Cloud console Quick evaluations and users who prefer a graphical interface. REST API Integrating evaluation into automated workflows or multi-language applications. Vertex AI SDK for Python Programmatic evaluation within a Python environment, ideal for MLOps pipelines and data scientists. Google Cloud consoleREST APIVertex AI SDK for Python

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI Model Registry page.

    Go to Vertex AI Model Registry

  2. Click the name of the model that you want to evaluate.

  3. In the Evaluate tab, click Create evaluation and configure as follows:
    • Objective: Select the task that you want to evaluate.
    • Target column or field: (Classification only) Enter the target column for prediction. Example: ground_truth.
    • Source path: Enter or select the URI of your evaluation dataset.
    • Output format: Enter the format of the evaluation output. Currently, only jsonl is supported.
    • Cloud Storage path: Enter or select the URI to store evaluation output.
    • Class names: (Classification only) Enter the list of possible class names.
    • Number of compute nodes: Enter the number of compute nodes to run the evaluation job.
    • Machine type: Select a machine type to use for running the evaluation job.
  4. Click Start evaluation.

To create a model evaluation job, send a POST request by using the pipelineJobs method. The evaluation job runs asynchronously and does not impact any existing deployments of the model or their resources.

Request parameters

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: The Google Cloud project that runs the pipeline components.
  • PIPELINEJOB_DISPLAYNAME: A display name for the pipelineJob.
  • LOCATION: The region to run the pipeline components. Currently, only us-central1 is supported.
  • DATASET_URI: The Cloud Storage URI of your reference dataset. You can specify one or multiple URIs. This parameter supports wildcards.
  • OUTPUT_DIR: The Cloud Storage URI to store evaluation output.
  • MODEL_NAME: Specify a publisher model or a tuned model resource as follows:
    • Publisher model: publishers/google/models/MODEL@MODEL_VERSION Example: publishers/google/models/text-bison@002
    • Tuned model: projects/PROJECT_NUMBER/locations/LOCATION/models/ENDPOINT_ID Example: projects/123456789012/locations/us-central1/models/1234567890123456789
  • EVALUATION_TASK: The task that you want to evaluate the model on. The evaluation job computes a set of metrics relevant to that specific task. Acceptable values include: summarization, question-answering, text-generation, classification.
  • INSTANCES_FORMAT: The format of your dataset. Currently, only jsonl is supported.
  • PREDICTIONS_FORMAT: The format of the evaluation output. Currently, only jsonl is supported.
  • MACHINE_TYPE: (Optional) The machine type for running the evaluation job. The default value is e2-highmem-16. For a list of supported machine types, see Machine types.
  • SERVICE_ACCOUNT: (Optional) The service account to use for running the evaluation job. If unspecified, the Vertex AI Custom Code Service Agent is used. To learn how to create a custom service account, see Configure a service account with granular permissions.
  • NETWORK: (Optional) The fully qualified name of the Compute Engine network to peer the evaluation job to. The format is projects/PROJECT_NUMBER/global/networks/NETWORK_NAME. If you specify this field, you need to have a VPC Network Peering for Vertex AI. If left unspecified, the job is not peered with any network.
  • KEY_NAME: (Optional) The name of the customer-managed encryption key (CMEK). If configured, resources created by the evaluation job are encrypted using the provided key. The format is projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/REGION/keyRings/KEY_RING/cryptoKeys/KEY. The key must be in the same region as the job.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/pipelineJobs

Request JSON body:

{
  "displayName": "PIPELINEJOB_DISPLAYNAME",
  "runtimeConfig": {
    "gcsOutputDirectory": "gs://OUTPUT_DIR",
    "parameterValues": {
      "project": "PROJECT_ID",
      "location": "LOCATION",
      "batch_predict_gcs_source_uris": ["gs://DATASET_URI"],
      "batch_predict_gcs_destination_output_uri": "gs://OUTPUT_DIR",
      "model_name": "MODEL_NAME",
      "evaluation_task": "EVALUATION_TASK",
      "batch_predict_instances_format": "INSTANCES_FORMAT",
      "batch_predict_predictions_format: "PREDICTIONS_FORMAT",
      "machine_type": "MACHINE_TYPE",
      "service_account": "SERVICE_ACCOUNT",
      "network": "NETWORK",
      "encryption_spec_key_name": "KEY_NAME"
    }
  },
  "templateUri": "https://us-kfp.pkg.dev/vertex-evaluation/pipeline-templates/evaluation-llm-text-generation-pipeline/1.0.1"
}

To send your request, choose one of these options.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

import os

from google.auth import default

import vertexai
from vertexai.preview.language_models import (
    EvaluationTextClassificationSpec,
    TextGenerationModel,
)

PROJECT_ID = os.getenv("GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT")


def evaluate_model() -> object:
    """Evaluate the performance of a generative AI model."""

    # Set credentials for the pipeline components used in the evaluation task
    credentials, _ = default(scopes=["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"])

    vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1", credentials=credentials)

    # Create a reference to a generative AI model
    model = TextGenerationModel.from_pretrained("text-bison@002")

    # Define the evaluation specification for a text classification task
    task_spec = EvaluationTextClassificationSpec(
        ground_truth_data=[
            "gs://cloud-samples-data/ai-platform/generative_ai/llm_classification_bp_input_prompts_with_ground_truth.jsonl"
        ],
        class_names=["nature", "news", "sports", "health", "startups"],
        target_column_name="ground_truth",
    )

    # Evaluate the model
    eval_metrics = model.evaluate(task_spec=task_spec)
    print(eval_metrics)
    # Example response:
    # ...
    # PipelineJob run completed.
    # Resource name: projects/123456789/locations/us-central1/pipelineJobs/evaluation-llm-classification-...
    # EvaluationClassificationMetric(label_name=None, auPrc=0.53833705, auRoc=0.8...

    return eval_metrics

docs.title: View evaluation results
docs.text:
After the evaluation job is complete, you can find the results in the Cloud Storage output directory that you specified when creating the job. The results file is named evaluation_metrics.json.

For tuned models, you can also view evaluation results in the Google Cloud console.

Steps to view results in the Google Cloud console

  1. In the Vertex AI section of the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI Model Registry page.

    Go to Vertex AI Model Registry

  2. Click the name of the tuned model to view its evaluation metrics.

  3. In the Evaluate tab, click the name of the evaluation run that you want to view.

docs.title: Configure a judge model
docs.text:
Preview

This feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

Model-based metrics provide various approaches to customize and help you generate evaluation metrics based on your criteria and use cases. This page describes how to configure your judge model for your ideal use case.

For the basic evaluation workflow, see the Gen AI evaluation service quickstart. The Advanced judge model customization series includes the following pages:

  1. Evaluate a judge model
  2. Prompting for judge model customization
  3. Configure a judge model (current page)
Concepts
  • Judge model: An LLM used to evaluate the quality of another model's output based on specified criteria.
  • System instructions: A set of directives given to a model to guide its overall behavior, tone, and response style.
  • Response flipping: A technique to reduce positional bias by swapping the order of candidate and baseline model responses during pairwise evaluation.
  • Multi-sampling: The practice of querying the judge model multiple times for the same input to improve the consistency and reliability of its evaluation.
  • Tuned judge model: A judge model that has been fine-tuned on a specific dataset to improve its evaluation accuracy for a particular task.

docs.title: Overview of configuration methods
docs.text:
You can configure your judge model to improve evaluation quality using several methods. The following table provides a high-level comparison to help you choose the right approach for your needs.

Method Description Best for System instructions Provide high-level directives to the judge model to influence its persona, tone, and evaluation style. Setting a consistent evaluation context or persona (e.g., "You are an expert in medical writing"). Response flipping Swaps the order of the baseline and candidate model responses in half of the evaluation calls. Reducing positional bias in pairwise evaluations where the judge model might favor the first or second response. Multi-sampling Calls the judge model multiple times for the same evaluation to average out randomness. Improving the consistency and reliability of evaluation scores, especially when the judge model shows variability. Tuned judge model Uses a fine-tuned LLM as the judge model. Achieving the highest evaluation quality for a specific, well-defined use case with sufficient tuning data.

docs.title: Use system instructions
docs.text:
Gemini models can accept system instructions, which are a set of instructions that guide how the model processes prompts. You can use system instructions to specify roles, personas, contextual information, or a desired explanation style and tone. The judge model typically gives higher importance to system instructions than to input prompts.

For a list of models that support system instructions, see Supported models.

The following example using the Vertex AI SDK adds system_instruction at the metric level for a PointwiseMetric. You can use the same approach with PairwiseMetric.

system_instruction = "You are an expert evaluator."
linguistic_acceptability = PointwiseMetric(
    metric="linguistic_acceptability",
    metric_prompt_template=linguistic_acceptability_metric_prompt_template,
    system_instruction=system_instruction,
)

eval_result = EvalTask(
    dataset=EVAL_DATASET,
    metrics=[linguistic_acceptability]
).evaluate()

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Advanced judge model configurations
docs.text:
You can further customize the judge model for bias reduction, consistency, and accuracy by passing an AutoraterConfig object to your EvalTask.

Enable response flippingConfigure multi-samplingUse a tuned judge model

For PairwiseMetrics, the judge model evaluates which of two responses (one from a baseline model, one from a candidate model) better aligns with the specified criteria. However, the model might be biased toward the response presented first.

To reduce this bias, you can enable response flipping. When enabled, the service flips the baseline and candidate model responses in half of the calls to the judge model.

from vertexai.preview.evaluation import AutoraterConfig

pairwise_relevance_prompt_template = """
    # Instruction
    …

    ### Response A
    {baseline_model_response}

    ### Response B
    {candidate_model_response}
"""

my_pairwise_metric = PairwiseMetric(
    metric="my_pairwise_metric",
    metric_prompt_template=pairwise_relevance_prompt_template,
    candidate_response_field_name = "candidate_model_response",
    baseline_response_field_name = "baseline_model_response"
)


# Define an AutoraterConfig with flip_enabled
my_autorater_config = AutoraterConfig(flip_enabled=True)

# Define an EvalTask with autorater_config
flip_enabled_eval_result = EvalTask(
    dataset=EVAL_DATASET,
    metrics=[my_pairwise_metric],
    autorater_config=my_autorater_config,
).evaluate()

The judge model might show some randomness in its responses. Additional sampling can help negate this randomness and lead to more consistent results, though it increases latency.

You can set the sampling_count to an integer between 1 and 32. The recommended default is 4, which balances consistency and latency.

from vertexai.preview.evaluation import AutoraterConfig

# Define customized sampling count in AutoraterConfig
autorater_config = AutoraterConfig(sampling_count=6)

# Run evaluation with the sampling count.
eval_result = EvalTask(
    dataset=EVAL_DATASET,
    metrics=[METRICS],
    autorater_config=autorater_config
).evaluate()

If you have high-quality tuning data for your evaluation use case, you can tune a Gemini model and use it as your judge model for improved accuracy. You can specify a tuned model as the judge model through AutoraterConfig.

from vertexai.preview.evaluation import {
   AutoraterConfig,
   PairwiseMetric,
   tune_autorater,
   evaluate_autorater,
}

# Tune a model to be the judge model. The tune_autorater helper function returns an AutoraterConfig with the judge model set as the tuned model.
autorater_config: AutoRaterConfig = tune_autorater(
    base_model="gemini-1.0-pro",
    train_dataset=f"{BUCKET_URI}/train/sft_train_samples.jsonl",
    validation_dataset=f"{BUCKET_URI}/val/sft_val_samples.jsonl",
    tuned_model_display_name=tuned_model_display_name,
)

# Alternatively, you can set up the judge model with an existing tuned model endpoint
autorater_config = AutoraterConfig(autorater_model=TUNED_MODEL)

# Use the tuned judge model
eval_result = EvalTask(
    dataset=EVAL_DATASET,
    metrics=[METRICS],
    autorater_config=autorater_config,
).evaluate()

docs.text: • Evaluate a generative AI agent

docs.title: Define your evaluation metrics
docs.text: The first step to evaluate your generative models or applications is to identify your evaluation goal and define your evaluation metrics. This page provides an overview of concepts related to defining evaluation metrics for your use case.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Generative AI models can be used to create applications for a wide range of tasks, such as summarizing news articles, responding to customer inquiries, or assisting with code writing. The Gen AI evaluation service in Vertex AI lets you evaluate any model with explainable metrics.

To evaluate your application's performance on a specific task, you must define the criteria you want to measure and the metrics to score them:

  • Criteria: Single or multiple dimensions you would like to evaluate upon, such as conciseness, relevance, correctness, or appropriate choice of words.
  • Metrics: A single score that measures the model output against the defined criteria.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Judge Model: A model used to evaluate the output of another model based on specified criteria.
  • Ground Truth: A dataset of high-quality, reference examples used to evaluate a model's performance with computation-based metrics.
  • ROUGE (Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation): A set of metrics used for evaluating automatic summarization and machine translation by comparing a model's output to a human-created reference.
  • BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy): A metric for evaluating the quality of machine-translated text by measuring its similarity to a set of high-quality reference translations.
  • Chain-of-thought prompting: A technique that encourages a large language model (LLM) to explain its reasoning process step-by-step, which can improve the accuracy of its final answer.
  • Function Calling: The ability of a model to intelligently decide to call external tools or functions to perform actions or retrieve information.

docs.title: Types of evaluation metrics
docs.text:
The Gen AI evaluation service provides two major types of metrics: model-based and computation-based. Use the following table to decide which approach is best for your use case.

Evaluation approach How it works Data requirements Cost and speed Model-based metrics Use a judge model to assess performance based on descriptive evaluation criteria. Ground truth is optional. Slightly more expensive and slower. Computation-based metrics Use mathematical formulas to assess performance by comparing model output to a reference. Ground truth is usually required. Low cost and fast.

To get started after choosing your metrics, see Prepare your dataset and Run evaluation.

docs.title: Define your model-based metrics
docs.text:
Model-based evaluation involves using a machine learning model (a "judge model") to evaluate the outputs of your candidate model. Proprietary Google judge models, such as Gemini, are calibrated with human raters to ensure their quality and are available out of the box.

Model-based evaluation follows this process:

  1. Data preparation: You provide evaluation data in the form of input prompts. The candidate models receive the prompts and generate corresponding responses.
  2. Evaluation: The evaluation metrics and generated responses are sent to the judge model. The judge model evaluates each response individually, providing a row-based assessment.
  3. Aggregation and explanation: The Gen AI evaluation service aggregates these individual assessments into an overall score. The output also includes chain-of-thought explanations for each judgment, outlining the rationale behind the selection.

docs.title: Choose between pointwise and pairwise evaluation
docs.text:
You can measure model-based metrics pointwise or pairwise. Pairwise metrics are only supported with Gemini as a judge model. Use the following table to decide which evaluation method to use.

Evaluation type Definition When to use Example use cases Pointwise evaluation Evaluate one model and generate scores based on the criteria.
  • When you need a score for each model being evaluated.
  • When it is not difficult to define the rubric for each score.
  • Understanding how your model behaves in production.
  • Exploring the strengths and weaknesses of a single model.
  • Identifying which behaviors to focus on when tuning.
  • Getting the baseline performance of a model.
Pairwise evaluation Compare two models against each other, generating a preference based on the criteria.
  • When you want to compare two models and a score is not necessary.
  • When the score rubric for pointwise is difficult to define.
  • Determining which model to put into production.
  • Choosing between model types (e.g., Gemini Pro versus Claude 3).
  • Choosing between different prompts.
  • Determining if tuning improved a baseline model.

docs.title: Set up your model-based metrics
docs.text:
The Gen AI evaluation service offers the following options to set up your model-based metrics with the Vertex AI SDK.

Option Description Best for Use an existing example Use a prebuilt metric prompt template to get started. Common use cases, time-saving. Define metrics with our templated interface Get guided assistance in defining your metrics. Our templated interface provides structure and suggestions. Customization with support. Define metrics from scratch Have complete control over your metric definitions. Ideal for highly specific use cases. Requires more technical expertise and time investment.

As an example, you might want to develop a generative AI application that returns fluent and entertaining responses. For this application, you can define two criteria for evaluation using the templated interface:

  • Fluency: Sentences flow smoothly, avoiding awkward phrasing or run-on sentences. Ideas and sentences connect logically, using transitions effectively where needed.
  • Entertainment: Short, amusing text that incorporates emoji, exclamations, and questions to convey quick and spontaneous communication and diversion.

To turn those two criteria into a metric, you want an overall score ranging from -1 to 1 called custom_text_quality. You can define a metric like this:

# Define a pointwise metric with two criteria: Fluency and Entertaining.
pointwise_metric = PointwiseMetric(
    metric="custom_text_quality",
    metric_prompt_template=PointwiseMetricPromptTemplate(
        criteria={
            "fluency": (
                "Sentences flow smoothly and are easy to read, avoiding awkward"
                " phrasing or run-on sentences. Ideas and sentences connect"
                " logically, using transitions effectively where needed."
            ),
            "entertaining": (
                "Short, amusing text that incorporates emojis, exclamations and"
                " questions to convey quick and spontaneous communication and"
                " diversion."
            ),
        },
        rating_rubric={
            "1": "The response performs well on both criteria.",
            "0": "The response is somewhat aligned with both criteria",
            "-1": "The response falls short on both criteria",
        },
    ),
)

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

For a complete list of metric prompt templates, see Metric prompt templates for evaluation.

docs.title: Evaluate translation models
docs.text:
Preview

This product or feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA products and features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

The Gen AI evaluation service offers specialized metrics for translation tasks. You can use these to evaluate the quality and accuracy of translation model results, whether they are outputs of NMT, TranslationLLM, or Gemini models. You can also use Gemini as a judge model to evaluate your model for fluency, coherence, verbosity, and text quality in combination with these metrics.

Metric Type Description Scoring MetricX Model-based An error-based metric developed by Google. Available as both reference-based and reference-free (QE). Predicts a score between 0 and 25. A lower score is better. COMET Model-based Employs a reference-based regression approach. Provides scores from 0 to 1. A higher score is better. BLEU Computation-based Indicates how similar the candidate text is to the reference text. Provides scores from 0 to 1. A higher score is better.

Note that BLEU scores are not recommended for comparing across different corpora and languages. Many translation experts have shifted to model-based metric approaches like MetricX and COMET, which have a higher correlation with human ratings and are more granular in identifying error scenarios.

To learn how to run evaluations for translation models, see Evaluate a translation model.

docs.title: Define your computation-based metrics
docs.text:
Computation-based metrics compare whether the LLM-generated results are consistent with a ground-truth dataset of input and output pairs. These metrics can be categorized into the following groups:

  • Lexicon-based metrics: Use math to calculate the string similarities between LLM-generated results and ground truth, such as Exact Match and ROUGE.
  • Count-based metrics: Aggregate the number of rows that hit or miss certain ground-truth labels, such as F1-score, Accuracy, and Tool Name Match.
  • Embedding-based metrics: Calculate the distance between the LLM-generated results and ground truth in the embedding space, reflecting their level of similarity.

In the generative AI evaluation service, you can use computation-based metrics through the Vertex AI SDK for Python.

docs.title: General text generation
docs.text:
The following metrics help you to evaluate the model's ability to ensure the responses are useful, safe, and effective for your users.

Exact match

The exact_match metric computes whether a model response matches a reference exactly.

  • Token limit: None

Evaluation criteria

Not applicable.

Metric input parameters

Input parameter Description response The LLM response. reference The golden LLM response for reference.

Output scores

Value Description 0 Not matched 1 Matched BLEU

The bleu (BiLingual Evaluation Understudy) metric holds the result of an algorithm for evaluating the quality of the response, which has been translated from one natural language to another. The quality of the response is considered to be the correspondence between a response parameter and its reference parameter.

  • Token limit: None

Evaluation criteria

Not applicable.

Metric input parameters

Input parameter Description response The LLM response. reference The golden LLM response for the reference.

Output scores

Value Description A float in the range of [0,1] Higher scores indicate better translations. A score of 1 represents a perfect match to the reference. ROUGE

The ROUGE metric is used to compare the provided response parameter against a reference parameter. All rouge metrics return the F1 score. rouge-l-sum is calculated by default, but you can specify the rouge variant that you want to use.

  • Token limit: None

Evaluation criteria

Not applicable.

Metric input parameters

Input parameter Description response The LLM response. reference The golden LLM response for the reference.

Output scores

Value Description A float in the range of [0,1] A score closer to 0 means poor similarity between response and reference. A score closer to 1 means strong similarity between response and reference.

docs.title: Tool use and function calling
docs.text:
The following metrics help you to evaluate the model's ability to predict a valid tool (function) call.

Tool call valid

The tool_call_valid metric describes the model's ability to predict a valid tool call. Only the first tool call is inspected.

  • Token limit: None

Evaluation criteria

Evaluation criterion Description Validity The model's output contains a valid tool call. Formatting A JSON dictionary contains the name and arguments fields.

Metric input parameters

Input parameter Description prediction The candidate model output, which is a JSON serialized string that contains content and tool_calls keys. The content value is the text output from the model. The tool_calls value is a JSON serialized string of a list of tool calls. Here is an example:{"content": "", "tool_calls": [{"name": "book_tickets", "arguments": {"movie": "Mission Impossible Dead Reckoning Part 1", "theater":"Regal Edwards 14", "location": "Mountain View CA", "showtime": "7:30", "date": "2024-03-30","num_tix": "2"}}]} reference The ground-truth reference prediction, which follows the same format as prediction.

Output scores

Value Description 0 Invalid tool call 1 Valid tool call Tool name match

The tool_name_match metric describes the model's ability to predict a tool call with the correct tool name. Only the first tool call is inspected.

  • Token limit: None

Evaluation criteria

Evaluation criterion Description Name matching The model-predicted tool call matches the reference tool call's name.

Metric input parameters

Input parameter Description prediction The candidate model output, which is a JSON serialized string that contains content and tool_calls keys. The content value is the text output from the model. The tool_call value is a JSON serialized string of a list of tool calls. Here is an example:{"content": "","tool_calls": [{"name": "book_tickets", "arguments": {"movie": "Mission Impossible Dead Reckoning Part 1", "theater":"Regal Edwards 14", "location": "Mountain View CA", "showtime": "7:30", "date": "2024-03-30","num_tix": "2"}}]} reference The ground-truth reference prediction, which follows the same format as the prediction.

Output scores

Value Description 0 Tool call name doesn't match the reference. 1 Tool call name matches the reference. Tool parameter key match

The tool_parameter_key_match metric describes the model's ability to predict a tool call with the correct parameter names.

  • Token limit: None

Evaluation criteria

Evaluation criterion Description Parameter matching ratio The ratio between the number of predicted parameters that match the parameter names of the reference tool call and the total number of parameters.

Metric input parameters

Input parameter Description prediction The candidate model output, which is a JSON serialized string that contains the content and tool_calls keys. The content value is the text output from the model. The tool_call value is a JSON serialized string of a list of tool calls. Here is an example:{"content": "", "tool_calls": [{"name": "book_tickets", "arguments": {"movie": "Mission Impossible Dead Reckoning Part 1", "theater":"Regal Edwards 14", "location": "Mountain View CA", "showtime": "7:30", "date": "2024-03-30","num_tix": "2"}}]} reference The ground-truth reference model prediction, which follows the same format as prediction.

Output scores

Value Description A float in the range of [0,1] The higher score of 1 means more parameters match the reference parameters' names. Tool parameter KV match

The tool_parameter_kv_match metric describes the model's ability to predict a tool call with the correct parameter names and key values.

  • Token limit: None

Evaluation criteria

Evaluation criterion Description Parameter matching ratio The ratio between the number of the predicted parameters that match both the parameter names and values of the reference tool call and the total number of parameters.

Metric input parameters

Input parameter Description prediction The candidate model output, which is a JSON serialized string that contains content and tool_calls keys. The content value is the text output from the model. The tool_call value is a JSON serialized string of a list of tool calls. Here is an example:{"content": "", "tool_calls": [{"name": "book_tickets", "arguments": {"movie": "Mission Impossible Dead Reckoning Part 1", "theater":"Regal Edwards 14", "location": "Mountain View CA", "showtime": "7:30", "date": "2024-03-30","num_tix": "2"}}]} reference The ground-truth reference prediction, which follows the same format as prediction.

Output scores

Value Description A float in the range of [0,1] The higher score of 1 means more parameters match the reference parameters' names and values.

docs.title: Baseline evaluation quality for generative tasks
docs.text: When evaluating the output of generative AI models, note that the evaluation process is inherently subjective, and the quality of evaluation can vary depending on the specific task and evaluation criteria. This subjectivity also applies to human evaluators. For more information about the challenges of achieving consistent evaluation for generative AI models, see Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena and Learning to summarize from human feedback.

docs.title: Evaluate a judge model
docs.text:
Preview

This product or feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA products and features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

For model-based metrics, the Generative AI evaluation service evaluates your models with a foundational model, such as Gemini, that has been configured and prompted as a judge model.

Using a judge model is a scalable and cost-effective alternative to human evaluation for large language models (LLMs). By default, the evaluation service uses a configured Gemini 1.0 Pro model with customizable prompts to assess your model's performance across various use cases.

This document is the first part of the Advanced judge model customization series, which provides tools to evaluate and configure the judge model for your specific needs.

  • 1. Evaluate a judge model (this page)
  • 2. Prompting for judge model customization
  • 3. Configure a judge model

For the basic evaluation workflow, see the Generative AI evaluation service quickstart.

This document describes the workflow for evaluating a customized judge model. The following diagram shows the high-level steps.

flowchart TD
    A["Prepare the evaluation dataset"] --> B["Review available metrics"]
    B --> C["Evaluate the judge model"]

    click A "#prepare-the-evaluation-dataset"
    click B "#available-metrics"
    click C "#example-evaluate-a-custom-fluency-metric"
Before you begin

Prepare the evaluation dataset

To evaluate model-based metrics, you need an evaluation dataset that includes human ratings as the ground truth. The goal is to compare the scores from the judge model with human ratings to determine if the judge model's quality is sufficient for your use case.

Your dataset must contain a ground truth column that corresponds to the metric you are evaluating:

  • For PointwiseMetric, add a {metric_name}/human_rating column.
  • For PairwiseMetric, add a {metric_name}/human_pairwise_choice column.

Dataset schema

Model-based metric Human rating column PointwiseMetric {metric_name}/human_rating PairwiseMetric {metric_name}/human_pairwise_choice Concepts
  • PointwiseMetric: Evaluates a single model's response on a numeric scale (e.g., rating fluency from 1 to 5).
  • PairwiseMetric: Compares the responses of two models (a candidate and a baseline) and indicates a preference (e.g., Model A is better, Model B is better, or it's a tie).
  • Confusion matrix: A table used to evaluate the performance of a classification model by showing the counts of true positive, true negative, false positive, and false negative predictions.
  • f1 score: The harmonic mean of precision and recall, providing a single score that balances both concerns.
Available metrics

The evaluation service provides different metrics depending on the number of possible outcomes (classes) for your PointwiseMetric or PairwiseMetric.

| Metric Type | Available Metrics ...| | 2-Class(e.g., PointwiseMetric with scores 0/1, or PairwiseMetric with choices A/B) | 2-class balanced accuracy2-class balanced f1 scoreConfusion matrix (to calculate TPR, TNR, FPR, FNR) | | Multi-Class(e.g., PointwiseMetric with scores 1-5, or PairwiseMetric with choices A/B/Tie) | Multiple-class balanced accuracyMultiple-class balanced f1 score - To calculate other metrics, you can use open-source libraries.

Metric calculation details

Formulas

  • 2-class balanced accuracy: ( (1/2)*(True Positive Rate + True Negative Rate) )
  • Multiple-class balanced accuracy: ( (1/n) *∑_{i=1...n}(recall(class_i)) )
  • 2-class / Multiple-class balanced f1 score: ( ∑_{i=0,1} (cnt_i/sum) * f1(class_i) )
    • Where ( f1 = 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall) )
    • ( precision = True Positives / (True Positives + False Positives) )
    • ( recall = True Positives / (True Positives + False Negatives) )
    • ( n ) : number of classes
    • ( cnt_i ) : number of ( class_i ) in ground truth data
    • ( sum ): number of elements in ground truth data

Confusion matrix example

The result fields confusion_matrix and confusion_matrix_labels can be used to build a confusion matrix. For example, the following result:

confusion_matrix = [[20, 31, 15],
                    [10, 11,  3],
                    [ 3,  2,  2]]
confusion_matrix_labels = ['BASELINE', 'CANDIDATE', 'TIE']

Translates to the following confusion matrix, where rows represent the predicted label and columns represent the true label:

             BASELINE |  CANDIDATE | TIE
   BASELINE.    20         31        15
   CANDIDATE.   10         11         3
   TIE.         3          2         2
Example: Evaluate a custom fluency metric

The following example shows how to update a model-based metric with a custom definition of fluency and then evaluate the quality of that metric against human ratings.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

from vertexai.preview.evaluation import (
   AutoraterConfig,
   PairwiseMetric,
)
from vertexai.preview.evaluation.autorater_utils import evaluate_autorater


# Step 1: Prepare the evaluation dataset with the human rating data column.
human_rated_dataset = pd.DataFrame({
  "prompt": [PROMPT_1, PROMPT_2],
    "response": [RESPONSE_1, RESPONSE_2],
  "baseline_model_response": [BASELINE_MODEL_RESPONSE_1, BASELINE_MODEL_RESPONSE_2],
    "pairwise_fluency/human_pairwise_choice": ["model_A", "model_B"]
})

# Step 2: Get the results from model-based metric
pairwise_fluency = PairwiseMetric(
    metric="pairwise_fluency",
    metric_prompt_template="please evaluate pairwise fluency..."
)

eval_result = EvalTask(
    dataset=human_rated_dataset,
    metrics=[pairwise_fluency],
).evaluate()

# Step 3: Calibrate model-based metric result and human preferences.
# eval_result contains human evaluation result from human_rated_dataset.
evaluate_autorater_result = evaluate_autorater(
  evaluate_autorater_input=eval_result.metrics_table,
  eval_metrics=[pairwise_fluency]
)
