docs.title: Vertex AI RAG Engine supported models
docs.text:
The Vertex AI RAG Engine is compatible with various models, including Google's Gemini models, self-deployed open models, and third-party models with managed APIs. This page provides a list of supported models and guidance on how to integrate them.

The VPC-SC security controls and CMEK are supported by Vertex AI RAG Engine. Data residency and AXT security controls aren't supported.

Concepts
  • Vertex AI RAG Engine: A service that grounds generative AI models to your specified data sources to provide more factual and relevant responses.
  • Self-deployed models: Custom models that you deploy on a Vertex AI endpoint, giving you full control over the model and its serving infrastructure.
  • Models with managed APIs: Third-party models, like those from Meta or Mistral, that are hosted and managed by Google, accessible via a simple API call without needing to manage infrastructure.
  • RAG corpus: A collection of documents that you provide to the RAG Engine for retrieval and grounding.

To help you choose the best model type for your use case, the following table compares the available options.

Model Type Description Key Characteristics Gemini models Google's family of multimodal models, natively integrated with Vertex AI. - State-of-the-art performance.- Tight integration with Google Cloud services.- Optimized for various tasks and scales. Self-deployed models Any open model from Model Garden or your own custom model deployed on a Vertex AI endpoint. - Maximum flexibility and control.- Requires managing your own endpoint.- Use any compatible model. Models with managed APIs Third-party models (e.g., Llama, Mistral) hosted and managed by Google on Vertex AI. - Serverless and easy to use.- Pay-as-you-go pricing.- No infrastructure management required.

docs.title: Gemini models
docs.text:
The following Gemini models and their versions support Vertex AI RAG Engine:

Preview

Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite is in Preview.

  • Gemini 2.5 Pro
  • Gemini 2.5 Flash
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash

docs.title: Use self-deployed or third-party models
docs.text:
You can use Vertex AI RAG Engine with your self-deployed open model endpoints or with third-party models available as managed APIs on Vertex AI.

Self-deployed modelsModels with managed APIs

Vertex AI RAG Engine supports all models in Model Garden that can be self-deployed. To use a self-deployed model, create a model instance pointing to your endpoint.

The following code sample shows how to create a model instance with your self-deployed open model endpoint.

# Create a model instance with your self-deployed open model endpoint
rag_model = GenerativeModel(
    "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/endpoints/ENDPOINT_ID",
    tools=[rag_retrieval_tool]
)

Replace the following variables:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your project ID.
  • LOCATION: The region to process your request.
  • ENDPOINT_ID: Your endpoint ID.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

The models with managed APIs on Vertex AI that support Vertex AI RAG Engine include the following:

  • Mistral on Vertex AI
  • Llama 3.1 and 3.2

You can interact with these models using either the Gemini GenerateContent API or the OpenAI-compatible ChatCompletions API.

Use the GenerateContent API

The following code sample demonstrates how to use the Gemini GenerateContent API to create a generative model instance. The model ID, /publisher/meta/models/llama-3.1-405B-instruct-maas, is found in the model card.

# Create a model instance with Llama 3.1 MaaS endpoint
rag_model = GenerativeModel(
    "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publisher/meta/models/llama-3.1-405B-instruct-maas",
    tools=RAG_RETRIEVAL_TOOL
)

Replace the following variables:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your project ID.
  • LOCATION: The region to process your request.
  • RAG_RETRIEVAL_TOOL: Your RAG retrieval tool.

Use the ChatCompletions API

The following code sample demonstrates how to use the OpenAI-compatible ChatCompletions API to generate a model response.

# Generate a response with Llama 3.1 MaaS endpoint
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="MODEL_ID",
    messages=[{"ROLE": "USER", "content": "CONTENT"}],
    extra_body={
        "extra_body": {
            "google": {
                "vertex_rag_store": {
                    "rag_resources": {
                        "rag_corpus": "RAG_CORPUS_ID"
                    },
                    "similarity_top_k": 10
                }
            }
        }
    },
)

Replace the following variables:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your project ID.
  • LOCATION: The region to process your request.
  • MODEL_ID: The LLM model for content generation (e.g., meta/llama-3.1-405b-instruct-maas).
  • RAG_CORPUS_ID: The ID of the RAG corpus resource.
  • ROLE: Your role (e.g., user).
  • CONTENT: The input prompt for the LLM, which should be relevant to the documents in Vertex AI Search.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Use data ingestion with Vertex AI RAG Engine
docs.text:
This page explains how to perform data ingestion into Vertex AI RAG Engine from a supported data source. You can import data from sources like Cloud Storage, Google Drive, Slack, Jira, or SharePoint using the ImportRagFiles API.

Note: Vertex AI RAG Engine supports VPC-SC security controls and CMEK. Data residency and AXT security controls are not supported.

docs.title: Compare data sources
docs.text:
Before you begin, determine the most suitable data source for your needs. The following table provides a comparison of the supported data sources.

Data Source Description & Use Case Key Requirements Local File Upload A synchronous, single-file upload for files up to 25 MB. Ideal for quick tests or ingesting individual documents. File size limit of 25 MB. Cloud Storage Asynchronously import one or more files from a Cloud Storage bucket. Best for batch processing large collections of documents already in Google Cloud. IAM permissions for the service account to read from the bucket. Google Drive Asynchronously import files from a Google Drive folder. Useful for ingesting documents managed and stored in Google Workspace. Share the Google Drive folder with the service account and grant Viewer permissions. Slack Import conversation histories from Slack channels using a data connector. Ideal for building a knowledge base from team communications. Slack app with correct permissions and an API token stored in Secret Manager. Jira Import issues and project data from Jira using a data connector. Useful for querying information about projects, tasks, and tickets. Jira API token and user email. Data is fetched using project names or JQL queries. SharePoint Import files from a SharePoint site. Best for ingesting documents from a Microsoft 365 environment. Azure app registration with appropriate API permissions and credentials.

For more information on file size limits and supported document types, see Supported document types.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Before you begin

Create a RAG corpus

All data must be imported into a RAG corpus. A corpus is a collection of RagFiles that your application can query. To create one, follow the instructions at Create a RAG corpus.

Concepts
  • RAG Corpus: A collection of documents or files that are indexed and optimized for retrieval-augmented generation searches.
  • API Token: A unique string of characters used to authenticate your identity and grant access to an API (e.g., from Slack or Jira).
  • Secret Manager: A secure Google Cloud service for storing and managing sensitive data like API keys, passwords, and certificates.
  • JQL (Jira Query Language): A powerful, text-based search language used in Jira to find issues based on specific criteria.
  • Service Account: A special type of Google account used by an application or a virtual machine (VM) instance, not a person.

Set up permissions

To import data, you must grant the correct permissions to the Vertex AI RAG Engine service account.

  • For Google Drive:

    1. Go to the IAM page of your Google Cloud project.
    2. Select Include Google-provided role grant.
    3. Search for the Vertex AI RAG Data Service Agent service account and copy the email address.
    4. In Google Drive, click Share on the folder or file you want to import.
    5. Paste the service account email and grant it Viewer permission.

  • For Slack, Jira, or SharePoint:

    1. Obtain the necessary API token or client secret from the source service.
    2. Store the token or secret in Google Cloud Secret Manager.
    3. Grant the Secret Manager Secret Accessor (roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor) role to your project's Vertex AI RAG Data Service Agent service account to allow it to access the secret.

docs.title: Import data from a supported source
docs.text:
Choose one of the following sources to import your data.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Cloud Storage or Google DriveSlackJiraSharePoint

You can import files from either Cloud Storage or Google Drive. The system automatically checks the file's path, filename, and content hash to prevent re-indexing unchanged files. If a file with the same name and path is updated, it will be re-indexed.

To import your files, use the code samples in the Import RagFiles API reference. Ensure you have completed the permission setup described in the Before you begin section.

To import files from Slack, follow these steps:

Step 1: Set up a Slack app
  1. Go to the Slack API page and create a new app.
  2. From the app's dashboard, navigate to Features > OAuth & Permissions.
  3. In the Scopes section, add the following Bot Token Scopes:
    • channels:history
    • groups:history
    • im:history
    • mpim:history
  4. Navigate to Settings > Install App and click Install to Workspace to install the app.
  5. After installation, copy the Bot User OAuth Token. This is your API token.
Step 2: Store the API token and grant access
  1. Add your API token to Secret Manager.
  2. Grant the Secret Manager Secret Accessor role to your project's Vertex AI RAG Data Service Agent service account. See Set up permissions for details.
Step 3: Import the data

Use the following code samples to import messages from your Slack channels. You will need your Slack channel ID, which can be found in the channel's URL or details pane.

View curl example 
API_KEY_SECRET_VERSION=SLACK_API_KEY_SECRET_VERSION
CHANNEL_ID=SLACK_CHANNEL_ID
PROJECT_ID=us-central1

curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://${ ENDPOINT }/v1beta1/projects/${ PROJECT_ID }/locations/${ PROJECT_ID }/ragCorpora/${ RAG_CORPUS_ID }/ragFiles:import \
-d '{
  "import_rag_files_config": {
    "slack_source": {
      "channels": [
        {
          "apiKeyConfig": {
            "apiKeySecretVersion": "'"${ API_KEY_SECRET_VERSION }"'"
          },
          "channels": [
            {
              "channel_id": "'"${ CHANNEL_ID }"'"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}'
View Python example

You can specify a time range by setting START_TIME and END_TIME.

# Slack example
start_time = protobuf.timestamp_pb2.Timestamp()
start_time.GetCurrentTime()
end_time = protobuf.timestamp_pb2.Timestamp()
end_time.GetCurrentTime()
source = rag.SlackChannelsSource(
    channels = [
        SlackChannel("CHANNEL1", "api_key1"),
        SlackChannel("CHANNEL2", "api_key2", START_TIME, END_TIME)
    ],
)

response = rag.import_files(
    corpus_name="projects/my-project/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/my-corpus-1",
    source=source,
    chunk_size=512,
    chunk_overlap=100,
)

To import data from Jira, follow these steps:

Step 1: Create a Jira API token
  1. Sign in to your Atlassian account.
  2. Navigate to Security > API tokens and click Create API token.
  3. Give the token a label and copy the generated token value.
Step 2: Store the API token and grant access
  1. Add your API token to Secret Manager.
  2. Grant the Secret Manager Secret Accessor role to your project's Vertex AI RAG Data Service Agent service account. See Set up permissions for details.
Step 3: Import the data

Use the following code samples to import data. You must provide your Atlassian email, your Jira server URI (e.g., your-org.atlassian.net), and either project names or custom JQL queries. For more on JQL, see Use advanced search with Jira Query Language (JQL).

View curl example 
EMAIL=JIRA_EMAIL
API_KEY_SECRET_VERSION=JIRA_API_KEY_SECRET_VERSION
SERVER_URI=JIRA_SERVER_URI
CUSTOM_QUERY=JIRA_CUSTOM_QUERY
PROJECT_ID=JIRA_PROJECT
REGION= "us-central1"

curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://${ ENDPOINT }/v1beta1/projects/${ PROJECT_ID }/locations/REGION>/ragCorpora/${ RAG_CORPUS_ID }/ragFiles:import \
-d '{
  "import_rag_files_config": {
    "jiraSource": {
      "jiraQueries": [{
        "projects": ["'"${ PROJECT_ID }"'"],
        "customQueries": ["'"${ CUSTOM_QUERY }"'"],
        "email": "'"${ EMAIL }"'",
        "serverUri": "'"${ SERVER_URI }"'",
        "apiKeyConfig": {
          "apiKeySecretVersion": "'"${ API_KEY_SECRET_VERSION }"'"
        }
      }]
    }
  }
}'
View Python example 
# Jira Example
jira_query = rag.JiraQuery(
    email="xxx@yyy.com",
    jira_projects=["project1", "project2"],
    custom_queries=["query1", "query2"],
    api_key="api_key",
    server_uri="server.atlassian.net"
)
source = rag.JiraSource(
    queries=[jira_query],
)

response = rag.import_files(
    corpus_name="projects/my-project/locations/REGION/ragCorpora/my-corpus-1",
    source=source,
    chunk_size=512,
    chunk_overlap=100,
)

To import files from your SharePoint site, follow these steps:

Step 1: Set up an Azure app
  1. In the Azure portal, go to App Registrations and create a new registration.
    • Provide a name for the application.
    • Choose the option, Accounts in this organizational directory only.
    • Leave the redirect URIs empty.
  2. From the app's Overview page, copy the Application (client) ID and the Directory (tenant) ID.
  3. Under Manage > API permissions, add the following permissions:
    • SharePoint: Sites.Read.All
    • Microsoft Graph: Files.Read.All and Sites.Read.All (instead of Browser SiteLists.Read.All)
    • Click Grant admin consent for your directory to apply the changes.
  4. Under Manage > Certificates & secrets, create a new client secret and copy its Value.
Step 2: Store the client secret and grant access
  1. Add the client secret's value to Secret Manager.
  2. Grant the Secret Manager Secret Accessor role to your project's Vertex AI RAG Data Service Agent service account. See Set up permissions for details.
Step 3: Import the data

Use the following code samples to import files. You must specify your SharePoint site name (e.g., your-org.sharepoint.com) and a drive name or ID. You can optionally specify a folder path or ID to limit the import scope.

View curl example 
CLIENT_ID=SHAREPOINT_CLIENT_ID
API_KEY_SECRET_VERSION=SHAREPOINT_API_KEY_SECRET_VERSION
TENANT_ID=SHAREPOINT_TENANT_ID
SITE_NAME=SHAREPOINT_SITE_NAME
FOLDER_PATH=SHAREPOINT_FOLDER_PATH
DRIVE_NAME=SHAREPOINT_DRIVE_NAME

curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://${ ENDPOINT }/v1beta1/projects/${ PROJECT_ID }/locations/REGION>/ragCorpora/${ RAG_CORPUS_ID }/ragFiles:import \
-d '{
  "import_rag_files_config": {
    "sharePointSources": {
      "sharePointSource": [{
        "clientId": "'"${ CLIENT_ID }"'",
        "apiKeyConfig": {
          "apiKeySecretVersion": "'"${ API_KEY_SECRET_VERSION }"'"
        },
        "tenantId": "'"${ TENANT_ID }"'",
        "sharepointSiteName": "'"${ SITE_NAME }"'",
        "sharepointFolderPath": "'"${ FOLDER_PATH }"'",
        "driveName": "'"${ DRIVE_NAME }"'"
      }]
    }
  }
}'
View Python example 
from vertexai.preview import rag
from vertexai.preview.rag.utils import resources

CLIENT_ID="SHAREPOINT_CLIENT_ID"
API_KEY_SECRET_VERSION="SHAREPOINT_API_KEY_SECRET_VERSION"
TENANT_ID="SHAREPOINT_TENANT_ID"
SITE_NAME="SHAREPOINT_SITE_NAME"
FOLDER_PATH="SHAREPOINT_FOLDER_PATH"
DRIVE_NAME="SHAREPOINT_DRIVE_NAME"

# SharePoint Example.
source = resources.SharePointSources(
    share_point_sources=[
        resources.SharePointSource(
            client_id=CLIENT_ID,
            client_secret=API_KEY_SECRET_VERSION,
            tenant_id=TENANT_ID,
            sharepoint_site_name=SITE_NAME,
            folder_path=FOLDER_PATH,
            drive_id=DRIVE_ID,
        )
    ]
)

response = rag.import_files(
    corpus_name="projects/my-project/locations/REGION/ragCorpora/my-corpus-1",
    source=source,
    chunk_size=512,
    chunk_overlap=100,
)

docs.title: Data deduplication
docs.text:
RAG Engine avoids re-processing unchanged files. If you import the same file multiple times without any modifications to its content or the chunking configuration, the file is skipped. The response.skipped_rag_files_count in the API response indicates how many files were skipped for this reason.

A file is skipped if all of the following conditions are met:

  • The file has been imported previously.
  • The file content has not changed.
  • The chunking configuration for the file has not changed.

docs.title: Import failures and logging
docs.text:
To understand the outcome of an import job, you can inspect the API response or configure a data sink to log detailed results.

  • Response Metadata: The response.metadata object in the SDK response contains high-level information about the import job, including request and response times.

  • Import Result Sink: For detailed, file-level logging, you can specify an import_result_sink in your import request. This is an optional parameter that designates a destination for logging the status of each imported file. This makes it easier to identify which files failed to import and why.

    The sink can be a Cloud Storage path or a BigQuery table: * Cloud Storage: Provide a path like gs://my-bucket/my/object.ndjson. The object must not exist before the import. After the job completes, this object will contain one JSON object per line, detailing the status of each file. * BigQuery: Provide a table reference like bq://my-project.my-dataset.my-table. If the table does not exist, it will be created. If it exists, its schema will be verified.

docs.title: Use embedding models with Vertex AI RAG Engine
docs.text:
Preview

The VPC-SC security controls and CMEK are supported by Vertex AI RAG Engine. Data residency and AXT security controls aren't supported.

This page describes the available embedding models and shows you how to use your chosen model to create a RAG corpus. The association between an embedding model and a RAG corpus is fixed for the lifetime of the corpus.

docs.title: Introduction to embeddings
docs.text:
Embeddings are numerical representations of data, such as text, images, or video. They are essential for applications that need to understand complex meanings and semantic relationships in data.

Embeddings work by converting inputs into arrays of floating-point numbers called vectors. These vectors are designed so that the distance between them in a multi-dimensional "embedding space" corresponds to the semantic similarity of the original inputs.

For example, the phrases "I want a puppy" and "I would like to get a dog" would be mapped to vectors that are very close to each other, while the phrase "I need to fix my car" would be mapped to a vector that is much farther away.

Embedding models are a critical component of semantic retrieval systems like RAG Engine. The performance of the retrieval system depends on how effectively the embedding model captures the meaningful relationships within your data.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Embedding model: A model that converts data (like text) into numerical vector representations.
  • RAG corpus: A collection of documents that the RAG Engine can search to find relevant information for answering queries.
  • Dense embedding vector: A vector where most values are non-zero, capturing nuanced semantic meaning, unlike sparse vectors which primarily map words to numbers.
  • Fine-tuning: The process of further training a pre-trained model on a smaller, domain-specific dataset to improve its performance on specialized tasks.
  • Semantic retrieval: A search method that finds documents based on their meaning and contextual relevance to a query, rather than just keyword matching.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
The following diagram shows the workflow for using an embedding model with RAG Engine.

flowchart LR
    A[Choose an embedding model] --> B[Create a RAG corpus]

    click A "#embedding-model-choices"
    click B "#create-a-rag-corpus-with-an-embedding-model"

docs.title: Embedding model choices
docs.text:
Vertex AI RAG Engine offers several types of embedding models. The following table provides a comparison to help you select the best option for your use case.

Model Type Description Pros Cons Best for Vertex AI text embedding models Models trained and managed by Google on a large, general-purpose dataset. - No deployment required.- Strong baseline performance.- Easy to use. - Subject to model discontinuation policies.- Not customizable for specific domains. General-purpose applications where quick setup and strong out-of-the-box performance are key. Fine-tuned Vertex AI models Vertex AI models that you have fine-tuned with your own data. - Specialized knowledge and tailored performance.- You own the resulting model image.- Unaffected by publisher model deprecation. - Requires a tuning dataset.- Requires deployment to a Vertex AI endpoint, incurring costs. Applications requiring specialized domain knowledge or highly-tailored performance. Open source (OSS) models Third-party open-source embedding models available in Model Garden. - Access to a wide variety of model architectures.- You control the model lifecycle. - Requires deployment and management.- Performance can vary; requires evaluation. Users who want to experiment with different model architectures or have specific requirements met by an OSS model.

docs.title: Create a RAG corpus with an embedding model
docs.text:
After choosing a model type, you can create a RAG corpus. The following examples show how to create a corpus for each model type.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Vertex AI text embedding modelsFine-tuned Vertex AI text embedding modelsOpen source (OSS) embedding models

The Vertex AI text embedding API uses the Gecko embedding models, which produce a dense embedding vector with 768 dimensions. These models are available in English-only and multilingual versions. Because they don't need to be deployed, they are a simple and effective choice for many RAG applications.

Supported Gecko models

The following publisher models are recommended for use with a RAG corpus:

Model version Description text-embedding-005 Default embedding model. Recommended for use with a RAG corpus. text-embedding-004 text-multilingual-embedding-002 Recommended for use with a RAG corpus.

Note on model discontinuation

Publisher Gecko models might be discontinued. If a model you are using is discontinued, it can no longer be used with Vertex AI RAG Engine. You must migrate the RAG corpus by creating a new one with a supported model and re-importing your data. To avoid this, you can use a fine-tuned or self-deployed OSS model.

The following code samples demonstrate how to create a RAG corpus with a publisher Gecko model.

cURLVertex AI SDK for Python 
ENDPOINT=us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com
PROJECT_ID=YOUR_PROJECT_ID

// Set this to your choice of publisher Gecko model. Note that the full resource name of the publisher model is required.
// Example: projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/text-embedding-004
PUBLISHER_MODEL=YOUR_PUBLISHER_MODEL

// Set a display name for your corpus.
// For example, "my test corpus"
CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME=YOUR_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME

// CreateRagCorpus
// Input: ENDPOINT, PROJECT_ID, PUBLISHER_MODEL, CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME
curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://${ENDPOINT}/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora \
-d '{
      "display_name" : '\""${CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME}"\"',
      "rag_embedding_model_config" : {
            "publisher_model": '\""${PUBLISHER_MODEL}"\"'
      }
}'

import vertexai
from vertexai import rag

# Set Project
PROJECT_ID = "YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

# Configure a Google first-party embedding model
# Example: "publishers/google/models/text-embedding-004"
embedding_model_config = rag.RagEmbeddingModelConfig(
      publisher_model="YOUR_PUBLISHER_MODEL"
)

# Name your corpus
DISPLAY_NAME = "YOUR_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME"

rag_corpus = rag.create_corpus(
      display_name=DISPLAY_NAME, rag_embedding_model_config=embedding_model_config
)

While foundation models provide a strong baseline, you can fine-tune them on your own data to specialize their knowledge. This creates a new model image that you own, which is not affected by Gecko model deprecation. All fine-tuned Gecko embedding models produce embeddings with 768-dimensional vectors.

For more information, see Tune text embeddings.

Before creating the corpus, you must deploy your fine-tuned model to a Vertex AI endpoint. The following code samples demonstrate how to create a RAG corpus with a deployed, fine-tuned model.

cURLVertex AI SDK for Python 
ENDPOINT=us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com
PROJECT_ID=YOUR_PROJECT_ID

// Your Vertex AI endpoint resource with the deployed fine-tuned Gecko model
// Example: projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/${LOCATION}/endpoints/${ENDPOINT_ID}
ENDPOINT_NAME=YOUR_ENDPOINT_NAME

// Set a display name for your corpus.
// For example, "my test corpus"
CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME=YOUR_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME

// CreateRagCorpus
// Input: ENDPOINT, PROJECT_ID, ENDPOINT_NAME, CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME
curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \

docs.title: Use Vertex AI Feature Store in Vertex AI RAG Engine
docs.text:
Preview

Some of the RAG features are Preview offerings, subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" of the Google Cloud Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA products and features may have limited support, and changes to Pre-GA products and features may not be compatible with other Pre-GA versions. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions. Further, by using the Gemini API on Vertex AI, you agree to the Generative AI Preview terms and conditions (Preview Terms).

The VPC-SC security controls and CMEK are supported by Vertex AI RAG Engine. Data residency and AXT security controls aren't supported.

This page shows you how to set up Vertex AI Feature Store as the vector database to use with RAG Engine. By integrating Vertex AI Feature Store, RAG Engine can handle large data volumes with low latency, which helps to improve the performance and scalability of your RAG applications.

To see a complete example, you can run the "Vertex AI RAG Engine with Vertex AI Feature Store" Jupyter notebook.

Open in Colab Open in Colab Enterprise Open in Vertex AI Workbench View on GitHub

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Vertex AI Feature Store: A managed cloud-native service that simplifies machine learning (ML) feature management and online serving.
  • FeatureOnlineStore: A Feature Store resource that serves feature data with low latency for online applications.
  • FeatureView: A resource that connects a data source, like a BigQuery table, to a FeatureOnlineStore for serving.
  • RAG Corpus: A collection of documents or data that the RAG system uses to find relevant information for answering queries.
  • Embeddings: Numerical vector representations of text or other data, used to measure semantic similarity.

docs.title: Set up a Vertex AI Feature Store
docs.text:
Vertex AI Feature Store lets you manage feature data within a BigQuery table or view, enabling low-latency online feature serving. For FeatureOnlineStore instances created with optimized online serving, you can use vector similarity search to retrieve approximate nearest neighbors.

The following sections show you how to set up a Vertex AI Feature Store instance for your RAG application.

Step 1: Create a BigQuery table schema

Use the Google Cloud console or bq command-line tool to create a BigQuery table. It must contain the following fields to serve as the data source.

Field name Data type Status corpus_id String Required file_id String Required chunk_id String Required chunk_data_type String Nullable chunk_data String Nullable file_original_uri String Nullable embeddings Float Repeated

The following code sample demonstrates how to define your BigQuery table schema using SQL.

SQL 
CREATE TABLE `PROJECT_ID.input_us_central1.rag_source_new` (
  `corpus_id` STRING NOT NULL,
  `file_id` STRING NOT NULL,
  `chunk_id` STRING NOT NULL,
  `chunk_data_type` STRING,
  `chunk_data` STRING,
  `embeddings` ARRAY<FLOAT64>,
  `file_original_uri` STRING
);
Step 2: Provision a FeatureOnlineStore instance

To enable online serving of features, use the Vertex AI Feature Store CreateFeatureOnlineStore API to set up a FeatureOnlineStore instance. If you are provisioning a FeatureOnlineStore for the first time, the operation might take approximately five minutes to complete.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

RESTVertex AI SDK for Python

To create an online store instance, send a POST request by using the featureOnlineStores.create method.

Before you begin

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • LOCATION_ID: Region where you want to create the FeatureOnlineStore instance, such as us-central1.
  • PROJECT_ID: Your project ID.
  • FEATUREONLINESTORE_NAME: The name of the new FeatureOnlineStore instance.

Request

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION_ID-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION_ID/featureOnlineStores?feature_online_store_id=FEATUREONLINESTORE_NAME

Request JSON body:

{
  "optimized": {}
}

To send your request, choose one of these options:

cURLPowerShell

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d @request.json \
     "https://LOCATION_ID-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION_ID/featureOnlineStores?feature_online_store_id=FEATUREONLINESTORE_NAME"

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method POST `
    -Headers $headers `
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `
    -InFile request.json `
    -Uri "https://LOCATION_ID-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION_ID/featureOnlineStores?feature_online_store_id=FEATUREONLINESTORE_NAME" | Select-Object -Expand Content

You should receive a JSON response similar to the following:

{
  "name": "projects/PROJECT_NUMBER/locations/LOCATION_ID/featureOnlineStores/FEATUREONLINESTORE_NAME/operations/OPERATION_ID",
  "metadata": {
    "@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.CreateFeatureOnlineStoreOperationMetadata",
    "genericMetadata": {
      "createTime": "2023-09-18T17:49:23.847496Z",
      "updateTime": "2023-09-18T17:49:23.847496Z"
    }
  }
}

To learn how to install or update the Vertex AI SDK for Python, see Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python. For more information, see the Vertex AI SDK for Python API reference documentation.

from google.cloud import aiplatform
from vertexai.resources.preview import feature_store


def create_optimized_public_feature_online_store_sample(
    project: str,
    location: str,
    feature_online_store_id: str,
):
    aiplatform.init(project=project, location=location)
    fos = feature_store.FeatureOnlineStore.create_optimized_store(
        feature_online_store_id
    )
    return fos
  • project: Your project ID.
  • location: Region where you want to create the FeatureOnlineStore instance, such as us-central1.
  • feature_online_store_id: The name of the new FeatureOnlineStore instance.
Step 3: Create a FeatureView resource

To connect the BigQuery table to the FeatureOnlineStore instance, call the CreateFeatureView API. When you create a FeatureView, choose the default distance metric DOT_PRODUCT_DISTANCE, which is defined as the negative of the dot product (a smaller DOT_PRODUCT_DISTANCE indicates higher similarity).

RESTVertex AI SDK for Python 
# TODO(developer): Update and uncomment the following lines:
# Set feature_view_id
# Example: "feature_view_test"
# FEATURE_VIEW_ID = "your-feature-view-id"
#
# The big_query_uri generated in the above BigQuery table schema creation step
# The format should be "bq://" + BigQuery table ID
# Example: "bq://tester.ragtest1.rag_testdata"
# BIG_QUERY_URI=YOUR_BIG_QUERY_URI

# Call CreateFeatureView API to create a FeatureView
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/featureOnlineStores/${FEATURE_ONLINE_STORE_ID}/featureViews?feature_view_id=${FEATURE_VIEW_ID} \
  -d '{
        "vertex_rag_source": {
          "uri": '\""${BIG_QUERY_URI}"\"'
        }
    }'

# Call ListFeatureViews API to verify the FeatureView is created successfully
curl -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/featureOnlineStores/${FEATURE_ONLINE_STORE_ID}/featureViews

To learn how to install or update the Vertex AI SDK for Python, see Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python. For more information, see the Vertex AI SDK for Python API reference documentation.

from google.cloud import aiplatform
from vertexai.resources.preview import feature_store


def create_feature_view_from_rag_source(
    project: str,
    location: str,
    existing_feature_online_store_id: str,
    feature_view_id: str,
    bq_table_uri: str,
):
    aiplatform.init(project=project, location=location)
    fos = feature_store.FeatureOnlineStore(existing_feature_online_store_id)
    fv = fos.create_feature_view(
        name=feature_view_id,
        source=feature_store.utils.FeatureViewVertexRagSource(uri=bq_table_uri),
    )
    return fv

docs.title: Use Vertex AI Feature Store in RAG Engine
docs.text:
After the Vertex AI Feature Store instance is set up, the following sections show you how to use it as the vector database for your RAG application.

Step 4: Create a RAG corpus

To create the RAG corpus, you must provide the FEATURE_VIEW_RESOURCE_NAME. The RAG corpus is created and automatically associated with the Vertex AI Feature Store instance. RAG APIs use the generated rag_corpus_id to handle data uploads and retrieve relevant contexts.

RESTVertex AI SDK for Python 
# TODO(developer): Update and uncomment the following lines:
# CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME = "your-corpus-display-name"
#
# Full feature view resource name
# Format: projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/featureOnlineStores/${FEATURE_ONLINE_STORE_ID}/featureViews/${FEATURE_VIEW_ID}
# FEATURE_VIEW_RESOURCE_NAME = "your-feature-view-resource-name"

# Call CreateRagCorpus API to create a new RAG corpus
curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora -d '{
    "display_name" : '\""${CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME}"\"',
    "rag_vector_db_config" : {
      "vertex_feature_store": {
        "feature_view_resource_name":'\""${FEATURE_VIEW_RESOURCE_NAME}"\"'
      }
    }
  }'

# Call ListRagCorpora API to verify the RAG corpus is created successfully
curl -sS -X GET \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
"https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora"

To learn how to install or update the Vertex AI SDK for Python, see Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python. For more information, see the Vertex AI SDK for Python API reference documentation.

from vertexai.preview import rag
import vertexai

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# feature_view_name = "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/{LOCATION}/featureOnlineStores/{FEATURE_ONLINE_STORE_ID}/featureViews/{FEATURE_VIEW_ID}"
# display_name = "test_corpus"
# description = "Corpus Description"

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

# Configure embedding model (Optional)
embedding_model_config = rag.EmbeddingModelConfig(
    publisher_model="publishers/google/models/text-embedding-004"
)

# Configure Vector DB
vector_db = rag.VertexFeatureStore(resource_name=feature_view_name)

corpus = rag.create_corpus(
    display_name=display_name,
    description=description,
    embedding_model_config=embedding_model_config,
    vector_db=vector_db,
)
print(corpus)
# Example response:
# RagCorpus(name='projects/1234567890/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/1234567890',
# display_name='test_corpus', description='Corpus Description', embedding_model_config=...
# ...
Step 5: Import files into the BigQuery table

Use the ImportRagFiles API to import files from Google Cloud Storage or Google Drive into the BigQuery table of the Vertex AI Feature Store instance. The files are embedded and stored in the BigQuery table.

RESTVertex AI SDK for Python 
# TODO(developer): Update and uncomment the following lines:
# RAG_CORPUS_ID = "your-rag-corpus-id"
#
# Google Cloud Storage bucket/file location.
# For example, "gs://rag-fos-test/"
# GCS_URIS= "your-gcs-uris"

# Call ImportRagFiles API to embed files and store in the BigQuery table
curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/${RAG_CORPUS_ID}/ragFiles:import \
-d '{
  "import_rag_files_config": {
    "gcs_source": {
      "uris": '\""${GCS_URIS}"\"'
    },
    "rag_file_chunking_config": {
      "chunk_size": 512
    }
  }
}'

# Call ListRagFiles API to verify the files are imported successfully
curl -X GET \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/${RAG_CORPUS_ID}/ragFiles

To learn how to install or update the Vertex AI SDK for Python, see Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python. For more information, see the Vertex AI SDK for Python API reference documentation.

from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# corpus_name = "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/{rag_corpus_id}"
# paths = ["https://drive.google.com/file/123", "gs://my_bucket/my_files_dir"]  # Supports Google Cloud Storage and Google Drive Links

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

response = rag.import_files(
    corpus_name=corpus_name,
    paths=paths,
    transformation_config=rag.TransformationConfig(
        rag.ChunkingConfig(chunk_size=512, chunk_overlap=100)
    ),
    import_result_sink="gs://sample-existing-folder/sample_import_result_unique.ndjson",  # Optional, this has to be an existing storage bucket folder, and file name has to be unique (non-existent).
    max_embedding_requests_per_min=900,  # Optional
)
print(f"Imported {response.imported_rag_files_count} files.")
# Example response:
# Imported 2 files.
Step 6: Synchronize the FeatureOnlineStore index

After uploading your data into the BigQuery table, run a synchronization process to make your data available for online serving. This process constructs a FeatureOnlineStore index using the FeatureView and might take 20 minutes to complete.

REST

Before you begin

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • LOCATION_ID: Region where the online store is located, such as us-central1.
  • PROJECT_ID: Your project ID.
  • FEATUREONLINESTORE_NAME: The name of the online store containing the feature view.
  • FEATUREVIEW_NAME: The name of the feature view where you want to manually start the data sync.

Request

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION_ID-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION_ID/featureOnlineStores/FEATUREONLINESTORE_NAME/featureViews/FEATUREVIEW_NAME:sync

To send your request, choose one of these options:

cURLPowerShell

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Execute the following command:

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d "" \
     "https://LOCATION_ID-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION_ID/featureOnlineStores/FEATUREONLINESTORE_NAME/featureViews/FEATUREVIEW_NAME:sync"

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method POST `
    -Headers $headers `
    -Uri "https://LOCATION_ID-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION_ID/featureOnlineStores/FEATUREONLINESTORE_NAME/featureViews/FEATUREVIEW_NAME:sync" | Select-Object -Expand Content

You should receive a JSON response similar to the following:

{
  "featureViewSync": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION_ID/featureOnlineStores/FEATUREONLINESTORE_NAME/featureViews/FEATUREVIEW_NAME/featureViewSyncs/OPERATION_ID"
}
Step 7: Retrieve relevant contexts

After the synchronization process completes, you can retrieve relevant contexts from the FeatureOnlineStore index through the RetrieveContexts API.

RESTVertex AI SDK for Python

  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1:retrieveContexts \
  -d '{
    "vertex_rag_store": {
      "rag_resources": {
          "rag_corpus": '\""${RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE}"\"',
        },
    },
    "query": {
      "text": '\""${RETRIEVAL_QUERY}"\"',
      "similarity_top_k": 10
    }
  }'

import vertexai

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines

response = rag.retrieval_query(

Call the Vertex AI GenerateContent API to use Gemini models to generate content. Specify RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE in the request to retrieve data from the FeatureOnlineStore index.

-H "Content-Type: application/json"  https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/${MODEL_ID}:generateContent \
-d '{

    "role": "user",
    "parts": {
      "text": '\""${GENERATE_CONTENT_PROMPT}"\"'
    }
  },
  "tools": {
    "retrieval": {
      "vertex_rag_store": {
        "rag_resources": {
            "rag_corpus": '\""${RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE}"\"',
          },
        "similarity_top_k": 8,
      }
    }
  }
}'

To learn how to install or update the Vertex AI SDK for Python, see Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python. For more information, see the Vertex AI SDK for Python API reference documentation.

from vertexai import rag
from vertexai.generative_models import GenerativeModel, Tool
import vertexai

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# corpus_name = "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/{rag_corpus_id}"

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

rag_retrieval_tool = Tool.from_retrieval(
    retrieval=rag.Retrieval(
        source=rag.VertexRagStore(
            rag_resources=[
                rag.RagResource(
                    rag_corpus=corpus_name,
                    # Optional: supply IDs from `rag.list_files()`.
                    # rag_file_ids=["rag-file-1", "rag-file-2", ...],
                )
            ],
            rag_retrieval_config=rag.RagRetrievalConfig(
                top_k=10,
                filter=rag.utils.resources.Filter(vector_distance_threshold=0.5),
            ),
        ),
    )
)

rag_model = GenerativeModel(
    model_name="gemini-2.0-flash-001", tools=[rag_retrieval_tool]
)
response = rag_model.generate_content("Why is the sky blue?")
print(response.text)
# Example response:
#   The sky appears blue due to a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering.
#   Sunlight, which contains all colors of the rainbow, is scattered
#   by the tiny particles in the Earth's atmosphere....

docs.title: Use Pinecone with Vertex AI RAG Engine
docs.text:
Preview

The VPC-SC security controls and CMEK are supported by Vertex AI RAG Engine. Data residency and AXT security controls aren't supported.

This page shows you how to connect Vertex AI RAG Engine to your existing Pinecone database. By using your own Pinecone instance, you can leverage its vector search capabilities for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) while maintaining control over your vector database environment.

A similarity search finds text that is semantically similar to a given query, which requires an embedding model to generate vector representations of the text. This search is used to retrieve relevant contexts for grounding, which helps the LLM return more accurate and factual responses.

With this integration, you continue to manage your Pinecone vector database, including provisioning and scaling, while Vertex AI RAG Engine uses it for storage, indexing, and search.

To see a complete example, you can run the "RAG Engine with Pinecone" Jupyter notebook in one of the following environments:

Open in Colab Open in Colab Enterprise Open in Vertex AI Workbench View on GitHub

This tutorial outlines the steps to connect your Pinecone database to RAG Engine.

flowchart TD
    A[Step 1: Create your Pinecone index] --> B[Step 2: Create and store your Pinecone API key];
    B --> C[Step 3: Provision the RAG Engine service account];
    C --> D[Step 4: Create a RAG corpus with a Pinecone index];

    click A "#step-1-create-your-pinecone-index"
    click B "#step-2-create-and-store-your-pinecone-api-key"
    click C "#step-3-provision-the-rag-engine-service-account"
    click D "#create-a-rag-corpus-with-a-pinecone-index"

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation): A technique to enhance LLM responses by retrieving relevant information from an external knowledge base.
  • Pinecone: A managed vector database service for storing and searching high-dimensional vector embeddings.
  • Vector Embedding: A numerical representation of text or other data in a high-dimensional space, capturing its semantic meaning.
  • RAG Corpus: A collection of documents within RAG Engine that are indexed for retrieval.
  • Secret Manager: A Google Cloud service for securely storing and managing secrets like API keys, passwords, and certificates.
Prerequisites

Step 1: Create your Pinecone index

First, create a Pinecone index configured to be compatible with RAG Engine.

  1. Follow the Pinecone quickstart guide to understand the basic index configuration.
  2. To reduce latency and meet data residency requirements, create your Pinecone index in a location that is the same as or geographically close to where you use Vertex AI RAG Engine.

  3. When creating the index, specify the embedding dimension that matches the embedding model you will use with RAG Engine.

    Model Dimension size First-party Gecko 768 Fine-tuned first-party Gecko 768 E5 See Use OSS embedding models.

  4. Choose one of the following supported distance metrics:

    • cosine
    • dotproduct
    • euclidean
  5. Optional: If you create a pod-based index, you must specify file_id on the pod.metadata_config.indexed field. For more information, see Selective metadata indexing.

Step 2: Create and store your Pinecone API key

RAG Engine authenticates to your Pinecone index using an API key. You must create this key in Pinecone and store it securely in Google Cloud's Secret Manager.

  1. Create the API key: Follow the Pinecone authentication guide to create an API key in your Pinecone project.
  2. Store the API key in Secret Manager:
    • Go to the Secret Manager page in the Google Cloud console and create a new secret containing your Pinecone API key.
    • Grant your project's RAG Engine service account access to this secret.
      1. Navigate to your project's IAM page.
      2. Enable the option Include Google-provided role grants.
      3. Find the service account with the format: service-{project-number}@gcp-sa-vertex-rag.iam.gserviceaccount.com.
      4. Edit the service account's principals and add the Secret Manager Secret Accessor role.

Step 3: Provision the RAG Engine service account

When you create the first RAG corpus in your project, Vertex AI RAG Engine automatically provisions a dedicated service account. You can find this service account on your project's Identity and Access Management page.

The service account follows this format: service-{project-number}@gcp-sa-vertex-rag.iam.gserviceaccount.com

For example: service-123456789@gcp-sa-vertex-rag.iam.gserviceaccount.com

Considerations for using Pinecone

Review the following points to determine if using a self-managed Pinecone database is the best choice for your RAG application.

  • Management Overhead: You are responsible for creating, configuring, and managing the scaling of your Pinecone database instance.
  • Namespace Usage: Vertex AI RAG Engine uses the default namespace on your index. Ensure that this namespace is not modified by other processes.
  • API Key Management: You must provide a Pinecone API key stored in Secret Manager. RAG Engine accesses the secret resource using your service account during interactions with the corpus.
  • Corpus-Index Mapping: Each RAG corpus has a one-to-one mapping with a Pinecone index. This association is permanent and is made during the CreateRagCorpus or UpdateRagCorpus API call.

The primary difference between using Pinecone and Vertex AI Vector Search is the management model:

Feature Pinecone Vertex AI Vector Search Management Self-managed (you provision, scale, and configure) Google-managed (fully integrated and automated) Setup Requires manual index creation and API key management Simplified setup within Google Cloud Control Full control over the database environment Managed by Google Cloud, less operational overhead

docs.title: Create a RAG corpus with a Pinecone index
docs.text:
After completing the prerequisites, you can create a RAG corpus and associate it with your Pinecone index. The association is defined by setting the following fields on the RAG corpus:

  • rag_vector_db_config.pinecone: Specifies Pinecone as the vector database. If not set, the default RagManagedDb (Vertex AI Vector Search) is used.
  • rag_vector_db_config.pinecone.index_name: The name of your Pinecone index.
  • rag_vector_db_config.api_auth.api_key_config.api_key_secret_version: The full resource name of the secret in Secret Manager containing your Pinecone API key. The format is projects/{PROJECT_NUMBER}/secrets/{SECRET_ID}/versions/{VERSION_ID}.

You can provide these details when you create the corpus or add them later.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Create a RAG corpus Method 1: Create a corpus with full Pinecone detailsMethod 2: Create a corpus and add Pinecone details later

If you have your Pinecone index name and the Secret Manager resource name ready, you can create the RAG corpus and associate it in a single step.

Python

Before trying this sample, follow the Python setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Python API reference documentation.

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# pinecone_index_name = "pinecone-index-name"
# pinecone_api_key_secret_manager_version = "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/secrets/{SECRET_NAME}/versions/latest"
# display_name = "test_corpus"
# description = "Corpus Description"

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

# Configure embedding model (Optional)
embedding_model_config = rag.RagEmbeddingModelConfig(
    vertex_prediction_endpoint=rag.VertexPredictionEndpoint(
        publisher_model="publishers/google/models/text-embedding-005"
    )
)

# Configure Vector DB
vector_db = rag.Pinecone(
    index_name=pinecone_index_name,
    api_key=pinecone_api_key_secret_manager_version,
)

corpus = rag.create_corpus(
    display_name=display_name,
    description=description,
    backend_config=rag.RagVectorDbConfig(
        rag_embedding_model_config=embedding_model_config,
        vector_db=vector_db,
    ),
)
print(corpus)
# Example response:
# RagCorpus(name='projects/1234567890/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/1234567890',
# display_name='test_corpus', description='Corpus Description', embedding_model_config=...
# ...

REST

# Set your project ID under which you want to create the corpus
PROJECT_ID="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"

# Choose a display name for your corpus
CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME="YOUR_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME"

# Set your Pinecone index name
PINECONE_INDEX_NAME="YOUR_INDEX_NAME"

# Set the full resource name of your secret. Follows the format
# projects/{PROJECT_NUMER}/secrets/{SECRET_ID}/versions/{VERSION_ID}
SECRET_RESOURCE_NAME="YOUR_SECRET_RESOURCE_NAME"

# Call CreateRagCorpus API with all the Vector DB information.
# You can also add the embedding model choice or set other RAG corpus parameters on
# this call per your choice.
curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora -d '{
      "display_name" : '\""${CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME}"\"',
      "rag_vector_db_config" : {
         "pinecone": {"index_name": '\""${PINECONE_INDEX_NAME}"\"'},
         "api_auth": {"api_key_config":
               {"api_key_secret_version": '\""${SECRET_RESOURCE_NAME}"\"'}
         }
      }
   }'

# To poll the status of your RAG corpus creation, get the operation_id returned in
# response of your CreateRagCorpus call.
OPERATION_ID="YOUR_OPERATION_ID"

# Poll Operation status until done = true in the response.
# The response to this call will contain the ID for your created RAG corpus
curl -X GET \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/operations/${OPERATION_ID}

If you have not yet provisioned your Pinecone index or set up your API key in Secret Manager, you can create the RAG corpus first and update it with the Pinecone details later.

  • When you create a corpus without the index name and API key, you cannot import files into it.
  • Once you choose Pinecone as the vector database, this choice cannot be changed.

Python

import vertexai
from vertexai.preview import rag

# Set Project
PROJECT_ID = "YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

# Configure the Pinecone vector DB information
vector_db = rag.Pinecone()

# Name your corpus
DISPLAY_NAME = "YOUR_CORPUS_NAME"

rag_corpus = rag.create_corpus(display_name=DISPLAY_NAME, vector_db=vector_db)

REST

# Set your project ID under which you want to create the corpus
PROJECT_ID = "YOUR_PROJECT_ID"

# Choose a display name for your corpus
CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME="YOUR_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME"

# Call CreateRagCorpus API with all the Vector DB information.
# You can also add the embedding model choice or set other RAG corpus parameters on
# this call per your choice.
curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora -d '{
      "display_name" : '\""${CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME}"\"',
      "rag_vector_db_config" : {
         "pinecone": {}
      }
   }'

# To poll the status of your RAG corpus creation, get the operation_id returned in
# response of your CreateRagCorpus call.
OPERATION_ID="YOUR_OPERATION_ID"

# Poll Operation status until done = true in the response.
# The response to this call will contain the ID for your created RAG corpus
curl -X GET \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/operations/${OPERATION_ID}

docs.title: Update your RAG corpus
docs.text:
Update a RAG corpus

You can use the UpdateRagCorpus API to add or change the vector database configuration. If the Pinecone index name and API key secret were not set during creation, you can add them with this API.

The following table describes the mutability of the configuration fields.

Field Mutability Required or Optional rag_vector_db_config.vector_db Immutable after a choice is made. Required rag_vector_db_config.pinecone.index_name Immutable after it is set. Required rag_vector_db_config.api_auth.api_key_config.api_key_secret_version Mutable. You can update the key, but you cannot remove it once set. Optional

Python

import vertexai
from vertexai.preview import rag

# Set Project
PROJECT_ID = "YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

# Configure the Pinecone vector DB information
vector_db = rag.Pinecone(index_name=)

# Name your corpus
DISPLAY_NAME = "YOUR_CORPUS_NAME"

rag_corpus = rag.create_corpus(display_name=DISPLAY_NAME, vector_db=vector_db)

PROJECT_ID = "YOUR_PROJECT_ID"

# Set your Pinecone index name
PINECONE_INDEX_NAME="YOUR_INDEX_NAME"

# projects/{PROJECT_NUMER}/secrets/{SECRET_ID}/versions/{VERSION_ID}
SECRET_RESOURCE_NAME="YOUR_SECRET_RESOURCE_NAME"

# Call UpdateRagCorpus API with the Vector DB information.

-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora -d '{
      "rag_vector_db_config" : {
         "pinecone": {"index_name": '\""${PINECONE_INDEX_NAME}"\"'},
         "api_auth": {"api_key_config":
               {"api_key_secret_version": '\""${SECRET_RESOURCE_NAME}"\"'}
         }
      }
   }'

# To poll the status of your RAG corpus creation, get the operation_id returned in
# response of your CreateRagCorpus call.
OPERATION_ID="YOUR_OPERATION_ID"

# Poll Operation status until done = true in the response.
# The response to this call will contain the ID for your created RAG corpus
curl -X GET \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/operations/${OPERATION_ID}

docs.title: Use Vertex AI RAG Engine in Gemini Live API
docs.text:
Preview

Some of the RAG features are Preview offerings, subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" of the Google Cloud Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA products and features may have limited support, and changes to Pre-GA products and features may not be compatible with other Pre-GA versions. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions. Further, by using the Gemini API on Vertex AI, you agree to the Generative AI Preview terms and conditions (Preview Terms).

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a technique that retrieves and provides relevant information to large language models (LLMs) to generate verifiable and grounded responses. You can use the Vertex AI RAG Engine with the Gemini Live API in two primary ways:

  • Information Retrieval: Connect to a standard RAG corpus to ground model responses with your specific data.
  • Context Storage: Use a special MemoryCorpus to store conversation history, enabling the model to recall past interactions within or across sessions.

The VPC-SC security controls and CMEK are supported by Vertex AI RAG Engine. Data residency and AXT security controls aren't supported.

This page shows you how to use Vertex AI RAG Engine with the multimodal Live API for both information retrieval and context storage.

docs.title: RAG Engine use cases with the Live API
docs.text:
The following table compares the two methods for using RAG Engine with the Gemini Live API.

Feature Standard RAG Corpus (Information Retrieval) MemoryCorpus (Context Storage) Primary Use Case Grounding model responses with factual data from your documents. Storing and retrieving conversation history to maintain context across turns or sessions. Corpus Type Standard RagCorpus. MemoryCorpus, a specialized type of RagCorpus. Key Configuration Specify the rag_corpus resource in the retrieval tool. Specify the rag_corpus resource and set store_context=True in the retrieval tool.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Before you begin Concepts
  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): A technique that enhances LLM responses by retrieving relevant information from an external knowledge base.
  • RAG Corpus: A collection of documents that you provide to the RAG Engine for indexing and retrieval.
  • Gemini Live API: A streaming API designed for real-time, multimodal conversational AI applications.
  • Websocket: A communication protocol that enables persistent, two-way communication between a client and a server.
  • MemoryCorpus: A specialized RAG corpus designed to store and index conversation history for context recall.

Prerequisites

The following prerequisites must be completed before you can use Vertex AI RAG Engine with the multimodal Live API:

  1. Enable the RAG API in Vertex AI.
  2. Create a RAG Corpus.
  3. Import files to the RAG Corpus.

docs.title: Retrieve information from a RAG corpus
docs.text:
This section shows how to connect to a standard RAG corpus to retrieve information and ground model responses in real-time.

The following diagram shows the workflow for retrieving information from a RAG corpus.

flowchart TD
    A["Step 1: Configure the RAG tool"] --> B["Step 2: Connect and stream responses"]

    click A "#step-1-configure-the-rag-tool"
    click B "#step-2-connect-and-stream-responses"
Steps

Step 1: Configure the RAG tool

To use your RAG corpus, specify it as a retrieval tool in your Live API request. This configuration points the Gemini model to your data source for grounding its responses.

Replace the following variables in the code sample: * YOUR_PROJECT_ID: The ID of your Google Cloud project. * YOUR_CORPUS_ID: The ID of your RAG corpus. * YOUR_LOCATION: The region where your resources are located (for example, us-central1).

PROJECT_ID = "YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
RAG_CORPUS_ID = "YOUR_CORPUS_ID"
LOCATION = "YOUR_LOCATION"

TOOLS = {
  "retrieval": {
    "vertex_rag_store": {
    "rag_resources": {
          "rag_corpus": "projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/${LOCATION}/ragCorpora/${RAG_CORPUS_ID}"
        }
     }
  }
}

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Step 2: Connect and stream responses

To enable real-time communication, you must use a Websocket. You can connect using the Python API for low-level control or the Python SDK for a more abstracted experience.

Python APIPython SDK

This method uses the websockets library to interact directly with the API endpoint.

CONFIG = {"response_modalities": ["TEXT"], "speech_config": { "language_code": "en-US" }}
headers = {
  "Content-Type": "application/json",
  "Authorization": f"Bearer {bearer_token[0]}",
}
HOST= "${LOCATION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com"
SERVICE_URL = f"wss://{HOST}/ws/google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.LlmBidiService/BidiGenerateContent"
MODEL="gemini-2.0-flash-exp"

# Connect to the server
async with connect(SERVICE_URL, additional_headers=headers) as ws:
  # Setup the session
  await ws.send(
json.dumps(
          {
              "setup": {
                  "model": MODEL,
                  "generation_config": CONFIG,
                  # Setup RAG as a retrieval tool
                  "tools": TOOLS,
              }
          }
      )
  )

  # Receive setup response
  raw_response = await ws.recv(decode=False)
  setup_response = json.loads(raw_response.decode("ascii"))

  # Send text message
  text_input = "What are popular LLMs?"
  display(Markdown(f"**Input:** {text_input}"))

  msg = {
      "client_content": {
          "turns": [{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": text_input}]}],
          "turn_complete": True,
      }
  }

  await ws.send(json.dumps(msg))

  responses = []

  # Receive chunks of server response
  async for raw_response in ws:
      response = json.loads(raw_response.decode())
      server_content = response.pop("serverContent", None)
      if server_content is None:
          break

      model_turn = server_content.pop("modelTurn", None)
      if model_turn is not None:
          parts = model_turn.pop("parts", None)
          if parts is not None:
              display(Markdown(f"**parts >** {parts}"))
              responses.append(parts[0]["text"])

      # End of turn
      turn_complete = server_content.pop("turnComplete", None)
      if turn_complete:
          grounding_metadata = server_content.pop("groundingMetadata", None)
          if grounding_metadata is not None:
            grounding_chunks = grounding_metadata.pop("groundingChunks", None)
            if grounding_chunks is not None:
              for chunk in grounding_chunks:
                display(Markdown(f"**grounding_chunk >** {chunk}"))
          break

  # Print the server response
  display(Markdown(f"**Response >** {''.join(responses)}"))

This method uses the Vertex AI SDK for Python, which provides a higher-level abstraction. To learn how to install the SDK, see Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python.

from google import genai
from google.genai import types
from google.genai.types import (Content, LiveConnectConfig, HttpOptions, Modality, Part,)
from IPython import display

MODEL="gemini-2.0-flash-exp"

client = genai.Client(
  vertexai=True,
  project=PROJECT_ID,
  location=LOCATION
)

async with client.aio.live.connect(
  model=MODEL,
  config=LiveConnectConfig(response_modalities=[Modality.TEXT],
                            tools=TOOLS),
) as session:
  text_input = "\'What are core LLM techniques?\'"
  print("> ", text_input, "\n")
  await session.send_client_content(
      turns=Content(role="user", parts=[Part(text=text_input)])
  )

  async for message in session.receive():
      if message.text:
          display.display(display.Markdown(message.text))
          continue

docs.title: Use a RAG corpus as a context store
docs.text:
You can use a MemoryCorpus to store session context, allowing the Live API to form and retrieve past contexts related to your conversation. This enriches the current context for model generation and lets you share context across different Live API sessions. Vertex AI RAG Engine supports storing and indexing text and audio speech from session contexts.

The following diagram shows the workflow for using a MemoryCorpus as a context store.

flowchart TD
    A["Step 1: Create a MemoryCorpus"] --> B["Step 2: Specify the memory corpus to store context"]

    click A "#step-1-create-a-memorycorpus"
    click B "#step-2-specify-the-memory-corpus-to-store-context"
Steps

Step 1: Create a MemoryCorpus

To store and index conversation history, you must create a RAG corpus of the MemoryCorpus type. You must also specify an LLM parser in your configuration, which is used to parse session contexts from the Live API to build memory for indexing.

Replace the following variables in the code sample: * YOUR_EMBEDDING_MODEL: The embedding model to use, such as publishers/google/models/text-embedding-005. * YOUR_MEMORY_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME: A display name for your memory corpus. * YOUR_LLM_PARSER_MODEL_NAME: The LLM parser model, such as projects/{project_id}/locations/{location}/publishers/google/models/gemini-1.5-pro-preview-0514.

# Currently supports Google first-party embedding models
EMBEDDING_MODEL = YOUR_EMBEDDING_MODEL
MEMORY_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME = YOUR_MEMORY_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME
LLM_PARSER_MODEL_NAME = YOUR_LLM_PARSER_MODEL_NAME

memory_corpus = rag.create_corpus(
   display_name=MEMORY_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME,
   corpus_type_config=rag.RagCorpusTypeConfig(
       corpus_type_config=rag.MemoryCorpus(
           llm_parser=rag.LlmParserConfig(
               model_name=LLM_PARSER_MODEL_NAME,
           )
       )
   ),
   backend_config=rag.RagVectorDbConfig(
       rag_embedding_model_config=rag.RagEmbeddingModelConfig(
           vertex_prediction_endpoint=rag.VertexPredictionEndpoint(
               publisher_model=EMBEDDING_MODEL
           )
       )
   ),
)

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Step 2: Specify the memory corpus to store context

When using your memory corpus with the Live API, specify it as a retrieval tool and set store_context to true. This setting allows the Live API to automatically store the session contexts in your MemoryCorpus.

Replace the following variables in the code sample: * YOUR_PROJECT_ID: The ID of your Google Cloud project. * YOUR_LOCATION: The region where your resources are located. * YOUR_TEXT_INPUT: The initial text input for the conversation. * YOUR_MODEL_NAME: The model to use, such as gemini-2.0-flash-exp.

from google import genai
from google.genai import types
from google.genai.types import (Content, LiveConnectConfig, HttpOptions, Modality, Part)
from IPython import display

PROJECT_ID=YOUR_PROJECT_ID
LOCATION=YOUR_LOCATION
TEXT_INPUT=YOUR_TEXT_INPUT
MODEL_NAME=YOUR_MODEL_NAME

client = genai.Client(
   vertexai=True,
   project=PROJECT_ID,
   location=LOCATION,
)

memory_store=types.VertexRagStore(
   rag_resources=[
       types.VertexRagStoreRagResource(
           rag_corpus=memory_corpus.name
       )
   ],
   store_context=True
)

async with client.aio.live.connect(
   model=MODEL_NAME,
   config=LiveConnectConfig(response_modalities=[Modality.TEXT],
                            tools=[types.Tool(
                                retrieval=types.Retrieval(
                                    vertex_rag_store=memory_store))]),
) as session:
   text_input=TEXT_INPUT
   await session.send_client_content(
       turns=Content(role="user", parts=[Part(text=text_input)])
   )

   async for message in session.receive():
       if message.text:
           display.display(display.Markdown(message.text))
           continue

docs.title: Use RagManagedDb with Vertex AI RAG Engine
docs.text:
Vertex AI RAG Engine uses RagManagedDb, an enterprise-ready vector database, to store and manage vector representations of your documents. The vector database is then used to retrieve relevant documents based on the document's semantic similarity to a given query.

This page shows you how to choose a retrieval strategy and service tier for RagManagedDb, and how to manage encryption for your RAG corpora.

Preview

The VPC-SC security controls and CMEK are supported by Vertex AI RAG Engine. Data residency and AXT security controls aren't supported.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • RagManagedDb: An enterprise-ready, Google-managed vector database used by Vertex AI RAG Engine to store and query document embeddings.
  • RAG corpus: A collection of documents that you provide to the RAG Engine for retrieval.
  • k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN): An exact retrieval method that finds the most similar vectors by comparing a query against all data points in the corpus.
  • Approximate Nearest Neighbors (ANN): An approximate retrieval method that uses indexing techniques to find similar vectors much faster than KNN, with a small trade-off in recall.
  • Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK): A data encryption solution that allows you to use your own cryptographic keys, managed in Cloud KMS, to protect your data at rest in Google Cloud services.
