docs.title: Tune a custom subject model (standard and instant tuning)
docs.text:
Preview

This feature and documentation are available to approved users. To request access to use this Imagen feature, fill out the Imagen on Vertex AI access request form.

With Imagen, Google's text-to-image model, you can fine-tune a model to generate images of a specific person, object, or style. This process, known as subject tuning, allows you to create a personalized model that understands a new concept based on a small set of input images.

This document guides you through the two methods available for subject tuning: Standard tuning and Instant tuning.

docs.title: Before you begin: Choose a tuning method
docs.text:
Imagen on Vertex AI offers two methods for tuning a custom subject model. Choose the method that best fits your use case.

Feature Standard Tuning Instant Tuning Use Case High-quality, production-level models with greater style diversity. Quick previews, concept testing, and experimentation. Training Time Longer (e.g., 1-2 hours) Faster (e.g., 10-20 minutes) Input Images More images recommended (10-20) for best results. Fewer images required (4-8). Output Quality Higher fidelity and consistency. Good quality, suitable for rapid iteration.

docs.title: Model tuning workflow
docs.text:
The following diagram shows the high-level workflow for tuning and using a custom subject model.

flowchart LR
    A[Prepare your dataset] --> B[Tune the model]
    B --> C[Generate images with the tuned model]

    click A "#prepare-your-dataset"
    click B "#tune-the-model"
    click C "#generate-images-with-the-tuned-model"

docs.title: Prepare your dataset
docs.text:
To tune a model, you first need to gather a set of images that clearly depict your subject. The images should be high-quality and show the subject from various angles, in different lighting conditions, and against different backgrounds.

  • For Standard tuning: We recommend 10-20 images.
  • For Instant tuning: You can use as few as 4-8 images.

Upload your images to a Cloud Storage bucket.

docs.title: Tune the model
docs.text:
After preparing your dataset, you can start the tuning process using either the standard or instant method.

Standard tuningInstant tuning

The standard tuning method is ideal for creating high-quality models for production use.

Steps for standard tuning

1. Start the tuning job

You can start a tuning job using the Google Cloud console or the Vertex AI API. You will need to provide the following: * A name for your model. * The path to your dataset in Cloud Storage. * The base model to fine-tune (e.g., imagen-3.0). * A unique text identifier for your subject (e.g., a photo of sks person).

2. Monitor the job

Navigate to the Models section in the Vertex AI console to monitor the status of your tuning job. Standard tuning jobs typically take one to two hours to complete.

3. Access the tuned model

Once the job is complete, your new model will be available in your project's model registry.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with the tuning process, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

The instant tuning method is designed for rapid experimentation and concept validation.

Steps for instant tuning

1. Start the tuning job

The process for starting an instant tuning job is similar to standard tuning but is optimized for speed. You will provide: * A name for your model. * The path to your smaller dataset in Cloud Storage. * The base model and a unique text identifier.

2. Access the tuned model

Instant tuning jobs are much faster and are typically complete in 10 to 20 minutes. Once finished, the model is ready for use in your project.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with the tuning process, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Generate images with the tuned model
docs.text:
Once your model is tuned, you can use it to generate images by referencing the unique text identifier you assigned to your subject in your prompts.

For example, if your identifier is a photo of sks person, your prompt might be:

a photo of sks person smiling and wearing a blue hat

You can generate images using the Vertex AI Studio or the Vertex AI API.

docs.title: Tune a custom style model
docs.text:
Preview

This feature is in Preview.

This feature and its documentation are available to approved users. To request access to use this Imagen feature, fill out the Imagen on Vertex AI access request form.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Style tuning in Imagen on Vertex AI lets you create a custom model that generates images in a specific artistic style. By providing just a few example images (as few as 10) that represent your desired aesthetic, you can train a model to apply that style consistently to new images generated from different text prompts.

This is useful for maintaining a consistent brand identity, creating artwork with a unique signature look, or applying a specific photographic style across a series of images.

For example, you can train a model on images with a distinct "golden hour" photographic style and then use it to generate new images, like a freight truck, that adhere to that same visual theme.

docs.title: Style tuning example
docs.text:
The following example shows four images used to train a custom style model, and the resulting image generated by the tuned model from a new prompt.

Training images: Four images with a consistent "golden photo style" used to train a custom model. Generated image: An image created by the custom model from the prompt "A high quality photo of a freight truck in golden photo style."

docs.title: How to tune a style model
docs.text:
You can tune a style model using the Vertex AI API or the Google Cloud console. The following table can help you decide which option is best for your use case.

Method Best for Vertex AI API Automating your tuning and image generation workflows, integrating with existing applications, and programmatic control over all parameters. Google Cloud console Quickly experimenting with style tuning, visual feedback during the process, and managing models without writing code.

docs.title: Tutorial
docs.text:
This tutorial shows you how to tune a custom style model and use it to generate images.

flowchart LR
    A[Prepare training data] --> B[Tune the model] --> C[Generate images with the tuned model]

    click A "#prepare-your-training-data"
    click B "#tune-the-model"
    click C "#generate-images-with-the-tuned-model"
Before you begin
  1. Set up your Google Cloud project: In the Google Cloud console, on the project selector page, select or create a Google Cloud project.
  2. Enable billing: Make sure that billing is enabled for your Google Cloud project.
  3. Enable the Vertex AI API: Enable the Vertex AI API.
  4. Set up authentication: How you set up authentication depends on the interface you use to access Vertex AI.
    • Google Cloud console: You don't need to set up authentication to use the console.
    • Vertex AI API: If you are using a client library or the Vertex AI SDK for Python, you can set up Application Default Credentials (ADC). For more information, see Set up authentication for Vertex AI.
Step 1: Prepare your training data

To tune a style model, you need a small dataset of 10 to 20 images that clearly represent the style you want to replicate.

Vertex AI APIGoogle Cloud console
  1. Collect your images: Gather 10-20 high-quality images in your desired style.
  2. Upload to Cloud Storage: Create a Cloud Storage bucket and upload your images to it. 
    gsutil mb gs://YOUR_BUCKET_NAME
gsutil -m cp /local/path/to/images/*.jpg gs://YOUR_BUCKET_NAME/style-training-images/
  3. Create a JSONL file: Create a JSON Lines file that points to your images in the Cloud Storage bucket. Each line should contain a file_path key. 
    {"file_path": "gs://YOUR_BUCKET_NAME/style-training-images/image1.jpg"}
{"file_path": "gs://YOUR_BUCKET_NAME/style-training-images/image2.jpg"}
...
  4. Upload the JSONL file to your Cloud Storage bucket.
  1. Collect your images: Gather 10-20 high-quality images in your desired style on your local machine.
  2. Navigate to Imagen: In the Google Cloud console, go to the Imagen section.
  3. Start a tuning job: In the Tune & filter tab, click Tune a model and select Style tuning. The console UI will guide you to upload your images directly from your computer.
Step 2: Tune the model

After preparing your data, you can start the tuning job.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Vertex AI APIGoogle Cloud console

Use the TuningJob resource to start a style tuning job. You will need to specify the base model, the path to your training data JSONL file, and a name for your tuned model.

# Example using the Vertex AI SDK for Python
from google.cloud import aiplatform

aiplatform.init(project="YOUR_PROJECT_ID", location="us-central1")

tuning_job = aiplatform.ModelGarden.get_tuned_model(
    source_model_id="imagen-3.0-fast-style-tuner",
    display_name="my-golden-photo-style-model",
    training_data_uri="gs://YOUR_BUCKET_NAME/style-training-data.jsonl",
    train_steps=1000,
)

print(f"Tuning job created: {tuning_job.resource_name}")
  1. In the style tuning workflow you started in the previous step, give your model a name.
  2. Select the base model you want to tune.
  3. Click Start Tuning. You can monitor the progress of the job in the console.
Step 3: Generate images with the tuned model

Once the tuning job is complete, your custom model is ready to use.

Vertex AI APIGoogle Cloud console

You can get predictions from your tuned model by referencing its resource name or ID.

# Example using the Vertex AI SDK for Python
from vertexai.preview.vision_models import ImageGenerationModel

# Use the resource name from the tuning job output
tuned_model = ImageGenerationModel.from_pretrained("projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/models/YOUR_MODEL_ID")

response = tuned_model.generate_images(
    prompt="A high quality photo of a freight truck in golden photo style.",
    number_of_images=1,
)

response.images[0].save(location="generated_truck.png", include_generation_parameters=True)
  1. Once your model is finished tuning, it will appear in the Tune & filter tab.
  2. Select your model and click Generate Images.
  3. Enter a prompt, such as "A high quality photo of a freight truck in golden photo style," and click Generate.

docs.title: Generate images with text
docs.text:
To see examples of image generation using Imagen, run the following Jupyter notebooks in the environment of your choice:

  • Image Generation with Imagen on Vertex AI:

    Open in Colab | Open in Colab Enterprise | Open in Vertex AI Workbench user-managed notebooks | View on GitHub

  • Create High Quality Visual Assets with Imagen and Gemini:

    Open in Colab | Open in Colab Enterprise | Open in Vertex AI Workbench user-managed notebooks | View on GitHub

You can generate novel images using only descriptive text as an input. The following samples show you basic instructions to generate images, but you can also use additional parameters depending on your use case.

ConsolePythonREST

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI Studio > Media Studio page.

    Go to Media Studio

  2. Click Image.

  3. Optional: In the Settings pane, configure the following settings:
    • Model: Choose a model from the available options. For more information, see Imagen models.
    • Aspect ratio: Choose an aspect ratio from the available options.
    • Number of results: Adjust the slider or enter a value between 1 and 4.
    • Negative prompt: Enter a prompt that describes what you don't want generated in the image (supported models only).
  4. Optional: In the Advanced options section, select a Region to generate your images in.
  5. Optional: In the Safety section, configure Person generation and Safety filter threshold settings.
  6. Optional: In the Style section, choose a predefined style from the menu (supported models only).
  7. In the Write your prompt box, enter your text prompt that describes the images to generate. For example, small boat on water in the morning watercolor illustration.
    • To get help writing your prompt, click Help me write to use the prompt enhancement feature.
  8. Click Generate.

A digital watermark is automatically added to generated images. You can't disable the digital watermark for image generation using the Google Cloud console. You can select an image to view it in the Image detail window.

Image detail view of a watermarked image generated with Imagen 2 from the prompt: small red boat on water in the morning watercolor illustration muted colors.

Before trying this sample, follow the Python setup instructions in the Before you begin section. For more information, see the Vertex AI Python API reference documentation.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

In this sample, you call the generate_images method on the ImageGenerationModel and save generated images locally. You can then optionally use the show() method in a notebook to show you the generated images. For more information on model versions and features, see Imagen models.

from google import genai

client = genai.Client()

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below line
# output_file = "output-image.png"

image = client.models.generate_images(
    model="imagen-4.0-generate-preview-06-06",
    prompt="A dog reading a newspaper",
)

image.generated_images[0].image.save(output_file)

print(f"Created output image using {len(image.generated_images[0].image.image_bytes)} bytes")
# Example response:
# Created output image using 1234567 bytes

For more information about imagegeneration model requests, see the imagegeneration model API reference.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_VERSION:predict

Request body:

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "TEXT_PROMPT"
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "sampleCount": 4
  }
}

Request parameters:

The following table provides a summary of the parameters for an image generation request.

Field Type Description prompt string Required. The text prompt that guides what images the model generates. sampleCount integer The number of images to generate. Default: 4. Max: 8 (model dependent). addWatermark boolean Whether to add a digital watermark. Default: true. aspectRatio string The aspect ratio of the generated image (e.g., 1:1, 16:9). enhancePrompt boolean Enables an LLM-based prompt rewriter for higher quality images. Default: true. language string The language of the input text prompt (e.g., en, es, ja). negativePrompt string A description of what to omit in the generated images. seed integer A number to make generated images deterministic. Requires addWatermark to be false. personGeneration string Safety setting to control generation of people (e.g., allow_adult, dont_allow). safetySetting string Controls safety filter thresholds (e.g., block_medium_and_above). includeRaiReason boolean Whether to include the reason for a Responsible AI filter block. Default: false. includeSafetyAttributes boolean Whether to include Responsible AI safety scores. Default: false. sampleImageStyle string A predefined style for the image (e.g., photograph, watercolor). storageUri string A Cloud Storage bucket to store output images. outputOptions object Options for the output file, such as mimeType and compressionQuality. View parameter details

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • LOCATION: Your project's region. For a list of available regions, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.
  • MODEL_VERSION: The imagegeneration model version to use. For a list of available models, see Imagen models.
  • TEXT_PROMPT: The text prompt that guides what images the model generates.

Request Parameters:

  • sampleCount: integer. The number of generated images. Accepted integer values: 1-8 (imagegeneration@002), 1-4 (all other model versions). Default value: 4.
  • addWatermark: boolean. Optional. Whether to enable a watermark for generated images. Any image generated when the field is set to true contains a digital SynthID that you can use to verify a watermarked image. If you omit this field, the default value of true is used; you must set the value to false to disable this feature. You can use the seed field to get deterministic output only when this field is set to false.
  • aspectRatio: string. Optional. A generation mode parameter that controls aspect ratio. Supported ratio values and their intended use: 1:1 (default, square), 3:4 (Ads, social media), 4:3 (TV, photography), 16:9 (landscape), 9:16 (portrait).
  • enhancePrompt: boolean. Optional. A parameter to use an LLM-based prompt rewriting feature to deliver higher quality images that better reflect the original prompt's intent. Disabling this feature may impact image quality and prompt adherence. Default value: true.
  • includeRaiReason: boolean. Optional. Whether to enable the Responsible AI filtered reason code in responses with blocked input or output. Default value: false.
  • includeSafetyAttributes: boolean. Optional. Whether to enable rounded Responsible AI scores for a list of safety attributes in responses for unfiltered input and output. Safety attribute categories: "Death, Harm & Tragedy", "Firearms & Weapons", "Hate", "Health", "Illicit Drugs", "Politics", "Porn", "Religion & Belief", "Toxic", "Violence", "Vulgarity", "War & Conflict". Default value: false.
  • outputOptions: object. Optional. Contains the following fields:
    • mimeType: string. The MIME type of the content of the image. Available values: image/jpeg, image/gif, image/png, image/webp, image/bmp, image/tiff, image/vnd.microsoft.icon.
    • compressionQuality: integer. Only applies to JPEG output files. The level of detail the model preserves for images generated in JPEG file format. Values: 0 to 100, where a higher number means more compression. Default: 75.
  • personGeneration: string. Optional. The safety setting that controls the type of people or face generation the model allows. Available values: allow_adult (default), dont_allow.
  • safetySetting: string. Optional. A setting that controls safety filter thresholds for generated images. Available values: block_low_and_above, block_medium_and_above (default), block_only_high.
  • seed: integer. Optional. Any non-negative integer you provide to make output images deterministic. Providing the same seed number always results in the same output images. If the model you're using supports digital watermarking, you must set "addWatermark": false to use this field. Accepted integer values: 1 - 2147483647.
  • storageUri: string. Optional. The Cloud Storage bucket to store the output images. If not provided, base64-encoded image bytes are returned in the response. Sample value: gs://image-bucket/output/.
  • negativePrompt: string. Optional. A description of what you want to omit in generated images. For example, "people".
  • language: string. Optional. The language code that corresponds to your text prompt language. Available values: auto, en (default), es, hi, ja, ko, pt, zh-TW, zh or zh-CN.
  • sampleImageStyle: string. Optional. A predefined style for the image. Available values: photograph, digital_art, landscape, sketch, watercolor, cyberpunk, pop_art.

To send your request, choose one of these options:

curlPowerShell

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login , or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI . You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d @request.json \
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_VERSION:predict"

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login . You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method POST `
    -Headers $headers `
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `
    -InFile request.json `
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_VERSION:predict" | Select-Object -Expand Content

Sample response:

The following sample response is for a request with "sampleCount": 2. The response returns two prediction objects, with the generated image bytes base64-encoded.

{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES",
      "mimeType": "image/png"
    },
    {
      "mimeType": "image/png",
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES"
    }
  ]
}

If you use a model that supports prompt enhancement, the response includes an additional prompt field with the enhanced prompt used for generation:

{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "mimeType": "MIME_TYPE",
      "prompt": "ENHANCED_PROMPT_1",
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES_1"
    },
    {
      "mimeType": "MIME_TYPE",
      "prompt": "ENHANCED_PROMPT_2",
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES_2"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Upscale an image
docs.text:
Use upscaling to increase the size of existing, generated, or edited images without losing quality.

ConsoleREST

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI Studio > Media Studio page.

    Go to Media Studio

  2. Click Image.

  3. In the Write your prompt box, enter your text prompt that describes the images to generate.
  4. Click Generate.
  5. Click an image to upscale. The Image pane is displayed.
  6. Click Export image. The Export image dialog is displayed.
  7. Click Also upscale image and then select a Scale factor.
  8. To download the upscaled image, click Export.

When you upscale an image using the API, specify "mode": "upscale" and upscaleConfig in the parameters object.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • LOCATION: Your project's region. For example, us-central1.
  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • B64_BASE_IMAGE: The base image to upscale, specified as a base64-encoded byte string. Size limit: 10 MB.
  • IMAGE_SOURCE: The Cloud Storage location of the image you want to upscale. For example: gs://output-bucket/source-photos/photo.png.
  • UPSCALE_FACTOR: Optional. The factor to which the image will be upscaled. Available values: x2 or x4.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagegeneration@002:predict

Request JSON body:

In the image object, use either bytesBase64Encoded or gcsUri to specify the image to upscale.

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "",
      "image": {
        "bytesBase64Encoded": "B64_BASE_IMAGE"
      }
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "sampleCount": 1,
    "mode": "upscale",
    "upscaleConfig": {
      "upscaleFactor": "UPSCALE_FACTOR"
    }
  }
}

To send your request, choose one of these options:

curlPowerShell

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login , or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI . You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d @request.json \
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagegeneration@002:predict"

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login . You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method POST `
    -Headers $headers `
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `
    -InFile request.json `
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagegeneration@002:predict" | Select-Object -Expand Content

You should receive a JSON response similar to the following:

{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "mimeType": "image/png",
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "iVBOR..[base64-encoded-upscaled-image]...YII="
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Responsible AI safety filtering
docs.text:
The image captioning and Visual Question Answering (VQA) feature model doesn't support user-configurable safety filters. However, the overall Imagen safety filtering occurs on the following data:

  • User input
  • Model output

As a result, your output may differ from the sample output if Imagen applies these safety filters. Consider the following examples.

docs.title: Filtered input
docs.text:
If the input is filtered, the response is similar to the following:

{
  "error": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Media reasoning failed with the following error: The response is blocked, as it may violate our policies. If you believe this is an error, please send feedback to your account team. Error Code: 63429089, 72817394",
    "status": "INVALID_ARGUMENT",
    "details": [
      {
        "@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.DebugInfo",
        "detail": "[ORIGINAL ERROR] generic::invalid_argument: Media reasoning failed with the following error: The response is blocked, as it may violate our policies. If you believe this is an error, please send feedback to your account team. Error Code: 63429089, 72817394 [google.rpc.error_details_ext] { message: \"Media reasoning failed with the following error: The response is blocked, as it may violate our policies. If you believe this is an error, please send feedback to your account team. Error Code: 63429089, 72817394\" }"
      }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: Filtered output
docs.text:
If the number of responses returned is less than the sample count you specify, this means the missing responses are filtered by Responsible AI. For example, the following is a response to a request with "sampleCount": 2, but one of the responses is filtered out:

{
  "predictions": [
    "cappuccino"
  ]
}

If all the output is filtered, the response is an empty object similar to the following:

{}

docs.title: Get short-form image captions
docs.text:
Use the following samples to generate short-form captions for an image.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

RESTPythonNode.js

For more information about imagetext model requests, see the imagetext model API reference.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • LOCATION: Your project's region. For example, us-central1, europe-west2, or asia-northeast3. For a list of available regions, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.
  • B64_IMAGE: The image to get captions for. The image must be specified as a base64-encoded byte string. Size limit: 10 MB.
  • RESPONSE_COUNT: The number of image captions you want to generate. Accepted integer values: 1-3.
  • LANGUAGE_CODE: One of the supported language codes.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagetext:predict

Request JSON body:

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "image": {
          "bytesBase64Encoded": "B64_IMAGE"
      }
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "sampleCount": RESPONSE_COUNT,
    "language": "LANGUAGE_CODE"
  }
}

To send your request, choose one of these options. The following commands assume that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell.

curlPowerShell

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d @request.json \
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagetext:predict"

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method POST `
    -Headers $headers `
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `
    -InFile request.json `
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagetext:predict" | Select-Object -Expand Content

The following sample responses are for a request with "sampleCount": 2.

English (en):

{
  "predictions": [
    "a yellow mug with a sheep on it sits next to a slice of cake",
    "a cup of coffee with a heart shaped latte art next to a slice of cake"
  ],
  "deployedModelId": "DEPLOYED_MODEL_ID",
  "model": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/models/MODEL_ID",
  "modelDisplayName": "MODEL_DISPLAYNAME",
  "modelVersionId": "1"
}

Spanish (es):

{
  "predictions": [
    "una taza de café junto a un plato de pastel de chocolate",
    "una taza de café con una forma de corazón en la espuma"
  ]
}

Before trying this sample, follow the Python setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Python API reference documentation.

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

In this sample you use the load_from_file method to reference a local file as the base Image to get a caption for. After you specify the base image, you use the get_captions method on the ImageTextModel and print the output.

import vertexai
from vertexai.preview.vision_models import Image, ImageTextModel

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# input_file = "input-image.png"

vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

model = ImageTextModel.from_pretrained("imagetext@001")
source_img = Image.load_from_file(location=input_file)

captions = model.get_captions(
    image=source_img,
    # Optional parameters
    language="en",
    number_of_results=2,
)

print(captions)
# Example response:
# ['a cat with green eyes looks up at the sky']

Before trying this sample, follow the Node.js setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Node.js API reference documentation.

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

In this sample, you call the predict method on a PredictionServiceClient. The service returns captions for the provided image.

/**
 * TODO(developer): Update these variables before running the sample.
 */
const projectId = process.env.CAIP_PROJECT_ID;
const location = 'us-central1';
const inputFile = 'resources/cat.png';

const aiplatform = require('@google-cloud/aiplatform');

// Imports the Google Cloud Prediction Service Client library
const {PredictionServiceClient} = aiplatform.v1;

// Import the helper module for converting arbitrary protobuf.Value objects
const {helpers} = aiplatform;

// Specifies the location of the api endpoint
const clientOptions = {
  apiEndpoint: `${location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com`,
};

// Instantiates a client
const predictionServiceClient = new PredictionServiceClient(clientOptions);

async function getShortFormImageCaptions() {
  const fs = require('fs');
  // Configure the parent resource
  const endpoint = `projects/${projectId}/locations/${location}/publishers/google/models/imagetext@001`;

  const imageFile = fs.readFileSync(inputFile);
  // Convert the image data to a Buffer and base64 encode it.
  const encodedImage = Buffer.from(imageFile).toString('base64');

  const instance = {
    image: {
      bytesBase64Encoded: encodedImage,
    },
  };
  const instanceValue = helpers.toValue(instance);
  const instances = [instanceValue];

  const parameter = {
    // Optional parameters
    language: 'en',
    sampleCount: 2,
  };
  const parameters = helpers.toValue(parameter);

  const request = {
    endpoint,
    instances,
    parameters,
  };

  // Predict request
  const [response] = await predictionServiceClient.predict(request);
  const predictions = response.predictions;
  if (predictions.length === 0) {
    console.log(
      'No captions were generated. Check the request parameters and image.'
    );
  } else {
    predictions.forEach(prediction => {
      console.log(prediction.stringValue);
    });
  }
}
await getShortFormImageCaptions();

docs.title: Use parameters for image captioning
docs.text:
When you get image captions there are several parameters you can set depending on your use case.

Number of results

Use the number of results parameter to limit the amount of captions returned for each request you send. For more information, see the imagetext (image captioning) model API reference.

Seed number

A number you add to a request to make generated descriptions deterministic. Adding a seed number with your request is a way to assure you get the same prediction (descriptions) each time. However, the image captions aren't necessarily returned in the same order. For more information, see the imagetext (image captioning) model API reference.

docs.title: Prompt and image attribute guide
docs.text:
To use Imagen on Vertex AI, you provide a text description of what you want to generate or edit. These descriptions are called prompts, and they are the primary way you communicate with Generative AI models on Vertex AI.

This guide shows you how modifying parts of a text-to-image prompt can produce different results and provides examples of images you can create. This guide also provides guidance on how you can edit images using text prompts and iteration.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Product usage
docs.text: To view usage standards and content restrictions associated with Imagen on Vertex AI, see the usage guidelines.

docs.title: Content filtering
docs.text:
Generated images are filtered for undesirable or harmful content. Similarly, any input Imagen on Vertex AI receives is checked for offensive content. This includes the input text prompt and uploaded photos in the case of image editing. For more information, see Responsible AI and usage guidelines for Imagen.

You can also report suspected abuse of Imagen on Vertex AI or any generated output that contains inappropriate material or inaccurate information using the Report suspected abuse on Google Cloud form.

docs.title: Prompt writing basics
docs.text:
While there's no single way to write a perfect prompt, most good prompts are descriptive, clear, and include a few key components. A great starting point is to think in terms of subject, context, and style.

Prompt: A sketch (style) of a modern apartment building (subject) surrounded by skyscrapers (context and background).
  • Subject: The object, person, animal, or scenery you want an image of.
  • Context and background: The environment or setting where the subject is placed, such as a studio with a white background, an outdoor landscape, or an indoor scene.
  • Style: The artistic look of the image. Styles can be general (painting, photograph, sketch) or very specific (pastel painting, charcoal drawing, isometric 3D).

After you write an initial prompt, refine it by adding more details until you get the image you want. Iteration is key. Start with a core idea, and then expand upon it until the generated image matches your vision.

Prompt: A park in the spring next to a lake Prompt: A park in the spring next to a lake, the sun sets across the lake, golden hour Prompt: A park in the spring next to a lake, the sun sets across the lake, golden hour, red wildflowers

docs.title: Imagen 3 features
docs.text:
View Imagen for Generation model card

Imagen 3 includes several features to give you more control over the image generation process.

Enhanced prompt understandingText generationPrompt parameterizationAspect ratiosNegative prompts

Imagen 3 can transform your ideas into detailed images, whether your prompts are short and simple or long and detailed. Refine your vision through iterative prompting, adding details until you achieve the perfect result.

Prompt: close-up photo of a woman in her 20s, street photography, movie still, muted orange warm tones Prompt: captivating photo of a woman in her 20s utilizing a street photography style. The image should look like a movie still with muted orange warm tones.

Additional advice for Imagen 3 prompt writing:

  • Use descriptive language: Employ detailed adjectives and adverbs to paint a clear picture for Imagen 3.
  • Provide context: If necessary, include background information to aid the AI's understanding.
  • Reference specific artists or styles: If you have a particular aesthetic in mind, referencing specific artists or art movements can be helpful.
  • Use prompt engineering tools: Consider exploring prompt engineering tools or resources to help you refine your prompts and achieve optimal results.
  • Enhance facial details: To improve facial details in personal and group images, specify it as a focus (e.g., use the word "portrait") and consider using a larger model like Imagen 3 instead of Imagen 3 Fast.

Imagen 3 can render text within your images. Use the following guidance to get the most out of this feature:

  • Iterate with confidence: You might have to regenerate images until you achieve the look you want.
  • Keep it short: Limit text to 25 characters or less for optimal generation.
  • Use multiple phrases: Experiment with two or three distinct phrases. Avoid exceeding three phrases for cleaner compositions.
  • Guide placement: While Imagen can attempt to position text as directed, expect occasional variations.
  • Inspire font style: Specify a general font style (e.g., "bold font") to influence Imagen's choices.
  • Influence font size: Specify a font size or a general indication of size (e.g., small, medium, large).

Prompt: A poster with the text "Summerland" in bold font as a title, underneath this text is the slogan "Summer never felt so good"

When using the Imagen API or Vertex AI SDK for Python, you can parameterize prompts to better control output. For example, you can create a template that allows customers to generate logos by selecting from a predefined menu of options.

You can create a parameterized prompt similar to the following:

A {logo_style} logo for a {company_area} company on a solid color background. Include the text {company_name}.

In your application, the user's choices for {logo_style}, {company_area}, and {company_name} populate the prompt that Imagen receives.

Example 1: A minimalist logo for a health care company on a solid color background. Include the text Journey.

Example 2: A modern logo for a software company on a solid color background. Include the text Silo.

Example 3: A traditional logo for a baking company on a solid color background. Include the text Seed.

Imagen 3 lets you set five distinct image aspect ratios.

Available Aspect Ratios
  • Square (1:1, default): A standard square photo, common for social media posts.

  • Fullscreen (4:3): Commonly used in media, film, and older TVs. It captures more of the scene horizontally compared to 1:1.

    Prompt: close up of a musician's fingers playing the piano, black and white film, vintage (4:3 aspect ratio) Prompt: A professional studio photo of french fries for a high end restaurant, in the style of a food magazine (4:3 aspect ratio)

  • Portrait full screen (3:4): The fullscreen aspect ratio rotated 90 degrees. It captures more of the scene vertically.

    Prompt: a woman hiking, close of her boots reflected in a puddle, large mountains in the background, in the style of an advertisement, dramatic angles (3:4 aspect ratio) Prompt: aerial shot of a river flowing up a mystical valley (3:4 aspect ratio)

  • Widescreen (16:9): The most common aspect ratio for modern TVs, monitors, and landscape mobile phone screens. Use this to capture more of the background, such as scenic landscapes.

    Prompt: a man wearing all white clothing sitting on the beach, close up, golden hour lighting (16:9 aspect ratio)

  • Portrait (9:16): Widescreen rotated 90 degrees, popularized by short-form video apps. Use this for tall subjects like buildings, trees, or waterfalls.

    Prompt: a digital render of a massive skyscraper, modern, grand, epic with a beautiful sunset in the background (9:16 aspect ratio)

You can provide a negative prompt along with your main prompt to specify what elements to omit from an image.

  • Recommended: Plainly describe what you don't want (e.g., greenery, plants, forest, trees).
  • Not recommended: Avoid instructive language like "no" or "don't" (e.g., no trees).
Prompt (no negative prompt): 4K video game concept art, urban jungle, cyberpunk city, detailed rendering Prompt: 4K video game concept art, urban jungle, cyberpunk city, detailed rendering Negative prompt: greenery, plants, forest, trees Prompt (no negative prompt): Illustration of a mythical wyvern flying over mountains Prompt: Illustration of a mythical wyvern flying over mountains Negative prompt: snow, frost :--- :---

docs.title: Prompting techniques and modifiers
docs.text:
Use the following examples to create more specific prompts by adding attributes for style, materials, and quality.

Style: PhotographyStyle: Illustration and artShapes and materialsHistorical art referencesImage quality modifiers

To generate a photograph, start your prompt with keywords like "A photo of...". You can then add modifiers to control the camera, lighting, and film type.

Camera Proximity

Keywords: Close up, taken from far away

Prompt: A close-up photo of coffee beans Prompt: A zoomed out photo of a small bag of coffee beans in a messy kitchen Camera Position

Keywords: aerial, from below

Prompt: aerial photo of urban city with skyscrapers Prompt: A photo of a forest canopy with blue skies from below Lighting

Keywords: natural, dramatic, warm, cold

Prompt: studio photo of a modern arm chair, natural lighting Prompt: studio photo of a modern arm chair, dramatic lighting Camera Settings

Keywords: motion blur, soft focus, bokeh, portrait

Prompt: photo of a city with skyscrapers from the inside of a car with motion blur Prompt: soft focus photograph of a bridge in an urban city at night Lens Types

Keywords: 35mm, 50mm, fisheye, wide angle, macro

Prompt: photo of a leaf, macro lens Prompt: street photography, new york city, fisheye lens Film Types

Keywords: black and white, polaroid

Prompt: a polaroid portrait of a dog wearing sunglasses Prompt: black and white photo of a dog wearing sunglasses

Image source: Each image was generated using its corresponding text prompt with the Imagen 3 model.

To generate illustrations or art, specify the style or creation technique in your prompt. Art styles can range from monochrome sketches to hyper-realistic digital art.

The following images use the same base prompt with different styles: "An [art style or creation technique] of an angular sporty electric sedan with skyscrapers in the background"

Prompt: A technical pencil drawing of an angular... Prompt: A charcoal drawing of an angular... Prompt: A color pencil drawing of an angular... Prompt: A pastel painting of an angular... Prompt: A digital art of an angular... Prompt: An art deco (poster) of an angular... :--- :--- :---

Image source: Each image was generated using its corresponding text prompt with the Imagen 2 model.

You can create imagery that is otherwise difficult or impossible by specifying unusual shapes and materials.

Keywords: "...made of...", "...in the shape of..."

Prompt: a duffle bag made of cheese Prompt: neon tubes in the shape of a bird Prompt: an armchair made of paper, studio photo, origami style

Image source: Each image was generated using its corresponding text prompt with the Imagen 3 model.

Referencing historical art periods or movements can produce iconic styles.

Keywords: "...in the style of..."

The following images use the base prompt: "generate an image in the style of [art period or movement]: a wind farm"

Prompt: generate an image in the style of an impressionist painting: a wind farm Prompt: generate an image in the style of a renaissance painting: a wind farm Prompt: generate an image in the style of pop art: a wind farm

Image source: Each image was generated using its corresponding text prompt with the Imagen 3 model.

Certain keywords can signal to the model that you are looking for a high-quality asset.

  • General Modifiers: high-quality, beautiful, stylized
  • Photos: 4K, HDR, Studio Photo
  • Art, Illustration: by a professional, detailed
Prompt (no quality modifiers): a photo of a corn stalk Prompt (with quality modifiers): 4k HDR beautiful photo of a corn stalk taken by a professional photographer

Image source: Each image was generated using its corresponding text prompt with the Imagen 3 model.

docs.title: Migrate to Imagen 3
docs.text: This guide explains how to migrate your applications from earlier versions of Imagen to Imagen 3.

docs.title: Why migrate to Imagen 3?
docs.text: Imagen 3 offers significant performance and quality improvements over previous versions. While most applications can be upgraded to Imagen 3 by simply updating the model name, some prompts or features may require changes. We recommend testing your existing prompts with Imagen 3 to evaluate the output.

docs.title: Migration paths
docs.text:
In most cases, you can migrate by updating the model name you are using. However, for certain features, we recommend migrating to a different model or using a new API to take advantage of improved capabilities.

The following table summarizes the recommended migration paths for common use cases.

If you use... We recommend migrating to... Key Changes General text-to-image generation Imagen 3 Update the model name. Prompts might require minor adjustments. Text-to-Live Images Veo on Vertex AI New API, improved video quality. Image Captioning & VQA Gemini API New API, improved image analysis and description capabilities. Inpainting, outpainting, product editing Imagen 3 API changes are required. Personalization (Avatar stylization) Imagen 3 Subject customization New feature with improved capabilities.

docs.title: General text-to-image generation
docs.text: For standard text-to-image generation, you can typically migrate by updating the model identifier in your code from an older version (like imagegeneration@005 or imagegeneration@006) to the latest Imagen 3 model.

docs.title: Specialized features
docs.text:
For the following specialized features, migration involves moving to a new model or API.

  • Text-to-Live Images If you use the Text-to-Live Images feature, we recommend migrating to the Text-to-Video feature in Veo on Vertex AI for improved image quality and capabilities.

  • Image Captioning and Visual Question Answering (VQA) If you use Imagen's captioning or VQA features, we recommend migrating to the Gemini API for image understanding. Gemini provides superior capabilities for analyzing and describing images.

  • Inpainting, outpainting, and product editing Migrating inpainting, outpainting, and product editing workflows to Imagen 3 requires API changes. For detailed instructions, see the following guides:

    • Inpainting (bring your own mask)
    • Outpainting
    • Product image editing (automatic background detection)

  • Personalization For avatar stylization, migrate from Imagen 2 Personalization to Imagen 3's Subject customization, which provides enhanced capabilities and higher-quality results.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues during migration, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Before you begin

Complete the following steps to set up your Google Cloud project and development environment.

  2. Select or create a Google Cloud project. In the Google Cloud console, on the project selector page, select or create a Google Cloud project.

Step 1: Set up authentication

To use the Vertex AI SDK, you need to authenticate. Select the tab for how you plan to use the samples on this page.

PythonREST

To use the Python samples on this page in a local development environment, install and initialize the gcloud CLI, and then set up Application Default Credentials with your user credentials.

  1. Install the Google Cloud CLI.

  2. If you're using an external identity provider (IdP), you must first sign in to the gcloud CLI with your federated identity.

  3. To initialize the gcloud CLI, run the following command:

    gcloud init

  4. If you're using a local shell, create local authentication credentials for your user account:

    gcloud auth application-default login

You don't need to do this if you're using Cloud Shell.

If an authentication error is returned, and you are using an external identity provider (IdP), confirm that you have signed in to the gcloud CLI with your federated identity.

For more information, see Set up ADC for a local development environment in the Google Cloud authentication documentation.

To use the REST API samples on this page in a local development environment, you use the credentials you provide to the gcloud CLI.

After installing the Google Cloud CLI, initialize it by running the following command:

gcloud init

If you're using an external identity provider (IdP), you must first sign in to the gcloud CLI with your federated identity.

For more information, see Authenticate for using REST in the Google Cloud authentication documentation.

Step 2: Generate an image

Use the following samples to generate an image from a text prompt.

  1. Set environment variables:

Step-by-step guide

Generate images and save a local copy

docs.title: Responsible AI and usage guidelines for Imagen
docs.text:
Imagen on Vertex AI brings Google's state-of-the-art generative AI capabilities to application developers. As an early-stage technology, Imagen's evolving capabilities and uses create potential for misapplication, misuse, and unintended or unforeseen consequences. For example, Imagen could generate output that you don't expect, such as images that are offensive, insensitive, or contextually incorrect.

Given these risks and complexities, Imagen on Vertex AI is designed with Google's AI Principles in mind. However, it is important for developers to understand and test their models to deploy them safely and responsibly. To aid developers, Imagen on Vertex AI has built-in safety filters to help customers block potentially harmful outputs.

When Imagen on Vertex AI is integrated into your unique use case and context, you may need to consider additional responsible AI factors and model limitations. We encourage you to use fairness, interpretability, privacy, and security recommended practices.

View Imagen for Generation model card View Imagen for Editing and Customization model card

docs.title: Imagen usage guidelines
docs.text:
Before you use Imagen on Vertex AI, review the following guidelines:

  • Image and text filtering: Images (generated or uploaded) and text prompts are assessed against safety filters. Imagen aims to filter content that violates our Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) or Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy.
  • Original content generation: Our generative imagery models are intended to generate original content and not replicate existing content. We have designed our systems to limit the chances of this occurring and will continue to improve how these systems function.
  • Configurable safety filter thresholds: Google blocks model responses that exceed designated confidence scores for certain safety attributes. To request the ability to modify a safety threshold, contact your Google Cloud account team.
  • Text rendering support: Adding text to images using a text prompt is not supported in imagegeneration@004 and earlier model versions.
  • Report suspected abuse: You can report suspected abuse of Imagen on Vertex AI or any generated output that contains inappropriate material or inaccurate information using the Report suspected abuse on Google Cloud form.
  • Trusted Tester Program opt-out: If you previously opted in to permit Google to use your data to improve pre-GA AI/ML services, you can opt out using the Trusted Tester Program - Opt Out Request form.

docs.title: Safety filters
docs.text:
Text prompts and images (generated or uploaded) submitted to Imagen are assessed against a list of safety filters. These filters cover harmful categories such as violence, sexual, derogatory, and toxic content. The goal is to block content that violates our Acceptable Use Policy (AUP), Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy, or AI Principles.

If the model responds with an error like "The prompt couldn't be submitted" or "it might violate our policies," the input has triggered a safety filter. If fewer images are returned than you requested, it means some of the generated images were blocked for not meeting safety requirements.

You can adjust the safetySetting parameter to control how aggressively the model filters for sensitive content.

docs.title: Safety attributes
docs.text:
Safety attributes are distinct from safety filters. Safety attributes are the set of categories and confidence scores returned in the API response when you set includeSafetyAttributes to true. Safety filters are the internal mechanisms used to block harmful content.

Not all safety attribute categories are used for filtering. For example, content is not filtered based on the "Health" safety attribute score. Additionally, the confidence scores for some internal, sensitive safety filters are not exposed in the API response.

docs.title: Configure safety filter behavior
docs.text: You can use several parameters with the image generation models to control content filtering. You can configure the model to report safety codes for blocked content, disable people or face generation, adjust filtering sensitivity, and more. For technical details about each field, see the Image generation model API reference.

docs.title: Content filtering parameters
docs.text:
The following optional parameters affect content filtering and how filtering is reported.

Parameter Description safetySetting Adjusts how aggressively the model filters for potentially sensitive output content. includeRaiReason Provides more verbose information when output is filtered. personGeneration Controls the generation of people, faces, and children. Available options are allow_adult, allow_all, and disallow. disablePersonFace Deprecated. Use personGeneration instead to allow or disallow person and face generation. includeSafetyAttributes Returns safety attribute information for the input text, input image (for editing), and all generated images. This includes the safety category (e.g., "Firearms & Weapons") and a confidence score.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: The following limitations apply to different Imagen capabilities.

docs.title: Image generation and editing limitations
docs.text:
• Bias amplification: Imagen can generate high-quality images, but the content might reflect biases from its training data. This can perpetuate stereotypes or discriminate against certain groups. Careful monitoring and evaluation are necessary to ensure outputs align with your use case.
  • Transparency and disclosure: It can be difficult to differentiate between AI-generated and non-AI-generated imagery. When using AI-generated images, clearly disclose this fact to users to maintain transparency and trust. We apply metadata labeling to AI-generated images to help combat misinformation.
  • Insufficient context: Imagen may lack the contextual understanding to generate images appropriate for all situations. Check that generated images align with your context, purpose, and intended audience.
  • Misrepresentation and authenticity: Editing images, especially of people, can result in misrepresentation or manipulation, potentially leading to deceptive content. Use editing features responsibly to maintain the authenticity of the images. We apply metadata labeling to AI-edited images as part of our responsible approach to AI.

docs.title: Visual captioning limitations
docs.text:
• Accuracy and context sensitivity: Visual captioning may struggle to accurately describe complex or ambiguous images. The generated descriptions might not capture the full context.
  • Ambiguity and subjective interpretations: Images can be open to multiple interpretations. Generated captions might not align with human understanding, which is shaped by subjective and cultural experiences.
  • Accessibility considerations: While automated captions can improve accessibility, they may not fully replace human-generated alt-text tailored to specific accessibility needs.

docs.title: Visual Question Answering (VQA) limitations
docs.text: • Overconfidence and uncertainty: VQA models might provide answers with high confidence even when the correct answer is ambiguous. It is essential to communicate the model's uncertainty rather than conveying a false sense of certainty.

docs.title: Recommended practices
docs.text:
To use this technology safely and responsibly, we recommend the following steps in addition to using the built-in technical safeguards:

  1. Assess your application's security risks.
  2. Consider adjustments to mitigate safety risks.
  3. Perform safety testing appropriate to your use case.
  4. Solicit user feedback and monitor content.

docs.title: Upscale an image
docs.text:
Preview

This product or feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Google Cloud Terms of Service. Pre-GA products and features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

You can use an image generation model to upscale a low-resolution image, increasing its resolution and enhancing its quality. For example, you can use image upscaling to improve a photo's quality before printing it.

This page shows you how to upscale an image by sending a request to the imagegeneration@006 model.

Before you begin

  • Enable the Vertex AI API.
  • Create a custom service account. If you don't have a custom service account, you must be granted the Vertex AI User role to run the Vertex AI SDK. For more information, see Configure a service account to use with Vertex AI.

docs.title: How to upscale an image
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Before you begin] --> B{Select method};
    B -- Google Cloud console --> C[Upscale in the console];
    B -- Vertex AI API --> D[Upscale with the API];

    click A "#before-you-begin"
    click C "#upscale-in-the-console"
    click D "#upscale-with-the-api"

You can upscale an image using the Google Cloud console for quick tests or the Vertex AI API for integration into your applications.

Feature Google Cloud console Vertex AI API Use Case Best for quick experiments and users who prefer a graphical interface. Best for integrating image upscaling into applications and automated workflows. Ease of Use High (no coding required). Medium (requires programming with the Vertex AI SDK for Python). Flexibility Limited to the options available in the UI. High (programmatic control over requests and integration with other services). Google Cloud consoleVertex AI API

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Model Garden page.

    Go to Model Garden

  2. Find the Image Upscaling model card and click Open.

  3. Upload an image that you want to upscale.
  4. Click Submit to upscale your image. The upscaled image appears on the right side of the page.

To upscale an image, call the upscale_image method on an Image object.

The following is a sample request:

import vertexai
from vertexai.preview.vision_models import Image, ImageGenerationModel

vertexai.init(project="my-project", location="us-central1")

model = ImageGenerationModel.from_pretrained("imagegeneration@006")
source_image = Image.load_from_file(location="my-source-image.png")

images = model.upscale_image(
    image=source_image,
)

images[0].save(location="my-upscaled-image.png")

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Use Visual Question Answering (VQA) to get image information
docs.text:
Visual Question Answering (VQA) lets you provide an image to the model and ask a question about its contents. In response to your question, you get one or more natural language answers.

Note: The Gemini API can answer questions based on multiple image inputs, while the imagetext model for Imagen can process one image in each input.

An example of a VQA prompt and response in the Google Cloud console. Image source: Sharon Pittaway on Unsplash.
  • Prompt question: What objects are in the image?
  • Answer 1: marbles
  • Answer 2: glass marbles

docs.title: Languages supported
docs.text:
VQA is available in the following languages:

  • English (en)

docs.title: Responsible AI safety filtering
docs.text:
The Visual Question Answering (VQA) feature model doesn't support user-configurable safety filters. However, the overall Imagen safety filtering occurs on the following data:

  • User input
  • Model output

As a result, your output might differ from the sample output if Imagen applies these safety filters. Consider the following examples.

Example of a filtered input response

If the input is filtered, the response is similar to the following:

{
  "error": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Media reasoning failed with the following error: The response is blocked, as it may violate our policies. If you believe this is an error, please send feedback to your account team. Error Code: 63429089, 72817394",
    "status": "INVALID_ARGUMENT",
    "details": [
      {
        "@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.DebugInfo",
        "detail": "[ORIGINAL ERROR] generic::invalid_argument: Media reasoning failed with the following error: The response is blocked, as it may violate our policies. If you believe this is an error, please send feedback to your account team. Error Code: 63429089, 72817394 [google.rpc.error_details_ext] { message: \"Media reasoning failed with the following error: The response is blocked, as it may violate our policies. If you believe this is an error, please send feedback to your account team. Error Code: 63429089, 72817394\" }"
      }
    ]
  }
}
Example of a partially filtered output response

If the number of responses returned is less than the sample count you specify, the missing responses were filtered by Responsible AI. For example, the following is a response to a request with "sampleCount": 2, but one of the responses is filtered out:

{
  "predictions": [
    "cappuccino"
  ]
}
Example of a fully filtered output response

If all the output is filtered, the response is an empty object similar to the following:

{}

docs.title: Get information from an image
docs.text:
This section shows you how to ask a question about an image and get answers.

flowchart LR
    A[Prepare your request] --> B[Send the request]

click A "#prepare-your-request"
click B "#send-the-request"

docs.title: Prepare your request
docs.text:
Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • LOCATION: The region for your project. For example, us-central1, europe-west2, or asia-northeast3. For a list of available regions, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.
  • VQA_PROMPT: The question you want to ask about your image. For example:
    • What color is this shoe?
    • What type of sleeves are on the shirt?
  • B64_IMAGE: The image to get information about. The image must be specified as a base64-encoded byte string. Size limit: 10 MB.
  • RESPONSE_COUNT: The number of answers you want to generate. Accepted integer values: 1-3.

docs.title: Send the request
docs.text:
Use the following samples to ask a question and get an answer about an image.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

RESTPythonNode.js

For more information about imagetext model requests, see the imagetext model API reference.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagetext:predict

Request JSON body:

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "VQA_PROMPT",
      "image": {
          "bytesBase64Encoded": "B64_IMAGE"
      }
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "sampleCount": RESPONSE_COUNT
  }
}

To send your request, choose one of these options:

curlPowerShell

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d @request.json \
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagetext:predict"

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method POST `
    -Headers $headers `
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `
    -InFile request.json `
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagetext:predict" | Select-Object -Expand Content

Sample response

The following sample response is for a request with "sampleCount": 2 and "prompt": "What is this?". The response returns two prediction string answers.

{
  "predictions": [
    "cappuccino",
    "coffee"
  ]
}

Before trying this sample, follow the Python setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Python API reference documentation.

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

In this sample, you use the load_from_file method to reference a local file. After you specify the image, you use the ask_question method on the ImageTextModel and print the answers.

import vertexai
from vertexai.preview.vision_models import Image, ImageTextModel

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# input_file = "input-image.png"
# question = "" # The question about the contents of the image.

vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

model = ImageTextModel.from_pretrained("imagetext@001")
source_img = Image.load_from_file(location=input_file)

answers = model.ask_question(
    image=source_img,
    question=question,
    # Optional parameters
    number_of_results=1,
)

print(answers)
# Example response:
# ['tabby']

Before trying this sample, follow the Node.js setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Node.js API reference documentation.

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

In this sample, you call the predict method on a PredictionServiceClient. The service returns answers for the provided question.

/**
 * TODO(developer): Update these variables before running the sample.
 */
const projectId = process.env.CAIP_PROJECT_ID;
const location = 'us-central1';
const inputFile = 'resources/cat.png';
// The question about the contents of the image.
const prompt = 'What breed of cat is this a picture of?';

const aiplatform = require('@google-cloud/aiplatform');

// Imports the Google Cloud Prediction Service Client library
const {PredictionServiceClient} = aiplatform.v1;

// Import the helper module for converting arbitrary protobuf.Value objects
const {helpers} = aiplatform;

// Specifies the location of the api endpoint
const clientOptions = {
  apiEndpoint: `${location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com`,
};

// Instantiates a client
const predictionServiceClient = new PredictionServiceClient(clientOptions);

async function getShortFormImageResponses() {
  const fs = require('fs');
  // Configure the parent resource
  const endpoint = `projects/${projectId}/locations/${location}/publishers/google/models/imagetext@001`;

  const imageFile = fs.readFileSync(inputFile);
  // Convert the image data to a Buffer and base64 encode it.
  const encodedImage = Buffer.from(imageFile).toString('base64');

  const instance = {
    prompt: prompt,
    image: {
      bytesBase64Encoded: encodedImage,
    },
  };
  const instanceValue = helpers.toValue(instance);
  const instances = [instanceValue];

  const parameter = {
    // Optional parameters
    sampleCount: 2,
  };
  const parameters = helpers.toValue(parameter);

  const request = {
    endpoint,
    instances,
    parameters,
  };

  // Predict request
  const [response] = await predictionServiceClient.predict(request);
  const predictions = response.predictions;
  if (predictions.length === 0) {
    console.log(
      'No responses were generated. Check the request parameters and image.'
    );
  } else {
    predictions.forEach(prediction => {
      console.log(prediction.stringValue);
    });
  }
}
await getShortFormImageResponses();

docs.title: Customize your VQA request with parameters
docs.text:
When you get VQA responses, there are several parameters you can set depending on your use case.

Number of results

Use the number of results parameter to limit the number of responses returned for each request you send. For more information, see the imagetext (VQA) model API reference.

Seed number

A number you add to a request to make generated responses deterministic. Adding a seed number with your request is a way to ensure you get the same prediction (responses) each time. However, the answers aren't necessarily returned in the same order. For more information, see the imagetext (VQA) model API reference.

docs.title: Abuse monitoring
docs.text: As outlined in Section 4.3 "Generative AI Safety and Abuse" of the Google Cloud Platform Terms of Service, Google uses the following process to detect potential abuse and violations of its Acceptable Use Policy and Prohibited Use Policy as part of providing Generative AI Services to customers.

docs.title: Abuse monitoring process
docs.text:
• Automated detection: Google uses automated safety classifiers to detect potential abuse and violations. For technical details on how safety classifiers work, see Configure safety filters.
  • Prompt logging: If automated safety classifiers detect suspicious activity that requires further investigation into whether a customer has violated our policies, then Google may log customer prompts solely for the purpose of examining whether a violation of the AUP or Prohibited Use Policy has occurred. This data won't be used to train or fine-tune any AI/ML models. This data is stored securely for up to 30 days in the same region or multi-region selected by the customer for their project and adheres to Google Cloud assurances, such as Data Residency, Access Transparency and VPC Service Controls.
  • Action: Authorized Google employees may assess the flagged prompts and may reach out to the customer for clarification. Failure to address the behavior—or recurring or severe abuse—may result in suspension or termination of the customer's access to Vertex AI or Google Cloud services.

docs.title: Scope and opt-out
docs.text:
• Services in scope: Vertex AI API, when used with Google's large language models.
  • Customers in scope: Only customers whose use of Google Cloud is governed by the Google Cloud Platform Terms of Service and who don't have an invoiced (offline) Cloud Billing account are subject to prompt logging for abuse monitoring.
  • Customer opt-out: Customers may request an exception by filling out this form. If approved, Google won't store any prompts associated with the approved Google Cloud account.

docs.title: Deployments and endpoints
docs.text:
Generative AI models and features on Vertex AI are accessible through two types of service endpoints: a global endpoint and specific regional endpoints. This document helps you understand the differences and choose the right endpoint for your use case.

Note that model endpoints don't guarantee in-region ML processing. For information about data residency, see Data residency.

docs.title: Choose an endpoint type
docs.text:
Before you start, use the following table and diagram to decide whether a global or regional endpoint is better for your application.

Feature Global Endpoint Regional Endpoints Availability Higher availability and reliability, as requests can be routed to multiple regions. Availability is tied to a single, specific region. Data Residency & ML Processing Not guaranteed. You cannot control which region processes your requests. Guaranteed. Requests are processed in the specified region, which is necessary for data residency requirements. Supported Features Limited. Does not support features like model tuning, batch prediction, or context caching. Full support for all features, including tuning, batch prediction, and context caching. Best For Applications that prioritize high availability and can tolerate a lack of regional control for data processing. Applications with strict data residency requirements or those that need access to all Vertex AI features. 
flowchart LR
    A[Review endpoint options] --> B{Need data residency or specific features like tuning?};
    B -- No --> C[Use the Global Endpoint];
    B -- Yes --> D[Use a Regional Endpoint];

    click A "#choose-an-endpoint-type"
    click C "#global-endpoint"
    click D "#regional-endpoints"

docs.title: Use an endpoint
docs.text:
Once you have chosen an endpoint type, use the following tabs to find instructions and availability details.

Global endpointRegional endpoints

Selecting a global endpoint for your requests can improve overall availability and reduce 429 (resource exhausted) errors. Do not use the global endpoint if you have ML processing requirements, because you cannot control which region your requests are sent to.

Supported models

The global endpoint is supported for the following Google models:

  • Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite
  • Gemini 2.5 Pro
  • Gemini 2.5 Flash
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite

For information about partner models, see Google Cloud partner model endpoint locations.

How to use the global endpoint

To use the global endpoint, set the location to global and exclude the location from the hostname in the endpoint URL.

Example global endpoint URL:

https://**aiplatform.googleapis.com**/v1/projects/test-project/locations/**global**/publishers/google/models/gemini-2.0-flash-001:generateContent

The following examples show how to configure the SDKs to use the global location.

Google Gen AI SDK

client = genai.Client(
    vertexai=True, project='PROJECT_ID', location='global'
)

Vertex AI SDK for Python

import vertexai
from vertexai.generative_models import GenerativeModel

vertexai.init(project='PROJECT_ID', location='global')

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Limitations

The following capabilities are not available when using the global endpoint:

  • Tuning
  • Batch prediction
  • Context caching
  • Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) corpus (RAG requests are supported)

Usage of the global endpoint with Provisioned Throughput is available only for the following models:

  • Gemini 2.0 Flash
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite

Regional endpoints ensure that your requests are processed within the specified geographic region. This is required for applications with data residency needs or for using features not available on the global endpoint.

Important: Starting April 29, 2025, Gemini 1.5 Pro and Gemini 1.5 Flash are not available in projects that have no prior usage of these models, including new projects. For details, see Model versions and lifecycle.

View Google model availability by region View partner model availability by region

Google serves partner model requests from the region that you specify. For some models, Google also offers a global endpoint to improve availability, which might have separate quotas and does not support data residency. For more information, see the "Regional and global endpoint" section in Vertex AI partner models for MaaS.
