docs.title: Live API reference
docs.text:
Preview

This feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

The Live API enables low-latency, bidirectional voice and video interactions with Gemini. Using the Live API, you can provide end users with natural, human-like voice conversations and the ability to interrupt the model's responses using voice commands. The Live API can process text, audio, and video input, and it can provide text and audio output.

The Live API is designed for server-to-server communication. For web and mobile apps, we recommend using the integration from our partners at Daily.

To try a tutorial that lets you use your voice and camera to talk to Gemini through the Live API, see the websocket-demo-app tutorial.

For more information about the Live API, see Live API.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
The Live API includes the following key capabilities:

  • Multimodality: The model can see, hear, and speak.
  • Low-latency realtime interaction: The model can provide fast responses.
  • Session memory: The model retains memory of all interactions within a single session, recalling previously heard or seen information.
  • Support for function calling, code execution, and Search as a Tool: You can integrate the model with external services and data sources.

docs.title: Supported models
docs.text:
• Gemini 2.5 Flash with Live API native audio (Preview)
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash with Live API (Preview)
  • Gemini 2.5 Flash

docs.title: How the Live API works
docs.text:
The Live API is a stateful API that uses WebSockets to establish a persistent session between your application and the Gemini server. The following diagram shows the typical workflow of a Live API session.

flowchart LR
    A[Start: Client initiates WebSocket connection] --> B[Configure session];
    B -- BidiGenerateContentSetup --> C[Server confirms setup];
    C -- BidiGenerateContentSetupComplete --> D{Exchange messages};
    D -- Send: ClientContent/RealtimeInput --> D;
    D -- Receive: ServerContent/ToolCall --> D;
    D -- End session --> E[Close connection];

click A "#"
click B "#configure-a-session"
click C "#configure-a-session"
click D "#send-and-receive-messages"
click E "#"
  1. Initiate Connection: The client establishes a WebSocket connection with the Gemini server.
  2. Configure Session: In the first message, the client sends a BidiGenerateContentSetup message to configure the session, specifying the model, generation parameters, system instructions, and tools.
  3. Exchange Messages: Once the server confirms the setup, the client and server can exchange messages to send text, audio, or video, and receive text, audio, or function call requests.
  4. Close Connection: The session ends when the connection is closed.

docs.title: Get started with the Live API
docs.text:
To try the Live API, go to the Vertex AI Studio, and then click Start Session.

The following tutorial shows how to use the Live API for a text-to-text conversation using the Gen AI SDK for Python (version 3.9+).

Steps to connect and interact with the Live API

1. Install the SDK and configure your client

First, install the necessary library and configure the client with your project and location details.

# Replace the `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` values
# with appropriate values for your project.

from google import genai
from google.genai.types import (
    Content,
    LiveConnectConfig,
    Modality,
    Part,
)

client = genai.Client(
    vertexai=True,
    project=GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT,
    location=GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION
)
MODEL_ID = "gemini-live-2.5-flash"

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

2. Connect to the service and exchange messages

Use an async context to connect to the service. After connecting, you can send user content and asynchronously listen for the model's response.

async with client.aio.live.connect(
    model=MODEL_ID,
    config=LiveConnectConfig(response_modalities=[Modality.TEXT]),
) as session:
    text_input = "Hello? Gemini, are you there?"
    print("> ", text_input, "\n")
    await session.send_client_content(
        turns=Content(role="user", parts=[Part(text=text_input)])
    )

    response = []

    async for message in session.receive():
        if message.text:
            response.append(message.text)

    print("".join(response))
# Example output:
# >  Hello? Gemini, are you there?
# Yes, I'm here. What would you like to talk about?

docs.title: API Integration Guide
docs.text: This section describes the core components of the Live API integration.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text:
A WebSocket connection establishes a session between the client and the Gemini server. After a client initiates a connection, the session can exchange messages to send text, audio, or video to the server and receive audio, text, or function call requests from the server.

The session configuration is sent in the first message after connection. A session configuration includes the model, generation parameters, system instructions, and tools.

View an example session configuration 

{
  "model": string,
  "generationConfig": {
    "candidateCount": integer,
    "maxOutputTokens": integer,
    "temperature": number,
    "topP": number,
    "topK": integer,
    "presencePenalty": number,
    "frequencyPenalty": number,
    "responseModalities": [string],
    "speechConfig": object
  },

  "systemInstruction": string,
  "tools": [object]
}
For more information, see BidiGenerateContentSetup.

docs.title: Send messages (Client-to-Server)
docs.text:
Messages are JSON-formatted objects exchanged over the WebSocket connection. To send a message, the client must send a JSON object with exactly one of the supported fields.

Supported client messages

Message Description BidiGenerateContentSetup Session configuration to be sent in the first message. BidiGenerateContentClientContent Incremental content update of the current conversation. BidiGenerateContentRealtimeInput Real-time audio or video input. BidiGenerateContentToolResponse Response to a ToolCallMessage received from the server.

docs.title: Receive messages (Server-to-Client)
docs.text:
To receive messages from Gemini, listen for the WebSocket message event and parse the result.

View an example event listener 
ws.addEventListener("message", async (evt) => {
  if (evt.data instanceof Blob) {
    // Process the received data (audio, video, etc.)
  } else {
    // Process JSON response
  }
});

Server messages will have exactly one of the supported fields.

Supported server messages

Message Description BidiGenerateContentSetupComplete Confirms that the session setup is complete. BidiGenerateContentServerContent Content generated by the model in response to a client message. BidiGenerateContentToolCall Request for the client to run function calls. BidiGenerateContentToolCallCancellation Sent when a function call is canceled due to user interruption. UsageMetadata A report of the number of tokens used by the session so far. GoAway A signal that the current connection will soon be terminated. SessionResumptionUpdate A session checkpoint, which can be resumed. BidiGenerateContentTranscription A transcription of either the user's or model's speech.

docs.title: Incremental content updates
docs.text:
Use incremental updates (BidiGenerateContentClientContent) to send text input, establish session context, or restore session context. For short contexts, you can send turn-by-turn interactions. For longer contexts, it is recommended to provide a single summary message to free up the context window for follow-up interactions.

View an example context message 

{
  "clientContent": {
    "turns": [
      {
          "parts":[
          {
            "text": ""
          }
        ],
        "role":"user"
      },
      {
          "parts":[
          {
            "text": ""
          }
        ],
        "role":"model"
      }
    ],
    "turnComplete": true
  }
}
Note that BidiGenerateContentClientContent should only be used to establish previous context or provide text input. To respond to function calls, use BidiGenerateContentToolResponse.

docs.title: System instructions
docs.text: You can provide system instructions at the beginning of a session to control the model's output and specify the tone and sentiment of audio responses. System instructions remain in effect for the entire session and cannot be changed after the session starts.

docs.title: Interruptions
docs.text: Users can interrupt the model's output at any time. When Voice Activity Detection (VAD) detects an interruption, the ongoing generation is canceled. The server sends a BidiGenerateContentServerContent message to report the interruption and a BidiGenerateContentToolCallCancellation message if any pending function calls were discarded.

docs.title: Voices and audio
docs.text:
To specify a voice, set the voiceName within the speechConfig object as part of your session configuration. For a list of supported voices, see Change voice and language settings. For a list of supported audio formats, see Supported audio formats.

View an example speechConfig object 
{
  "voiceConfig": {
    "prebuiltVoiceConfig": {
      "voiceName": "VOICE_NAME"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
Consider the following limitations when planning your project:

  • Client authentication: The Live API only provides server-to-server authentication. Client input should be routed through an intermediate application server for secure authentication.
  • Maximum session duration: The default maximum length of a session is 10 minutes. For more information, see Session length.
  • Voice activity detection (VAD): VAD is enabled by default but can be configured or disabled. If disabled, the client is responsible for sending ActivityStart and ActivityEnd messages.
  • Additional limitations: Manual endpointing is not supported. Audio inputs and outputs can negatively impact the model's ability to use function calling.
  • Token count: Token count is not supported.
  • Rate limits:
    • 5,000 concurrent sessions per API key
    • 4M tokens per minute

docs.title: Messages and events reference
docs.text: This section provides detailed descriptions of the messages and events used in the Live API.

docs.title: Client messages
docs.text:
BidiGenerateContentClientContent

Incremental update of the current conversation delivered from the client. This content is appended to the conversation history and used as part of the prompt for the model. Sending this message will interrupt any current model generation.

Field Description turns[] [Content](/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/reference/rpc/google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1#google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.Content) Optional. The content appended to the current conversation. For single-turn queries, this is a single instance. For multi-turn queries, this is a repeated field containing conversation history and the latest request. turn_complete bool Optional. If true, indicates that the server should start content generation with the currently accumulated prompt. Otherwise, the server will await additional messages. BidiGenerateContentRealtimeInput

User input that is sent in real time, such as streaming audio or video. This can be sent continuously without interrupting model generation.

Field Description media_chunks[] [Blob](/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/reference/rpc/google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1#google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.Blob) Optional. Inlined bytes data for media input. activity_start [ActivityStart](#activitystart) Optional. Marks the start of user activity. Can only be sent if server-side activity detection is disabled. activity_end [ActivityEnd](#activityend) Optional. Marks the end of user activity. Can only be sent if server-side activity detection is disabled. BidiGenerateContentSetup

Configuration message sent only once at the beginning of a session. Clients must wait for a BidiGenerateContentSetupComplete response before sending other messages.

Field Description model string Required. The fully qualified name of the publisher model (e.g., projects/{project}/locations/{location}/publishers/*/models/*). generation_config [GenerationConfig](/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/reference/rpc/google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1#google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.GenerationConfig) Optional. Generation config. Several fields are not supported. system_instruction [Content](/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/reference/rpc/google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1#google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.Content) Optional. System instructions for the model. Only text should be used. tools[] [Tool](/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/reference/rpc/google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1#google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.Tool) Optional. A list of Tools the model may use. session_resumption [SessionResumptionConfig](/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/reference/rpc/google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1#google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.SessionResumptionConfig) Optional. Configures session resumption. context_window_compression [ContextWindowCompressionConfig](/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/reference/rpc/google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1#google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.ContextWindowCompressionConfig) Optional. Configures context window compression. realtime_input_config [RealtimeInputConfig](#realtimeinputconfig) Optional. Configures the handling of real-time input. input_audio_transcription [AudioTranscriptionConfig](#audiotranscriptionconfig) Optional. Configures transcription for input audio. output_audio_transcription [AudioTranscriptionConfig](#audiotranscriptionconfig) Optional. Configures transcription for output audio. BidiGenerateContentToolResponse

Client-generated response to a ToolCall received from the server.

Field Description function_responses[] [FunctionResponse](/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/reference/rpc/google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1#google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.FunctionResponse) Optional. The response to the function calls, matched by ID.

docs.title: Server messages
docs.text:
BidiGenerateContentServerContent

Incremental server update generated by the model in response to client messages.

Field Description turn_complete bool Output only. If true, the model is done generating for the current turn. interrupted bool Output only. If true, a client message has interrupted the current model generation. generation_complete bool Output only. If true, the model has finished generating its entire response. grounding_metadata [GroundingMetadata](/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/reference/rpc/google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1#google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.GroundingMetadata) Output only. Metadata specifying sources used to ground generated content. input_transcription [Transcription](#transcription) Optional. Transcription of the user's speech. output_transcription [Transcription](#transcription) Optional. Transcription of the model's speech. model_turn [Content](/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/reference/rpc/google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1#google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.Content) Output only. The content generated by the model. BidiGenerateContentSetupComplete

Sent in response to a BidiGenerateContentSetup message from the client, confirming the session is ready. This type has no fields.

BidiGenerateContentToolCall

Request for the client to execute function calls.

Field Description function_calls[] [FunctionCall](/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/reference/rpc/google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1#google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.FunctionCall) Output only. The function call to be executed. BidiGenerateContentToolCallCancellation

Notification that a previously issued ToolCallMessage should be canceled.

Field Description ids[] string Output only. The IDs of the tool calls to be canceled. GoAway

A signal that the server will terminate the connection soon.

Field Description time_left [Duration](https://protobuf.dev/reference/protobuf/google.protobuf/#duration) The remaining time before the connection is terminated. SessionResumptionUpdate

An update on the session resumption state, sent only if session resumption is configured.

Field Description new_handle string A new handle that represents a resumable state. resumable bool True if the session can be resumed at this point. last_consumed_client_message_index int64 The index of the last client message included in this state. UsageMetadata

Metadata on the token usage of the cached content.

Field Description total_token_count int32 Total number of tokens consumed. text_count int32 Number of text characters. image_count int32 Number of images. video_duration_seconds int32 Duration of video in seconds. audio_duration_seconds int32 Duration of audio in seconds.

docs.title: Other types and enums
docs.text:
ActivityEnd

Marks the end of user activity. This type has no fields.

ActivityStart

Marks the start of user activity. This type has no fields.

AudioTranscriptionConfig

Configuration for audio transcription. This type has no fields.

RealtimeInputConfig

Configures the real-time input behavior.

Field Description automatic_activity_detection [AutomaticActivityDetection](#automaticactivitydetection) Optional. Configures automatic activity detection. Enabled by default. activity_handling [ActivityHandling](#activityhandling) Optional. Defines what effect user activity has (e.g., interrupting the model). turn_coverage [TurnCoverage](#turncoverage) Optional. Defines which input is included in the user's turn. AutomaticActivityDetection

Configures automatic detection of activity.

Field Description start_of_speech_sensitivity [StartSensitivity](#startsensitivity) Optional. Determines how likely speech is to be detected. end_of_speech_sensitivity [EndSensitivity](#endsensitivity) Optional. Determines how likely detected speech is to be considered ended. prefix_padding_ms int32 Optional. Required duration of detected speech before start-of-speech is committed. silence_duration_ms int32 Optional. Required duration of silence before end-of-speech is committed. disabled bool Optional. If true, disables automatic activity detection. Transcription

An audio transcription message.

Field Description text string Optional. The transcription text. finished bool Optional. Indicates the end of the transcription. ActivityHandling Enum Description ACTIVITY_HANDLING_UNSPECIFIED Default behavior is START_OF_ACTIVITY_INTERRUPTS. START_OF_ACTIVITY_INTERRUPTS Start of user activity will interrupt the model's response ("barge-in"). NO_INTERRUPTION The model's response will not be interrupted by user activity. EndSensitivity Enum Description END_SENSITIVITY_UNSPECIFIED Default is END_SENSITIVITY_LOW. END_SENSITIVITY_HIGH Automatic detection ends speech more often. END_SENSITIVITY_LOW Automatic detection ends speech less often. StartSensitivity Enum Description START_SENSITIVITY_UNSPECIFIED Default is START_SENSITIVITY_LOW. START_SENSITIVITY_HIGH Automatic detection detects the start of speech more often. START_SENSITIVITY_LOW Automatic detection detects the start of speech less often. TurnCoverage Enum Description TURN_COVERAGE_UNSPECIFIED Default behavior is TURN_INCLUDES_ALL_INPUT. TURN_INCLUDES_ONLY_ACTIVITY The user's turn only includes activity since the last turn (e.g., speech). TURN_INCLUDES_ALL_INPUT The user's turn includes all real-time input since the last turn, including inactivity (e.g., silence).

docs.title: Prompt management
docs.text:
Preview

This feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

Effective prompt management is crucial for building scalable and maintainable generative AI applications. By treating prompts as manageable assets, you can version them, reuse them across different applications, and collaborate more effectively with your team.

Vertex AI provides two primary ways to manage your prompts: the Vertex AI Studio UI and the Vertex AI SDK. The following table helps you choose the best tool for your needs.

Tool Best for Description Vertex AI Studio - Experimenting and iterating on prompts.- Users who prefer a graphical interface.- Manually creating and managing a small number of prompts. A web-based UI for creating, testing, and saving prompts without writing code. It provides a user-friendly environment for prompt engineering. Vertex AI SDK - Programmatic management of prompts.- Integrating prompt management into CI/CD pipelines.- Managing a large number of prompts at scale. A Python library (vertexai.preview.prompts) that lets you define, save, version, and manage prompts as part of your application's code.

This document focuses on using the Vertex AI SDK for programmatic prompt management.

docs.title: Manage prompts with the Vertex AI SDK
docs.text:
The vertexai.preview.prompts module in the Vertex AI SDK for Python provides the tools to programmatically manage the entire lifecycle of a prompt. The Prompt class is the central component, encapsulating prompt templates, variables, and generation configurations.

The following diagram shows the typical workflow for managing a prompt using the SDK.

flowchart LR
    A[Create and use a local prompt] --> B[Save a prompt]
    B --> C[Load a saved prompt]
    C --> D[Update a saved prompt]
    D --> E[List prompts and versions]
    E --> F[Restore a prompt version]
    F --> G[Delete a prompt]

    click A "#create-and-use-a-local-prompt"
    click B "#save-a-prompt"
    click C "#load-a-saved-prompt"
    click D "#update-a-saved-prompt"
    click E "#list-prompts-and-versions"
    click F "#restore-a-prompt-version"
    click G "#delete-a-prompt"
Tutorial: Manage the prompt lifecycle

Before you begin

Initialize the Vertex AI SDK for Python.

import vertexai

# Replace PROJECT_ID with your Google Cloud project ID
vertexai.init(project="PROJECT_ID", location="us-central1")

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Step 1: Create and use a local prompt

A Prompt object can be created locally in your development environment. It can contain a template with placeholder variables, system instructions, and model configuration.

The following example creates a local prompt to act as a movie critic, then generates content for two different sets of variables.

from vertexai.preview import prompts
from vertexai.preview.prompts import Prompt

# from vertexai.generative_models import GenerationConfig, SafetySetting # Optional

# Create local Prompt
local_prompt = Prompt(
    prompt_name="movie-critic",
    prompt_data="Compare the movies {movie1} and {movie2}.",
    variables=[
        {"movie1": "The Lion King", "movie2": "Frozen"},
        {"movie1": "Inception", "movie2": "Interstellar"},
    ],
    model_name="gemini-1.0-pro-002",
    system_instruction="You are a movie critic. Answer in a short sentence.",
    # generation_config=GenerationConfig, # Optional,
    # safety_settings=SafetySetting, # Optional,
)

# Generate content using the assembled prompt for each variable set.
for i in range(len(local_prompt.variables)):
    response = local_prompt.generate_content(
        contents=local_prompt.assemble_contents(**local_prompt.variables[i])
    )
    print(response)

Prompt class parameters

  • prompt_name: The display name of the prompt.
  • prompt_data: A string that can be a simple prompt or a template with {variable} placeholders.
  • variables: A list of dictionaries, where each dictionary contains variable names and their corresponding values.
  • model_name: The resource name of the generative model to use (e.g., gemini-1.0-pro-002).
  • system_instruction: A string that provides context or instructions for the model.
  • generation_config: (Optional) A GenerationConfig object containing parameters for generation.
  • safety_settings: (Optional) A SafetySetting object containing safety settings for generation.

Prompts also support function calling. To learn more, see Introduction to function calling.

Step 2: Save a prompt

To save a local prompt to a persistent online resource, use the prompts.create_version() method. This action creates version 1 of your prompt, which can then be accessed in the Google Cloud console or loaded in other sessions. Any subsequent updates made to the Prompt object are local until create_version() is called again.

from vertexai.preview import prompts

# Save the local_prompt object from the previous step.
# This returns a new Prompt object associated with the online resource.
saved_prompt = prompts.create_version(prompt=local_prompt)

print(saved_prompt)

Step 3: Load a saved prompt

To load a prompt that has been saved, use the prompts.get() method with the prompt's ID. This is useful for reusing prompts across different applications or sessions.

from vertexai.preview import prompts

# Use the prompt ID from the saved_prompt object.
# Replace "123456789" with your actual prompt ID.
prompt_id = "123456789"

loaded_prompt = prompts.get(prompt_id=prompt_id)

print(loaded_prompt)

Step 4: Update a saved prompt

To update a saved prompt, first load it using prompts.get(), modify its properties, and then save the changes by calling prompts.create_version(). This creates a new version of the prompt with the updated information, preserving the version history.

from vertexai.preview import prompts

# Assume loaded_prompt is the object from the previous step.
# Replace "123456789" with your actual prompt ID.
prompt_id = "123456789"
loaded_prompt = prompts.get(prompt_id=prompt_id)

# Update prompt data (changes are local until create_version is called)
loaded_prompt.prompt_data = "Write a short, positive review for the movie {movie1}."

# Save the changes as a new version.
updated_prompt = prompts.create_version(prompt=loaded_prompt)

print(updated_prompt)

Step 5: List prompts and versions

You can retrieve a list of all prompts in your project or list all versions of a specific prompt.

List all prompts

Use the prompts.list() method to see the display names and IDs of all prompts saved in your project.

from vertexai.preview import prompts

all_prompts_metadata = prompts.list()

for prompt_meta in all_prompts_metadata:
    print(f"Prompt ID: {prompt_meta.prompt_id}, Name: {prompt_meta.display_name}")

List all versions of a prompt

Use the prompts.list_versions() method to see the version history for a specific prompt ID.

from vertexai.preview import prompts

# Replace "123456789" with your actual prompt ID.
prompt_id = "123456789"

prompt_versions_metadata = prompts.list_versions(prompt_id=prompt_id)

for version_meta in prompt_versions_metadata:
    print(f"Version ID: {version_meta.version_id}, Create Time: {version_meta.create_time}")

Step 6: Restore a prompt version

You can restore an older version to be the new "latest" version of the prompt using the prompts.restore_version() method.

from vertexai.preview import prompts

# Replace "123456789" with your actual prompt ID.
prompt_id = "123456789"
version_to_restore = "1"

# Restore version "1"
restored_version_metadata = prompts.restore_version(
    prompt_id=prompt_id, version_id=version_to_restore
)

# Fetch the newly restored latest version of the prompt
restored_prompt = prompts.get(prompt_id=restored_version_metadata.prompt_id)

print(f"Restored to version: {restored_prompt.version_id}")

Step 7: Delete a prompt

To permanently delete a prompt and all its versions, use the prompts.delete() method. This action cannot be undone.

from vertexai.preview import prompts

# Replace "123456789" with your actual prompt ID.
prompt_id = "123456789"

prompts.delete(prompt_id=prompt_id)

print(f"Prompt with ID {prompt_id} has been deleted.")

docs.title: RAG Engine API
docs.text: The Vertex AI RAG Engine is a component of the Vertex AI platform that facilitates Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). RAG Engine enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to access and incorporate data from external knowledge sources, such as documents and databases. By using RAG, LLMs can generate more accurate and informative responses.

docs.title: API Parameters
docs.text: This section lists the parameters for the RAG Engine API, organized by resource type.

docs.title: Corpus management
docs.text:
Parameters for creating and managing RAG corpora. For more information, see Corpus management.

Create a RAG corpus

These parameters are used to create a RAG corpus.

Body Request

Parameters Description display_name Required: string The display name of the RAG corpus. description Optional: string The description of the RAG corpus. vector_db_config Optional: Immutable: vectorDbConfig The configuration for the Vector DBs. vertex_ai_search_config.serving_config Optional: string The configuration for the Vertex AI Search. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collections/{collection}/engines/{engine}/servingConfigs/{serving_config} or projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collections/{collection}/dataStores/{data_store}/servingConfigs/{serving_config}

vectorDbConfig

Parameters Description rag_managed_db oneof vector_db: vectorDbConfig.RagManagedDb If no vector database is specified, rag_managed_db is the default vector database. pinecone oneof vector_db: vectorDbConfig.Pinecone Specifies your Pinecone instance. pinecone.index_name string This is the name used to create the Pinecone index that's used with the RAG corpus. This value can't be changed after it's set. docs.title: API Examples
docs.text:
This section provides examples of how to use the API to manage your RAG resources.

Before you begin

  • Before using any of the request data, make the necessary replacements for placeholders like PROJECT_ID, LOCATION, CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME, etc.
  • The cURL and PowerShell commands assume that you have authenticated with the Google Cloud CLI by running gcloud auth login or by using Cloud Shell. You can verify the active account by running gcloud auth list.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Create a RAG corpus
docs.text:
These code samples demonstrate how to create a RAG corpus.

PythonRESTcURLPowerShell

To learn how to install or update the Vertex AI SDK for Python, see Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python. For more information, see the Vertex AI SDK for Python API reference documentation.

from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# display_name = "test_corpus"
# description = "Corpus Description"

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

# Configure backend_config
backend_config = rag.RagVectorDbConfig(
    rag_embedding_model_config=rag.RagEmbeddingModelConfig(
        vertex_prediction_endpoint=rag.VertexPredictionEndpoint(
            publisher_model="publishers/google/models/text-embedding-005"
        )
    )
)

corpus = rag.create_corpus(
    display_name=display_name,
    description=description,
    backend_config=backend_config,
)
print(corpus)
# Example response:
# RagCorpus(name='projects/1234567890/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/1234567890',
# display_name='test_corpus', description='Corpus Description', embedding_model_config=...
# ...

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/ragCorpora

Request JSON body:

{
  "display_name" : "CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME",
  "description": "CORPUS_DESCRIPTION",
}

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and run the following command:

curl -X POST \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
    -d @request.json \
    "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/ragCorpora"

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and run the following command:

  $cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
  $headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

  Invoke-WebRequest `
      -Method POST `
      -Headers $headers `
      -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `
      -InFile request.json `
      -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/ragCorpora" | Select-Object -Expand Content

docs.title: Import RAG files
docs.text:
Files and folders can be imported from Google Drive or Cloud Storage. You can use response.metadata to view partial failures, request time, and response time in the SDK's response object.

The response.skipped_rag_files_count refers to the number of files that were skipped during import. A file is skipped when the following conditions are met: 1. The file has already been imported. 2. The file hasn't changed. 3. The chunking configuration for the file hasn't changed.

PythonRESTcURLPowerShell 
from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

# paths = ["https://drive.google.com/file/123", "gs://my_bucket/my_files_dir"]  # Supports Cloud Storage and Google Drive Links

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

response = rag.import_files(
    corpus_name=corpus_name,
    paths=paths,
    transformation_config=rag.TransformationConfig(
        rag.ChunkingConfig(chunk_size=1024, chunk_overlap=256)
    ),
    import_result_sink="gs://sample-existing-folder/sample_import_result_unique.ndjson",  # Optional: This must be an existing Cloud Storage bucket folder, and the filename must be unique (non-existent).
    llm_parser=rag.LlmParserConfig(
      model_name="gemini-2.5-pro-preview-05-06",
      max_parsing_requests_per_min=100,
    ),  # Optional
    max_embedding_requests_per_min=900,  # Optional
)
print(f"Imported {response.imported_rag_files_count} files.")

The LLM generates a grounded response using the retrieved contexts.

docs.title: RAG Engine API
docs.text:
Preview

Some of the RAG features are Preview offerings, subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" of the Google Cloud Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA products and features may have limited support, and changes to Pre-GA products and features may not be compatible with other Pre-GA versions. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions. Further, by using the Gemini API on Vertex AI, you agree to the Generative AI Preview terms and conditions (Preview Terms).

The Vertex AI RAG Engine is a component of the Vertex AI platform that facilitates Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). RAG Engine enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to access and incorporate data from external knowledge sources, such as documents and databases. By using RAG, LLMs can generate more accurate and informative responses.

docs.title: Corpus management
docs.text: A RAG corpus is a collection of RagFiles that you can query. For more information, see Corpus management.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameters for creating a RAG corpus

When creating a RAG corpus, you must choose a vector database to store your data. The following table compares the available options.

Vector Database Option Description rag_managed_db Default. A fully managed, low-maintenance vector database provided by Vertex AI. It offers two tiers: basic for cost-effective solutions and enterprise for production-scale performance. weaviate Specifies an integration with a self-hosted or managed Weaviate instance. pinecone Specifies an integration with a Pinecone instance. vertex_feature_store Specifies an integration with a Vertex AI Feature Store instance. vertex_vector_search Specifies an integration with a Vertex AI Vector Search instance.

Body Request

Parameters Description display_name Required: string The display name of the RAG corpus. description Optional: string The description of the RAG corpus. corpus_type_config Optional: Immutable. RagCorpus.CorpusTypeConfig The configuration to specify the corpus type. vector_db_config Optional: Immutable: RagVectorDbConfig The configuration for the Vector DBs. vertex_ai_search_config.serving_config Optional: string The configuration for Vertex AI Search. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collections/{collection}/engines/{engine}/servingConfigs/{serving_config} or projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collections/{collection}/dataStores/{data_store}/servingConfigs/{serving_config}

CorpusTypeConfig

Parameters Description document_corpus oneof RagCorpus.CorpusTypeConfig.DocumentCorpus The default value of corpus_type_config, which represents a conventional document-based RAG corpus. memory_corpus oneof RagCorpus.CorpusTypeConfig.MemoryCorpus If you set this type, the RAG corpus is a MemoryCorpus that can be used with the Gemini Live API as a memory store. For more information, see Use Vertex AI RAG Engine as the memory store. memory_corpus.llm_parser oneof RagFileParsingConfig.LlmParser The LLM parser that's used to parse and store session contexts from the Gemini Live API. You can build memories for indexing.

RagVectorDbConfig

Parameters Description rag_managed_db oneof vector_db: RagVectorDbConfig.RagManagedDb If no vector database is specified, rag_managed_db is the default vector database. rag_managed_db.knn oneof retrieval_strategy: KNN Default. Finds the exact nearest neighbors by comparing all data points in your RAG corpus. If you don't specify a strategy during the creation of your RAG corpus, KNN is the default retrieval strategy used. rag_managed_db.ann oneof retrieval_strategy: ANN tree_depth: Determines the number of layers or levels in the tree. If you have O(10K) RAG files in the RAG corpus, set this value to 2. If more layers or levels are required, set this value to 3. If the number of layers or levels isn't specified, Vertex AI RAG Engine assigns a default value of 2 for this parameter. leaf_count: Determines the number of leaf nodes in the tree-based structure. The recommended value is 10 * sqrt(num of RAG files in your RAG corpus). If not specified, Vertex AI RAG Engine assigns a default value of 500 for this parameter. rebuild_ann_index: Set to true in your ImportRagFiles API request to rebuild your ANN index. Before you query the RAG corpus, it's required to rebuild the ANN index once. Only one concurrent index rebuild is supported on a project in each location. weaviate oneof vector_db: RagVectorDbConfig.Weaviate Specifies your Weaviate instance. weaviate.http_endpoint string The Weaviate instance's HTTP endpoint. This value can't be changed after it's set. You can leave it empty in the CreateRagCorpus API call, and set it with a non-empty value in a follow up UpdateRagCorpus API call. weaviate.collection_name string The Weaviate collection that the RAG corpus maps to. This value can't be changed after it's set. You can leave it empty in the CreateRagCorpus API call, and set it with a non-empty value in a follow up UpdateRagCorpus API call. pinecone oneof vector_db: RagVectorDbConfig.Pinecone Specifies your Pinecone instance. pinecone.index_name string This is the name used to create the Pinecone index that's used with the RAG corpus. This value can't be changed after it's set. You can leave it empty in the CreateRagCorpus API call, and set it with a non-empty value in a follow up UpdateRagCorpus API call. vertex_feature_store oneof vector_db: RagVectorDbConfig.VertexFeatureStore Specifies your Vertex AI Feature Store instance. vertex_feature_store.feature_view_resource_name string The Vertex AI Feature Store FeatureView that the RAG corpus maps to. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/featureOnlineStores/{feature_online_store}/featureViews/{feature_view} This value can't be changed after it's set. You can leave it empty in the CreateRagCorpus API call, and set it with a non-empty value in a follow up UpdateRagCorpus API call. vertex_vector_search oneof vector_db: RagVectorDbConfig.VertexVectorSearch Specifies your Vertex Vector Search instance. vertex_vector_search.index string This is the resource name of the Vector Search index that's used with the RAG corpus. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/indexEndpoints/{index_endpoint} This value can't be changed after it's set. You can leave it empty in the CreateRagCorpus API call, and set it with a non-empty value in a follow up UpdateRagCorpus API call. vertex_vector_search.index_endpoint string This is the resource name of the Vector Search index endpoint that's used with the RAG corpus. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/indexes/{index} This value can't be changed after it's set. You can leave it empty in the CreateRagCorpus API call, and set it with a non-empty value in a follow up UpdateRagCorpus API call. api_auth.api_key_config.api_key_secret_version string This the full resource name of the secret that is stored in Secret Manager, which contains your Weaviate or Pinecone API key that depends on your choice of vector database. Format: projects/{PROJECT_NUMBER}/secrets/{SECRET_ID}/versions/{VERSION_ID} You can leave it empty in the CreateRagCorpus API call, and set it with a non-empty value in a follow up UpdateRagCorpus API call. rag_embedding_model_config.vertex_prediction_endpoint.endpoint Optional: Immutable: string The embedding model to use for the RAG corpus. This value can't be changed after it's set. If you leave it empty, we use text-embedding-005 as the embedding model. Parameters for updating a RAG corpus

Body Request

Parameters Description display_name Optional: string The display name of the RAG corpus. description Optional: string The description of the RAG corpus. rag_vector_db.weaviate.http_endpoint string The Weaviate instance's HTTP endpoint. If your RagCorpus was created with a Weaviate configuration, and this field has never been set before, then you can update the Weaviate instance's HTTP endpoint. rag_vector_db.weaviate.collection_name string The Weaviate collection that the RAG corpus maps to. If your RagCorpus was created with a Weaviate configuration, and this field has never been set before, then you can update the Weaviate instance's collection name. rag_vector_db.pinecone.index_name string This is the name used to create the Pinecone index that's used with the RAG corpus. If your RagCorpus was created with a Pinecone configuration, and this field has never been set before, then you can update the Pinecone instance's index name. rag_vector_db.vertex_feature_store.feature_view_resource_name string The Vertex AI Feature Store FeatureView that the RAG corpus maps to. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/featureOnlineStores/{feature_online_store}/featureViews/{feature_view} If your RagCorpus was created with a Vertex AI Feature Store configuration, and this field has never been set before, then you can update it. rag_vector_db.vertex_vector_search.index string This is the resource name of the Vector Search index that's used with the RAG corpus. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/indexEndpoints/{index_endpoint} If your RagCorpus was created with a Vector Search configuration, and this field has never been set before, then you can update it. rag_vector_db.vertex_vector_search.index_endpoint string This is the resource name of the Vector Search index endpoint that's used with the RAG corpus. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/indexes/{index} If your RagCorpus was created with a Vector Search configuration, and this field has never been set before, then you can update it. rag_vector_db.api_auth.api_key_config.api_key_secret_version string The full resource name of the secret that is stored in Secret Manager, which contains your Weaviate or Pinecone API key depends on your choice of vector database. Format: projects/{PROJECT_NUMBER}/secrets/{SECRET_ID}/versions/{VERSION_ID} Parameters for listing RAG corpora Parameters Description page_size Optional: int The standard list page size. page_token Optional: string The standard list page token. Typically obtained from [ListRagCorporaResponse.next_page_token][] of the previous [VertexRagDataService.ListRagCorpora][] call. Parameters for getting a RAG corpus Parameters Description name string The name of the RagCorpus resource. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/ragCorpora/{rag_corpus_id} Parameters for deleting a RAG corpus Parameters Description name string The name of the RagCorpus resource. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/ragCorpora/{rag_corpus_id}

You can import files from various sources. The following table provides an overview of the supported sources.

Import Source Description gcs_source Import files from a Cloud Storage location. Supports individual files and entire directories. google_drive_source Import files from a Google Drive location. Supports individual files and folders. slack_source Import messages from a Slack channel. jira_source Import issues from a Jira query. share_point_sources Import files from SharePoint sources.

Body Request

If this field isn't set, RAG uses the default parser. max_embedding_requests_per_min Optional: int32 The maximum number of queries per minute that this job is allowed to make to the embedding model specified on the corpus. This value is specific to this job and not shared across other import jobs. Consult the Quotas page on the project to set an appropriate value. If unspecified, a default value of 1,000 QPM is used.

GoogleDriveSource

Parameters Description resource_ids.resource_id Required: string The ID of the Google Drive resource. resource_ids.resource_type Required: string The type of the Google Drive resource.

See: https://api.slack.com/tutorials/tracks/getting-a-token. Format: projects/{PROJECT_NUMBER}/secrets/{SECRET_ID}/versions/{VERSION_ID}

Troubleshooting

Example: Upload a RAG file

Before using the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your project ID.
  • LOCATION: The region to process the request.
  • RAG_CORPUS_ID: The corpus ID of your RAG corpus.
  • LOCAL_FILE_PATH: The local path to the file to be uploaded.
  • DISPLAY_NAME: The display name of the RAG file.
  • DESCRIPTION: The description of the RAG file.

To send your request, use the following command:

curl -X POST \
  -H "X-Goog-Upload-Protocol: multipart" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -F metadata="{'rag_file': {'display_name':' DISPLAY_NAME', 'description':'DESCRIPTION'}}" \
  -F file=@LOCAL_FILE_PATH \
  "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/upload/v1beta1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/ragCorpora/RAG_CORPUS_ID/ragFiles:upload"
Example: Import RAG files

Files and folders can be imported from Drive or Cloud Storage. The response.skipped_rag_files_count refers to the number of files that were skipped during import. A file is skipped when the following conditions are met:

  1. The file has already been imported.
  2. The file hasn't changed.
  3. The chunking configuration for the file hasn't changed.
From Cloud StorageFrom Google Drive

The following sample demonstrates how to import a file from Cloud Storage. Use the max_embedding_requests_per_min control field to limit the rate at which RAG Engine calls the embedding model during the ImportRagFiles indexing process. The field has a default value of 1000 calls per minute.

      "chunk_overlap": CHUNK_OVERLAP
    },

  }
}

docs.title: Retrieval and prediction
docs.text:
After setting up your corpus and files, you can perform retrieval and generation. This is a two-step process: first, retrieve relevant contexts based on a query, and second, use those contexts to generate a grounded response from a large language model.

flowchart LR
    A[Step 1: Retrieve contexts] --> B[Step 2: Generate a grounded response]

click A "#step-1-retrieve-contexts"
click B "#step-2-generate-a-grounded-response"

docs.title: Step 1: Retrieve contexts
docs.text:
When a user asks a question or provides a prompt, the retrieval component in RAG searches through its knowledge base to find information that is relevant to the query.

Parameters for retrieveContexts

Body Request

Parameters Description parent Required: string The resource name of the Location to retrieve RagContexts. The users must have permission to make a call in the project. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location} vertex_rag_store VertexRagStore The data source for Vertex RagStore. query Required: RagQuery Single RAG retrieve query.

VertexRagStore

Parameters Description rag_resources list: RagResource The representation of the RAG source. It can be used to specify the corpus only or RagFiles. Only support one corpus or multiple files from one corpus. rag_resources.rag_corpus Optional: string RagCorpora resource name. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/ragCorpora/{rag_corpus} rag_resources.rag_file_ids list: string A list of RagFile resources. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/ragCorpora/{rag_corpus}/ragFiles/{rag_file}

RagQuery

Parameters Description text string The query in text format to get relevant contexts. rag_retrieval_config Optional: RagRetrievalConfig The retrieval configuration for the query.

RagRetrievalConfig

Parameters Description top_k Optional: int32 The number of contexts to retrieve. hybrid_search.alpha Optional: float Alpha value controls the weight between dense and sparse vector search results. The range is [0, 1], where 0 means sparse vector search only and 1 means dense vector search only. The default value is 0.5, which balances sparse and dense vector search equally. Hybrid Search is only available for Weaviate. filter.vector_distance_threshold oneof vector_db_threshold: double Only returns contexts with a vector distance smaller than the threshold. filter.vector_similarity_threshold oneof vector_db_threshold: double Only returns contexts with vector similarity larger than the threshold. ranking.rank_service.model_name Optional: string The model name of the rank service. Example: semantic-ranker-512@latest ranking.llm_ranker.model_name Optional: string The model name used for ranking. Example: gemini-2.0-flash Example: Retrieve contexts

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

RESTcurlPowerShell

Before using the request data, make the following replacements:

  • LOCATION: The region to process the request.
  • PROJECT_ID: Your project ID.
  • RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE: The name of the RagCorpus resource. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/ragCorpora/{rag_corpus}.
  • VECTOR_DISTANCE_THRESHOLD: Only contexts with a vector distance smaller than the threshold are returned.
  • TEXT: The query text to get relevant contexts.
  • SIMILARITY_TOP_K: The number of top contexts to retrieve.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION:retrieveContexts

Request JSON body:

{
 "vertex_rag_store": {
    "rag_resources": {
      "rag_corpus": "RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE"
    },
    "vector_distance_threshold": VECTOR_DISTANCE_THRESHOLD
  },
  "query": {
   "text": "TEXT",
   "similarity_top_k": SIMILARITY_TOP_K
  }
}

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d @request.json \
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION:retrieveContexts"

docs.title: Project-level configuration
docs.text: The tier is a project-level setting available under the RagEngineConfig resource and impacts RAG corpora using RagManagedDb. To get or update the tier configuration, use the GetRagEngineConfig and UpdateRagEngineConfig respectively. For more information, see Manage your tier.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameters for RagEngineConfig Parameters Description RagManagedDbConfig.enterprise This tier offers production-scale performance along with auto scaling functionality. RagManagedDbConfig.basic This tier offers a cost-effective and low-compute tier.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Example: Get project configuration PythonREST 
from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

PROJECT_ID = YOUR_PROJECT_ID
LOCATION = YOUR_RAG_ENGINE_LOCATION

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location=LOCATION)

rag_engine_config = rag.rag_data.get_rag_engine_config(
    name=f"projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/{LOCATION}/ragEngineConfig"
)

print(rag_engine_config)

curl -X GET \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
https://${LOCATION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/${LOCATION}/ragEngineConfig
Example: Update project configuration Update to Enterprise tierUpdate to Basic tier

The following code samples demonstrate how to set the RagEngineConfig to the Enterprise tier.

==== "Python"

```python
from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

PROJECT_ID = YOUR_PROJECT_ID
LOCATION = YOUR_RAG_ENGINE_LOCATION

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location=LOCATION)

rag_engine_config_name=f"projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/{LOCATION}/ragEngineConfig"

new_rag_engine_config = rag.RagEngineConfig(
name=rag_engine_config_name,
rag_managed_db_config=rag.RagManagedDbConfig(tier=rag.Enterprise()),
)

updated_rag_engine_config = rag.rag_data.update_rag_engine_config(
rag_engine_config=new_rag_engine_config
)

print(updated_rag_engine_config)
```

==== "REST"

```bash
curl -X GET \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
https://${LOCATION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/${LOCATION}/ragEngineConfig -d "{'ragManagedDbConfig': {'enterprise': {}}}"
```

The following code samples demonstrate how to set the RagEngineConfig to the Basic tier. If you have a large amount of data in your RagManagedDb across your RAG corpora, downgrading to a Basic tier can fail due to insufficient compute and storage capacity.

==== "Python"

```python
from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

PROJECT_ID = YOUR_PROJECT_ID
LOCATION = YOUR_RAG_ENGINE_LOCATION

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location=LOCATION)

rag_engine_config_name=f"projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/{LOCATION}/ragEngineConfig"

new_rag_engine_config = rag.RagEngineConfig(
name=rag_engine_config_name,
rag_managed_db_config=rag.RagManagedDbConfig(tier=rag.Basic()),
)

updated_rag_engine_config = rag.rag_data.update_rag_engine_config(
```

docs.title: Retrieval and generation output of Vertex AI RAG Engine
docs.text: This page explains the fields in the output from the Vertex AI RAG Engine for both retrieval and generation requests.

docs.title: retrieveContexts output
docs.text: The retrieveContexts API returns a list of text chunks (contexts) that are relevant to the user's query.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
The following table describes the fields in each context object returned by the retrieveContexts API.

Field name Description source_uri The original source file URI before it was imported into RAG. For files from Cloud Storage or Google Drive, this is the original file URI. For uploaded files, this is the file's display name. source_display_name The display name of the source file. text The text chunk that is relevant to the query. score The similarity or distance score between the query and the text chunk. The metric depends on the vectorDB you choose. For the managed vector database, the score is the COSINE_DISTANCE.

docs.title: Sample output
docs.text:
View a sample retrieveContexts output 
contexts {
    source_uri: "gs://sample_folder/hello_world.txt"
    source_display_name: "hello_world.txt"
    text: "Hello World!"
    score: 0.60545359030757784
  }

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with the API output, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: generateContent output
docs.text:
The generateContent API returns a response that includes the generated text from the model and grounding metadata that connects the response to the retrieved source data.

Most of the top-level fields in the generateContent response can be found in the Response body documentation. This section focuses on the fields within the grounding_metadata object, which is specific to RAG.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
The following table describes the fields within the grounding_metadata object of the generateContent response.

Field name Description grounding_chunks A repeated field containing the chunks returned by the RAG engine. grounding_chunks.retrieved_context Contains a single chunk used to ground the generated content. grounding_chunks.retrieved_context.uri The source_uri specifying where the original data is stored. grounding_chunks.retrieved_context.title The source_display_name (filename or display name) of the original file. grounding_chunks.retrieved_context.text The text of the chunk used to ground the Gemini response. grounding_supports A repeated field describing the relationship between a segment of the generated text and the grounding chunks. grounding_supports.segment The specific segment of the generated text that is grounded. grounding_supports.segment.start_index The starting character index of the grounded text segment. If missing, the index is 0. grounding_supports.segment.end_index The ending character index of the grounded text segment. grounding_supports.segment.text The text of the grounded segment. grounding_supports.grounding_chunk_indices A list of indices pointing to the chunks in the grounding_chunks field that are used to ground this text segment. The index starts from 0. grounding_supports.confidence_scores A list of confidence scores for the grounding relationship. Each score corresponds to a grounding_chunk_indices entry. The score ranges up to 1.0, with higher scores indicating higher confidence. Only chunks with a confidence score of at least 0.6 are included.

docs.title: Agent Engine API
docs.text:
Agent Engine (formerly known as Reasoning Engine) provides a managed runtime for your agents. You can create an agent using Python orchestration frameworks such as LangChain and deploy it with Agent Engine. Agent Engine provides the security, privacy, observability, and scalability benefits of Vertex AI integration.

For more conceptual information about Agent Engine, see Agent Engine Overview.

Note: Because the name of Vertex AI Agent Engine changed over time, the API resource is named ReasoningEngine to maintain backwards compatibility.

docs.title: Agent Engine Workflow
docs.text:
The following diagram shows the typical workflow for creating and using an agent with Agent Engine.

flowchart LR
    A[Create and deploy an agent] --> B[Query an agent]
    B --> C[List agents]
    C --> E[Get an agent]
    E --> F[Delete an agent]

click A "#create-and-deploy-an-agent"
click B "#query-an-agent"
click C "#list-agents"
click E "#get-an-agent"
click F "#delete-an-agent"
Before you begin

Before you run the code samples on this page, complete the following steps:

Set up your project

  1. In the Google Cloud console, on the project selector page, select or create a Google Cloud project.
  2. Make sure that billing is enabled for your Google Cloud project.
  3. Enable the Vertex AI API.
  4. Install and initialize the gcloud CLI.

Authenticate

To use the Vertex AI SDK for Python, you need to authenticate. For this quickstart, the recommended way to authenticate is to set up Application Default Credentials (ADC) in your environment.

For more information, see Set up Application Default Credentials.

Install the Vertex AI SDK

Install the latest version of the Vertex AI SDK for Python:

pip install --upgrade google-cloud-aiplatform

docs.title: Create and deploy an agent
docs.text:
You can deploy a simple Python application or a more advanced application that uses a framework like LangChain.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Basic appAdvanced app (LangChain)

This example deploys a simple application that adds two integers.

import vertexai
from vertexai.preview import reasoning_engines

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# staging_bucket = "gs://YOUR_BUCKET_NAME"
vertexai.init(
    project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1", staging_bucket=staging_bucket
)

class SimpleAdditionApp:
    def query(self, a: int, b: int) -> str:
        """Query the application.
        Args:
            a: The first input number
            b: The second input number
        Returns:
            int: The additional result.
        """
        return f"{int(a)} + {int(b)} is {int(a + b)}"

# Locally test
app = SimpleAdditionApp()
app.query(a=1, b=2)

# Create a remote app with Reasoning Engine.
# This may take 1-2 minutes to finish.
reasoning_engine = reasoning_engines.ReasoningEngine.create(
    SimpleAdditionApp(),
    display_name="Demo Addition App",
    description="A simple demo addition app",
    requirements=["cloudpickle==3"],
    extra_packages=[],
)
# Example response:
# Using bucket YOUR_BUCKET_NAME
# Writing to gs://YOUR_BUCKET_NAME/reasoning_engine/reasoning_engine.pkl
# ...
# ReasoningEngine created. Resource name: projects/123456789/locations/us-central1/reasoningEngines/123456
# To use this ReasoningEngine in another session:
# reasoning_engine = vertexai.preview.reasoning_engines.ReasoningEngine('projects/123456789/locations/...

This example deploys a more advanced application that uses LangChain's chain, prompt templates, and the Gemini API.

from typing import List

import vertexai
from vertexai.preview import reasoning_engines

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# staging_bucket = "gs://YOUR_BUCKET_NAME"

vertexai.init(
    project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1", staging_bucket=staging_bucket
)

class LangchainApp:
    def __init__(self, project: str, location: str) -> None:
        self.project_id = project
        self.location = location

    def set_up(self) -> None:
        from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate
        from langchain_google_vertexai import ChatVertexAI

        system = (
            "You are a helpful assistant that answers questions "
            "about Google Cloud."
        )
        human = "{text}"
        prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages(
            [("system", system), ("human", human)]
        )
        chat = ChatVertexAI(project=self.project_id, location=self.location)
        self.chain = prompt | chat

    def query(self, question: str) -> Union[str, List[Union[str, Dict]]]:
        """Query the application.
        Args:
            question: The user prompt.
        Returns:
            str: The LLM response.
        """
        return self.chain.invoke({"text": question}).content

# Locally test
app = LangchainApp(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")
app.set_up()
print(app.query("What is Vertex AI?"))

# Create a remote app with Reasoning Engine
# Deployment of the app should take a few minutes to complete.
reasoning_engine = reasoning_engines.ReasoningEngine.create(
    LangchainApp(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1"),
    requirements=[
        "google-cloud-aiplatform[langchain,reasoningengine]",
        "cloudpickle==3.0.0",
        "pydantic==2.7.4",
    ],
    display_name="Demo LangChain App",
    description="This is a simple LangChain app.",
    # sys_version="3.10",  # Optional
    extra_packages=[],
)
# Example response:
# Model_name will become a required arg for VertexAIEmbeddings starting...
# ...
# Create ReasoningEngine backing LRO: projects/123456789/locations/us-central1/reasoningEngines/...
# ReasoningEngine created. Resource name: projects/123456789/locations/us-central1/reasoningEngines/...
# ...

docs.text:
After deploying your agent, you can send queries to it. This example uses the SimpleAdditionApp from the basic deployment example.

Troubleshooting

Vertex AI SDK for PythonREST

docs.title: Text embeddings API
docs.text: The Text embeddings API converts textual data into numerical vectors. These vector representations are designed to capture the semantic meaning and context of the words they represent.

docs.title: Supported Models
docs.text:
You can get text embeddings by using the following models. For the best performance, we recommend using gemini-embedding-001.

Model name Description Output Dimensions Max sequence length Supported text languages gemini-embedding-001 State-of-the-art performance across English, multilingual and code tasks. It unifies the previously specialized models like text-embedding-005 and text-multilingual-embedding-002 and achieves better performance in their respective domains. Read our Tech Report for more detail. up to 3072 2048 tokens Supported text languages text-embedding-005 Specialized in English and code tasks. up to 768 2048 tokens English text-multilingual-embedding-002 Specialized in multilingual tasks. up to 768 2048 tokens Supported text languages

For superior embedding quality, gemini-embedding-001 is our large model designed to provide the highest performance. Note that gemini-embedding-001 supports one instance per request.

docs.title: HTTP request
docs.text: POST https://{REGION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/{REGION}/publishers/google/models/{MODEL_ID}:predict

docs.title: Request body
docs.text:
The request body is a JSON object containing a list of instances and a parameters object to control the output.

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "task_type": "RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT",
      "title": "document title",
      "content": "I would like embeddings for this text!"
    },
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "autoTruncate": true,
    "outputDimensionality": 256
  }
}

docs.title: Request parameters
docs.text:
Field Type Description instances array A list of objects to generate embeddings for. For gemini-embedding-001, only one instance is supported per request. For other models, the limit is five instances per request. instances.content string The text that you want to generate embeddings for. instances.task_type string (Optional) Specifies the intended downstream application to help the model produce higher-quality embeddings. If left blank, the default is RETRIEVAL_QUERY.
  • RETRIEVAL_QUERY: The text is a query in a search/retrieval setting.
  • RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT: The text is a document in a search/retrieval setting.
  • SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY: The text is used for Semantic Textual Similarity (STS).
  • CLASSIFICATION: The embedding is used for classification.
  • CLUSTERING: The embedding is used for clustering.
  • QUESTION_ANSWERING: The query embedding is used for answering questions.
  • FACT_VERIFICATION: The query embedding is used for fact verification.
  • CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY: The query embedding is used for code retrieval (Java and Python).
For more information, see Choose an embeddings task type. instances.title string (Optional) The title of the document. This field is only valid when task_type is RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT. parameters object An object containing model parameters. parameters.autoTruncate boolean (Optional) When set to true, input text is truncated if it's longer than the maximum length supported by the model. When false, an error is returned for oversized text. Defaults to true. parameters.outputDimensionality integer (Optional) The desired size for the output embedding vector. If set, the output embeddings are truncated to this size.

docs.title: Response body
docs.text:
The response body is a JSON object containing the predictions for each input instance.

{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "embeddings": {
        "statistics": {
          "truncated": false,
          "token_count": 8
        },
        "values": [
          0.0058424929156899452,
          0.011848051100969315,
          0.032247550785541534,
          -0.031829461455345154,
          -0.055369812995195389,
          ...
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Response fields
docs.text: Field Type Description predictions array A list of prediction objects, one for each instance in the request. predictions.embeddings object The embedding result generated from the input text. predictions.embeddings.statistics object Statistics computed from the input text. predictions.embeddings.statistics.truncated boolean Indicates whether the input text was truncated (true) because it was longer than the model's maximum token limit. predictions.embeddings.statistics.token_count integer The number of tokens in the input text. predictions.embeddings.values array of numbers The embedding vector, which is a numerical encoding of the semantic content of the input text.

from __future__ import annotations

from vertexai.language_models import TextEmbeddingInput, TextEmbeddingModel


def embed_text() -> list[list[float]]:
    """Embeds texts with a pre-trained, foundational model.

    Returns:
        A list of lists containing the embedding vectors for each input text
    """

    # A list of texts to be embedded.
    texts = ["banana muffins? ", "banana bread? banana muffins?"]
    # The dimensionality of the output embeddings.
    dimensionality = 3072
    # The task type for embedding. Check the available tasks in the model's documentation.
    task = "RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT"

    model = TextEmbeddingModel.from_pretrained("gemini-embedding-001")
    kwargs = dict(output_dimensionality=dimensionality) if dimensionality else {}

    embeddings = []
    # gemini-embedding-001 takes one input at a time
    for text in texts:
        text_input = TextEmbeddingInput(text, task)
        embedding = model.get_embeddings([text_input], **kwargs)
        print(embedding)
        # Example response:
        # [[0.006135190837085247, -0.01462465338408947, 0.004978656303137541, ...]]
        embeddings.append(embedding[0].values)

    return embeddings

    aiplatform "cloud.google.com/go/aiplatform/apiv1"
    "cloud.google.com/go/aiplatform/apiv1/aiplatformpb"

    "google.golang.org/api/option"
    "google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/structpb"
)

// embedTexts shows how embeddings are set for gemini-embedding-001 model
func embedTexts(w io.Writer, project, location string) error {
    // location := "us-central1"
    ctx := context.Background()

    apiEndpoint := fmt.Sprintf("%s-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443", location)
    dimensionality := 3072
    model := "gemini-embedding-001"
    texts := []string{"banana muffins? ", "banana bread? banana muffins?"}

    client, err := aiplatform.NewPredictionClient(ctx, option.WithEndpoint(apiEndpoint))
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    defer client.Close()

    endpoint := fmt.Sprintf("projects/%s/locations/%s/publishers/google/models/%s", project, location, model)
    allEmbeddings := make([][]float32, 0, len(texts))
    // gemini-embedding-001 takes 1 input at a time
    for _, text := range texts {
        instances := make([]*structpb.Value, 1)
        instances[0] = structpb.NewStructValue(&structpb.Struct{
            Fields: map[string]*structpb.Value{
                "content":   structpb.NewStringValue(text),
                "task_type": structpb.NewStringValue("QUESTION_ANSWERING"),
            },
        })

        params := structpb.NewStructValue(&structpb.Struct{
            Fields: map[string]*structpb.Value{
                "outputDimensionality": structpb.NewNumberValue(float64(dimensionality)),
            },
        })

        req := &aiplatformpb.PredictRequest{
            Endpoint:   endpoint,
            Instances:  instances,
            Parameters: params,
        }
        resp, err := client.Predict(ctx, req)
        if err != nil {
            return err
        }

        // Process the prediction for the single text
        // The response will contain one prediction because we sent one instance.
        if len(resp.Predictions) == 0 {
            return fmt.Errorf("no predictions returned for text \"%s\"", text)
        }

        prediction := resp.Predictions[0]
        embeddingValues := prediction.GetStructValue().Fields["embeddings"].GetStructValue().Fields["values"].GetListValue().Values

        currentEmbedding := make([]float32, len(embeddingValues))
        for j, value := range embeddingValues {
            currentEmbedding[j] = float32(value.GetNumberValue())
        }
        allEmbeddings = append(allEmbeddings, currentEmbedding)
    }

    if len(allEmbeddings) > 0 {
        fmt.Fprintf(w, "Dimensionality: %d. Embeddings length: %d", len(allEmbeddings[0]), len(allEmbeddings))
    } else {
        fmt.Fprintln(w, "No texts were processed.")
    }
    return nil
}

public class PredictTextEmbeddingsSample {
  public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
    // TODO(developer): Replace these variables before running the sample.
    // Details about text embedding request structure and supported models are available in:
    // https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/generative-ai/embeddings/get-text-embeddings
    String endpoint = "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443";
    String project = "YOUR_PROJECT_ID";
    String model = "gemini-embedding-001";
    predictTextEmbeddings(
        endpoint,
        project,
        model,
        List.of("banana bread?", "banana muffins?"),
        "QUESTION_ANSWERING",
        OptionalInt.of(3072));
  }

  // Gets text embeddings from a pretrained, foundational model.
  public static List<List<Float>> predictTextEmbeddings(
      String endpoint,
      String project,
      String model,
      List<String> texts,
      String task,
      OptionalInt outputDimensionality)
      throws IOException {
    [PredictionServiceSettings](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/google-cloud-aiplatform/latest/com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.PredictionServiceSettings.html) settings =
        [PredictionServiceSettings](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/google-cloud-aiplatform/latest/com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.PredictionServiceSettings.html).newBuilder().setEndpoint(endpoint).build();
    Matcher matcher = Pattern.compile("^(?<Location>\\w+-\\w+)").matcher(endpoint);
    String location = matcher.matches() ? matcher.group("Location") : "us-central1";
    [EndpointName](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/google-cloud-aiplatform/latest/com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.EndpointName.html) endpointName =
        [EndpointName](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/google-cloud-aiplatform/latest/com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.EndpointName.html).ofProjectLocationPublisherModelName(project, location, "google", model);

    List<List<Float>> floats = new ArrayList<>();
    // You can use this prediction service client for multiple requests.
    try ([PredictionServiceClient](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/google-cloud-aiplatform/latest/com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.PredictionServiceClient.html) client = [PredictionServiceClient](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/google-cloud-aiplatform/latest/com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.PredictionServiceClient.html).create(settings)) {
      // gemini-embedding-001 takes one input at a time.
      for (int i = 0; i < texts.size(); i++) {
        [PredictRequest](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/google-cloud-aiplatform/latest/com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.PredictRequest.html).Builder request = 
            [PredictRequest](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/google-cloud-aiplatform/latest/com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.PredictRequest.html).newBuilder().setEndpoint(endpointName.[toString](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/google-cloud-aiplatform/latest/com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.EndpointName.html#com_google_cloud_aiplatform_v1_EndpointName_toString__)());
        if (outputDimensionality.isPresent()) {
          request.setParameters(
              [Value](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/protobuf/latest/com.google.protobuf.Value.html).newBuilder()
                  .setStructValue(
                      [Struct](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/protobuf/latest/com.google.protobuf.Struct.html).newBuilder()
                          .putFields(
                              "outputDimensionality", valueOf(outputDimensionality.getAsInt()))
                          .build()));
        }
        request.addInstances(
            [Value](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/protobuf/latest/com.google.protobuf.Value.html).newBuilder()
                .setStructValue(
                    [Struct](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/protobuf/latest/com.google.protobuf.Struct.html).newBuilder()
                        .putFields("content", valueOf(texts.get(i)))
                        .putFields("task_type", valueOf(task))
                        .build()));
        [PredictResponse](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/google-cloud-aiplatform/latest/com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.PredictResponse.html) response = client.predict(request.build());

        for ([Value](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/protobuf/latest/com.google.protobuf.Value.html) prediction : response.[getPredictionsList](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/google-cloud-aiplatform/latest/com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.PredictResponse.html#com_google_cloud_aiplatform_v1_PredictResponse_getPredictionsList__)()) {
          [Value](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/protobuf/latest/com.google.protobuf.Value.html) embeddings = prediction.getStructValue().getFieldsOrThrow("embeddings");
          [Value](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/protobuf/latest/com.google.protobuf.Value.html) values = embeddings.[getStructValue](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/protobuf/latest/com.google.protobuf.Value.html#com_google_protobuf_Value_getStructValue__)().getFieldsOrThrow("values");
          floats.add(
              values.[getListValue](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/protobuf/latest/com.google.protobuf.Value.html#com_google_protobuf_Value_getListValue__)().getValuesList().stream()
                  .map(Value::getNumberValue)
                  .map(Double::floatValue)
                  .collect(toList()));
        }
      }
      return floats;
    }
  }

  private static [Value](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/protobuf/latest/com.google.protobuf.Value.html) valueOf(String s) {
    return [Value](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/protobuf/latest/com.google.protobuf.Value.html).newBuilder().setStringValue(s).build();
  }

  private static [Value](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/protobuf/latest/com.google.protobuf.Value.html) valueOf(int n) {
    return [Value](https://cloud.google.com/java/docs/reference/protobuf/latest/com.google.protobuf.Value.html).newBuilder().setNumberValue(n).build();
  }
}
