docs.title: Reranking for Vertex AI RAG Engine
docs.text:
The VPC-SC security control is supported by RAG Engine. Data residency, CMEK, and AXT security controls aren't supported.

This page explains what reranking is and compares the available reranker options in Vertex AI RAG Engine. Reranking takes an initial set of retrieved search results and re-orders them using a more sophisticated relevance model to improve the quality of the final results.

This document provides instructions on how to implement each reranker option to improve the relevance of your retrieved search results.

flowchart LR
    A[Choose a reranker] --> B[Implement with Vertex AI ranking API]
    A --> C[Implement with an LLM reranker]

    click A "#available-rerankers"
    click B "#implement-a-reranker"
    click C "#implement-a-reranker"

docs.title: Available rerankers
docs.text:
Choose a reranker based on your requirements for latency, accuracy, and cost.

Ranker option Description Latency Accuracy Pricing Vertex AI ranking API A standalone semantic reranker designed for highly-precise relevance scoring and low latency. For more information, see Improve search and RAG quality with ranking API. Very low (< 100ms) State-of-the-art performance Per Vertex AI RAG Engine request LLM reranker Uses a separate call to a Gemini model to assess the relevance of chunks to a query. High (1-2 seconds) Model dependent LLM token pricing

docs.title: Implement a reranker
docs.text:
After choosing a reranker, use the following code samples to implement it.

Vertex AI ranking APILLM reranker

To use the Vertex AI ranking API, you must enable the Discovery Engine API. All supported models can be found in Improve search and RAG quality with ranking API.

These code samples demonstrate how to enable reranking with the Vertex AI ranking API in the tool configuration.

PythonREST

To learn how to install or update the Vertex AI SDK for Python, see Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python. For more information, see the Python API reference documentation.

Before you begin, replace the following variables:

  • PROJECT_ID: The ID of your Google Cloud project.
  • LOCATION: The region to process the request.
  • MODEL_NAME: The LLM model for content generation. For example, gemini-1.0-pro.
  • INPUT_PROMPT: The text sent to the LLM for content generation.
  • RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE: The name of the RAG corpus resource. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/ragCorpora/{rag_corpus}.
  • SIMILARITY_TOP_K: Optional: The number of top contexts to retrieve.
  • RANKER_MODEL_NAME: The name of the model used for reranking. For example, semantic-ranker-default@latest.
from vertexai import rag
from vertexai.generative_models import GenerativeModel, Tool
import vertexai

PROJECT_ID = "PROJECT_ID"
CORPUS_NAME = "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/LOCATION/ragCorpora/RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE"

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="LOCATION")

config = rag.RagRetrievalConfig(
    top_k=10,
    ranking=rag.Ranking(
        rank_service=rag.RankService(
            model_name="RANKER_MODEL_NAME"
        )
    )
)

rag_retrieval_tool = Tool.from_retrieval(
    retrieval=rag.Retrieval(
        source=rag.VertexRagStore(
            rag_resources=[
                rag.RagResource(
                    rag_corpus=CORPUS_NAME,
                )
            ],
            rag_retrieval_config=config
        ),
    )
)

rag_model = GenerativeModel(
    model_name="MODEL_NAME", tools=[rag_retrieval_tool]
)
response = rag_model.generate_content("INPUT_PROMPT")
print(response.text)
# Example response:
#   The sky appears blue due to a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering.
#   Sunlight, which contains all colors of the rainbow, is scattered
#   by the tiny particles in the Earth's atmosphere....
#   ...

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

To generate content using Gemini models, make a call to the Vertex AI GenerateContent API. By specifying the RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE when you make the request, the model automatically retrieves data from the Vertex AI RAG Engine.

Before you begin, replace the following variables:

  • PROJECT_ID: The ID of your Google Cloud project.
  • LOCATION: The region to process the request.
  • MODEL_NAME: The LLM model for content generation. For example, gemini-1.0-pro.
  • GENERATION_METHOD: The LLM method for content generation. Options include generateContent and streamGenerateContent.
  • INPUT_PROMPT: The text sent to the LLM for content generation.
  • RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE: The name of the RAG corpus resource. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/ragCorpora/{rag_corpus}.
  • SIMILARITY_TOP_K: Optional: The number of top contexts to retrieve.
  • RANKER_MODEL_NAME: The name of the model used for reranking. For example, semantic-ranker-default@latest.
curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
"https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_NAME:GENERATION_METHOD" \
-d '{
  "contents": {
    "role": "user",
    "parts": {
      "text": "INPUT_PROMPT"
    }
  },
  "tools": {
    "retrieval": {
      "disable_attribution": false,
      "vertex_rag_store": {
        "rag_resources": {
            "rag_corpus": "RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE"
          },
        "rag_retrieval_config": {
          "top_k": SIMILARITY_TOP_K,
          "ranking": {
            "rank_service": {
              "model_name": "RANKER_MODEL_NAME"
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}'

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

The LLM reranker supports only Gemini models, which are accessible when the Vertex AI RAG Engine API is enabled. To view the list of supported models, see Gemini models.

To retrieve relevant contexts using the Vertex AI RAG Engine API, do the following:

PythonREST

To learn how to install or update the Vertex AI SDK for Python, see Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python. For more information, see the Python API reference documentation.

Before you begin, replace the following variables:

  • PROJECT_ID: The ID of your Google Cloud project.
  • LOCATION: The region to process the request.
  • RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE: The name of the RAG corpus resource. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/ragCorpora/{rag_corpus}.
  • TEXT: The query text to get relevant contexts.
  • MODEL_NAME: The name of the model used for reranking.
from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

PROJECT_ID = "PROJECT_ID"
CORPUS_NAME = "projects/[PROJECT_ID]/locations/LOCATION/ragCorpora/RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE"
MODEL_NAME= "MODEL_NAME"

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="LOCATION")

rag_retrieval_config = rag.RagRetrievalConfig(
    top_k=10,
    ranking=rag.Ranking(
        llm_ranker=rag.LlmRanker(
            model_name=MODEL_NAME
        )
    )
)

response = rag.retrieval_query(
    rag_resources=[
        rag.RagResource(
            rag_corpus=CORPUS_NAME,
        )
    ],
    text="TEXT",
    rag_retrieval_config=rag_retrieval_config,
)
print(response)

#     source_uri: "gs://your-bucket-name/file.txt"
#     text: "....
#   ....

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Expand to see all prerequisites

Create a RAG corpus

All data must be imported into a RAG corpus. A corpus is a collection of RagFiles that structures and optimizes your data for retrieval. To create one, see Create a RAG corpus.

Grant permissions to the service account

To import files, the Vertex AI RAG Data Service Agent requires permissions to access the data source.

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the IAM page.

    Go to IAM

  2. Select the Include Google-provided role grants checkbox.

  3. Search for the Vertex AI RAG Data Service Agent service account. The service account is in the format service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-rag-data-service.iam.gserviceaccount.com.
  4. Grant this service account the necessary permissions for your chosen data source. For example:
    • Cloud Storage: Grant the Storage Object Viewer role on the bucket.
    • Google Drive: Share the Google Drive folder or file with the service account email address and grant it Viewer permission.
    • Secret Manager: If you are using data connectors for Slack, Jira, or SharePoint, grant the Secret Manager Secret Accessor role to the service account so it can access the API tokens stored in Secret Manager.

docs.title: Import files from a data source
docs.text:
After you have completed the prerequisites, you can import files from your chosen data source. Select one of the following tabs for detailed instructions.

Cloud Storage or Google DriveSlackJiraSharePoint

To import files from Cloud Storage or Google Drive, use the import_rag_files method and specify the Google Cloud Storage URI or Google Drive path in your request. For a complete code sample, see the ImportRagFiles API template.

The system automatically checks your file's path, filename, and version_id. The version_id is a hash calculated from the file's content, which prevents the same unchanged file from being re-indexed. If a file with the same name and path is updated, it will be re-indexed.

Step 1: Get your Slack channel ID and create an app
  1. Get your CHANNEL_ID from the Slack channel you want to import.
  2. Go to the Slack API page and create a new app.
Step 2: Configure app permissions
  1. From the Slack UI, in the Add features and functionality section, click Permissions.
  2. In the Bot Token Scopes section, add the following permissions:
    • channels:history
    • groups:history
    • im:history
    • mpim:history
  3. Click Install to Workspace to install the app into your Slack workspace.
Step 3: Get your API token and store it in Secret Manager
  1. After installing the app, copy the Bot User OAuth Token.
  2. Add this token as a new secret in Secret Manager.
Step 4: Import files from Slack

Use the following code samples to import files from your Slack channel. Replace the placeholder variables with your project and Slack information.

API_KEY_SECRET_VERSION=SLACK_API_KEY_SECRET_VERSION
CHANNEL_ID=SLACK_CHANNEL_ID
PROJECT_ID=us-central1

-d '{
  "import_rag_files_config": {
    "slack_source": {
      "channels": [
        {
          "apiKeyConfig": {
            "apiKeySecretVersion": "'"${ API_KEY_SECRET_VERSION }"'"
          },
          "channels": [
            {
              "channel_id": "'"${ CHANNEL_ID }"'"
            }
          ]

      ]
    }
  }
}'

docs.title: Understand import results
docs.text: This section explains how to interpret the results of an import job, including how data is deduplicated and how to track failures.

docs.title: Data deduplication
docs.text:
If the same file is imported multiple times with no changes, the file is skipped to avoid redundant processing. The response.skipped_rag_files_count in the API response indicates the number of files that were skipped.

A file is skipped if all of the following conditions are met: * The file has been imported previously. * The file content has not changed. * The chunking configuration for the file has not changed.

docs.title: Import failures
docs.text:
To understand why some files might fail to import, you can inspect the API response or configure a data sink to log detailed results.

  • Response metadata: The response.metadata object contains high-level information about the import job, including request and response times.

  • Import result sink: For detailed logging, you can specify an import_result_sink in your import request. This is an optional parameter that designates a destination for detailed logs of both successful and failed file imports. The sink must be a Cloud Storage path or a BigQuery table.

    • Cloud Storage sink: Provide a path in the format gs://my-bucket/my/object.ndjson. The object must not exist before the import. After the job completes, this object will contain one JSON object per line, detailing the operation ID, timestamp, filename, status, and file ID for each file.
    • BigQuery sink: Provide a table reference in the format bq://my-project.my-dataset.my-table. If the table does not exist, it will be created. If it exists, its schema will be verified.

docs.title: Use embedding models with Vertex AI RAG Engine
docs.text:
Preview

The VPC-SC security control is supported by RAG Engine. Data residency, CMEK, and AXT security controls aren't supported.

This page describes the choices of embedding models and shows you how to use your chosen embedding model to create a RAG corpus. The association between an embedding model and a RAG corpus is fixed for the lifetime of the corpus.

docs.title: Introduction to embeddings
docs.text:
Embeddings are numerical representations of data, such as text, images, or video. They work by converting these inputs into high-dimensional arrays of floating-point numbers called vectors.

By capturing the semantic meaning and relationships between inputs, embeddings enable computers to understand complex concepts. The closer two vectors are in the embedding space, the more similar their corresponding inputs are. For example, the text "dog" and "puppy" would have vector embeddings that are very close together, while the vector for "car" would be much farther away.

Embedding models are a critical component of semantic retrieval systems like RAG Engine. The performance of the retrieval system depends on how effectively the embedding model maps the relationships in your data.

docs.title: Embedding model choices
docs.text:
Vertex AI RAG Engine lets you choose from three types of embedding models for your RAG corpus. Use the following table to help you decide which model type is right for your use case.

Model Type Description Best for... Pros Cons Vertex AI publisher models Google-trained foundation models, such as Gecko. General-purpose tasks where a strong baseline model is sufficient. - No deployment required.- Easy to use.- Strong performance on a wide range of tasks. - Can be discontinued, requiring corpus migration.- Not customizable for domain-specific data. Fine-tuned models Vertex AI publisher models that you have tuned using your own data. Specialized tasks requiring domain-specific knowledge or highly tailored performance. - Unaffected by publisher model discontinuations.- Optimized for your specific data and use case. - Requires a separate tuning process.- Must be deployed to a Vertex AI endpoint, incurring costs. OSS models Third-party open-source software (OSS) models available in Model Garden. Scenarios requiring specific model architectures (e.g., E5) or non-English language support. - Access to a variety of model architectures.- You control the model lifecycle. - Must be deployed to a Vertex AI endpoint, incurring costs.- Performance may vary.

docs.text:
The following diagram shows the workflow for using an embedding model with RAG Engine.

docs.title: Create a RAG corpus
docs.text:
After you have chosen an embedding model, you can create a RAG corpus. The following examples show how to create a corpus with each type of model.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Use a publisher modelUse a fine-tuned modelUse an OSS model

Publisher models, like the Gecko models, are foundation models trained by Google. They provide a strong baseline for many tasks and are the easiest to use because they don't require deployment. The association between your embedding model and the RAG corpus remains fixed for the lifetime of your RAG corpus.

Supported publisher models

The following Gecko models are recommended for use with a RAG corpus:

Model version Description text-embedding-005 Default embedding model. Recommended for use with a RAG corpus. text-embedding-004 text-multilingual-embedding-002 Recommended for use with a RAG corpus.

Considerations for model discontinuation

If a publisher model is discontinued, it can no longer be used with RAG Engine, even for a corpus created before the discontinuation. In this event, you must migrate your RAG corpus by creating a new one with a supported model and re-importing your data. To avoid this, you can use a fine-tuned model or a self-deployed OSS model.

Code examples

These samples demonstrate how to create a RAG corpus with a publisher Gecko model.

cURLVertex AI SDK for Python 
ENDPOINT=us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com
PROJECT_ID=YOUR_PROJECT_ID

# Set this to your choice of publisher Gecko model. Note that the full resource name of the publisher model is required.
# Example: projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/text-embedding-004
PUBLISHER_MODEL="publishers/google/models/text-embedding-004"

# Set a display name for your corpus.
# For example, "my test corpus"
CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME="YOUR_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME"

# CreateRagCorpus
# Input: ENDPOINT, PROJECT_ID, PUBLISHER_MODEL, CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME
curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://${ENDPOINT}/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora \
-d '{
      "display_name" : '\""${CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME}"\"',
      "rag_embedding_model_config" : {
            "publisher_model": '\"'"${PUBLISHER_MODEL}"\"'
      }
}'

import vertexai
from vertexai import rag

# Set Project
PROJECT_ID = "YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

# Configure a Google first-party embedding model
embedding_model_config = rag.RagEmbeddingModelConfig(
      publisher_model="publishers/google/models/text-embedding-004"
)

# Name your corpus
DISPLAY_NAME = "YOUR_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME"

rag_corpus = rag.create_corpus(
      display_name=DISPLAY_NAME, rag_embedding_model_config=embedding_model_config
)

You can fine-tune a publisher text embedding model to improve its performance for a specific domain or task. After tuning, the model is owned by you and is unaffected by publisher model discontinuations. All fine-tuned Gecko embedding models produce embeddings with 768-dimensional vectors.

Before you can use a fine-tuned model, you must deploy it to a Vertex AI endpoint. For more information, see Tune text embeddings.

Code examples

These samples demonstrate how to create a RAG corpus with your deployed, fine-tuned model.

cURLVertex AI SDK for Python 
ENDPOINT=us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com
PROJECT_ID=YOUR_PROJECT_ID

# Your Vertex AI endpoint resource with the deployed fine-tuned Gecko model
# Example: projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/${LOCATION}/endpoints/${ENDPOINT_ID}
ENDPOINT_NAME="YOUR_ENDPOINT_NAME"

# Set a display name for your corpus.
# For example, "my test corpus"
CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME="YOUR_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME"

# CreateRagCorpus
# Input: ENDPOINT, PROJECT_ID, ENDPOINT_NAME, CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME
curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://${ENDPOINT}/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora \
-d '{
      "display_name" : '\""${CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME}"\"',
      "rag_embedding_model_config" : {
              "vertex_prediction_endpoint": {
                    "endpoint": '\""${ENDPOINT_NAME}"\"'
              }
      }
  }'

import vertexai

# Set Project

)

Before you can use an OSS model, you must deploy it from Model Garden to a Vertex AI endpoint. To deploy your E5 model, see E5 Text Embedding in the Google Cloud console.

    display_name=DISPLAY_NAME, rag_embedding_model_config=embedding_model_config
)

docs.title: Use Pinecone with Vertex AI RAG Engine
docs.text:
Preview

The VPC-SC security control is supported by RAG Engine. Data residency, CMEK, and AXT security controls aren't supported.

To see an example of using RAG Engine with Pinecone, run the "RAG Engine with Pinecone" Jupyter notebook in one of the following environments:

Open in Colab Open in Colab Enterprise Open in Vertex AI Workbench View on GitHub

This page shows you how to connect your RAG corpus to your Pinecone database.

You can use your Pinecone database instance with Vertex AI RAG Engine to index and conduct a vector-based similarity search. A similarity search finds pieces of text that are similar to your query by using an embedding model. The embedding model produces vector data for each piece of text, which is then used to retrieve semantic contexts for grounding and returning the most relevant content from your LLM.

With Vertex AI RAG Engine, you can continue to use your fully-managed Pinecone vector database, which you are responsible for provisioning and managing. Vertex AI RAG Engine uses your vector database for storage, index management, and search.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Prerequisites and considerations

Considerations for using Pinecone

Before connecting Pinecone to RAG Engine, review the following requirements and responsibilities:

  • You must create, configure, and manage the scaling of your Pinecone database instance.
  • Vertex AI RAG Engine uses the default namespace on your index. Ensure that this namespace isn't modified by other processes.
  • You must provide a Pinecone API key to allow RAG Engine to interact with your Pinecone database. RAG Engine does not store your Pinecone API key. Instead, you must:
    • Store your key in Google Cloud Secret Manager.
    • Grant your project's service account permissions to access the secret.
    • Provide RAG Engine with the secret's resource name.
  • Each RAG corpus has a one-to-one mapping with a Pinecone index. This association is made during the CreateRagCorpus or UpdateRagCorpus API call and is permanent.

Supported configurations

  • Embedding models and dimensions: When creating your Pinecone index, you must specify the embedding dimension that matches the model you intend to use with RAG Engine.
Model Dimension size First-party Gecko (text-embedding-004 and later) 768 Fine-tuned first-party Gecko 768 E5 See Use OSS embedding models. 
*   **Distance metrics**: Choose one of the following supported distance metrics for your index:
    *   `cosine`
    *   `dotproduct`
    *   `euclidean`

docs.title: How to connect RAG Engine to Pinecone
docs.text:
This section outlines the workflow for connecting your Pinecone index to Vertex AI RAG Engine.

flowchart LR
    A[Step 1: Create Pinecone index] --> B[Step 2: Create Pinecone API key]
    B --> C[Step 3: Provision RAG Engine service account]
    C --> D[Step 4: Store API key in Secret Manager]
    D --> E[Step 5: Create RAG corpus]

    click A "#create-pinecone-index"
    click B "#create-pinecone-api-key"
    click C "#provision-service-account"
    click D "#store-api-key"
    click E "#create-rag-corpus"
Step-by-step guide to connect Pinecone

Step 1: Create your Pinecone index

Follow the Pinecone quickstart guide to create and configure your index.

  • Location: To reduce latency and meet data residency requirements, create your Pinecone index in a location that is the same as or geographically close to where you use Vertex AI RAG Engine.
  • Metadata indexing: If you create a pod-based index, you must specify file_id on the pod.metadata_config.indexed field. For more information, see Selective metadata indexing.

Step 2: Create your Pinecone API key

RAG Engine requires an API key to authenticate to your Pinecone index. Follow the Pinecone authentication guide to create an API key in your Pinecone project.

Step 3: Provision your Vertex AI RAG Engine service account

When you create the first RAG corpus in your project, RAG Engine provisions a dedicated service account. You can find this service account on your project's Identity and Access Management (IAM) page.

The service account follows this format: service-{project-number}@gcp-sa-vertex-rag.iam.gserviceaccount.com

For example: service-123456789@gcp-sa-vertex-rag.iam.gserviceaccount.com

Step 4: Store your API key in Secret Manager

An API key is sensitive information. To protect it, you must store it in Secret Manager and grant the RAG Engine service account access to it.

  1. Store your API key in Secret Manager.
  2. Grant the RAG Engine service account permissions to access the secret:
    1. Navigate to your project's IAM page.
    2. Enable the option Include Google-provided role grants.
    3. Find the service account: service-{project-number}@gcp-sa-vertex-rag.iam.gserviceaccount.com.
    4. Edit the service account's principals.
    5. Add the Secret Manager Secret Accessor role to the service account.

Step 5: Create your RAG corpus

To use your Pinecone index, you must associate it with a RAG corpus. This binding is permanent. You can create the corpus with all the Pinecone details upfront or create it first and add the details later.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Create a corpus with full detailsCreate a corpus and add details later

Use this method if you have already provisioned your Pinecone index and stored your API key in Secret Manager.

To associate the corpus, set the following fields in your CreateRagCorpus request: * rag_vector_db_config.pinecone: Sets Pinecone as the vector database. * rag_vector_db_config.pinecone.index_name: The name of your Pinecone index. * rag_vector_db_config.api_auth.api_key_config.api_key_secret_version: The full resource name of the secret version containing your Pinecone API key, in the format projects/{PROJECT_NUMBER}/secrets/{SECRET_ID}/versions/{VERSION_ID}.

PythonREST

Before trying this sample, follow the Python setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Python API reference documentation.

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# pinecone_index_name = "pinecone-index-name"
# pinecone_api_key_secret_manager_version = "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/secrets/{SECRET_NAME}/versions/latest"
# display_name = "test_corpus"
# description = "Corpus Description"

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

# Configure embedding model (Optional)
embedding_model_config = rag.RagEmbeddingModelConfig(
    vertex_prediction_endpoint=rag.VertexPredictionEndpoint(
        publisher_model="publishers/google/models/text-embedding-004"
    )
)

# Configure Vector DB
vector_db = rag.Pinecone(
    index_name=pinecone_index_name,
    api_key=pinecone_api_key_secret_manager_version,
)

corpus = rag.create_corpus(
    display_name=display_name,
    description=description,
    backend_config=rag.RagVectorDbConfig(
        rag_embedding_model_config=embedding_model_config,
        vector_db=vector_db,
    ),
)
print(corpus)
# Example response:
# RagCorpus(name='projects/1234567890/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/1234567890',
# display_name='test_corpus', description='Corpus Description', embedding_model_config=...
# ...

# Set your project ID under which you want to create the corpus
PROJECT_ID="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"

# Choose a display name for your corpus
CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME="YOUR_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME"

# Set your Pinecone index name
PINECONE_INDEX_NAME="YOUR_INDEX_NAME"

# Set the full resource name of your secret. Follows the format
# projects/{PROJECT_NUMBER}/secrets/{SECRET_ID}/versions/{VERSION_ID}
SECRET_RESOURCE_NAME="YOUR_SECRET_RESOURCE_NAME"

# Call CreateRagCorpus API with all the Vector DB information.
curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora -d '{
      "display_name" : "'\""${CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME}"\"'",
      "rag_vector_db_config" : {
         "pinecone": {"index_name": "'\""${PINECONE_INDEX_NAME}"\"'"},
         "api_auth": {"api_key_config":
               {"api_key_secret_version": "'\""${SECRET_RESOURCE_NAME}"\"'"}
         }
      }
   }'

# To poll the status of your RAG corpus creation, get the operation_id returned in
# response of your CreateRagCorpus call.
OPERATION_ID="YOUR_OPERATION_ID"

# Poll Operation status until done = true in the response.
# The response to this call will contain the ID for your created RAG corpus
curl -X GET \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/operations/${OPERATION_ID}

If this is your first RAG corpus and you don't have the service account details yet, or if your Pinecone index is not ready, you can create the corpus first and update it with the required information later.

Considerations: * You cannot import files into the RAG corpus until you provide the index name and API key secret. * Once you choose Pinecone as the vector database, you cannot switch to a different database later.

PythonREST 
import vertexai
from vertexai.preview import rag

# Set Project
PROJECT_ID = "YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

# Configure the Pinecone vector DB information (empty for now)
vector_db = rag.Pinecone()

# Name your corpus
DISPLAY_NAME = "YOUR_CORPUS_NAME"

rag_corpus = rag.create_corpus(display_name=DISPLAY_NAME, vector_db=vector_db)
print(rag_corpus)

# Set your project ID under which you want to create the corpus
PROJECT_ID="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"

# Choose a display name for your corpus
CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME="YOUR_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME"

# Call CreateRagCorpus API with an empty Pinecone configuration.
curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora -d '{
      "display_name" : "'\""${CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME}"\"'",
      "rag_vector_db_config" : {
         "pinecone": {}
      }
   }'

# To poll the status of your RAG corpus creation, get the operation_id returned in
# response of your CreateRagCorpus call.
OPERATION_ID="YOUR_OPERATION_ID"

# Poll Operation status until done = true in the response.
# The response to this call will contain the ID for your created RAG corpus
curl -X GET \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/operations/${OPERATION_ID}

docs.title: Update your RAG corpus
docs.text:
You can use the UpdateRagCorpus API to add or change the vector database configuration. This is necessary if you created a corpus without providing the Pinecone index name and API key secret version.

Field Mutability Required or Optional rag_vector_db_config.vector_db Immutable after you make a choice. Required rag_vector_db_config.pinecone.index_name Immutable after you set the field on the RAG corpus. Required rag_vector_db_config.api_auth.api_key_config.api_key_secret_version Mutable. After you set the API key, you can't remove it. Optional PythonREST 
import vertexai
from vertexai.preview import rag

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# RAG_CORPUS_ID = "your-rag-corpus-id" # e.g., "1234567890"
# pinecone_index_name = "pinecone-index-name"
# pinecone_api_key_secret_manager_version = "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/secrets/{SECRET_NAME}/versions/latest"

vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

# Get the existing corpus
corpus = rag.get_corpus(RAG_CORPUS_ID)

# Configure the Pinecone vector DB information to update
vector_db = rag.Pinecone(
    index_name=pinecone_index_name,
    api_key=pinecone_api_key_secret_manager_version,
)

# Update the corpus
updated_corpus = corpus.update(
    backend_config=rag.RagVectorDbConfig(vector_db=vector_db)
)
print(updated_corpus)

# Set your project ID for the corpus that you want to update.
PROJECT_ID="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"

# Set the ID of the corpus to update
CORPUS_ID="YOUR_CORPUS_ID"

# Set your Pinecone index name
PINECONE_INDEX_NAME="YOUR_INDEX_NAME"

# Set the full resource name of your secret. Follows the format
# projects/{PROJECT_NUMBER}/secrets/{SECRET_ID}/versions/{VERSION_ID}
SECRET_RESOURCE_NAME="YOUR_SECRET_RESOURCE_NAME"

# Call UpdateRagCorpus API with the Vector DB information.
# The updateMask specifies which fields to update.
curl -X PATCH \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
"https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/${CORPUS_ID}?updateMask=ragVectorDbConfig" -d '{
      "rag_vector_db_config" : {
         "pinecone": {"index_name": "'\""${PINECONE_INDEX_NAME}"\"'"},
         "api_auth": {"api_key_config":
               {"api_key_secret_version": "'\""${SECRET_RESOURCE_NAME}"\"'"}
         }
      }
   }'

# To poll the status of your RAG corpus update, get the operation_id returned in
# the response of your UpdateRagCorpus call.
OPERATION_ID="YOUR_OPERATION_ID"

# Poll Operation status until done = true in the response.
curl -X GET \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/operations/${OPERATION_ID}

docs.title: Use Vertex AI RAG Engine in Gemini Live API
docs.text:
Preview

Some of the RAG features are Preview offerings, subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" of the Google Cloud Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA products and features may have limited support, and changes to Pre-GA products and features may not be compatible with other Pre-GA versions. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions. Further, by using the Gemini API on Vertex AI, you agree to the Generative AI Preview terms and conditions (Preview Terms).

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a technique used to enhance Large Language Model (LLM) responses by retrieving relevant, verifiable information from an external knowledge source. This allows the model to generate more accurate and grounded answers.

This page shows you how to use the Vertex AI RAG Engine with the Gemini Live API. You can use the RAG Engine in two primary ways: * For real-time retrieval: To query a RAG corpus for information during a live session. * As a context store: To save conversation history, creating a persistent memory for your application across multiple sessions.

The VPC-SC security control is supported by RAG Engine. Data residency, CMEK, and AXT security controls aren't supported.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
The following diagram shows the workflow for using the RAG Engine with the Gemini Live API.

flowchart LR
    A[Before you begin] --> B{Choose your use case};
    B -- Real-time retrieval --> C[Use RAG for real-time retrieval];
    B -- Context store --> D[Use RAG as a context store];

    click A "#before-you-begin"
    click B "#choose-your-rag-use-case"
    click C "#use-rag-for-real-time-retrieval"
    click D "#use-rag-as-a-context-store"

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Expand to see the prerequisites

The following prerequisites must be completed before you can use Vertex AI RAG Engine with the multimodal Live API:

  1. Enable the RAG API in Vertex AI.
  2. Create a RAG Corpus.
  3. To upload files to the RAG Corpus, see Import RAG files.

docs.title: Choose your RAG use case
docs.text:
You can integrate the RAG Engine with the Gemini Live API for two distinct purposes. The following table compares the two use cases to help you decide which approach best suits your needs.

Feature RAG for Real-Time Retrieval RAG as a Context Store Purpose Augment LLM responses with information from a pre-existing data corpus. Store and retrieve conversation history to provide memory across sessions. Corpus Type Standard RAG Corpus. MemoryCorpus type, specifically designed for conversation history. Setup Specify the RAG corpus as a retrieval tool. Specify the MemoryCorpus as a retrieval tool and set store_context=True. Use Case Answering questions based on a knowledge base (e.g., product manuals, internal wikis). Creating a chatbot with persistent memory of past interactions.

Follow the instructions in the corresponding tab for your chosen use case.

Use RAG for real-time retrievalUse RAG as a context store

This approach lets you specify and retrieve information from a standard RAG corpus to ground model responses in real time.

Step 1: Configure the RAG retrieval tool

To use the RAG Engine with the Live API, specify it as a tool in your configuration. The following code sample demonstrates how to define the RAG Engine as a retrieval tool.

Replace the following variables: * YOUR_PROJECT_ID: The ID of your Google Cloud project. * YOUR_CORPUS_ID: The ID of your corpus. * YOUR_LOCATION: The region to process the request (e.g., us-central1).

PROJECT_ID = "YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
RAG_CORPUS_ID = "YOUR_CORPUS_ID"
LOCATION = "YOUR_LOCATION"

TOOLS = {
  "retrieval": {
    "vertex_rag_store": {
    "rag_resources": {
          "rag_corpus": "projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/${LOCATION}/ragCorpora/${RAG_CORPUS_ID}"
        }
     }
  }
}

Step 2: Use WebSocket for real-time communication

To enable real-time communication between a client and a server, you must use a WebSocket. The following examples demonstrate how to connect using the Python API or the Python SDK.

Python APIPython SDK 
CONFIG = {"response_modalities": ["TEXT"], "speech_config": { "language_code": "en-US" }}
headers = {
  "Content-Type": "application/json",
  "Authorization": f"Bearer {bearer_token[0]}",
}
HOST= "${LOCATION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com"
SERVICE_URL = f"wss://{HOST}/ws/google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.LlmBidiService/BidiGenerateContent"
MODEL="gemini-2.0-flash-exp"

# Connect to the server
async with connect(SERVICE_URL, additional_headers=headers) as ws:
  # Setup the session
  await ws.send(
json.dumps(
          {
              "setup": {
                  "model": MODEL,
                  "generation_config": CONFIG,
                  # Setup RAG as a retrieval tool
                  "tools": TOOLS,
              }
          }
      )
  )

  # Receive setup response
  raw_response = await ws.recv(decode=False)
  setup_response = json.loads(raw_response.decode("ascii"))

  # Send text message
  text_input = "What are popular LLMs?"
  display(Markdown(f"**Input:** {text_input}"))

  msg = {
      "client_content": {
          "turns": [{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": text_input}]}],
          "turn_complete": True,
      }
  }

  await ws.send(json.dumps(msg))

  responses = []

  # Receive chunks of server response
  async for raw_response in ws:
      response = json.loads(raw_response.decode())
      server_content = response.pop("serverContent", None)
      if server_content is None:
          break

      model_turn = server_content.pop("modelTurn", None)
      if model_turn is not None:
          parts = model_turn.pop("parts", None)
          if parts is not None:
              display(Markdown(f"**parts >** {parts}"))
              responses.append(parts[0]["text"])

      # End of turn
      turn_complete = server_content.pop("turnComplete", None)
      if turn_complete:
          grounding_metadata = server_content.pop("groundingMetadata", None)
          if grounding_metadata is not None:
            grounding_chunks = grounding_metadata.pop("groundingChunks", None)
            if grounding_chunks is not None:
              for chunk in grounding_chunks:
                display(Markdown(f"**grounding_chunk >** {chunk}"))
          break

  # Print the server response
  display(Markdown(f"**Response >** {''.join(responses)}"))

To learn how to install the generative AI SDK, see Install a library.

from google import genai
from google.genai import types
from google.genai.types import (Content, LiveConnectConfig, HttpOptions, Modality, Part,)
from IPython import display

MODEL="gemini-2.0-flash-exp"

client = genai.Client(
  vertexai=True,
  project=PROJECT_ID,
  location=LOCATION
)

async with client.aio.live.connect(
  model=MODEL,
  config=LiveConnectConfig(response_modalities=[Modality.TEXT],
                            tools=TOOLS),
) as session:
  text_input = "\'What are core LLM techniques?\'"
  print("> ", text_input, "\n")
  await session.send_client_content(
      turns=Content(role="user", parts=[Part(text=text_input)])
  )

  async for message in session.receive()
      if message.text:
          display.display(display.Markdown(message.text))
          continue

You can use the RAG Engine as a context store for the Gemini Live API. This allows you to store session context (such as text and audio speech) to form and retrieve past contexts related to your conversation. This enriches the current context for model generation and enables you to share context across different Live API sessions.

Step 1: Create a MemoryCorpus type corpus

To store and index conversation texts from the session context, you must create a RAG corpus of the MemoryCorpus type. You must also specify an LLM parser in your memory corpus configuration, which is used to parse session contexts stored from the Live API to build memory for indexing.

Replace the following variables before running the code: * YOUR_EMBEDDING_MODEL: The embedding model to use, such as "publishers/google/models/text-embedding-005". * YOUR_MEMORY_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME: A display name for your memory corpus. * YOUR_LLM_PARSER_MODEL_NAME: The LLM parser model, such as "projects/{project_id}/locations/{location}/publishers/google/models/gemini-2.5-pro-preview-05-06".

# Currently supports Google first-party embedding models
EMBEDDING_MODEL = YOUR_EMBEDDING_MODEL
MEMORY_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME = YOUR_MEMORY_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME
LLM_PARSER_MODEL_NAME = YOUR_LLM_PARSER_MODEL_NAME

memory_corpus = rag.create_corpus(
   display_name=MEMORY_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME,
   corpus_type_config=rag.RagCorpusTypeConfig(
       corpus_type_config=rag.MemoryCorpus(
           llm_parser=rag.LlmParserConfig(
               model_name=LLM_PARSER_MODEL_NAME,
           )
       )
   ),
   backend_config=rag.RagVectorDbConfig(
       rag_embedding_model_config=rag.RagEmbeddingModelConfig(
           vertex_prediction_endpoint=rag.VertexPredictionEndpoint(
               publisher_model=EMBEDDING_MODEL
           )
       )
   ),
)

Step 2: Specify your memory corpus to store contexts

When using your memory corpus with the Live API, you must specify it as a retrieval tool and set store_context to true. This allows the Live API to store the session contexts in your MemoryCorpus.

Replace the following variables before running the code: * YOUR_PROJECT_ID: The ID of your Google Cloud project. * YOUR_LOCATION: The region to process the request (e.g., us-central1). * YOUR_TEXT_INPUT: The initial text input for the conversation. * YOUR_MODEL_NAME: The model to use, such as "gemini-2.0-flash-exp".

from google import genai
from google.genai import types
from google.genai.types import (Content, LiveConnectConfig, HttpOptions, Modality, Part)
from IPython import display

PROJECT_ID=YOUR_PROJECT_ID
LOCATION=YOUR_LOCATION
TEXT_INPUT=YOUR_TEXT_INPUT
MODEL_NAME=YOUR_MODEL_NAME

client = genai.Client(
   vertexai=True,
   project=PROJECT_ID,
   location=LOCATION,
)

memory_store=types.VertexRagStore(
   rag_resources=[
       types.VertexRagStoreRagResource(
           rag_corpus=memory_corpus.name
       )
   ],
   store_context=True
)

async with client.aio.live.connect(
   model=MODEL_NAME,
   config=LiveConnectConfig(response_modalities=[Modality.TEXT],
                            tools=[types.Tool(
                                retrieval=types.Retrieval(
                                    vertex_rag_store=memory_store))]),
) as session:
   text_input=TEXT_INPUT
   await session.send_client_content(
       turns=Content(role="user", parts=[Part(text=text_input)])
   )

   async for message in session.receive():
       if message.text:
           display.display(display.Markdown(message.text))
           continue

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Use RagManagedDb with Vertex AI RAG Engine
docs.text:
Preview

The VPC-SC security control is supported by RAG Engine. Data residency, CMEK, and AXT security controls aren't supported.

This page introduces you to RagManagedDb and shows you how to manage its retrieval strategy and tier configuration.

Vertex AI RAG Engine uses RagManagedDb, an enterprise-ready vector database, to store and manage vector representations of your documents. The vector database retrieves relevant documents based on their semantic similarity to a given query.

flowchart LR
    A[Choose a retrieval strategy] --> B[Create a RAG corpus]
    B --> C[Import data into an ANN RagManagedDb]
    C --> D[Manage your tier]

click A "#choose-a-retrieval-strategy"
click B "#create-a-rag-corpus"
click C "#import-data-into-an-ann-ragmanageddb"
click D "#manage-your-tier"

docs.title: Choose a retrieval strategy
docs.text:
RagManagedDb offers two retrieval strategies to support your RAG use cases: k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and Approximate Nearest Neighbors (ANN). Use the following table to decide which strategy is best for your needs.

Strategy Description Best for k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) (Default) Finds the exact nearest neighbors by comparing all data points in your RAG corpus. This strategy ensures perfect recall (1.0). - Recall-sensitive applications.- Small to medium-sized RAG corpora (less than 10,000 files). Approximate Nearest Neighbors (ANN) Uses approximation techniques to find similar neighbors faster than KNN. This significantly reduces query latency on large corpora at the cost of slightly lower recall. - Large-scale RAG corpora (more than 10,000 files).- Use cases where improved query performance is an acceptable tradeoff for a minor loss in recall.

docs.title: Create a RAG corpus
docs.text:
After choosing a retrieval strategy, create a RAG corpus configured for that strategy.

Create a RAG corpus with KNNCreate a RAG corpus with ANN

The following code sample demonstrates how to create a RAG corpus using the default KNN retrieval strategy.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

PythonREST 
from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

PROJECT_ID = YOUR_PROJECT_ID
LOCATION = YOUR_RAG_ENGINE_LOCATION
DISPLAY_NAME = YOUR_RAG_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location=LOCATION)

vector_db = rag.RagManagedDb(retrieval_strategy=rag.KNN())
rag_corpus = rag.create_corpus(
    display_name=DISPLAY_NAME, backend_config=rag.RagVectorDbConfig(vector_db=vector_db))

Replace the following variables: * PROJECT_ID: Your project ID. * LOCATION: The region to process the request. * CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME: The display name of the RAG corpus.

PROJECT_ID=PROJECT_ID
LOCATION=LOCATION
CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME=CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME

curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://${LOCATION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/${LOCATION}/ragCorpora \
-d '{
      "display_name" : '\""${CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME}"\"',
      "vector_db_config": {
        "ragManagedDb": {
          "knn": {}
        }
      }
    }'

To use the ANN feature, RagManagedDb uses a tree-based structure to partition data for faster searches. To optimize recall and latency, you can configure the tree_depth and leaf_count of this tree based on your data size and distribution.

  • tree_depth: Determines the number of layers in the tree.

    • For approximately 10,000 RAG files, set the value to 2 (default).
    • For more than 10,000 RAG files, set the value to 3.

  • leaf_count: Determines the number of leaf nodes in the tree.

    • The recommended value is 10 * sqrt(number of RAG files).
    • If not specified, the default value is 500.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

PythonREST 
from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

PROJECT_ID = YOUR_PROJECT_ID
LOCATION = YOUR_RAG_ENGINE_LOCATION
DISPLAY_NAME = YOUR_RAG_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME
TREE_DEPTH = YOUR_TREE_DEPTH # Optional: Acceptable values are 2 or 3. Default is 2.
LEAF_COUNT = YOUR_LEAF_COUNT # Optional: Default is 500.

ann_config = rag.ANN(tree_depth=TREE_DEPTH, leaf_count=LEAF_COUNT)
vector_db = rag.RagManagedDb(retrieval_strategy=ann_config)
rag_corpus = rag.create_corpus(
    display_name=DISPLAY_NAME, backend_config=rag.RagVectorDbConfig(vector_db=vector_db))

Replace the following variables: * PROJECT_ID: Your project ID. * LOCATION: The region to process the request. * CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME: The display name of the RAG corpus. * TREE_DEPTH: Your tree depth. * LEAF_COUNT: Your leaf count.

PROJECT_ID=PROJECT_ID
LOCATION=LOCATION
CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME=CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME
TREE_DEPTH=TREE_DEPTH
LEAF_COUNT=LEAF_COUNT

curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://${LOCATION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/${LOCATION}/ragCorpora \
-d '{
      "display_name" : '\""${CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME}"\"',
      "vector_db_config": {
        "ragManagedDb": {
          "ann": {
            "tree_depth": '"${TREE_DEPTH}"',
            "leaf_count": '"${LEAF_COUNT}"'
          }
        }
      }
    }'

docs.title: Import data into an ANN RagManagedDb
docs.text:
You can use either the ImportRagFiles API or the UploadRagFile API to import your data. Unlike the KNN strategy, the ANN approach requires the underlying tree-based index to be rebuilt for optimal recall.

Important considerations: 1. You must rebuild the ANN index at least once before you can query the RAG corpus. 2. Only one concurrent index rebuild is supported per project in each location.

To have Vertex AI RAG Engine rebuild your ANN index, set rebuild_ann_index to true in your ImportRagFiles API request.

The following code sample demonstrates how to import data from Cloud Storage and trigger an ANN index rebuild. For information on other supported data sources, see Data sources supported for RAG.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

PythonREST 
from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

PROJECT_ID = YOUR_PROJECT_ID
LOCATION = YOUR_RAG_ENGINE_LOCATION
CORPUS_ID = YOUR_CORPUS_ID
PATHS = ["gs://my_bucket/my_files_dir"]
REBUILD_ANN_INDEX = REBUILD_ANN_INDEX # Choose true or false.

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location=LOCATION)

corpus_name = f"projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/{LOCATION}/ragCorpora/{CORPUS_ID}"
# This is a non blocking call.
response = await rag.import_files_async(
    corpus_name=corpus_name,
    paths=PATHS,
    rebuild_ann_index=REBUILD_ANN_INDEX
)

# Wait for the import to complete.
await response.result()

GCS_URI=GCS_URI
REBUILD_ANN_INDEX=<true/false>

curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://${LOCATION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/${LOCATION}/ragCorpora/${CORPUS_ID}/ragFiles:import \
-d '{
  "import_rag_files_config": {
    "gcs_source": {
      "uris": '\""${GCS_URI}"\"',
      },
    "rebuild_ann_index": '${REBUILD_ANN_INDEX}'
  }
}'

docs.title: Manage your tier
docs.text:
Vertex AI RAG Engine lets you scale your RagManagedDb instance using one of two tiers. The tier is a project-level setting that impacts all RAG corpora using RagManagedDb.

Tier Description Best for Enterprise tier (Default) Offers production-scale performance with auto-scaling functionality. - Large amounts of data.- Performance-sensitive workloads. Basic tier A cost-effective, low-compute tier. - Experimenting with RagManagedDb.- Small data sizes.- Latency-insensitive workloads.

Use the GetRagEngineConfig and UpdateRagEngineConfig APIs to manage your tier settings.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Read your RagEngineConfig

The following sample demonstrates how to read your current RagEngineConfig.

PythonREST 
from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

PROJECT_ID = "PROJECT_ID"
LOCATION = "LOCATION"

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location=LOCATION)

rag_engine_config = rag.rag_data.get_rag_engine_config(
    name=f"projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/{LOCATION}/ragEngineConfig"
)

print(rag_engine_config)

Replace the following variables: * PROJECT_ID: Your project ID. * LOCATION: The region to process the request.

curl -X GET \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
https://${LOCATION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/${LOCATION}/ragEngineConfig
Update your RagEngineConfig to the Enterprise tier

The following code sample demonstrates how to set the RagEngineConfig to the Enterprise tier.

LOCATION = "LOCATION"

vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location=LOCATION)

rag_engine_config_name=f"projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/{LOCATION}/ragEngineConfig"

new_rag_engine_config = rag.RagEngineConfig(
    name=rag_engine_config_name,
    rag_managed_db_config=rag.RagManagedDbConfig(tier=rag.Enterprise()),
)

updated_rag_engine_config = rag.rag_data.update_rag_engine_config(
    rag_engine_config=new_rag_engine_config
)

print(updated_rag_engine_config)

Replace the following variables: * PROJECT_ID: Your project ID. * LOCATION: The region to process the request.

https://${LOCATION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/${LOCATION}/ragEngineConfig -d "{'ragManagedDbConfig': {'enterprise': {}}}"

docs.title: Benefits of using Vertex AI Search with RAG Engine
docs.text:
Vertex AI Search provides a powerful solution for retrieving and managing data within your Vertex AI RAG applications. Using Vertex AI Search as your retrieval backend can improve performance, scalability, and ease of integration.

  • Enhanced performance and scalability: Vertex AI Search is designed to handle large volumes of data with low latency. This translates to faster response times and improved performance for your RAG applications, especially when dealing with extensive knowledge bases.
  • Simplified data management: You can import data from various sources, such as websites, BigQuery datasets, and Cloud Storage buckets, which streamlines your data ingestion process.
  • Seamless integration: Vertex AI provides built-in integration with Vertex AI Search, which lets you select it as the corpus backend for your RAG application. This simplifies the integration process and ensures optimal compatibility.
  • Improved LLM output quality: The advanced retrieval capabilities of Vertex AI Search ensure that your RAG application retrieves the most relevant information from your corpus, leading to more accurate and informative LLM-generated outputs.

docs.title: Configure Vertex AI Search
docs.text:
Vertex AI Search combines deep information retrieval, natural language processing, and the latest LLM features to understand user intent and return the most relevant results. To use it with RAG Engine, you first need to set up a search application with your data.

To set up Vertex AI Search, do the following:

  1. Create a search data store.
  2. Create a search application.

With Vertex AI Search, you can build a Google-quality search application using data that you control.

docs.title: Create a RAG corpus
docs.text:
After setting up Vertex AI Search, create a RAG corpus that points to your Vertex AI Search serving configuration.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

RESTPython

To use the command line to create a RAG corpus, you first submit a creation request and then monitor the operation's progress.

Step 1: Create a RAG corpus

Replace the following variables in the code sample:

  • PROJECT_ID: The ID of your Google Cloud project.
  • LOCATION: The region to process the request (for example, us-central1).
  • DISPLAY_NAME: The display name of the RAG corpus you want to create.
  • ENGINE_NAME: The full resource name of the Vertex AI Search engine or Datastore.
curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
"https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/ragCorpora" \
-d '{
  "display_name" : "DISPLAY_NAME",
  "vertex_ai_search_config" : {
    "serving_config": "ENGINE_NAME/servingConfigs/default_search"
  }
}'
Step 2: Monitor progress

Replace the following variables in the code sample:

  • PROJECT_ID: The ID of your Google Cloud project.
  • LOCATION: The region where the request is processed.
  • OPERATION_ID: The ID of the RAG corpus creation operation, returned from the previous step.
curl -X GET \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
"https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/operations/OPERATION_ID"

Before trying this sample, follow the Python setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Python API reference documentation.

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# vertex_ai_search_engine_name = "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/{LOCATION}/collections/default_collection/engines/{ENGINE_ID}"
# display_name = "test_corpus"
# description = "Corpus Description"

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

# Configure Search
vertex_ai_search_config = rag.VertexAiSearchConfig(
    serving_config=f"{vertex_ai_search_engine_name}/servingConfigs/default_search",
)

corpus = rag.create_corpus(
    display_name=display_name,
    description=description,
    vertex_ai_search_config=vertex_ai_search_config,
)
print(corpus)
# Example response:
# RagCorpus(name='projects/1234567890/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/1234567890',
# display_name='test_corpus', description='Corpus Description'.
# ...

docs.title: Retrieve contexts
docs.text:
After the RAG corpus is created, you can retrieve relevant contexts from Vertex AI Search through the RetrieveContexts API.

Troubleshooting

RESTPython

This code sample demonstrates how to retrieve contexts using REST.

Replace the following variables in the code sample:

  • PROJECT_ID: The ID of your Google Cloud project.
  • LOCATION: The region to process the request.
  • RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE: The name of the RAG corpus resource. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/ragCorpora/{rag_corpus}.
  • TEXT: The query text to get relevant contexts.
curl -X POST \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
"https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION:retrieveContexts" \
  -d '{
    "vertex_rag_store": {
      "rag_resources": {
        "rag_corpus": "RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE"
      }
    },
    "query": {
      "text": "TEXT"
    }
  }'

docs.title: Generate content
docs.text:
To generate content using Gemini models, call the Vertex AI GenerateContent API. By specifying the RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE in the request, the API automatically retrieves data from Vertex AI Search to ground the model's response.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

RESTPython

Replace the following variables in the sample code:

  • PROJECT_ID: The ID of your Google Cloud project.
  • LOCATION: The region to process the request.
  • MODEL_ID: The LLM model for content generation (for example, gemini-1.0-pro).
  • GENERATION_METHOD: The LLM method for content generation (for example, generateContent or streamGenerateContent).
  • INPUT_PROMPT: The text prompt to send to the LLM. Use a prompt relevant to the documents in your Vertex AI Search data store.
  • RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE: The name of the RAG corpus resource. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/ragCorpora/{rag_corpus}.
  • SIMILARITY_TOP_K: Optional: The number of top contexts to retrieve.
curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
"https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:GENERATION_METHOD" \
-d '{
  "contents": {
    "role": "user",
    "parts": {
      "text": "INPUT_PROMPT"
    }
  },
  "tools": {
    "retrieval": {
      "disable_attribution": false,
      "vertex_rag_store": {
        "rag_resources": {
            "rag_corpus": "RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE"
          },
        "similarity_top_k": SIMILARITY_TOP_K
      }
    }
  }
}'

To learn how to install or update the Vertex AI SDK for Python, see Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python. For more information, see the Vertex AI SDK for Python API reference documentation.

from vertexai import rag
from vertexai.generative_models import GenerativeModel, Tool
import vertexai

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# corpus_name = "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/{rag_corpus_id}"

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

rag_retrieval_tool = Tool.from_retrieval(
    retrieval=rag.Retrieval(
        source=rag.VertexRagStore(
            rag_resources=[
                rag.RagResource(
                    rag_corpus=corpus_name,
                    # Optional: supply IDs from `rag.list_files()`.
                    # rag_file_ids=["rag-file-1", "rag-file-2", ...],
                )
            ],
            rag_retrieval_config=rag.RagRetrievalConfig(
                top_k=10,
                filter=rag.utils.resources.Filter(vector_distance_threshold=0.5),
            ),
        ),
    )
)

rag_model = GenerativeModel(
    model_name="gemini-1.0-pro-002", tools=[rag_retrieval_tool]

response = rag_model.generate_content("Why is the sky blue?")
print(response.text)

docs.title: Before you begin: Set up Vertex AI Vector Search
docs.text:
Steps to set up Vertex AI Vector Search

Vertex AI Vector Search is based on vector search technology developed by Google research. With Vector Search, you can use the same infrastructure that provides a foundation for Google products such as Google Search, YouTube, and Google Play.

To integrate with Vertex AI RAG Engine, an empty Vector Search index is required.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

1. Create a Vector Search index

To create a Vector Search index that's compatible with your RAG Corpus, the index must meet the following criteria:

  • IndexUpdateMethod must be STREAM_UPDATE. See Create a stream update index.
  • Distance measure type must be explicitly set to either DOT_PRODUCT_DISTANCE or COSINE_DISTANCE.
  • The dimension of the vector must be consistent with the embedding model you plan to use in the RAG corpus.
Python

To learn how to install or update the Vertex AI SDK for Python, see Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python. For more information, see the Vertex AI SDK for Python API reference documentation.

def vector_search_create_streaming_index(
    project: str, location: str, display_name: str, gcs_uri: Optional[str] = None
) -> aiplatform.MatchingEngineIndex:
    """Create a vector search index.

    Args:
        project (str): Required. Project ID
        location (str): Required. The region name
        display_name (str): Required. The index display name
        gcs_uri (str): Optional. The Google Cloud Storage uri for index content

    Returns:
        The created MatchingEngineIndex.
    """
    # Initialize the Vertex AI client
    aiplatform.init(project=project, location=location)

    # Create Index
    index = aiplatform.MatchingEngineIndex.create_tree_ah_index(
        display_name=display_name,
        contents_delta_uri=gcs_uri,
        description="Matching Engine Index",
        dimensions=100,
        approximate_neighbors_count=150,
        leaf_node_embedding_count=500,
        leaf_nodes_to_search_percent=7,
        index_update_method="STREAM_UPDATE",  # Options: STREAM_UPDATE, BATCH_UPDATE
        distance_measure_type=aiplatform.matching_engine.matching_engine_index_config.DistanceMeasureType.DOT_PRODUCT_DISTANCE,
    )

    return index

2. Create a Vector Search index endpoint

Vertex AI RAG Engine supports public endpoints.

Python

To learn how to install or update the Vertex AI SDK for Python, see Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python. For more information, see the Vertex AI SDK for Python API reference documentation.

def vector_search_create_index_endpoint(
    project: str, location: str, display_name: str
) -> None:
    """Create a vector search index endpoint.

    Args:
        project (str): Required. Project ID
        location (str): Required. The region name
        display_name (str): Required. The index endpoint display name
    """
    # Initialize the Vertex AI client
    aiplatform.init(project=project, location=location)

    # Create Index Endpoint
    index_endpoint = aiplatform.MatchingEngineIndexEndpoint.create(
        display_name=display_name,
        public_endpoint_enabled=True,
        description="Matching Engine Index Endpoint",
    )

    print(index_endpoint.name)

3. Deploy an index to an index endpoint

Before you can perform a nearest neighbor search, the index must be deployed to an index endpoint.

Python

To learn how to install or update the Vertex AI SDK for Python, see Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python. For more information, see the Vertex AI SDK for Python API reference documentation.

def vector_search_deploy_index(
    project: str,
    location: str,
    index_name: str,
    index_endpoint_name: str,
    deployed_index_id: str,
) -> None:
    """Deploy a vector search index to a vector search index endpoint.

    Args:
        project (str): Required. Project ID
        location (str): Required. The region name
        index_name (str): Required. The index to update. A fully-qualified index
          resource name or a index ID.  Example:
          "projects/123/locations/us-central1/indexes/my_index_id" or
          "my_index_id".
        index_endpoint_name (str): Required. Index endpoint to deploy the index
          to.
        deployed_index_id (str): Required. The user specified ID of the
          DeployedIndex.
    """
    # Initialize the Vertex AI client
    aiplatform.init(project=project, location=location)

    # Create the index instance from an existing index
    index = aiplatform.MatchingEngineIndex(index_name=index_name)

    # Create the index endpoint instance from an existing endpoint.
    index_endpoint = aiplatform.MatchingEngineIndexEndpoint(
        index_endpoint_name=index_endpoint_name
    )

    # Deploy Index to Endpoint
    index_endpoint = index_endpoint.deploy_index(
        index=index, deployed_index_id=deployed_index_id
    )

    print(index_endpoint.deployed_indexes)

If it's the first time that you're deploying an index to an index endpoint, it takes approximately 30 minutes to automatically build and initiate the backend before the index can be stored. After the first deployment, subsequent deployments are ready in seconds. To see the status of the index deployment, go to the Vector Search Console, select the Index endpoints tab, and choose your index endpoint.

Go to the Vector Search Console

Identify the resource name of your index and index endpoint, which have the following formats:

  • projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/${LOCATION_ID}/indexes/${INDEX_ID}
  • projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/${LOCATION_ID}/indexEndpoints/${INDEX_ENDPOINT_ID}

docs.title: Use Vertex AI Vector Search in RAG Engine
docs.text:
After the Vector Search instance is set up, follow these steps to set the Vector Search instance as the vector database for the RAG application.

Steps to use Vector Search in RAG Engine

1. Create a RAG corpus

When you create the RAG corpus, specify the full INDEX_ENDPOINT_NAME and INDEX_NAME. Make sure to use the numeric ID for both index and index endpoint resource names. The RAG corpus is created and automatically associated with the Vector Search index. Validations are performed on the criteria. If any of the requirements aren't met, the request is rejected.

PythonREST

Before trying this sample, follow the Python setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# vector_search_index_name = "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/{LOCATION}/indexes/{INDEX_ID}"
# vector_search_index_endpoint_name = "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/{LOCATION}/indexEndpoints/{INDEX_ENDPOINT_ID}"
# display_name = "test_corpus"
# description = "Corpus Description"

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

# Configure embedding model (Optional)
embedding_model_config = rag.RagEmbeddingModelConfig(
    vertex_prediction_endpoint=rag.VertexPredictionEndpoint(
        publisher_model="publishers/google/models/text-embedding-005"
    )
)

# Configure Vector DB
vector_db = rag.VertexVectorSearch(
    index=vector_search_index_name, index_endpoint=vector_search_index_endpoint_name
)

corpus = rag.create_corpus(
    display_name=display_name,
    description=description,
    backend_config=rag.RagVectorDbConfig(
        rag_embedding_model_config=embedding_model_config,
        vector_db=vector_db,
    ),
)
print(corpus)
# Example response:
# RagCorpus(name='projects/1234567890/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/1234567890',
# display_name='test_corpus', description='Corpus Description', embedding_model_config=...
# ...

  # TODO(developer): Update and un-comment the following lines:
  # CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME = "YOUR_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME"
  # Full index/indexEndpoint resource name
  # Index: projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/${LOCATION_ID}/indexes/${INDEX_ID}
  # IndexEndpoint: projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/${LOCATION_ID}/indexEndpoints/${INDEX_ENDPOINT_ID}
  # INDEX_RESOURCE_NAME = "YOUR_INDEX_ENDPOINT_RESOURCE_NAME"
  # INDEX_NAME = "YOUR_INDEX_RESOURCE_NAME"
  # Call CreateRagCorpus API to create a new RagCorpus
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://${LOCATION_ID}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/${LOCATION_ID}/ragCorpora -d '{
        "display_name" : '\""${CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME}"\"',
        "rag_vector_db_config" : {
                "vertex_vector_search": {
                  "index":'\""${INDEX_NAME}"\"'
              "index_endpoint":'\""${INDEX_ENDPOINT_NAME}"\"'
                }
          }
    }'

  # Call ListRagCorpora API to verify the RagCorpus is created successfully
  curl -sS -X GET \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  "https://${LOCATION_ID}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/${LOCATION_ID}/ragCorpora"

2. Import files

Use the ImportRagFiles API to import files from Cloud Storage or Google Drive into the Vector Search index. The files are embedded and stored in the Vector Search index.

PythonREST 
from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# corpus_name = "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/{rag_corpus_id}"
# paths = ["https://drive.google.com/file/123", "gs://my_bucket/my_files_dir"]  # Supports Google Cloud Storage and Google Drive Links

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

response = rag.import_files(
    corpus_name=corpus_name,
    paths=paths,
    transformation_config=rag.TransformationConfig(
        rag.ChunkingConfig(chunk_size=512, chunk_overlap=100)
    ),
    import_result_sink="gs://sample-existing-folder/sample_import_result_unique.ndjson",  # Optional, this has to be an existing storage bucket folder, and file name has to be unique (non-existent).
    max_embedding_requests_per_min=900,  # Optional
)
print(f"Imported {response.imported_rag_files_count} files.")
# Example response:
# Imported 2 files.

# TODO(developer): Update and uncomment the following lines:
# RAG_CORPUS_ID = "your-rag-corpus-id"
#
# Google Cloud Storage bucket/file location.
# For example, "gs://rag-fos-test/"
# GCS_URIS= "your-gcs-uris"

# Call ImportRagFiles API to embed files and store in the BigQuery table
curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/${RAG_CORPUS_ID}/ragFiles:import \
-d '{
  "import_rag_files_config": {
    "gcs_source": {
      "uris": '\""${GCS_URIS}"\"'
    },
    "rag_file_chunking_config": {
      "chunk_size": 512
    }
  }
}'

# Call ListRagFiles API to verify the files are imported successfully
curl -X GET \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/${RAG_CORPUS_ID}/ragFiles

3. Retrieve relevant contexts or generate content

After the file import is complete, you can either retrieve relevant contexts from the Vector Search index using the RetrieveContexts API or generate content directly using the Gemini API, which will retrieve data from the index automatically.

Retrieve relevant contexts

PythonREST 
from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# corpus_name = "projects/[PROJECT_ID]/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/[rag_corpus_id]"

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

response = rag.retrieval_query(
    rag_resources=[
        rag.RagResource(
            rag_corpus=corpus_name,
            # Optional: supply IDs from `rag.list_files()`.
            # rag_file_ids=["rag-file-1", "rag-file-2", ...],
        )
    ],
    text="Hello World!",
    rag_retrieval_config=rag.RagRetrievalConfig(
        top_k=10,
        filter=rag.utils.resources.Filter(vector_distance_threshold=0.5),
    ),
)
print(response)
# Example response:
# contexts {
#   contexts {
#     source_uri: "gs://your-bucket-name/file.txt"
#     text: "....
#   ....

# TODO(developer): Update and uncomment the following lines:
# RETRIEVAL_QUERY="your-retrieval-query"
#
# Full RAG corpus resource name
# Format:
# "projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/${RAG_CORPUS_ID}"
# RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE="your-rag-corpus-resource"

# Call RetrieveContexts API to retrieve relevant contexts
curl -X POST \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/us-central1:retrieveContexts \
  -d '{
    "vertex_rag_store": {
      "rag_resources": {
          "rag_corpus": '\""${RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE}"\"',
        },
    },
    "query": {
      "text": '\""${RETRIEVAL_QUERY}"\"',
      "similarity_top_k": 10
    }
  }'

Generate content using Vertex AI Gemini API

To generate content using Gemini models, make a call to the Vertex AI GenerateContent API. By specifying the RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE in the request, the API automatically retrieves data from the Vector Search index.

PythonREST 
from vertexai import rag
from vertexai.generative_models import GenerativeModel, Tool
import vertexai

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# corpus_name = "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/{rag_corpus_id}"

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

rag_retrieval_tool = Tool.from_retrieval(
    retrieval=rag.Retrieval(
        source=rag.VertexRagStore(
            rag_resources=[
                rag.RagResource(
                    rag_corpus=corpus_name,
                    # Optional: supply IDs from `rag.list_files()`.
                    # rag_file_ids=["rag-file-1", "rag-file-2", ...],
                )
            ],
            rag_retrieval_config=rag.RagRetrievalConfig(
                top_k=10,
                filter=rag.utils.resources.Filter(vector_distance_threshold=0.5),
            ),
        ),
    )
)

rag_model = GenerativeModel(
    model_name="gemini-2.0-flash-001", tools=[rag_retrieval_tool]
)
response = rag_model.generate_content("Why is the sky blue?")
print(response.text)
# Example response:
#   The sky appears blue due to a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering.
#   Sunlight, which contains all colors of the rainbow, is scattered
#   by the tiny particles in the Earth's atmosphere....
#   ...

# TODO(developer): Update and uncomment the following lines:
# MODEL_ID=gemini-2.0-flash
# GENERATE_CONTENT_PROMPT="your-generate-content-prompt"

# GenerateContent with contexts retrieved from the FeatureStoreOnline index
curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json"  https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/${MODEL_ID}:generateContent \
-d '{
  "contents": {
    "role": "user",
    "parts": {
      "text": '\""${GENERATE_CONTENT_PROMPT}"\"'
    }
  },
  "tools": {
    "retrieval": {
      "vertex_rag_store": {
        "rag_resources": {
            "rag_corpus": '\""${RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE}"\"',
          },
        "similarity_top_k": 8,
        "vector_distance_threshold": 0.32
      }
    }
  }
}'
