docs.title: Step 3: Create a load balancer
docs.text:
In this step, you create an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic to backend instances hosted on Cloud Run. In the load balancer configuration, you define routing rules, which determine how the load balancer directs traffic. Routing rules include host rules and path matches, which constitute the configuration components of an external Application Load Balancer's URL map.

Note that to complete this step, you must have a valid domain name or a valid self-managed certificate.

    B --> C[Configure Backend]

docs.title: Create a load balancer for the Cloud Run service
docs.text:
Steps to create a load balancer

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Load balancing page.

    Go to Load balancing

  2. Click Create load balancer.

  3. In the Type of load balancer section, click Application Load Balancer (HTTP/HTTPS), and then click Next.
  4. In the Public facing or internal section, click Public facing (external), and then click Next.
  5. In the Global or single region deployment section, click Best for global workloads, and then click Next.
  6. In the Load balancer generation section, click Global external Application Load Balancer, and then click Next.
  7. Click Configure.
  8. In the Load Balancer name field, enter gemini-streamlit-app-lb.
  9. Configure the load balancer by completing the Frontend configuration, Backend configuration, and Routing rules sections.

Frontend Configuration

    • Name: Enter gemini-streamlit-app-frontend.
    • Protocol: Select HTTPS (includes HTTP/2 and HTTP/3).
    • Network Service Tier: Set the IP address by reserving a new external static IP address. While reserving the new IP address, specify genai-app-ip as the Name.
    • Certificate: Perform the following steps to create a new Google-managed certificate:
      1. Click Create a new certificate.
      2. Specify the following details:
        • Name: Enter my-genai-app-certificate.
        • Create mode: Click Create Google-managed certificate.
        • Domains: Enter the domain name for provisioning the certificate.
      3. Click Create.

    Specify the following Frontend configuration:

    For more information about Google-managed SSL certificates, see Use Google-managed SSL certificates.

    • Select the Enable HTTP to HTTPS redirect checkbox.

  2. Click Done.

  3. Click Backend configuration to configure the backend.

Backend configuration

  1. Click the Backend services & backend buckets list, click Create a backend service, and enter the following details:
    • Name: Enter gemini-streamlit-app-backend.
    • Backend type: Click Serverless network endpoint group.
    • Backends: On the New Backend card, perform the following steps:
      1. Click the Serverless network endpoint groups list, and then click Create serverless network endpoint group.
      2. Enter the following details:
        • Name: Enter streamlit-app-neg.
        • Region: Select us-central1.
        • Serverless network endpoint group type: Select Cloud Run.
        • Select service: Select the gemini-streamlit-cloudrun Cloud Run service.
      3. Click Create.
      4. Click Done.
  2. Clear the Enable Cloud CDN checkbox.
  3. In the Policy name box, enter default-security-policy-gemini-app-backend.
  4. Click Create, and then click OK.
  5. Click Routing rules to configure the routing rules.

Routing rules

  1. Click Advanced host and path rule.
    • Action: Select Route traffic to a single backend.
    • Backend: Select gemini-streamlit-app-backend.

    In the Host and path rules section, click (Default) Route traffic to backend "" for any unmatched hosts, and then enter the following details:

    Note: This rule handles the traffic for any unmatched host.

  3. Click Done.

  4. Click Add host and path rule to add a new rule.
    • Hosts: Enter the domain name used while creating the Google-managed certificate.
    • Path Matcher: Copy the following URL map configuration:

    Under New host and path rule, enter the following details:

    defaultService: projects/PROJECT_ID/global/backendServices/gemini-streamlit-app-backend
name: matcher1
routeRules:
  - matchRules:
      - prefixMatch: /gemini-streamlit-app
    priority: PRIORITY
    routeAction:
      weightedBackendServices:
        - backendService: projects/PROJECT_ID/global/backendServices/gemini-streamlit-app-backend
          weight: 100

    Replace the following: * PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID. * PRIORITY: Specify the priority of the backend service by which the route rules are evaluated. In this scenario, set this to any value because you created only one backend service.

  6. Click Done.

  7. Click Review and finalize to review the configuration and create the load balancer.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Review and finalize

  1. Review the load balancer configuration.
  2. To create the load balancer, click Create.

docs.title: Set up and test your application
docs.text:
Step-by-step guide

Set up the source repository

  1. In GitHub, fork the GoogleCloudPlatform/generative-ai repository. Learn more about forking repositories in GitHub.

    Fork the repository in GitHub

  2. In the Google Cloud console, activate Cloud Shell.

    Activate Cloud Shell

    At the bottom of the Google Cloud console, a Cloud Shell session starts and displays a command-line prompt. Cloud Shell is a shell environment with the Google Cloud CLI already installed and with values already set for your current project. It can take a few seconds for the session to initialize.

  3. In the Cloud Shell terminal, run the following commands to clone your forked repository and set the gemini-streamlit-cloudrun directory as the active directory:

    cd
git clone https://github.com/GIT_USER_NAME/FORK_NAME/
cd FORK_NAME/gemini/sample-apps/gemini-streamlit-cloudrun

    Replace the following:

    • GIT_USER_NAME: Your GitHub username.
    • FORK_NAME: The name of the forked repository that you created in GitHub.

Set up the environment and dependencies

  1. In the Cloud Shell terminal, run the following commands to set up a virtual environment:

    python3 -m venv gemini-streamlit
source gemini-streamlit/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

  2. Run the following commands to set the environment variables needed for Vertex AI initialization:

    export GCP_PROJECT=$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
export GCP_REGION='us-central1'

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Test the app locally

    streamlit run app.py \
  --browser.serverAddress=localhost \
  --server.enableCORS=false \
  --server.enableXsrfProtection=false \
  --server.port 8080

  2. To preview the app, in the Cloud Shell taskbar, click Web Preview, and then select Preview on port 8080.

    For more information about using the Web Preview feature, see Preview web apps.

docs.title: Secure a generative AI app by using IAP
docs.text:
This tutorial shows you how to deploy a generative AI application to Cloud Run and secure it with Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP). IAP provides a central authorization layer for HTTPS applications, letting you establish application-level access control policies instead of relying on network-level firewalls.

This tutorial uses the Gemini API and the Streamlit framework to build the application. While other authentication methods are available for Cloud Run, IAP is recommended for applications with high traffic volumes or multi-region deployments to ensure service stability.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Before you begin, ensure you have a basic understanding of the following tools, frameworks, and services.

docs.title: Required tools and frameworks
docs.text:
• Streamlit: An open-source Python framework for creating and deploying data applications. Learn more at Streamlit.
  • Git: A version control system to manage your application's source code. For more information, see the Git documentation.

docs.title: Required Google Cloud services
docs.text:
• Vertex AI: Provides access to Google's large language models (LLMs) to test, tune, and deploy them in your applications. Learn more about Vertex AI.
  • Cloud Run: A managed compute platform for deploying and running containerized applications.
  • Cloud Build: A service that executes your builds on Google Cloud. You will set up a trigger to automatically build and deploy your app to Cloud Run.
  • Cloud Load Balancing: Distributes traffic across multiple instances of your application. An Application Load Balancer is required to use IAP with Cloud Run.
  • Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP): Creates a central authorization layer to secure your application. To learn more, see the IAP overview.

docs.title: Step 5: Test your IAP-secured app
docs.text:
This section guides you through testing the Streamlit application you deployed to Cloud Run. Before you can view the app, you must wait for the Google-managed SSL certificate to become active, which can take up to 60 minutes. This certificate is required to secure your custom domain with HTTPS.

For more information, see Use Google-managed SSL certificates.

flowchart LR
    A[Check certificate status] --> B{Is certificate active?}
    B -- Yes --> C[View the deployed app]
    B -- No --> A

click A "#check-certificate-status"
click C "#view-the-deployed-app"
Test your IAP-secured app

1. Check the status of your certificate

  • Go to the Classic Certificates tab in the Google Cloud console.

    Go to Classic Certificates

  • In the Status column, find the my-genai-app-certificate and check its status.

  • You can proceed to the next step only after the status changes to Active.

2. View the deployed app

  • Sign in to Google Cloud with a user account that you granted the "IAP-secured Web App User" role to.
  • In your browser, open the following URL. Replace DOMAIN_NAME with the domain you configured during certificate creation.
https://DOMAIN_NAME/app

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with the setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

<-- Previous: Configure IAP Next: Clean up your project -->

docs.title: Translate text
docs.text: For translation tasks, Generative AI on Vertex AI offers the choice between Gemini models and two specialized translation models from the Cloud Translation API: Translation LLM and the Neural Machine Translation (NMT) model.

docs.title: Choose a translation model
docs.text:
Before you start, it's important to select the model that best fits your use case. The Translation LLM offers the highest quality for nuanced translations, while the NMT model provides the fastest real-time results. Gemini models offer a balance and can be further customized with prompt engineering.

Use the following table to compare the features of each model.

Feature Translation LLM (Powered by Gemini) NMT model Description A translation-specialized Large Language Model powered by Gemini, fine-tuned for translation. Available with Generative AI on Vertex AI and the Cloud Translation - Advanced API. Google's Neural Machine Translation model, available through Cloud Translation - Advanced and Cloud Translation - Basic APIs. Optimized for simplicity and scale. Quality Highest quality translation. Outperforms NMT and Gemini models in benchmarks. It is more likely to rewrite sentences for natural flow rather than providing literal, word-for-word translations. High quality for many language pairs. Among the best-performing real-time NMT models for many language-domain combinations. Latency Latency is significantly better than Gemini 1.0 Flash, but slower than NMT. Fastest Real-Time Translation. Low latency, suitable for chat and real-time applications. Achieves latencies up to 20x faster than Gemini 1.0 Flash. Language support Supports 49 languages. Supports 189 languages, including Cantonese, Fijian, and Balinese. Customization Supports Advanced Glossaries, Supervised Fine-tuning on Vertex AI for domain-specific adaptations, and Adaptive translation for real-time style customization with a few examples. Supports Glossaries to control terminology and training Custom Models with AutoML Translation. Translation features HTML translation HTML, Batch, and Formatted document translation API Integration Cloud Translation - Advanced API, Vertex AI API Cloud Translation - Basic API, Cloud Translation - Advanced API, Vertex AI API

docs.title: Translate text
docs.text:
This section shows you how to translate text from one language to another using the Google Cloud console or the API. The following workflow shows the two primary methods for translating text.

flowchart LR
    A[Use the Google Cloud console]
    B[Use the API]
    A --> C[Get Translation]
    B --> C

click A "#translate-text-using-the-google-cloud-console"
click B "#translate-text-using-the-api"

Note that the languages that each model supports can vary. Before you request translations, check that the model you're using supports your source and target languages.

docs.title: Translate text using the Google Cloud console
docs.text:
Steps to translate text in the console
  1. In the Vertex AI section of the Google Cloud console, go to the Translate text page in Vertex AI Studio.

Go to Vertex AI Studio

  1. In the Run settings pane, select a translation model in the Model field.

  2. To change the model settings (such as temperature), expand Advanced.

  3. Set the source and target languages.

  4. In the input field, enter the text to translate.

  5. Click Submit.

  6. To get the code or curl command that demonstrates how to request translations, click code Get code.

In Vertex AI Studio, the Translation LLM lets you provide example translations to tailor model responses to more closely match your style, tone, and industry domain. The model uses your examples as few-shot context before translating your text.

docs.title: Translate text using the API
docs.text:
You can use the Translation LLM, Gemini, or the NMT model to translate text by using the API.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Translation LLMGeminiNMT

Use the Vertex AI API and Translation LLM to translate text.

REST

Before you begin

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_NUMBER_OR_ID: The numeric or alphanumeric ID of your Google Cloud project.
  • LOCATION: The location where you want to run this operation. For example, us-central1.
  • SOURCE_LANGUAGE_CODE: The language code of the input text.
  • TARGET_LANGUAGE_CODE: The target language to translate the input text to.
  • SOURCE_TEXT: Text in the source language to translate.
  • MIME_TYPE (Optional): The format of the source text, such as text/html or text/plain. By default, the MIME type is set to text/plain.

HTTP method and URL

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/cloud-translate-text:predict

Request JSON body

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "source_language_code": "SOURCE_LANGUAGE_CODE",
      "target_language_code": "TARGET_LANGUAGE_CODE",
      "contents": [
        "SOURCE_TEXT"
      ],
      "mimeType": "MIME_TYPE",
      "model": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/models/general/translation-llm"
    }
  ]
}

To send your request, expand one of these options:

curl (Linux, macOS, or Cloud Shell)PowerShell (Windows)

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \  
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \  
     -H "x-goog-user-project: PROJECT_NUMBER_OR_ID" \  
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \  
     -d @request.json \  
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/cloud-translate-text:predict"

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token  
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred"; "x-goog-user-project" = "PROJECT_NUMBER_OR_ID" }  

Invoke-WebRequest `  
    -Method POST `  
    -Headers $headers `  
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `  
    -InFile request.json `  
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/cloud-translate-text:predict" | Select-Object -Expand Content

You should receive a JSON response similar to the following:

{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "translations": [
        {
          "translatedText": "TRANSLATED_TEXT",
          "model": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/models/general/translation-llm"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
Node.js

Before trying this sample, follow the Node.js setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Node.js API reference documentation.

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

async function translate() {
  const request = {
    instances: [{
      source_language_code: SOURCE_LANGUAGE_CODE,
      target_language_code: TARGET_LANGUAGE_CODE,
      contents: [SOURCE_TEXT],
      model: "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/models/general/translation-llm"
    }]
  };
  const {google} = require('googleapis');
  const aiplatform = google.cloud('aiplatform');
  const endpoint = aiplatform.predictionEndpoint('projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/cloud-translate-text');

  const [response] = await endpoint.predict(request)
  console.log('Translating')
  console.log(response)
}

Before trying this sample, follow the Python setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Python API reference documentation.

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

from google.cloud import aiplatform

def translate():
  # Create a client
  client_options = {"api_endpoint": "LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com"}
  client = aiplatform.gapic.PredictionServiceClient(client_options=client_options)

  # Initialize the request
  endpoint_id = f"projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/cloud-translate-text"
  instances=[{
    "model": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/models/general/translation-llm",
    "source_language_code": 'SOURCE_LANGUAGE_CODE',
    "target_language_code": 'TARGET_LANGUAGE_CODE',
    "contents": ["SOURCE_TEXT"],
  }]

  # Make the request
  response = client.predict(instances=instances, endpoint=endpoint_id)
  # Handle the response
  print(response)

Use the Vertex AI API and a Gemini model to translate text. You can further customize Gemini responses through open prompting and prompt engineering.

REST

Before you begin

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_NUMBER_OR_ID: The numeric or alphanumeric ID of your Google Cloud project.
  • LOCATION: The location to process the request.
  • MODEL_ID: The ID of the model, such as gemini-1.0-pro-002.
  • SOURCE_LANGUAGE_CODE: The language of the input text.
  • TARGET_LANGUAGE_CODE: The target language to translate the input text to.
  • SOURCE_TEXT: The text to translate.
  • For parameter definitions, see Parameter descriptions.
View a partial list of available regions
  • us-central1
  • us-west4
  • northamerica-northeast1
  • us-east4
  • us-west1
  • asia-northeast3
  • asia-southeast1
  • asia-northeast1

HTTP method and URL

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:streamGenerateContent

Request JSON body

{
  "contents": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "parts": [
        {
        "text": "SOURCE_LANGUAGE_CODE: SOURCE_TEXT\nTARGET_LANGUAGE_CODE:"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "generation_config": {
    "temperature": TEMPERATURE,
    "topP": TOP_P,
    "topK": TOP_K,
    "candidateCount": 1,
    "maxOutputTokens": MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS
  }
  "safetySettings": [
    {
      "category": "SAFETY_CATEGORY",
      "threshold": "THRESHOLD"
    }
  ]
}

To send your request, expand one of these options:

curl (Linux, macOS, or Cloud Shell)PowerShell (Windows)

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \  
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \  
     -H "x-goog-user-project: PROJECT_NUMBER_OR_ID" \  
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \  
     -d @request.json \  
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:streamGenerateContent"

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token  
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred"; "x-goog-user-project" = "PROJECT_NUMBER_OR_ID" }  

Invoke-WebRequest `  
    -Method POST `  
    -Headers $headers `  
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `

    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:streamGenerateContent" | Select-Object -Expand Content

You should receive a successful status code (2xx) and an empty response.

Node.js

Before trying this sample, follow the Node.js setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Node.js API reference documentation.

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

const {VertexAI} = require('@google-cloud/vertexai');

// Initialize Vertex with your Cloud project and location
const vertex_ai = new VertexAI({project: 'PROJECT_ID', location: 'LOCATION'});
const model = 'gemini-1.0-pro';

// Instantiate the models
const generativeModel = vertex_ai.preview.getGenerativeModel({
  model: model,
  generationConfig: {
    'candidate_count': 1,
    'max_output_tokens': MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS,
    'temperature': TEMPERATURE,
    'top_p': TOP_P,
    'top_k': TOP_K,
  },
  safetySettings: [
    {
        'category': 'HARM_CATEGORY_HATE_SPEECH',
        'threshold': 'BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE'
    },
    {
        'category': 'HARM_CATEGORY_DANGEROUS_CONTENT',
        'threshold': 'BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE'
    },
    {
        'category': 'HARM_CATEGORY_SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT',
        'threshold': 'BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE'
    },
    {
        'category': 'HARM_CATEGORY_HARASSMENT',
        'threshold': 'BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE'
    }
  ],
});


async function generateContent() {
  const req = {
    contents: [
      {role: 'user', parts: [{text: `SOURCE_LANGUAGE_CODE: TEXT
TARGET_LANGUAGE_CODE:`}]}
    ],
  };

  const streamingResp = await generativeModel.generateContentStream(req);

  for await (const item of streamingResp.stream) {
    process.stdout.write('stream chunk: ' + JSON.stringify(item) + '\n');
  }

  process.stdout.write('aggregated response: ' + JSON.stringify(await streamingResp.response));
}

generateContent();
Python

Before trying this sample, follow the Python setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Python API reference documentation.

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

import base64
import vertexai
from vertexai.generative_models import GenerativeModel, Part, FinishReason
import vertexai.preview.generative_models as generative_models

def generate():
  vertexai.init(project="PROJECT_ID", location="LOCATION")
  model = GenerativeModel("gemini-1.0-pro")
  responses = model.generate_content(
      ["""SOURCE_LANGUAGE_CODE: TEXT
TARGET_LANGUAGE_CODE:"""],
      generation_config=generation_config,
      safety_settings=safety_settings,
  )

  print(responses)


generation_config = {
    "candidate_count": 1,
    "max_output_tokens": MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS,
    "temperature": TEMPERATURE,
    "top_p": TOP_P,
    "top_k": TOP_K,
}

safety_settings = {
    generative_models.HarmCategory.HARM_CATEGORY_HATE_SPEECH: generative_models.HarmBlockThreshold.BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE,
    generative_models.HarmCategory.HARM_CATEGORY_DANGEROUS_CONTENT: generative_models.HarmBlockThreshold.BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE,
    generative_models.HarmCategory.HARM_CATEGORY_SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT: generative_models.HarmBlockThreshold.BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE,
    generative_models.HarmCategory.HARM_CATEGORY_HARASSMENT: generative_models.HarmBlockThreshold.BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE,
}

generate()
Parameter descriptions

  • TEMPERATURE: The temperature is used for sampling during response generation, which occurs when topP and topK are applied. Temperature controls the degree of randomness in token selection. Lower temperatures are good for prompts that require a less open-ended or creative response, while higher temperatures can lead to more diverse or creative results. A temperature of 0 means that the highest probability tokens are always selected. In this case, responses for a given prompt are mostly deterministic, but a small amount of variation is still possible.
  • TOP_P: Top-P changes how the model selects tokens for output. Tokens are selected from the most probable to least probable until the sum of their probabilities equals the top-P value. For example, if tokens A, B, and C have a probability of 0.3, 0.2, and 0.1 and the top-P value is 0.5, then the model will select either A or B as the next token by using temperature and excludes C as a candidate. Specify a lower value for less random responses and a higher value for more random responses.
  • TOP_K: Top-K changes how the model selects tokens for output. A top-K of 1 means the next selected token is the most probable among all tokens in the model's vocabulary (also called greedy decoding), while a top-K of 3 means that the next token is selected from among the three most probable tokens by using temperature. For each token selection step, the top-K tokens with the highest probabilities are sampled. Then tokens are further filtered based on top-P with the final token selected using temperature sampling. Specify a lower value for less random responses and a higher value for more random responses.
  • MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS: Maximum number of tokens that can be generated in the response. A token is approximately four characters. 100 tokens correspond to roughly 60-80 words. Specify a lower value for shorter responses and a higher value for potentially longer responses.
  • SAFETY_CATEGORY: The safety category to configure a threshold for. ??? "View safety categories" * HARM_CATEGORY_SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT * HARM_CATEGORY_HATE_SPEECH * HARM_CATEGORY_HARASSMENT * HARM_CATEGORY_DANGEROUS_CONTENT

  • THRESHOLD: The threshold for blocking responses that could belong to the specified safety category based on probability. ??? "View blocking thresholds" * BLOCK_NONE * BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH * BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE (default) * BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE

    BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE blocks the most while BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH blocks the least.

Use the Cloud Translation API and the NMT model to translate text.

REST

Before you begin

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_NUMBER_OR_ID: The numeric or alphanumeric ID of your Google Cloud project.
  • SOURCE_LANGUAGE (Optional): The language code of the input text. For supported language codes, see Language support.
  • TARGET_LANGUAGE: The target language to translate the input text to. Set to one of the supported language codes.
  • SOURCE_TEXT: The text to translate.

HTTP method and URL

POST https://translation.googleapis.com/v3/projects/PROJECT_ID:translateText

Request JSON body

{
  "sourceLanguageCode": "SOURCE_LANGUAGE",
  "targetLanguageCode": "TARGET_LANGUAGE",
  "contents": ["SOURCE_TEXT1", "SOURCE_TEXT2"]
}

To send your request, expand one of these options:

curl (Linux, macOS, or Cloud Shell)PowerShell (Windows)

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \  
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \  
     -H "x-goog-user-project: PROJECT_NUMBER_OR_ID" \  
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token  
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred"; "x-goog-user-project" = "PROJECT_NUMBER_OR_ID" }

Before trying this sample, follow the Node.js setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Node.js API reference documentation.

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

Python

Before trying this sample, follow the Python setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Python API reference documentation.

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

import os

# Import the Google Cloud Translation library.
from google.cloud import translate_v3

PROJECT_ID = os.environ.get("GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT")


def translate_text(
    text: str = "YOUR_TEXT_TO_TRANSLATE",
    source_language_code: str = "en-US",
    target_language_code: str = "fr",
) -> translate_v3.TranslationServiceClient:
    """Translate Text from a Source language to a Target language.
    Args:
        text: The content to translate.
        source_language_code: The code of the source language.
        target_language_code: The code of the target language.
            For example: "fr" for French, "es" for Spanish, etc.
            Find available languages and codes here:
            https://cloud.google.com/translate/docs/languages#neural_machine_translation_model
    """

    # Initialize Translation client.
    client = translate_v3.TranslationServiceClient()
    parent = f"projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/global"

    # MIME type of the content to translate.
    # Supported MIME types:
    # https://cloud.google.com/translate/docs/supported-formats
    mime_type = "text/plain"

    # Translate text from the source to the target language.
    response = client.translate_text(
        contents=[text],
        parent=parent,
        mime_type=mime_type,
        source_language_code=source_language_code,
        target_language_code=target_language_code,
    )

    # Display the translation for the text.
    # For example, for "Hello! How are you doing today?":
    # Translated text: Bonjour comment vas-tu aujourd'hui?
    for translation in response.translations:
        print(f"Translated text: {translation.translated_text}")

    return response

docs.title: Custom translations with the Translation LLM
docs.text:
Customize responses from the Translation LLM by providing your own example translations. This feature, also known as adaptive translation, only works with the Translation LLM.

You can request customized translations through the Vertex AI Studio console or the API. The console supports custom translations by uploading a file with examples, while the API supports providing examples inline with the request.

docs.title: Data requirements
docs.text:
If you provide example translations in a file for the Google Cloud console, the examples must be written as segment pairs in a TMX or TSV file. Each pair includes a source language segment and its translated counterpart. For more information, see Prepare example translations in the Cloud Translation documentation.

To get the most accurate results, include specific examples from a wide variety of scenarios. You must include at least five sentence pairs but no more than 10,000 pairs. Also, a segment pair can be at most a total of 512 characters.

ConsoleAPI Steps for custom translation in the console
  1. In the Vertex AI section of the Google Cloud console, go to the Translate text page in Vertex AI Studio.

Go to Vertex AI Studio

  1. In the Run settings pane, configure your translation settings.

    • In the Model field, select Translation LLM.
    • To change the temperature, expand Advanced.

  2. Click Add examples.

    • Select a local file or a file from Cloud Storage. Vertex AI Studio determines the source and target languages from your file.
    • Select the number of examples for the model to use before generating a response. The number of examples you select counts toward the input character limit per request of 3,000.

  3. In the input field, enter the text to translate.

  4. Click Submit. Vertex AI automatically selects your specified number of reference sentences that are most similar to your input. The translation model identifies patterns from your examples and then applies those patterns when generating a response. The output limit per request is 3,000 characters. Any text beyond this limit is dropped.

  5. To get the code or curl command that demonstrates how to request translations, click code Get code.

To request custom translations, include up to five reference sentence pairs in your translation request. The translation model uses all of them to identify patterns from your examples and then applies those patterns when generating a response.

REST

Before you begin

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_NUMBER_OR_ID: The numeric or alphanumeric ID of your Google Cloud project.
  • LOCATION: The location where you want to run this operation. For example, us-central1.
  • REFERENCE_SOURCE_1_1: A sentence in the source language that is part of a reference sentence pair.
  • REFERENCE_TARGET_1_1: A sentence in the target language that is part of a reference sentence pair.
  • SOURCE_LANGUAGE_CODE: The language code of the input text.
  • TARGET_LANGUAGE_CODE: The target language to translate the input text to.
  • SOURCE_TEXT: Text in the source language to translate.
  • MIME_TYPE (Optional): The format of the source text, such as text/html or text/plain. By default, the MIME type is set to text/plain.

HTTP method and URL

{

Node.js

Before trying this sample, follow the Node.js setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Node.js API reference documentation.

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

async function translate() {
  const request = {
    instances: [{
        "reference_sentence_config": {
          "reference_sentence_pair_lists": [{
            "reference_sentence_pairs": [{
              "source_sentence": 'SAMPLE_REFERENCE_SOURCE_1',
              "target_sentence": 'SAMPLE_REFERENCE_TARGET_1'
            },
            "reference_sentence_pairs": {
              "source_sentence": 'SAMPLE_REFERENCE_SOURCE_2',
              "target_sentence": 'SAMPLE_REFERENCE_TARGET_2'
            }]
          }],
          "source_language_code": 'SOURCE_LANGUAGE_CODE',
          "target_language_code": 'TARGET_LANGUAGE_CODE'
        },
        "contents": ["SOURCE_TEXT"]
    }]
  };
  const {google} = require('googleapis');
  const aiplatform = google.cloud('aiplatform');
  const endpoint = aiplatform.predictionEndpoint('projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/translate-llm');

  const [response] = await endpoint.predict(request)
  console.log('Translating')
  console.log(response)
}
Python

Before trying this sample, follow the Python setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Python API reference documentation.

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

from google.cloud import aiplatform
from google.protobuf.json_format import MessageToDict

def translate():
  # Create a client
  client_options = {"api_endpoint": "LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com"}
  client = aiplatform.gapic.PredictionServiceClient(client_options=client_options)

  # Initialize the request
  endpoint_id = f"projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/translate-llm"
  instances=[{
      "reference_sentence_config": {
        "reference_sentence_pair_lists": [{
          "reference_sentence_pairs": [{
            "source_sentence": 'SAMPLE_REFERENCE_SOURCE_1',
            "target_sentence": 'SAMPLE_REFERENCE_TARGET_1'
          },
          {
            "source_sentence": 'SAMPLE_REFERENCE_SOURCE_2',
            "target_sentence": 'SAMPLE_REFERENCE_TARGET_2'
          }]
        }],
        "source_language_code": 'SOURCE_LANGUAGE_CODE',
        "target_language_code": 'TARGET_LANGUAGE_CODE'
      },
      "content": ["SOURCE_TEXT"]
  }]
  # Make the request
  response = client.predict(
      endpoint=endpoint_id, instances=instances,
  )
  # Handle the response
  print(response)

  # The predictions are a google.protobuf.Value representation of the model's predictions.
  predictions = MessageToDict(response._pb)['predictions']
  for prediction in predictions:
      print(prediction['translations'])

You can also use the Cloud Translation API to create a dataset and import your example sentence pairs. When you use the Cloud Translation API to request translations, you can include your dataset to customize responses. The dataset persists and can be reused with multiple translation requests. For more information, see Request adaptive translations in the Cloud Translation documentation.

docs.text:
Veo generates realistic and high-quality videos from natural language text and image prompts, including images of people of all ages. docs.title: Generate videos from text
docs.text:
You can generate novel videos using only descriptive text as an input. The following samples show you how to generate videos from a text prompt.

ConsoleRESTGen AI SDK for Python

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI Studio > Media Studio page.

    Go to Media Studio

  2. Click Video.

  3. Optional: In the Settings pane, configure the following settings:
    • Model: Choose a model from the available options.
    • Aspect ratio: Choose either 16:9 or 9:16. > Note: The 9:16 aspect ratio isn't supported by veo-3.0-generate-preview.
    • Number of results: Adjust the slider or enter a value between 1 and 4.
    • Video length: Select a length between 5 seconds and 8 seconds.
    • Output directory: Click Browse to create or select a Cloud Storage bucket to store output files.
  4. Optional: In the Safety section, select one of the following Person generation settings:
    • Allow (Adults only): Default value. Generate adult people or faces only.
    • Don't allow: Don't generate people or faces.
  5. Optional: In the Advanced options section, enter a Seed value for randomizing video generation.
  6. In the Write your prompt box, enter your text prompt that describes the videos to generate.
  7. Click Generate.

After you set up your environment, you can use the REST API to generate a video from a text prompt.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Step 1: Send a video generation request

Use the following command to send a video generation request. This request begins a long-running operation and stores the output in a Cloud Storage bucket you specify.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements: * PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID. * MODEL_ID: The model ID to use. Available values: veo-2.0-generate-001 (GA) or veo-3.0-generate-preview (Preview). * TEXT_PROMPT: The text prompt used to guide video generation. * OUTPUT_STORAGE_URI: Optional: The Cloud Storage bucket to store the output videos. If not provided, video bytes are returned in the response. For example: gs://video-bucket/output/. * RESPONSE_COUNT: The number of video files you want to generate. Accepted integer values: 1-4. * DURATION: The length of video files that you want to generate. Accepted integer values are 5-8.

View additional optional parameters

Use the following optional variables depending on your use case. Add some or all of the following parameters in the "parameters": {} object.

"parameters": {
  "aspectRatio": "ASPECT_RATIO",
  "negativePrompt": "NEGATIVE_PROMPT",
  "personGeneration": "PERSON_SAFETY_SETTING",
  "sampleCount": RESPONSE_COUNT,
  "seed": SEED_NUMBER
}
  • ASPECT_RATIO: string. Optional. Defines the aspect ratio of the generated videos. Values: 16:9 (default, landscape) or 9:16 (portrait).
  • NEGATIVE_PROMPT: string. Optional. A text string that describes what you want to discourage the model from generating.
  • PERSON_SAFETY_SETTING: string. Optional. The safety setting that controls whether people or face generation is allowed. Values: allow_adult (default value) or disallow.
  • RESPONSE_COUNT: int. Optional. The number of output images requested. Values: 1-4.
  • SEED_NUMBER: uint32. Optional. A number to make generated videos deterministic. Values: 0 - 4294967295.

HTTP method and URL: 

POST https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:predictLongRunning

Request JSON body: 

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "TEXT_PROMPT"
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "storageUri": "OUTPUT_STORAGE_URI",
    "sampleCount": "RESPONSE_COUNT"
  }
}

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

Check the status of the video generation long-running operation.

When "done": true, the response contains the URIs for the generated videos. 

{
  "name": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID/operations/OPERATION_ID",
  "done": true,

      {

        "mimeType": "video/mp4"
      }
    ]
  }
}

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Install the SDK

To learn more, see the SDK reference documentation.

pip install --upgrade google-genai
Run the Python code

Set environment variables to use the Gen AI SDK with Vertex AI:

# Replace the `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` values
# with appropriate values for your project.
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global
export GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=True

import time
from google import genai
from google.genai.types import GenerateVideosConfig

client = genai.Client()

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below line
# output_gcs_uri = "gs://your-bucket/your-prefix"

operation = client.models.generate_videos(
    model="veo-3.0-generate-preview",
    prompt="a cat reading a book",
    config=GenerateVideosConfig(
        aspect_ratio="16:9",
        output_gcs_uri=output_gcs_uri,
    ),
)

while not operation.done:
    time.sleep(15)
    operation = client.operations.get(operation)
    print(operation)

if operation.response:
    print(operation.result.generated_videos[0].video.uri)

# Example response:
# gs://your-bucket/your-prefix

docs.title: Generate videos from an image
docs.text:
You can generate novel videos using an image as an input, with or without a descriptive text prompt.

Input: Image of a crocheted elephant and the text prompt "the elephant moves around naturally". Output: A generated video of the elephant moving. The input image was generated using Imagen on Vertex AI from the prompt: A Crochet elephant in intricate patterns walking on the savanna.

The following samples show you how to generate videos from an image.

  5. Optional: In the Settings pane, configure the following settings:
    • Model: Choose a model from the available options.

    • Number of results: Adjust the slider or enter a value between 1 and 4.
    • Video length: Select a length between 5 seconds and 8 seconds.
    • Output directory: Click Browse to create or select a Cloud Storage bucket to store output files.
  6. Optional: In the Safety section, select one of the following Person generation settings:

    • Don't allow: Don't generate people or faces.
  7. Optional: In the Advanced options section, enter a Seed value for randomizing video generation.
  8. In the Write your prompt box, enter a text prompt that describes how the image should be animated.

Supported types: image/jpeg or image/png. * OUTPUT_STORAGE_URI: Optional: The Cloud Storage bucket to store the output videos.   • SEED_NUMBER: uint32. Optional. A number to make generated videos deterministic. Values: 0 - 4294967295.

HTTP method and URL:

docs.title: Prompt rewriter
docs.text:
Veo offers an LLM-based prompt enhancement tool, also known as a prompt rewriter. The prompt rewriter can rewrite your prompts to add more detail, such as camera motions, transcription, and sound effects. More detailed prompts can result in higher quality videos.

If you disable prompt enhancement, the quality of the videos and how well the output resembles the prompt that you supplied might be impacted. This feature is enabled by default for the following model versions:

  • veo-2.0-generate-001
  • veo-3.0-generate-preview (Preview)

Important: You can't disable the prompt rewriter when you use veo-3.0-generate-preview.

The rewritten prompt is delivered in the API response only if the original prompt is fewer than 30 words long.

To turn prompt enhancement off, do the following:

ConsoleREST

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI Studio > Media Studio page.

    Go to Media Studio

  2. Click Veo.

  3. In Settings, click the Enable prompt enhancement toggle to disable it.
  4. In the Write your prompt box, enter your prompt and then click Generate.

To disable prompt enhancement, set the enhancePrompt parameter to False in your request body.

Request JSON body: 

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "TEXT_PROMPT"
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "storageUri": "OUTPUT_STORAGE_URI",
    "sampleCount": "RESPONSE_COUNT",

docs.title: Responsible AI and usage guidelines for Veo
docs.text:
Veo on Vertex AI is designed in accordance with Google's AI principles. It is important for developers to understand how to test and deploy Google's models safely and responsibly. To support this, Veo on Vertex AI includes built-in safety features that help you block potentially harmful outputs.

We encourage you to apply fairness, interpretability, privacy, and security best practices when developing AI applications. For more information, see The People + AI Guidebook.

docs.title: Safety filters
docs.text:
Veo on Vertex AI accepts prompts in multiple formats to generate videos, including text, video, and images. All prompts provided to Veo are assessed against a list of safety filters that cover harmful categories such as violence, sexual, derogatory, and toxic. These filters are designed to block content that violates the Google Cloud Platform Acceptable Use Policy, the Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy, or Our AI Principles.

If your input triggers a safety filter, the model may respond with an error message like The prompt couldn't be submitted or it might violate our policies. In other cases, if the generated output doesn't meet safety requirements, you may receive fewer videos than you requested.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Safety filter error codes
docs.text:
When a safety filter is triggered, the output may contain a support code, as shown in this example message: "Veo could not generate videos because the input image violates Vertex AI's usage guidelines. If you think this was an error, send feedback. Support codes: 15236754"

The code in the output corresponds to a specific harmful category. The following table maps the error codes to their respective safety categories.

Error code Safety category Description 58061214, 17301594 Child Detects child content where it isn't allowed due to the API request settings or allowlisting. 29310472, 15236754 Celebrity Detects a photorealistic representation of a celebrity in the request. 62263041 Dangerous content Detects content that is potentially dangerous in nature. 57734940, 22137204 Hate Detects hate-related topics or content. 74803281, 29578790, 42876398 Other Detects other miscellaneous safety issues with the request. 92201652 Personal information Detects Personally Identifiable Information (PII) in the text, such as a credit card number, home address, or other such information. 89371032, 49114662, 72817394 Prohibited content Detects a request for prohibited content. 90789179, 63429089, 43188360 Sexual Detects content that is sexual in nature. 78610348 Toxic Detects toxic topics or content in the text. 61493863, 56562880 Violence Detects violence-related content from the image or text. 32635315 Vulgar Detects vulgar topics or content from the text.

docs.title: Vertex AI video generation prompt guide
docs.text:
This guide provides examples of the types of videos that you can create using Veo and shows you how to modify specific parts of a prompt to produce different results.

Request access: Advanced features & Veo waitlist

docs.title: What is a prompt?
docs.text: Vertex AI Veo is a text-to-video and image-to-video generation model. To use Veo, you provide a prompt, which is a text description of the video you want the model to generate. A good prompt is descriptive, clear, and provides enough detail for the model to create a video that aligns with your vision.

docs.title: Safety filters
docs.text:
Veo applies safety filters to help ensure that generated videos and uploaded photos don't contain offensive content. Prompts that violate responsible AI guidelines are blocked.

If you suspect abuse of Veo or any generated output that contains inappropriate material or inaccurate information, use the Report suspected abuse on Google Cloud form.

docs.title: Basics for writing prompts
docs.text:
Good prompts are descriptive and clear. To get your generated video closer to what you want, start with your core idea and then refine it by adding keywords and modifiers.

A comprehensive prompt should include the following elements:

  1. Subject: The object, person, animal, or scenery that you want in your video.
  2. Context: The background or setting in which the subject is placed.
  3. Action: What the subject is doing (for example, walking, running, or turning their head).
  4. Style: The aesthetic of the video. This can be general (e.g., cinematic) or very specific (e.g., film noir, 3D cartoon style).
  5. Camera motion: (Optional) What the camera is doing, such as an aerial view, eye-level shot, or dolly zoom.
  6. Composition: (Optional) How the shot is framed, such as a wide shot, close-up, or extreme close-up.
  7. Ambiance: (Optional) How color and light contribute to the scene's mood, such as warm tones, night lighting, or blue tones.

docs.title: Prompting techniques and examples
docs.text: This section provides examples of how to structure your prompts and refine them with additional detail to generate higher-quality videos.

docs.title: Refining prompts with progressive detail
docs.text:
Adding more descriptive language and specific details can significantly improve the quality and focus of the generated video.

Example: Man on the phone

This example shows how a prompt evolves from a basic description to a detailed cinematic instruction.

Prompt Generated output Analysis The camera dollies to show a close up of a desperate man in a green trench coat that's making a call on a rotary-style wall phone with a green neon light and a movie scene. Initial video generated from a basic prompt. This is the first generated video based on the prompt. A close-up cinematic shot follows a desperate man in a weathered green trench coat as he dials a rotary phone mounted on a gritty brick wall, bathed in the eerie glow of a green neon sign. The camera dollies in, revealing the tension in his jaw and the desperation etched on his face as he struggles to make the call. The shallow depth of field focuses on his furrowed brow and the black rotary phone, blurring the background into a sea of neon colors and indistinct shadows, creating a sense of urgency and isolation. Video generated from a more detailed prompt. A more detailed prompt results in a video that is more focused with a richer environment. A video with smooth motion that dollies in on a desperate man in a green trench coat, using a vintage rotary phone against a wall bathed in an eerie green neon glow. The camera starts from a medium distance, slowly moving closer to the man's face, revealing his frantic expression and the sweat on his brow as he urgently dials the phone. The focus is on the man's hands, his fingers fumbling with the dial as he desperately tries to connect. The green neon light casts long shadows on the wall, adding to the tense atmosphere. The scene is framed to emphasize the isolation and desperation of the man, highlighting the stark contrast between the vibrant glow of the neon and the man's grim determination. Video generated from a highly specific and descriptive prompt. Adding more detail about emotion and camera focus gave the subject a realistic expression and created an intense, vibrant scene.

Example: Snow leopard

This example shows how adding stylistic details can change the mood and action of the video.

Prompt Generated output A cute creature with snow leopard-like fur is walking in winter forest, 3D cartoon style render. A simple prompt results in a basic animation. Create a short 3D animated scene in a joyful cartoon style. A cute creature with snow leopard-like fur, large expressive eyes, and a friendly, rounded form happily prances through a whimsical winter forest. The scene should feature rounded, snow-covered trees, gentle falling snowflakes, and warm sunlight filtering through the branches. The creature's bouncy movements and wide smile should convey pure delight. Aim for an upbeat, heartwarming tone with bright, cheerful colors and playful animation. A detailed prompt creates a more dynamic and expressive animation.

docs.title: Adding specific elements to your prompt
docs.text:
The following examples demonstrate how to use each prompt element to control a specific aspect of your video.

SubjectContextActionStyleCamera MotionCompositionAmbiance

The subject can be a person, object, or scene. Be specific in your description.

Prompt: An architectural rendering of a white concrete apartment building with flowing organic shapes, seamlessly blending with lush greenery and futuristic elements

Generated output: A video of a futuristic apartment building.

The context or background is crucial for setting the scene. Try placing your subject in various environments.

Prompt: A satellite floating through outer space with the moon and some stars in the background.

Generated output: A satellite in the context of outer space.

Specify what the subject is doing in the scene.

Prompt: A wide shot of a woman walking along the beach, looking content and relaxed and looking towards the horizon at sunset.

Generated output: A woman performing the action of walking on a beach.

Add keywords to define the artistic style, such as film noir, minimalistic, surreal, vintage, or double-exposure.

Prompt: Film noir style, man and woman walk on the street, mystery, cinematic, black and white.

Generated output: A video generated in a film noir style.

Describe the camera's movement, such as POV shot, aerial view, tracking drone view, or tracking shot.

Prompt: A POV shot from a vintage car driving in the rain, Canada at night, cinematic.

Generated output: A point-of-view (POV) shot from a moving car.

Define how the shot is framed, such as wide shot, close-up, or low angle.

Prompt: Extreme close-up of an eye with a city reflected in it.

Generated output: An extreme close-up composition.

Use colors and lighting to set the mood. Color palettes like pastel blue and pink tones or lighting conditions like dim ambient lighting can dramatically influence the emotional impact.

Prompt: Cinematic close-up shot of a sad woman riding a bus in the rain, cool blue tones, sad mood.

Generated output: A scene with a sad ambiance created by color and context.

docs.title: General tips for writing prompts
docs.text:
• Use descriptive language: Use adjectives and adverbs to paint a clear picture for Veo.
  • Reference specific artistic styles: If you have a particular aesthetic in mind, reference specific artists, styles, or art movements.
  • Enhance facial details: To focus on facial details, use words like portrait in the prompt.
  • Explore prompt engineering: For more advanced techniques, see Introduction to prompting.

docs.title: Use reference images to generate videos
docs.text:
You can bring a static image to life by providing it as a reference along with a text prompt describing the desired action.

Input Image & Prompt Generated output Image:Prompt: Bunny runs away. The bunny from the image is now animated.

When using image-to-video, we recommend the following: * Ensure that actions and speech descriptions align with the subjects present in the input image. * When multiple subjects are present, clearly specify which character is performing an action or speaking by using distinguishing details (e.g., "The man in the red hat," "The woman in the blue dress").

docs.title: Use negative prompts
docs.text:
Negative prompts help you specify what to exclude from your video. Instead of using words like "no" or "don't," simply list the concepts you want to avoid.

  • ❌ Don't: "No walls" or "don't show buildings".
  • ✅ Do: "walls, buildings, urban".

Example: Solitary oak tree

Prompt Generated output Prompt: Generate a short, stylized animation of a large, solitary oak tree with leaves blowing vigorously in a strong wind. The tree should have a slightly exaggerated, whimsical form, with dynamic, flowing branches. The leaves should display a variety of autumn colors, swirling and dancing in the wind. The animation should feature a gentle, atmospheric soundtrack and use a warm, inviting color palette. Video generated without a negative prompt. Prompt: (Same as above)Negative prompt: urban background, man-made structures, dark, stormy, or threatening atmosphere. Video generated with a negative prompt to exclude unwanted elements.

docs.title: Include audio
docs.text:
Preview

Audio generation is supported by veo-3.0-generate-preview in Preview.

To include audio, clearly specify it in your prompt. We recommend using separate sentences to describe sound effects or speech.

  • Sound effects:
    • The audio features water splashing in the background.
    • Add soft music in the background.
  • Speech:
    • The man in the red hat says, "Where is the rabbit?" Then the woman in the green dress next to him replies, "There, in the woods."

docs.title: Aspect ratios
docs.text:
Veo supports the following aspect ratios for video generation.

Aspect ratio Description Widescreen (16:9) The most common aspect ratio for TVs, monitors, and landscape mobile video. Use this to capture more of the background, such as scenic landscapes. Portrait (9:16) A rotated widescreen, popularized by short-form video apps. Use this for portraits or tall subjects like skyscrapers, trees, or waterfalls.Note: The 9:16 aspect ratio isn't supported by veo-3.0-generate-preview.

docs.title: Widescreen example (16:9)
docs.text:
Prompt: Create a video with a tracking drone view of a man driving a red convertible car in Palm Springs, 1970s, warm sunlight, long shadows.

Generated output:

A video generated in a 16:9 widescreen aspect ratio.

docs.title: Portrait example (9:16)
docs.text:
Prompt: Create a video with a smooth motion of a majestic Hawaiian waterfall within a lush rainforest. Focus on realistic water flow, detailed foliage, and natural lighting to convey tranquility. Capture the rushing water, misty atmosphere, and dappled sunlight filtering through the dense canopy. Use smooth, cinematic camera movements to showcase the waterfall and its surroundings. Aim for a peaceful, realistic tone, transporting the viewer to the serene beauty of the Hawaiian rainforest.

Generated output:

A video generated in a 9:16 portrait aspect ratio.

docs.title: Overview of Generative AI on Vertex AI
docs.text:
Build production-ready generative AI agents and applications on Vertex AI using Google's advanced models and open, enterprise-grade infrastructure.

  • Build, deploy, and connect agents: Build agents with an open approach and deploy them with enterprise-grade controls. Connect agents across your enterprise ecosystem.
  • Enterprise ready: Deploy your generative AI agents and applications at scale with enterprise-grade security, data residency and privacy, access transparency, and low latency.
  • State-of-the-art features: Expand the capabilities of your applications by using the 2 million token context window that Gemini supports, and the built-in multimodality and thinking capabilities from Gemini 1.5 models.
  • Open and flexible platform: Vertex AI Model Garden provides a library of over 200 enterprise-ready models and Vertex AI Model Builder helps you test, customize, deploy, and monitor Google proprietary and select third-party models, including Anthropic's Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Meta's Llama 3, and Mistral AI's Mixtral 8x7B.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Agent: An AI system that can understand a user's goal and dynamically work to achieve it by interacting with users, tools, and external systems.
  • Multimodality: The ability of a model to process and understand information from multiple types of data, such as images, text, and audio, simultaneously.
  • Grounding: The process of connecting a model's responses to verifiable sources of information to improve accuracy and reduce hallucinations.
  • Embeddings: Numerical representations of text, images, or other data, used to capture semantic meaning and enable tasks like search and classification.
  • Tuning: The process of adapting a pre-trained model to perform better on a specific task by training it on a smaller, task-specific dataset.

docs.title: Get started
docs.text:
• Generate text using the Gemini API in Vertex AI: Use the Gen AI SDK to send requests to the Gemini API in Vertex AI.

  • Generate images and verify watermarks using Imagen: Create a watermarked image using Imagen on Vertex AI.

docs.title: Featured capabilities
docs.text:
• Agent Builder: A suite of features for building and deploying AI agents.
  • Live API: Use the Live API to provide your end users with the experience of natural, human-like voice conversations.
  • Thinking: Solve complex requests and show the model's thought process behind its response using Gemini's built-in reasoning capabilities.
  • Grounding: Ground your responses using Google Search, Maps, or even your own data.
  • Generate embeddings: Generate embeddings to perform tasks such as search, classification, clustering, and outlier detection.
  • Tuning: Adapt your model to perform specific tasks with greater precision and accuracy.
  • Image generation: Build next-generation AI products that transform your user's imagination into high quality visual assets using AI generation in seconds.
  • Video generation: Use Veo on Vertex AI to generate new videos from a text prompt or an image prompt.
  • Generative AI evaluation service: Vertex AI lets you evaluate any generative model or application and benchmark the evaluation results against your own judgment, using your own evaluation criteria.

docs.title: Cost of building and deploying AI models in Vertex AI
docs.text:
This document details the pricing for Generative AI services on Vertex AI. Prices are listed in US Dollars (USD). If you pay in a currency other than USD, the prices listed in your currency on Cloud Platform SKUs apply.

You are charged only for requests that return a 200 OK response code. Requests that result in other response codes, such as 4xx or 5xx, do not incur charges for input or output.

For all other Vertex AI pricing, including ML Platform and MLOps services, see the Vertex AI pricing page.

Model Availability

Starting April 29, 2025, Gemini 1.5 Pro and Gemini 1.5 Flash models are not available in projects that have no prior usage of these models, including new projects. For details, see Model versions and lifecycle.

Concepts
  • Token: The basic unit of text processed by a large language model; approximately 4 characters of English text equals one token.
  • Grounded Prompt: A request submitted to a model that includes one or more queries to an external data source like Google Search to provide more factual and up-to-date responses.
  • Provisioned Throughput: A service that provides a reserved amount of model processing capacity for a fixed price, ensuring consistent performance and throughput.
  • Generative AI Scale Unit (GSU): The unit of measure for purchasing provisioned throughput.
  • Context Caching: A feature that stores parts of your input (context) to reduce costs and latency on subsequent requests with similar context.

docs.title: Provisioned Throughput
docs.text:
Provisioned throughput guarantees a set amount of throughput for your generative AI workloads, transacted via generative AI scale units (GSUs). You can learn more about GSU throughput here and use our online estimator.

Duration Price per GSU Per 1 week commit $1,200 Week 1 month commit $2,700 Month 3 month commit $2,400 Month 1 year commit $2,000 Month

docs.title: Example cost calculation
docs.text:
A user needs to support 10 queries per second (QPS) for a query with 1,000 input text tokens, 500 input audio tokens, and 300 output text tokens using gemini-2.0-flash.

  1. Calculate Burndown-Adjusted Tokens per Query: Using the throughput and burndown rate table, we find the rates for gemini-2.0-flash:

    • Input text burndown rate: 1 token
    • Input audio burndown rate: 7 tokens

    • Output text burndown rate: 4 tokens

    • Input tokens: (1,000 text tokens * 1) + (500 audio tokens * 7) = 4,500 burndown-adjusted tokens

    • Output tokens: 300 text tokens * 4 = 1,200 burndown-adjusted tokens
    • Total per query: 4,500 + 1,200 = 5,700 total tokens

  2. Calculate Total Tokens per Second:

    • 5,700 tokens/query * 10 QPS = 57,000 total tokens per second.

  3. Calculate Required GSUs:

    • 57,000 tokens/sec ÷ 3,360 per-second throughput/GSU = 16.96 GSUs.
    • Since the minimum purchase increment is 1, the user needs 17 GSUs.

  4. Calculate Cost:

    • 1 week: 17 GSUs * $1,200/GSU = $20,400
    • 1 month: 17 GSUs * $2,700/GSU = $45,900
    • 3 months: 17 GSUs * $2,400/GSU = $40,800 per month
    • 1 year: 17 GSUs * $2,000/GSU = $34,000 per month

docs.title: Gemini Online Inference on Vertex AI Service Level Agreement (SLA)
docs.text:
During the Term of the agreement under which Google has agreed to provide Google Cloud Platform to Customer (as applicable, the "Agreement"), the Covered Service will provide a Monthly Uptime Percentage to Customer (the "Service Level Objective" or "SLO") as follows:

Covered Service Monthly Uptime Percentage generateContent and streamGenerateContent methods of Gemini Online Inference on Vertex AI 99.5%

If Google does not meet the SLO, and if Customer meets its obligations under this SLA, Customer will be eligible to receive the Financial Credits described below. Monthly Uptime Percentage and Financial Credit are determined on a calendar month basis per Project. This SLA states Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for any failure by Google to meet the SLO. Capitalized terms used in this SLA, but not defined in this SLA, have the meaning set forth in the Agreement. If the Agreement authorizes the resale or supply of Google Cloud Platform under a Google Cloud partner or reseller program, then all references to Customer in this SLA mean Partner or Reseller (as applicable), and any Financial Credit(s) will only apply for impacted Partner or Reseller order(s) under the Agreement.

docs.title: Definitions
docs.text:
The following definitions apply to the SLA:

  • "Covered Service" means the generateContent and streamGenerateContent methods of Gemini Online Inference API on Vertex AI.
  • "Downtime" means more than a five percent Error Rate and is measured based on server side Error Rate.
  • "Downtime Period" means a period of five or more consecutive minutes of Downtime. Partial minutes or intermittent Downtime for a period of less than five minutes will not count towards any Downtime Periods.
  • "Error Rate" means the number of Valid Requests that result in an error code response with HTTP Status 5XX divided by the total number of Valid Requests during the Downtime Period.
  • "Financial Credit" means the following:
Monthly Uptime Percentage Percentage of monthly bill for the Covered Service that does not meet SLO that will be credited to Customer's future monthly bills 99.0% - < 99.5% 10% 95.0% - < 99.0% 25% < 95.0% 50%
  • "Monthly Uptime Percentage" means total number of minutes in a month, minus the number of minutes of Downtime suffered from all Downtime Periods in a month, divided by the total number of minutes in a month.
  • "Valid Requests" are requests that conform to the Documentation, and that would normally result in a non-error response.

docs.title: Customer must request Financial Credit
docs.text: In order to receive any of the Financial Credits described above, Customer must notify Google technical support within 30 days from the time Customer becomes eligible to receive a Financial Credit. Customer must also provide Google with log files showing Downtime Periods and the date and time they occurred. If Customer does not comply with these requirements, Customer will forfeit its right to receive a Financial Credit. Further, Customer must be in good standing under the Agreement in order to receive a Financial Credit.

docs.title: Maximum Financial Credit
docs.text: The maximum aggregate number of Financial Credits issued by Google to Customer for all Downtime Periods in a single billing month will not exceed 50% of the amount due from Customer for the Covered Service that did not meet SLO for the applicable month. Financial Credits will be in the form of a monetary credit applied to future use of the Covered Service and will be applied within 60 days after the Financial Credit was agreed to by Google.

docs.title: SLA exclusions
docs.text:
The SLA does not apply to any (a) features or services designated pre-general availability (unless otherwise set forth in the associated Documentation); (b) features or services excluded from the SLA (in the associated Documentation), including requests made using Grounding with Google Search; or (c) errors (i) caused by factors outside of Google's reasonable control; (ii) that resulted from Customer's software or hardware or third party software or hardware, or both; (iii) that resulted from abuses or other behaviors that violate the Agreement; or (iv) that resulted from quotas applied by the system or listed in the Documentation or Admin Console.

docs.title: Access control
docs.text:
To use the generative AI features on Vertex AI, principals (for example, users, groups, and service accounts) in your project must be granted the appropriate Identity and Access Management (IAM) role. You can grant predefined roles for common use cases or create custom roles for least-privilege access.

This page describes the predefined roles available for generative AI features and lists the specific permissions you can use to create custom roles.

Concepts
  • Principal: An identity that can be granted access to a Google Cloud resource. A principal can be a Google Account (for an end user), a service account (for an application or compute workload), a Google group, or a Google Workspace account or Cloud Identity domain that can access the resource.
  • IAM Role: A collection of permissions that defines what actions are allowed on a resource. When you grant a role to a principal, you grant all the permissions that the role contains.
  • Permission: Determines what operations are allowed on a resource. Permissions are represented in the format service.resource.verb, such as aiplatform.endpoints.predict.

docs.title: Predefined roles
docs.text:
IAM provides predefined roles that grant access to specific resources and prevent unauthorized access to other resources. If a predefined role meets your needs, you can grant it to a principal instead of creating a custom role.

The following table compares the most common predefined roles for users of Vertex AI generative AI features:

Role Description Key Use Case Vertex AI Administrator (roles/aiplatform.admin) Provides full access to all Vertex AI resources, including the ability to manage models, endpoints, and jobs. For principals who need to manage the entire Vertex AI environment, including creating, deleting, and modifying all resources. Vertex AI User (roles/aiplatform.user) Provides permissions to use Vertex AI resources, such as running prediction jobs and managing datasets, but not to create or delete certain resources like endpoints. For developers, data scientists, and applications that need to use generative AI models and other Vertex AI features without having full administrative control.

To learn more about all available Vertex AI IAM roles, see Vertex AI access control with IAM.
