docs.title: Choose an embeddings task type
docs.text: Vertex AI embeddings models can generate optimized embeddings for various task types, such as document retrieval, question answering, and fact verification. Task types are labels that optimize the embeddings that the model generates based on your intended use case. This document describes how to choose the optimal task type for your embeddings.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Embeddings: Numerical vector representations of text, images, or other data, where similar items have vectors that are close to each other in the vector space.
  • Task Type: A parameter that optimizes the generated embeddings for a specific downstream application, such as retrieval, classification, or clustering.
  • Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG): A technique that enhances the responses of Large Language Models (LLMs) by retrieving relevant information from an external knowledge base and providing it as context.
  • Vector Search: A method for finding the most similar items to a given query in a high-dimensional vector space, commonly used with embeddings.
  • Symmetric vs. Asymmetric Search:
    • Symmetric: Use cases where the query and the documents are of similar length and structure (e.g., finding similar sentences). The SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY task type is symmetric.
    • Asymmetric: Use cases where the query is typically short and the documents are long (e.g., searching a database of articles with a keyword query). Retrieval-focused task types are asymmetric.

docs.title: Supported models
docs.text:
Task types are supported by the following models:

  • text-embedding-005
  • text-multilingual-embedding-002
  • gemini-embedding-001

Preview

The following limitations apply when using these models:

  • Don't use these preview models on mission critical or production systems.
  • These models are available in us-central1 only.
  • Batch predictions are not supported.
  • Customization is not supported.

docs.title: Benefits of using task types
docs.text:
Task types can improve the quality of embeddings generated by an embeddings model.

For example, when building Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, a common design is to use text embeddings and Vector Search to perform a similarity search. This can sometimes lead to poor search quality because questions and their answers are not always semantically similar. A question like "Why is the sky blue?" and its answer "The scattering of sunlight causes the blue color" have different meanings as standalone statements. Without task types, a RAG system might not recognize their relationship.

Figure 1. Questions and their answers aren't semantically similar, which means that embeddings won't automatically show their relation.

To overcome this, a developer might need to fine-tune a model to learn the relationship between queries and answers or use advanced techniques like LLM-based query expansion or HyDE, which can add latency and cost.

Task types solve this problem by generating optimized embeddings that place the query and its corresponding answer closer together in the embedding space. This saves the time and cost of developing custom task-specific embeddings and leads to improved similarity search results in RAG systems and other applications like classification, clustering, and fact verification.

Figure 2. Task types optimize embeddings for specific tasks. In this case, questions and answers are brought closer together in the embeddings space.

docs.title: How to choose a task type
docs.text:
The best task type depends on your specific use case. The following workflow helps you determine which task type to select. If your use case doesn't align with a documented use case, use the RETRIEVAL_QUERY task type by default.

flowchart TD
    A[Start: Determine your use case] --> B{What is your primary goal?};
    B --> C[Retrieve information from a text corpus?];
    B --> D[Classify text into predefined categories?];
    B --> E[Group similar texts together?];
    B --> F[Assess similarity between two texts?];

    C --> G["<b>Use Asymmetric Task Types:</b><br/>- RETRIEVAL_QUERY (for queries)<br/>- RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT (for corpus)<br/>- QUESTION_ANSWERING<br/>- FACT_VERIFICATION<br/>- CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY"];
    D --> H["<b>Use Symmetric Task Type:</b><br/>- CLASSIFICATION"];
    E --> I["<b>Use Symmetric Task Type:</b><br/>- CLUSTERING"];
    F --> J["<b>Use Symmetric Task Type:</b><br/>- SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY"];

    click G "#information-retrieval"
    click H "#classification"
    click I "#clustering"
    click J "#semantic-similarity"

The following table provides a summary of the available task types.

Task Type Description Use Case Type RETRIEVAL_QUERY Generates embeddings for a short query to search a large corpus of documents. Asymmetric RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT Generates embeddings for the documents in a corpus that will be searched over. Asymmetric QUESTION_ANSWERING Generates embeddings for a query that is phrased as a question. Asymmetric FACT_VERIFICATION Generates embeddings for a query to retrieve documents that support or refute a factual claim. Asymmetric CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY Generates embeddings for a natural language query to retrieve relevant code blocks. Asymmetric CLASSIFICATION Generates embeddings optimized to classify texts according to preset labels. Symmetric CLUSTERING Generates embeddings optimized to cluster texts based on their similarities. Symmetric SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY Generates embeddings optimized to assess the semantic similarity between two texts. Not for retrieval. Symmetric

docs.title: Task type use cases and examples
docs.text:
Information Retrieval

When building a search or retrieval system, you work with two types of text: a corpus (the collection of documents to search over) and a query (the user's search input). For the best performance, you must use different task types for the corpus and the queries.

1. Embed your document corpus: First, generate embeddings for your entire collection of documents using the RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT task type. You typically perform this step once to index your corpus and store the resulting embeddings in a vector database.

2. Embed user queries: Next, when a user submits a search, generate an embedding for their query in real time using a task type that matches their intent. The system uses this query embedding to find the most similar document embeddings in your vector database.

The following task types are used for queries:

  • RETRIEVAL_QUERY: Use for standard search queries to find relevant documents.
  • QUESTION_ANSWERING: Use when queries are expected to be questions (e.g., "How do I tie my shoelaces?").
  • FACT_VERIFICATION: Use to retrieve a document that proves or disproves a statement (e.g., "apples grow underground").
  • CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY: Use to retrieve a code block based on a natural language query (e.g., "sort an array"). Code blocks in the corpus should be embedded using RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT.

Key Point: To get embeddings for information retrieval, use RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT for your documents and a corresponding query task type (like RETRIEVAL_QUERY) for user queries.

Classification

If you want to use embeddings to classify texts according to preset labels, use the CLASSIFICATION task type. This task type generates embeddings in a space that is optimized for classification.

For example, to classify the sentiment of social media posts as positive, negative, or neutral, you would embed a post like "I don't like traveling on airplanes" using the CLASSIFICATION task type. The resulting embedding would be suitable for a model to classify its sentiment as negative.

Key Point: To get embeddings that are optimized to classify text using predefined labels, use the CLASSIFICATION task type.

Clustering

If you want to use embeddings to cluster texts based on their similarities, use the CLUSTERING task type. This task type generates embeddings that are optimized for being grouped based on similarity.

For example, you can generate embeddings for news articles to show users articles that are topically related to ones they have previously read. After the embeddings are generated and clustered, you can suggest additional sports-related articles to users who read a lot about sports.

Additional use cases for clustering include:

  • Customer segmentation: Group customers with similar profiles for targeted marketing.
  • Product segmentation: Cluster products based on titles, descriptions, or reviews for segment analysis.
  • Market research: Cluster survey responses or social media data to reveal hidden patterns and trends.
  • Healthcare: Cluster patients based on medical data to identify groups with similar conditions or treatment responses.
  • Customer feedback trends: Cluster feedback from surveys, social media, and support tickets to identify common pain points and feature requests.

Key Point: To get embeddings that are optimized for clustering based on similarities, use the CLUSTERING task type.

Semantic Similarity

If you want to use embeddings to assess the similarity between two texts, use the SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY task type. This task type is optimized for generating similarity scores.

For example, to compare the similarity of "The cat is sleeping" and "The feline is napping," you would generate embeddings for both texts. A similarity score calculated from these embeddings would be high because both texts have nearly the same meaning.

A real-world scenario is a recommendation system that identifies items (products, articles, movies) that are semantically similar to a user's preferred items to provide personalized recommendations.

Key Point: To get embeddings that are optimized to assess text similarity, use the SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY task type.

Note: SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY is not intended for retrieval use cases like document search. For retrieval, use RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT, RETRIEVAL_QUERY, QUESTION_ANSWERING, or FACT_VERIFICATION.

docs.title: Code examples
docs.text:
The following examples demonstrate how to generate an embedding for a code retrieval query.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

RESTPython 
PROJECT_ID=PROJECT_ID

curl \
-X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/text-embedding-005:predict -d \
$'{
  "instances": [
    {
      "task_type": "CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY",
      "content": "Function to add two numbers"
    }
  ],
}'

To learn how to install or update the Vertex AI SDK for Python, see Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python. For more information, see the Vertex AI SDK for Python API reference documentation.

from vertexai.language_models import TextEmbeddingInput, TextEmbeddingModel

MODEL_NAME = "gemini-embedding-001"
DIMENSIONALITY = 3072


def embed_text(
    texts: list[str] = ["Retrieve a function that adds two numbers"],
    task: str = "CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY",
    model_name: str = "gemini-embedding-001",
    dimensionality: int | None = 3072,
) -> list[list[float]]:
    """Embeds texts with a pre-trained, foundational model."""
    model = TextEmbeddingModel.from_pretrained(model_name)
    kwargs = dict(output_dimensionality=dimensionality) if dimensionality else {}

    embeddings = []
    # gemini-embedding-001 takes one input at a time
    for text in texts:
        text_input = TextEmbeddingInput(text, task)
        embedding = model.get_embeddings([text_input], **kwargs)
        print(embedding)
        # Example response:
        # [[0.006135190837085247, -0.01462465338408947, 0.004978656303137541, ...]]
        embeddings.append(embedding[0].values)

    return embeddings


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Embeds code retrieval query with a pre-trained, foundational model.
    # Using this function to calculate the embedding for the query.
    texts = ["Retrieve a function that adds two numbers"]
    task = "CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY"
    code_query_embeddings = embed_text(
        texts=texts, task=task, model_name=MODEL_NAME, dimensionality=DIMENSIONALITY
    )

    # Embeds code blocks with a pre-trained, foundational model.
    # Using this function to calculate the embedding for the corpus.
    texts = [
        "def func(a, b): return a + b",
        "def func(a, b): return a - b",
        "def func(a, b): return (a ** 2 + b ** 2) ** 0.5",
    ]
    task = "RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT"
    code_block_embeddings = embed_text(
        texts=texts, task=task, model_name=MODEL_NAME, dimensionality=DIMENSIONALITY
    )

docs.title: Ground responses using RAG
docs.text:
Grounding is a technique that helps produce model responses that are more trustworthy and factual by connecting them to verifiable sources of information. The recommended best practice for implementing grounding is retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). RAG retrieves relevant data from an indexed knowledge base and provides it to the generative model as context for its response.

Vertex AI provides multiple ways to implement a RAG solution, from a fully integrated experience to a custom, mix-and-match approach using individual components.

docs.title: Approaches to RAG in Vertex AI
docs.text:
Vertex AI offers both a managed, end-to-end RAG solution and individual APIs that you can use to build your own custom RAG pipeline. The following table compares these two approaches.

Approach Description Best for Key Components Vertex AI RAG Engine (Integrated) A fully managed, end-to-end RAG solution that handles document ingestion, parsing, indexing, retrieval, and generation. Users who want a quick and easy way to ground models on their own data without building a custom pipeline. An integrated service that abstracts away the underlying components. Custom RAG with Vertex AI Components A flexible approach where you build your own RAG pipeline using individual, swappable Vertex AI and Document AI components. Users who need full control and customization over their RAG workflow, such as using a custom retriever or a different vector database.
  • Document layout parser
  • Vertex AI Vector Search
  • Grounding generation API
  • Check grounding API

This document focuses on the integrated approach using the Vertex AI RAG Engine.

docs.title: Ground responses using the Vertex AI RAG Engine
docs.text: You can ground a model on your data directly in the Vertex AI Studio by connecting your prompt to a RAG Engine corpus.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Grounding: The process of connecting a generative model's output to verifiable sources of information to enhance its factuality and trustworthiness.
  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): A technique where a model retrieves relevant information from a data source before generating a response, allowing it to answer questions based on knowledge outside of its training data.
  • Corpus: A collection of documents that you provide to the RAG Engine to serve as the knowledge base for grounding.
  • Vertex AI RAG Engine: A managed Vertex AI service that ingests your data, indexes it for retrieval, and performs the RAG process to ground model responses.

Before you can ground a prompt, you must have a corpus of data created and ingested by the RAG Engine.

Steps to ground a prompt

1. Go to the Create prompt page

3. Select RAG Engine

docs.title: Use Google Search suggestions
docs.text:
When you use grounding with Google Search, you must display any Search suggestions returned in the model's response within your application.

For more information on grounding with Google Search, see Grounding with Google Search.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Grounding: The process of connecting a large language model's (LLM) response to verifiable sources of information, such as Google Search, to improve accuracy and reduce hallucinations.
  • Search suggestions: Search query terms, provided in the API response, that you must display alongside the grounded LLM response to allow users to explore the topic further on Google Search.

docs.title: Understanding the API response
docs.text:
When you make a grounded request, the API response includes the LLM-generated content and the search queries that you must display as Search suggestions. The key fields are:

  • "content": The LLM-generated response.
  • "webSearchQueries": A list of search query strings to be used for the Search suggestions.

For example, the following JSON snippet shows a grounded response to a prompt about a tropical plant.

"predictions": [
  {
    "content": "Monstera is a type of vine that thrives in bright indirect light…",
    "groundingMetadata": {
      "webSearchQueries": ["What's a monstera?"],
    }
  }
]

You must take the webSearchQueries from this output and display them as Search suggestions in your application according to the following requirements.

docs.title: Usage requirements
docs.text:
• Display the Search suggestion exactly as it is provided in the API response, without any modifications.
  • When a user interacts with a Search suggestion, they must be taken directly to the Google Search results page (SRP).
  • Do not include any intermediate screens or additional steps between the user's tap and the display of the SRP.
  • Do not display any other search results or suggestions next to the Search suggestion or its associated grounded LLM response.

docs.title: Display requirements
docs.text:
• Visual Fidelity: Display the Search suggestion exactly as provided, without modifying colors, fonts, or appearance. The suggestion must render as specified in the following light and dark mode mockups.

    Example of Search suggestion chips in light and dark modes.

  • Visibility: The corresponding Search suggestion must remain visible whenever a grounded response is shown.

  • Branding: You must strictly follow Google's guidelines for third-party use of Google brand features, available at the Brand Resource Center.
  • Layout: The field containing the Search suggestion chips must be the same width as the grounded response from the LLM.

docs.title: User interaction
docs.text:
When a user taps a Search suggestion chip, they are taken directly to an SRP for the search term displayed in the chip. The SRP can open either within your application's browser or in a separate browser application. Do not minimize, remove, or obstruct the SRP's display in any way.

The following animation illustrates the required tap-to-SRP interaction.

Animation showing the user flow from tapping a suggestion to viewing the SRP.

docs.title: Implementation using the API response
docs.text:
When you use the API to ground a response with Google Search, the model response provides compliant HTML and CSS styling in the renderedContent field. You can implement this field directly to display the Search suggestions in your application.

For a complete example of the API response containing the renderedContent field, see the response section in Grounding with Google Search.

Note: The HTML and CSS provided in the API response automatically adapt to the user's device settings, displaying in either light or dark mode based on the prefers-color-scheme media feature.

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Grounding with Elasticsearch
docs.text:
This page explains how to use your Elasticsearch instance to ground large language model (LLM) responses on your private data.

Grounding enhances LLM responses by providing factual context from specified data sources. By grounding with Elasticsearch, you can leverage your existing Elasticsearch indexes to improve the quality and reliability of Gemini's output. This helps reduce hallucinations and ensures responses are relevant to your data.

This capability allows you to build powerful Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) applications, such as:

  • Generative search summaries
  • Question-and-answer chatbots using enterprise data
  • Agents grounded in your proprietary data

You can ground a model on up to 10 data sources at once. For comprehensive results, you can combine grounding with Elasticsearch with Grounding with Google Search to connect the model to public information from the internet.

docs.title: Supported models
docs.text:
The following models support grounding with Elasticsearch for text-only input:

Preview

The following models are in Preview: * Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite * Gemini 2.5 Flash with Live API native audio * Gemini 2.0 Flash with Live API

  • Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Grounding: The process of connecting a large language model (LLM) to external data sources to provide factual, up-to-date context for its responses.
  • RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation): An AI framework that retrieves facts from an external knowledge base to ground LLMs before they generate a response.
  • Elasticsearch Index: A collection of related documents in Elasticsearch that are stored and indexed together for fast searching.
  • Search Template: A predefined search request in Elasticsearch that can be executed with different parameters, simplifying complex queries.
  • kNN (k-Nearest Neighbors) Search: A method for finding the 'k' most similar items in a dataset to a query, commonly used for semantic search with vector embeddings.
Prerequisites

Before you can ground LLM responses with Elasticsearch, complete the following:

  1. Enable the Vertex AI API: Ensure the Vertex AI API is enabled for your Google Cloud project.
  2. Install the gcloud CLI: Install and initialize the Google Cloud command-line tool.
  3. Set up Elasticsearch: You need an existing Elasticsearch cluster and index. Gather the following information:
    • Endpoint: The URL of your Elasticsearch cluster.
    • Index Name: The name of the index you want to search (e.g., my-data-index).
    • API Key: An API key that grants access to your Elasticsearch cluster. The key must have the prefix ApiKey.
  4. Create an Elasticsearch search template: Create a search template that returns result data for grounding. For more information, see the next section.

docs.title: Set up a search template in Elasticsearch
Generate grounded responses
docs.text:
This section shows you how to generate a response grounded in your Elasticsearch data. The following diagram shows the overall workflow.

flowchart TD
    A[Set up a search template in Elasticsearch] --> B[Generate grounded responses];
    B --> C[Understand your response];

    click A "#setup-template"
    click B "#generate-responses"
    click C "#understand-your-response"
ConsoleREST API

To ground a model with Elasticsearch in the Google Cloud console, follow these steps:

  1. Go to the Vertex AI Studio Create prompt page.

    Go to Create prompt

  2. In the Settings panel, click the Grounding: Your data toggle to enable it.

  3. In the Customize Grounding pane, select Elasticsearch.
  4. Enter your Elasticsearch endpoint.
  5. Enter your Elasticsearch API Key.
  6. Enter your Elasticsearch index.
  7. Enter your Elasticsearch search template.
  8. Adjust the Number of hits slider to set the number of results to retrieve.
  9. Click Save.
  10. Enter your prompt in the prompt input field.
  11. Click Submit to generate the grounded response.

This section shows how to use the Vertex AI API to ground a model with your Elasticsearch data source.

Prepare a grounded generation request

To send a text prompt and ground it with Elasticsearch, send a POST request to the Vertex AI API. In the request body, replace the following placeholders:

  • QUERY: The text prompt to ground.
  • ELASTIC_SEARCH_ENDPOINT: The absolute endpoint path for the Elasticsearch resource.
  • ELASTIC_SEARCH_API_KEY: The API key for the Elasticsearch data endpoint.
  • INDEX_NAME: The name of the Elasticsearch index to use for grounding.
  • SEARCH_TEMPLATE_NAME: The Elasticsearch search template to use for grounding.
  • NUM_HITS: The number of results to return from the Elasticsearch data source.

Request JSON body:

{
  "contents": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "parts": [
        {
          "text": "QUERY"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "tools": [{
    "retrieval": {
      "externalApi": {
        "api_spec": "ELASTIC_SEARCH",
        "endpoint": "ELASTIC_SEARCH_ENDPOINT",
        "apiAuth": {
          "apiKeyConfig": {
            "apiKeyString": "ApiKey ELASTIC_SEARCH_API_KEY"
          }
        },
        "elasticSearchParams": {
          "index": "INDEX_NAME",
          "searchTemplate": "SEARCH_TEMPLATE_NAME",
          "numHits": "NUM_HITS",
        }
      }
    }
  }]
}

For more information on other API fields, such as system instructions and multi-turn chats, see the Generative AI beginner's guide.

Send the API request

Save the request body in a file named request.json. Then, execute the following curl command. Replace the following placeholders:

  • LOCATION: The region to process the request. For available locations, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.
  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID. For more information, see Creating and managing projects.
  • MODEL_ID: The ID of the multimodal model you are using.
curl -X POST \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
    -d @request.json \
"https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:generateContent"

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.text:

Grounding with Google Maps in Vertex AI combines the power of Gemini with Google Maps, which has access to information on over 250 million places. This integration, available through Vertex AI, is designed to help you create a new generation of generative applications.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Grounding with Google Maps in Vertex AI is a service that lets you use Google Maps data with LLMs to provide more accurate and context-aware responses to your prompts. This feature is integrated with Vertex AI to support your use of geographical data with your Gemini model.

Grounding with Google Maps helps you to discover new places, plan for events, and get recommendations for a variety of locations. You can do the following:

  • Ask a conversational assistant about the area and any nearby places. Your assistant has access to travel time information and can let you know how far a place is from your location. For example, Are there any parks nearby?
  • See personalized descriptions of the place that matches your criteria. For example, Can you tell me more about the parks and any family-friendly restaurants that are within a walkable distance?

Grounding with Google Maps lets you create generative AI applications from an LLM-powered chat using geospatial context to generate a personalized location-based summary to help you make better decisions.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Grounding: The process of connecting a language model's responses to verifiable, real-world information from a specific data source, in this case, Google Maps.
  • Gemini: A family of powerful, multimodal large language models (LLMs) developed by Google.
  • LLM (Large Language Model): A type of artificial intelligence model trained on vast amounts of text data to understand and generate human-like language.
  • API Key: A unique identifier used to authenticate requests associated with your project for usage and billing purposes.
  • Contextual Widget: An interactive UI component that displays rich, contextual information from Google Maps related to the generated response.

This guide walks you through the process of setting up and enabling Grounding with Google Maps for your Vertex AI project.

docs.title: Ground your model
docs.text:
You can use the Google Maps API to ground your model's responses. These code samples demonstrate how to use the Maps API to ground your model's responses using either the Python SDK or the REST API.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Python SDKREST API

Install the SDK

pip install --upgrade google-genai

To learn more, see the SDK reference documentation.

Set environment variables and run the code

# Replace the `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` values
# with appropriate values for your project.
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global
export GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=True


from google import genai
from google.genai.types import (
    ApiKeyConfig,
    AuthConfig,
    GenerateContentConfig,
    GoogleMaps,
    HttpOptions,
    Tool,
)

# TODO(developer): Update below line with your Google Maps API key
GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY = "YOUR_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY"

client = genai.Client(http_options=HttpOptions(api_version="v1"))

response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents="Recommend a good restaurant in San Francisco.",
    config=GenerateContentConfig(
        tools=[
            # Use Google Maps Tool
            Tool(
                google_maps=GoogleMaps(
                    auth_config=AuthConfig(
                        api_key_config=ApiKeyConfig(
                            api_key_string=GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY,
                        )
                    )
                )
            )
        ],
    ),
)

print(response.text)
# Example response:
# 'San Francisco boasts a vibrant culinary scene...'

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • LOCATION: The region to process the request.
  • PROJECT_ID: Your project ID.
  • MODEL_ID: The model ID of the multimodal model.
  • TEXT: The text instructions to include in the prompt.
  • API_KEY: Your API key.
  • LATITUDE: The latitude of the location.
  • LONGITUDE: The longitude of the location.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:generateContent

Request JSON body:

{
  "contents": [{
    "role": "user",
    "parts": [{
      "text": "TEXT"
    }]
  }],
  "tools": [{
    "googleMaps": {
      "authConfig": {
        "apiKeyConfig": {
          "apiKeyString": "API_KEY"
        }
      }
    }
  }],
  "toolConfig": {
    "retrievalConfig": {
      "latLng": {
        "latitude": LATITUDE,
        "longitude": LONGITUDE
      }
    }
  },
  "model": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID"
}

To send your request, expand one of these options:

curlPowerShell

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login , or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI . You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \  
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \  
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \  
     -d @request.json \  
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:generateContent"

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login . You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token  
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }  

Invoke-WebRequest `  
    -Method POST `  
    -Headers $headers `  
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `  
    -InFile request.json `  
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:generateContent" | Select-Object -Expand Content

Your page that displays the widget must use the alpha version of the Google Maps JS API. For more information, see Load the Maps JavaScript API. You must use the same API key that was enabled for Grounding with Google Maps to load the Google Maps JS API.

Create a widget (HTML)Update a widget (JavaScript)Create a widget (JavaScript)Configure layoutDisable the map

This code sample demonstrates how to create a widget using HTML.

<body>
  <gmp-place-contextual id="widget"></gmp-place-contextual>
</body>

Use the following method to update the context token in your JavaScript.

function updateWidget(contextToken) {
  let widget = document.querySelector('#widget');
  widget.contextToken = contextToken;
}

You can also create a widget dynamically with the following code.

async function createWidget(contextToken) {
  await google.maps.importLibrary('places');
  let widgetContainer = document.querySelector('#wc');  // a div that contains the widget
  const placeContextualElement = new
      google.maps.places.PlaceContextualElement({ contextToken });
  widgetContainer.appendChild(placeContextualElement);
}

This HTML code sample demonstrates how to use configuration options to toggle between two different layouts (compact or vertical).

<gmp-place-contextual id="widget">
  <gmp-place-contextual-list-config layout="compact">
  </gmp-place-contextual-list-config>
</gmp-place-contextual>

This HTML code sample demonstrates how to disable the map.

<gmp-place-contextual id="widget">
  <gmp-place-contextual-list-config map-hidden>
  </gmp-place-contextual-list-config>
</gmp-place-contextual>

This JavaScript code sample demonstrates how to specify a compact layout and hide the map.

const widgetConfig = new google.maps.places.PlaceContextualListConfigElement({
  layout: 'compact',
  mapHidden: true
});
widget.appendChild(widgetConfig);

docs.title: Place properties
docs.text:
This section lists place properties that are used to describe locations and used by Grounding with Google Maps to generate responses. These properties are used to determine the types of questions that Grounding with Google Maps can answer.

Sample place properties

This list provides an alphabetized sampling of properties about places that might be used by your model to generate responses.

  • Address
  • Cash only
  • Credit card
  • Curbside pickup
  • Debit card
  • Distance
  • Free parking lot
  • Live music
  • Menu for children
  • Opening hours
  • Pet friendly
  • Serves beer
  • Serves vegetarian food
  • Wheelchair accessible
  • Wifi

Examples of using place properties

The following examples use place properties in questions about different types of places. Grounding with Google Maps uses the properties to understand your intent and then provides relevant answers based on the data associated with places in Google Maps.

  • Plan a family dinner: You might ask, Is "The Italian Place" good for children, and do they offer takeout? What is their rating? Answers to these questions help you to determine if a restaurant is suitable for a family and if the restaurant offers a convenient service.

  • Check accessibility for a friend: You might ask, I need a restaurant that has a wheelchair accessible entrance. A response to this prompt might help you to determine if the location meets specific accessibility needs.

  • Find a location for a late-night snack: You might ask, Is "Burger Joint" open now? Do they serve dinner? What are their opening hours for Friday? Answers to these questions help you to find an open establishment serving a specific meal during a particular time.

  • Meet a client for coffee: You might ask, Does "Cafe Central" have Wifi? Do they serve coffee? What is their price level, and do they accept credit cards? Answers to these questions help you to assess the suitability of a cafe for a business meeting based on amenities, offerings, and payment options.

docs.title: Grounding with Google Search
docs.text:
This page explains how to ground a model's responses using Google Search, which leverages publicly-available web data to provide more accurate and up-to-date answers.

Important: If you receive Google Search suggestions with a response, that response is a "Grounded Result" subject to the Grounding with Google Search terms in the Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. To use Google Search suggestions, see Use Google Search suggestions.

Note for web publishers: Grounding with Google Search on Vertex AI does not use web pages for grounding that have disallowed Google-Extended. Web publishers can manage inclusion in Google-Extended with a robots.txt file.

To learn more about model grounding in Vertex AI, see the Grounding overview.

docs.title: Why ground with Google Search?
docs.text:
Using Google Search as a tool for grounding enables complex prompts and workflows that require planning, reasoning, and up-to-date information. Key benefits include:

  • Factual Accuracy: Ground responses in the latest and most accurate information available on the public web.
  • Web Artifact Analysis: Retrieve and analyze artifacts from the web.
  • Multimodal Assistance: Find relevant images, videos, or other media to assist in multimodal reasoning or task generation.
  • Specialized Tasks: Perform coding, technical troubleshooting, and other specialized tasks with greater precision.
  • Region-Specific Information: Find region-specific information or assist in translating content accurately.
  • Web Browsing: Find relevant websites for browsing.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Grounding: The process of connecting a model's responses to verifiable sources of information to improve accuracy and reduce hallucinations.
  • Temperature: A parameter that controls the randomness of a model's output; a higher value (e.g., 1.0) results in more creative responses, while a lower value results in more deterministic ones.
  • Model: A specific version of a machine learning model, such as Gemini 2.5 Pro.
  • Prompt: The input text or instruction given to a model to generate a response.

  • Grounding with Google Search has a limit of one million queries per day. If you require more queries, contact Google Cloud support for assistance.

You can ground a model with publicly available web data using the Vertex AI Studio, the Generative AI SDKs, or the REST API.

ConsoleGenerative AI SDKREST API

Use the Vertex AI Studio

1. Go to Vertex AI Studio

In the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI Studio page.

Go to Vertex AI Studio

2. Select the Freeform tab

Click the Freeform tab.

3. Enable model grounding

In the side panel, click the Ground model responses toggle.

4. Set Google Search as the source

Click Customize and set Google Search as the source.

5. Submit your prompt

Enter your prompt in the text box and click Submit. Your prompt responses are now grounded to Google Search.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

==== "Python"

**Install the SDK**

```bash
pip install --upgrade google-genai
```

To learn more, see the [SDK reference documentation](https://googleapis.github.io/python-genai/).

**Set environment variables and run the code**

```bash
# Replace the `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` values
# with appropriate values for your project.
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global
export GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=True
```

```python
from google import genai
from google.genai.types import (
    GenerateContentConfig,
    GoogleSearch,
    HttpOptions,
    Tool,
)

client = genai.Client(http_options=HttpOptions(api_version="v1"))

response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents="When is the next total solar eclipse in the United States?",
    config=GenerateContentConfig(
        tools=[
            # Use Google Search Tool
            Tool(google_search=GoogleSearch())
        ],
    ),
)

print(response.text)
# Example response:
# 'The next total solar eclipse in the United States will occur on ...'
```

==== "Go"

**Install the SDK**

Learn how to install or update the [Gen AI SDK for Go](../sdks/overview.md). To learn more, see the [SDK reference documentation](https://pkg.go.dev/google.golang.org/genai).

**Set environment variables and run the code**

```bash
# Replace the `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` values
# with appropriate values for your project.
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global
export GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=True
```

```go
import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "io"

    genai "google.golang.org/genai"
)

// generateWithGoogleSearch shows how to generate text using Google Search.
func generateWithGoogleSearch(w io.Writer) error {
    ctx := context.Background()

    client, err := genai.NewClient(ctx, &genai.ClientConfig{
        HTTPOptions: genai.HTTPOptions{APIVersion: "v1"},
    })
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to create genai client: %w", err)
    }

    modelName := "gemini-2.0-flash-001"
    contents := []*genai.Content{
        {Parts: []*genai.Part{
            {Text: "When is the next total solar eclipse in the United States?"},
        }},
    }
    config := &genai.GenerateContentConfig{
        Tools: []*genai.Tool{
            {GoogleSearch: &genai.GoogleSearch{}},
        },
    }

    resp, err := client.Models.GenerateContent(ctx, modelName, contents, config)
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate content: %w", err)
    }

    respText, err := resp.Text()
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to convert model response to text: %w", err)
    }
    fmt.Fprintln(w, respText)

    // Example response:
    // The next total solar eclipse in the United States will occur on March 30, 2033, but it will only ...

    return nil
}
```

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Send a generateContent request
docs.text:
HTTP method and URL

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:generateContent

Request JSON body

{
  "contents": [{
    "role": "user",
    "parts": [{
      "text": "TEXT"
    }]
  }],
  "tools": [{
    "googleSearch": {}
  }],
  "model": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID"
}

To send your request, expand one of these options:

==== "curl (Linux, macOS, or Cloud Shell)"

**Note:** The following command assumes that you have logged in to the `gcloud` CLI with your user account by running `gcloud init` or `gcloud auth login`, or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the `gcloud` CLI. You can check the currently active account by running `gcloud auth list`.

Save the request body in a file named `request.json`, and execute the following command:

```bash
curl -X POST \  
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \  
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \  
     -d @request.json \  
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:generateContent"
```

==== "PowerShell (Windows)"

**Note:** The following command assumes that you have logged in to the `gcloud` CLI with your user account by running `gcloud init` or `gcloud auth login`. You can check the currently active account by running `gcloud auth list`.

Save the request body in a file named `request.json`, and execute the following command:

```powershell
$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token  
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }  

Invoke-WebRequest `  
    -Method POST `  
    -Headers $headers `  
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `  
    -InFile request.json `  
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:generateContent" | Select-Object -Expand Content
```

When using Grounding with Google Search a Customer Application can:

docs.title: Grounding with Vertex AI Search
docs.text:
This page explains how you can ground model responses by using your own data from Vertex AI Search.

Grounding connects a model to your organization's data to produce responses that are based on your information, which can reduce model hallucinations. If you want to perform retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), you can connect your model to your website data or your document sets by using Grounding with Vertex AI Search.

Grounding with your data supports a maximum of 10 Vertex AI Search data sources and can be combined with Grounding with Google Search.

docs.title: Supported models
docs.text:
The following models support grounding with your data:

  • Gemini 2.0 Flash

docs.title: Grounding workflow
docs.text:
The following diagram shows the workflow for grounding with Vertex AI Search.

flowchart TD
    A[Before you begin] --> B[Create a Vertex AI Search data store]
    B --> C[Generate grounded responses]

click A "#before-you-begin"
click B "#create-a-vertex-ai-search-data-store"
click C "#generate-grounded-responses"
Concepts
  • Grounding: A feature that connects model-generated responses to specific, verifiable data sources to enhance accuracy and reduce inaccuracies.
  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): A technique that enhances a large language model's responses by retrieving relevant information from an external knowledge base and incorporating it into the generated text.
  • Vertex AI Search: A Google Cloud service that lets you build powerful search applications using your own data.
  • Data Store: A repository within Vertex AI Search that holds your indexed data, such as documents or website content, and makes it available for search and grounding.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Prerequisites

Before you can ground model output to your data, complete the following steps:

1. Set up permissions

In the Google Cloud console, go to the IAM page and search for the discoveryengine.servingConfigs.search permission, which is required for the grounding service to work.

Go to IAM

2. Enable the Vertex AI Search API

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the AI Applications page. This page is part of the Vertex AI Search service.

    Go to AI Applications

  2. Read and agree to the terms of service, then click Continue and activate the API.

Important: You must accept the discovery solutions data use terms for every project that you want to use Vertex AI Search with.

Vertex AI Search is available in the global location, or the eu and us multi-regions. To learn more, see Vertex AI Search locations.

docs.title: Create a Vertex AI Search data store
docs.text:
To ground your model, you first need to create a data store in Vertex AI Search. You can create a data store from your website content or from documents stored in Cloud Storage. Choose the option that best fits your data source.

Feature Website Data Documents (from Cloud Storage) Use Case Grounding on publicly accessible web content. Grounding on private or unstructured documents (PDF, HTML, TXT). Data Source A list of website URLs to include or exclude. Files stored in a Cloud Storage bucket. Indexing Advanced website indexing crawls and parses content from specified URLs. Files are parsed and chunked according to configured options. Updates Content is re-indexed based on crawling schedules. Can be synchronized manually or on a schedule from the Cloud Storage bucket.

For more information, see the Introduction to Vertex AI Search.

Step-by-step guide Website dataDocuments

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Create Data Store page.

    Go to Create Data Store

  2. In the Website Content box, click Select.

  3. Select the Advanced website indexing checkbox to turn it on.
  4. In the Specify URL patterns to index section, add URLs for Sites to include. You can also optionally add URLs for Sites to exclude.
  5. Click Continue.
  6. On the Configure your data store pane, do the following:
    1. Select a Location of your data store.
    2. Enter a Your data store name. The ID is automatically generated. You will use this ID later.
    3. Click Create.

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Create Data Store page.

    Go to Create Data Store

  2. In the Cloud Storage box, click Select.

  3. In the Import data from Cloud Storage pane, select Unstructured documents (PDF, HTML, TXT and more).
  4. Select a Synchronization frequency.
  5. Select a folder or file to import from your Cloud Storage bucket.
  6. Click Continue.
  7. On the Configure your data store pane, do the following:
    1. Select a Location of your data store.
    2. Enter a Your data store name. The ID is automatically generated.
    3. To select parsing and chunking options, expand the Document Processing Options section. For more information, see Parse documents.
    4. Click Create.

docs.title: Generate grounded responses
docs.text:
After creating your data store, you can use it to ground model responses. You can ground a model with up to 10 data stores.

First, you need your data store ID. If you don't know it, follow these steps:

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Data stores page.

    Go to the Data stores page

  2. Click the name of your data store.

  3. On the Data page for your data store, copy the data store ID.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

ConsolePythonREST

To ground your model using Vertex AI Studio in the Google Cloud console, follow these steps:

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI Studio Freeform page.

    Go to Freeform

  2. Click the Grounding: your data toggle to turn on grounding.

  3. Click Customize.

    1. Select Vertex AI Search as your source.

    2. Enter the path to your data store using the following format, replacing PROJECT_ID and DATA_STORE_ID:

      projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/global/collections/default_collection/dataStores/DATA_STORE_ID

  4. Click Save.

  5. Enter your prompt in the text box and click Submit.

Your prompt responses are now grounded to your Vertex AI Search data store.

Before trying this sample, follow the Python setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Python API reference documentation.

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

from google import genai
from google.genai.types import (
    GenerateContentConfig,
    HttpOptions,
    Retrieval,
    Tool,
    VertexAISearch,
)

client = genai.Client(http_options=HttpOptions(api_version="v1"))

# Load Data Store ID from Vertex AI Search
# datastore = "projects/111111111111/locations/global/collections/default_collection/dataStores/data-store-id"

response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.0-flash-001",
    contents="How do I make an appointment to renew my driver's license?",
    config=GenerateContentConfig(
        tools=[
            # Use Vertex AI Search Tool
            Tool(
                retrieval=Retrieval(
                    vertex_ai_search=VertexAISearch(
                        datastore=datastore,
                    )
                )
            )
        ],
    ),
)

print(response.text)
# Example response:
# 'The process for making an appointment to renew your driver's license varies depending on your location. To provide you with the most accurate instructions...'

To test a text prompt by using the Vertex AI API, send a POST request to the publisher model endpoint.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • LOCATION: The region to process the request.
  • PROJECT_ID: Your project ID.
  • MODEL_ID: The model ID of the multimodal model.
  • TEXT: The text instructions to include in the prompt.
  • DATA_STORE_ID: The ID of your data store.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:generateContent

Request JSON body:

{
  "contents": [{
    "role": "user",
    "parts": [{
      "text": "TEXT"

  }],

    "retrieval": {

    }

  "model": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID"
}

To send your request, expand one of these options:

curl (Linux, macOS, or Cloud Shell)

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \  
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \

docs.title: Understand your response
docs.text:
If your model prompt successfully grounds to your Vertex AI Search data source, the API response includes grounding metadata that identifies the parts of the response derived from your data. There are several reasons this metadata might not be provided, such as low source relevance or incomplete information.

The following is a breakdown of the output data in the response:

  • role: Indicates the sender of the grounded answer. Because the response always contains grounded text, the role is always model.
  • text: The grounded answer generated by the LLM.
  • groundingMetadata: Information about the grounding source, which contains the following elements:
    • groundingChunks: A list of results from your data store that support the answer.
    • groundingSupports: Information about a specific claim within the answer that can be used to show citations:
      • segment: The part of the model's answer that is substantiated by a grounding chunk.
      • groundingChunkIndices: The index of the grounding chunks in the groundingChunks list that corresponds to this claim.
      • confidenceScores: A number from 0 to 1 that indicates how grounded the claim is in the provided set of grounding chunks. Not available for Gemini 2.5 and later.

A sample JSON response looks like this:

{
  "candidates": [
    {
      "content": {
        "role": "model",
        "parts": [
          {
            "text": "You can make an appointment on the website https://dmv.gov/"
          }
        ]
      },
      "finishReason": "STOP",
      "safetyRatings": [
        "..."
      ],
      "groundingMetadata": {
        "retrievalQueries": [
          "How to make appointment to renew driving license?"
        ],
        "groundingChunks": [
          {
            "retrievedContext": {
              "uri": "https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AXiHM.....QTN92V5ePQ==",
              "title": "dmv"
            }
          }
        ],
        "groundingSupport": [
          {
            "segment": {
              "startIndex": 25,
              "endIndex": 147
            },
            "segment_text": "ipsum lorem ...",
            "supportChunkIndices": [1, 2],
            "confidenceScore": [0.9541752, 0.97726375]
          },
          {
            "segment": {
              "startIndex": 294,
              "endIndex": 439
            },
            "segment_text": "ipsum lorem ...",
            "supportChunkIndices": [1],
            "confidenceScore": [0.9541752, 0.9325467]
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  ],
  "usageMetadata": {
    "..."
  }
}

docs.title: Grounding with your search API
docs.text:
You can connect Gemini to your external data sources by grounding with your search API. This lets you use any search service as a grounding source for Gemini, which helps to ensure that responses are based on the latest and most relevant information from your systems. This is particularly useful for enterprise-specific data that isn't publicly available.

This page explains how to configure and use grounding using any search API with Gemini.

docs.title: How grounding with your search API works
docs.text:
When you ground with your search API, Gemini can query an external API endpoint that you provide. This allows Gemini to use your custom search functionality as a tool to enhance its responses. It enables more dynamic and context-aware interactions, as the model can seek out information from your specified data sources when needed.

During a generation request, Gemini makes a call to the external API endpoint with a search query. Your API then returns relevant data snippets. Gemini uses these snippets as a source of truth to generate a more accurate and grounded response.

You can combine grounding using your search API with other grounding sources like Google Search. A generation request supports up to 10 grounding sources and multi-tool queries where Gemini can take advantage of different information sources to generate the best possible answer.

docs.title: Choose your setup path
docs.text:
Before you begin, decide whether you will use an existing, compatible API endpoint or set up a new one.

Option Description Pros Cons Use an existing API endpoint Connect Gemini to an existing search API that already meets the required schema and authentication specifications. - Fastest setup if your API is already compatible.- Leverages existing infrastructure without modification. - Requires your current API to strictly match the required request/response format.- May require backend changes if not compatible. Set up a new API endpoint Create a new, secure API endpoint using Google Cloud services like Cloud Functions and API Gateway to act as a wrapper for your search system. - Flexible: Adapt any backend search system to meet Gemini's requirements.- Secure: Uses API Gateway for robust authentication and management. - More setup steps: Requires creating and deploying new Google Cloud resources.- Involves managing additional infrastructure.

docs.title: Supported models
docs.text:
The following models support grounding with your API:

  • Vertex AI Model Optimizer
  • Gemini 2.5 Pro
  • Gemini 2.5 Flash
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash

For more information, see Gemini models.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Grounding: The process of connecting a model to external data sources to ensure its responses are based on specific, verifiable information.
  • Cloud Functions: A serverless compute service that lets you run code in response to events without managing servers.
  • API Gateway: A managed service that lets you create, secure, and monitor APIs for your backend services.
  • API key: A simple encrypted string that identifies an application or project without a principal, used for authenticating API requests.
  • Retrieval tool: A specific tool configuration in the Gemini API that enables the model to call an external system, like a search API, to fetch information.
Prerequisites
  1. Ensure that the Vertex AI API is enabled in your Google Cloud project.
  2. If you plan to follow the detailed setup guide for creating a new search API endpoint, make sure you have the Google Cloud CLI installed and initialized.
Use an existing API endpointSet up a new API endpoint

If you already have an API endpoint that meets the schema and authentication requirements, you can directly configure it in your Gemini API calls.

If you don't have an existing API endpoint that meets the requirements, this section guides you through setting one up using Cloud Functions and API Gateway.

The following diagram shows the workflow for setting up a new search API endpoint.

flowchart TD
    A[Step 1: Create the Cloud Function] --> B[Step 2: Secure the function with API Gateway]
    B --> C[Step 3: Create and restrict an API key]

click A "#step-1-create-the-cloud-function"
click B "#step-2-secure-the-function-with-api-gateway"
click C "#step-3-create-and-restrict-an-api-key"

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Step 1: Create the Cloud Function

A Cloud Function can act as an intermediary that receives queries from Gemini, issues appropriate queries to your existing search infrastructure (such as a database, internal search engine, or vector search), and then formats the results in the schema Gemini understands.

For more information, see the Cloud Functions documentation.

Example Cloud Function setup (Python)

This example uses a hardcoded product list for demonstration. You'll need to replace the data retrieval logic with calls to your actual search system.

main.pyrequirements.txt 
import functions_framework
import json
from flask import jsonify

@functions_framework.http
def custom_search_wrapper_minimal(request):
    """
    HTTP Cloud Function to provide a minimal, fixed response for Gemini grounding.
    """
    if request.method != 'POST':
        return 'Only POST requests are accepted', 405

    request_json = request.get_json(silent=True)

    if not request_json or 'query' not in request_json:
        return jsonify({"error": "Invalid request. JSON body with 'query' field is required."}), 400

    user_query = request_json['query']
    print(f"Received query: '{user_query}'. Responding with fixed data.")

    # --- FIXED RESPONSE ---
    # This is a hardcoded response. In a real scenario, you would
    # use the 'user_query' to fetch relevant data.
    fixed_results = [
        {
            "snippet": "This is a fixed snippet from your custom Search API. The original query was: " + user_query,
            "uri": "https://example.com/docs/fixed-test-data"
        },
        {
            "snippet": "Another piece of fixed information to demonstrate the list format.",
            "uri": "https://example.com/another-fixed-source"
        }
    ]
    # --- END OF FIXED RESPONSE ---

    return jsonify(fixed_results)

functions-framework>=3.0.0
Flask>=2.0.0

Deployment

Navigate to the directory containing main.py and requirements.txt and run the following command. * Replace YOUR_REGION with your chosen Google Cloud region, such as us-central1. * --allow-unauthenticated is specified because API Gateway handles authentication.

gcloud functions deploy custom_search_wrapper \
  --runtime python311 \
  --trigger-http \
  --entry-point custom_search_wrapper \
  --region YOUR_REGION \
  --allow-unauthenticated \
  --gen2
Important: The trigger URL after deployment has a format of https://....run.app. Use this format for the API Gateway configuration in the next step.

Step 2: Secure the function with API Gateway

API Gateway provides a secure, managed entry point to your Cloud Function and lets you enforce API key authentication.

For more information, see the API Gateway documentation.

1. Create an OpenAPI specification (openapi-spec.yaml)

This file defines how API Gateway exposes your Cloud Function. It specifies that the gateway expects a POST request to the /v0/search path and requires an API key sent as a query parameter named key.

Important: Replace YOUR_CLOUD_FUNCTION_TRIGGER_URL with the trigger URL that you noted when deploying your Cloud Function.

swagger: '2.0'
info:
  title: Custom Search API for Gemini Grounding
  description: Wraps an internal search function, secured by API Key for Gemini.
  version: 1.0.0
schemes:
  - https
produces:
  - application/json
consumes:
  - application/json
paths:
  /v0/search: # TODO: This will be part of API endpoint URL change if necessary
    post:
      summary: Custom search endpoint for Gemini
      operationId: customSearchForGemini # TODO: Change if needed
      x-google-backend:
        address: YOUR_CLOUD_FUNCTION_TRIGGER_URL # TODO: Replace with your Cloud Function trigger URL
      parameters:
        - name: body
          in: body
          required: true
          schema:
            type: object
            properties:
              query:
                type: string
      security:
        - api_key_query: []
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Search results
          schema:
            type: array
            items:
              type: object
              properties:
                snippet:
                  type: string
                uri:
                  type: string
        '400':
          description: Invalid request
        '401':
          description: Unauthorized (Missing or invalid API key)
        '500':
          description: Internal server error
securityDefinitions:
  api_key_query:
    type: apiKey
    name: key # Gemini will send its API key using this query parameter name
    in: query

2. Deploy API Gateway

After you replace the following variables, execute the gcloud CLI commands: * YOUR_PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID. * YOUR_REGION: The Google Cloud region that you used for your Cloud Function, such as us-central1.

# 1. Create an API
gcloud api-gateway apis create custom-search-gemini-api --project=YOUR_PROJECT_ID

# 2. Create an API Config from your OpenAPI spec
gcloud api-gateway api-configs create v1 \
  --api=custom-search-gemini-api \
  --openapi-spec=openapi-spec.yaml \
  --project=YOUR_PROJECT_ID \
  --display-name="Version 1"

# 3. Create a Gateway
gcloud api-gateway gateways create custom-search-gateway \
  --api=custom-search-gemini-api \
  --api-config=v1 \
  --location=YOUR_REGION \
  --project=YOUR_PROJECT_ID
After deployment, the hostname (gateway URL) has the following format: https://custom-search-gateway-UNIQUE_ID.nw.gateway.dev. You can use this hostname to construct the full endpoint URL for Gemini, for example: https://custom-search-gateway-UNIQUE_ID.nw.gateway.dev/v0/search.

Step 3: Create and restrict an API key

You must create an API key that Gemini uses to access your API Gateway endpoint. For more information, see Manage API keys.

To create and restrict an API key, do the following:

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the APIs & Services > Credentials page. Go to Credentials
  2. Click Create credentials and select API key.
  3. Copy the generated API key and store it in a secure location. This key is used by Gemini.
  4. Click Edit API key to configure its restrictions.
  5. Under API restrictions, do the following:
    • Select the Restrict key option.
    • In the dropdown menu, select your API. It might be named after your API's title, such as Custom Search API for Gemini Grounding.
    • Click OK.
  6. Click Save.

Your API Gateway endpoint is now secured. When you use the API Gateway endpoint, you must pass the API key as a query parameter. For example: https://custom-search-gateway-UNIQUE_ID.nw.gateway.dev/v0/search?key=YOUR_GENERATED_API_KEY.

docs.title: Search API requirements
docs.text:
To use your existing search infrastructure with Gemini, your API endpoint must meet the following requirements.

API schema

  • HTTP method: POST
  • Request Body (from Gemini to your API): 
    {
  "query": "the user's search query string"
}
  • Response body (from your API to Gemini): A JSON array of objects. Each object represents a search result and must contain snippet and uri fields. 
    [
  {
    "snippet": "A text snippet containing the answer or relevant information.",
    "uri": "A URI/URL linking to the source of the information, or a relevant identifier."
  },
  {
    "snippet": "Another piece of information.",
    "uri": "https://example.com/another-source"
  }
]
    If no results are found, your API endpoint should return an empty array [].

Authentication

Grounding with your search API supports the use of an API key to secure your endpoint. Gemini sends this API key as a query parameter named key.

docs.title: Configure the externalApi tool
docs.text:
When making a request to the Gemini API, include the tools parameter with a retrieval tool configured for the externalApi. Key fields include the following:

  • api_spec:"SIMPLE_SEARCH": This tells Gemini to use the predefined input and output schema.
  • endpoint: The full URL to your API Gateway endpoint, such as https://YOUR_GATEWAY_HOSTNAME/v0/search.
  • apiAuth.apiKeyConfig.apiKeyString: The API key that Gemini uses to authenticate with your API. Gemini appends this key as ?key=<YOUR_API_KEY> to the endpoint URL.

docs.title: Example request
docs.text:
Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • LOCATION: The region to process the request, such as us-central1.
  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • MODEL_ID: The model ID of a compatible Gemini model, such as gemini-2.0-flash-001.
  • USER_PROMPT: The text instructions to include in the prompt.
  • EXTERNAL_API_ENDPOINT: The full URL to your secured API Gateway endpoint that Gemini calls, such as https://YOUR_GATEWAY_HOSTNAME/v0/search. This endpoint must adhere to the specified API schema.
  • EXTERNAL_API_KEY: The API key you generated and configured for your API Gateway. Gemini uses this key to authenticate with your endpoint.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:generateContent

Request JSON body:

  {
  "contents": [{
      "role": "user",
      "parts": [{
          "text": "USER_PROMPT"
      }]
  }],
  "tools": [{
      "retrieval": {
        "externalApi": {
          "api_spec": "SIMPLE_SEARCH",
          "endpoint": "EXTERNAL_API_ENDPOINT",
          "apiAuth": {
            "apiKeyConfig": {
              "apiKeyString": "EXTERNAL_API_KEY"
            }
          }
        }
      }
  }]
}

docs.title: Considerations for your search API
docs.text:
Review the following considerations to help you choose your search API:

  • Snippet quality: The snippet text returned by your API is crucial. It should be concise yet informative enough for Gemini to use as a factual basis for its response.
  • Latency: Your search API should respond quickly. High latency in your API increases the overall response time from Gemini.
  • Error handling: Implement robust error handling in your Cloud Function or search API. If your API frequently errors or times out, it negatively impacts Gemini's ability to generate grounded responses.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text: • Grounding with Google Search.

docs.title: Grounding overview
docs.text:
In generative AI, grounding is the process of connecting a model's responses to verifiable sources of information. By providing a model with access to specific data sources, grounding tethers its output to that data, which reduces the chance of the model inventing content (a behavior known as hallucination). This is particularly important in situations where accuracy and reliability are critical.

For example, grounding can turn a potentially unverifiable statement into a fact-based response with a clear source:

  • Ungrounded response: "The new AI regulation bill was passed yesterday."
  • Grounded response: "According to the official legislative record, the new AI regulation bill was passed yesterday [source 1]."

Grounding provides the following benefits:

  • Reduces model hallucinations: Helps prevent the model from generating content that isn't factual or supported by the source data.
  • Anchors model responses: Ensures that model responses are directly tied to your specified data sources.
  • Enhances auditability: Provides citations and links back to the source documents, allowing users to verify the information.
Concepts
  • Grounding: The process of connecting a model's output to verifiable sources of information to ensure accuracy and reduce hallucinations.
  • Model Hallucination: An instance where a model generates content that is factually incorrect or not based on the provided source data.
  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): A technique that enhances model responses by first retrieving relevant information from an external knowledge base and then using that information to generate a more accurate and context-aware answer.

docs.title: Grounding options in Vertex AI
docs.text:
Vertex AI offers several methods to ground models, depending on your data source and use case. Use the following table to help you choose the best option for your needs.

Grounding Method Data Source Ideal Use Case Grounding with Google Search The public internet, indexed by Google Search. Answering questions about current events, general knowledge, or topics not contained in your private data. Grounding with Google Maps Google Maps data, including places, routes, and reviews. Building location-aware applications, providing directions, or answering geography-based queries. Your own data sources (RAG) Your private documents, website content, or databases. Answering questions based on internal knowledge bases, company policies, or proprietary product information. Grounding with Elasticsearch Data stored in your existing Elasticsearch indexes. Leveraging your existing Elasticsearch infrastructure to ground models without data migration. Web Grounding for Enterprise A curated web index of specified domains. Generating responses grounded in your public website content or other trusted web sources.

For language support, see Supported languages for prompts.

docs.title: Web Grounding for Enterprise
docs.text:
This page describes how to use the Web Grounding for Enterprise API to generate responses from Gemini models that are grounded on the web. This service is designed with compliance controls suitable for customers in highly-regulated industries, such as finance, healthcare, and the public sector.

Grounding helps to reduce model hallucinations by connecting model responses to verifiable information from a specific data source—in this case, a curated web index. When you ground a model, it can provide more accurate and trustworthy answers and include citations to the web pages it used to formulate its response.

docs.title: Choose a web grounding tool
docs.text:
Vertex AI offers two tools for grounding with web data. If you don't require the compliance controls offered by Web Grounding for Enterprise, use Grounding with Google Search, as it provides access to a broader web index.

The following table compares the two tools:

Feature Web Grounding for Enterprise Grounding with Google Search Primary Use Case Generating grounded responses with compliance controls for regulated industries. Generating grounded responses with access to the full Google Search index. Data Processing ML processing is restricted to the US or European Union multi-regions. Data is processed globally. Data Logging Customer data (prompts and responses) is not logged. Customer data might be logged based on service terms. Security Supports VPC Service Controls. Does not support VPC Service Controls. Data Persistence No customer data is persisted. CMEK and Access Transparency are not applicable. Data persistence policies apply.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Grounding: The process of connecting a large language model's responses to verifiable data sources to improve accuracy and reduce fabrications.
  • Web Grounding for Enterprise: A grounding service that uses a curated web index and includes compliance controls for regulated industries.
  • Gemini: A family of multimodal generative AI models developed by Google.
  • VPC Service Controls: A Google Cloud security feature that creates a service perimeter to protect against data exfiltration.

docs.title: Compliance and data handling
docs.text:
Web Grounding for Enterprise uses a dedicated web index to generate grounded responses and supports the following compliance features:

  • ML processing in the US or European Union multi-regions.
  • No logging of customer data.
  • VPC Service Controls.

Because no customer data is persisted, customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) and Access Transparency (AxT) are not applicable.

docs.title: How to use the Web Grounding for Enterprise API
docs.text:
This section demonstrates how to use the API to generate responses grounded with Web Grounding for Enterprise. The following workflow outlines the process.

flowchart TD
    A[Set up your environment] --> B[Construct the API request]
    B --> C[Receive the grounded response]

click A "#set-up-your-environment"
click B "#construct-the-api-request"
click C "#receive-the-grounded-response"

docs.title: Use the API
docs.text:
To generate grounded responses with Gemini, you must provide the enterpriseWebSearch tool in your API request. This signals to the model that it should use the Web Grounding for Enterprise service.

Python SDKREST Set up your environment and make an API call

1. Install the SDK

To get started, install the Python SDK for Google's Generative AI. 

pip install --upgrade google-genai

To learn more, see the SDK reference documentation.

2. Set environment variables

Set environment variables to configure the SDK to use your Vertex AI project. 

# Replace the `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` values
# with appropriate values for your project.
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global
export GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=True

3. Generate a grounded response

The following code snippet demonstrates how to send a request to the Gemini 2.0 Flash model and enable Web Grounding for Enterprise by adding the enterprise_web_search tool.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

from google import genai
from google.genai.types import (
    EnterpriseWebSearch,
    GenerateContentConfig,
    HttpOptions,
    Tool,
)

client = genai.Client(http_options=HttpOptions(api_version="v1"))

response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents="When is the next total solar eclipse in the United States?",
    config=GenerateContentConfig(
        tools=[
            # Use Enterprise Web Search Tool
            Tool(enterprise_web_search=EnterpriseWebSearch())
        ],
    ),
)

print(response.text)
# Example response:
# 'The next total solar eclipse in the United States will occur on ...'
Make an API call

To generate a grounded response using the REST API, send a POST request to the generateContent endpoint. In the request body, include your prompt and specify the enterpriseWebSearch tool.

Before running the command, replace the following variables:

  • PROJECT_NUMBER: Your Google Cloud project number.
  • LOCATION: The region for your request (e.g., us-central1).
  • TEXT: Your text prompt.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with the API request, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

curl -X POST \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -H "x-server-timeout: 60" \
    https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_NUMBER/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/gemini-2.0-flash:generateContent -d \
'{
  "contents": [{
    "role": "user",
    "parts": [{
      "text": "TEXT"
    }]
  }],
  "tools": [{
    "enterpriseWebSearch": {}
  }]
}'
