    B -- Image Generation --> C[Update model to `imagen-3.0-generate-001`];
    B -- Image Captioning / VQA --> D[Migrate to Gemini Pro Vision];
    B -- Image Editing --> E[Update to new Imagen 3 Editing APIs];
    B -- Personalization --> F[Migrate to Subject Customization];
    C --> G[Test your application];
    D --> G;
    E --> G;
    F --> G;

    click A "#migration-paths-by-feature"
    click B "#migration-paths-by-feature"
    click C "#detailed-migration-instructions"
    click D "#detailed-migration-instructions"
    click E "#detailed-migration-instructions"
    click F "#detailed-migration-instructions"
    click G "#detailed-migration-instructions"

docs.title: Migration paths by feature
docs.text:
To migrate to Imagen 3, first identify which feature your application uses. The following table summarizes the recommended migration path for each feature.

Current Feature / Model Recommended Migration Path Required Changes Image Generation (imagegeneration@002, @005, @006) Imagen 3 (imagen-3.0-generate-001) Model name update. Prompts might require minor tuning. Image Captioning & VQA Gemini Pro Vision Migrate to the Gemini API for improved capabilities. Image Editing (Inpainting, Outpainting, Product Editing) Imagen 3 Editing features API and parameter changes are required. Personalization (Avatar Stylization) Imagen 3 Subject Customization Migrate to the new Subject Customization workflow.

docs.title: Detailed migration instructions
docs.text:
After identifying your migration path in the table above, use the following tabs for detailed instructions and links to relevant documentation.

Image GenerationImage Captioning and VQAImage EditingPersonalization

For standard image generation, migrating primarily involves updating the model name in your code or API calls from an older version (e.g., imagegeneration@006) to the latest Imagen 3 model.

While most prompts work well with Imagen 3, some might require minor adjustments to achieve optimal results due to the model's improved understanding of natural language. We recommend testing your existing prompts with the new model.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

If you use Imagen's Image Captioning or Visual Question Answering (VQA) features, migrate your application to Gemini Pro Vision. Gemini offers more advanced capabilities for analyzing, understanding, and describing images.

For more information, see Image understanding with Gemini.

Migrating image editing workloads for inpainting, outpainting, and product editing requires API changes. The workflows and parameters for these features have been updated in Imagen 3.

For detailed instructions, see the following guides:

  • Inpainting: Edit images by inserting content with a mask
  • Outpainting: Edit images by outpainting
  • Product image editing: Edit product images

If you use Imagen 2 Personalization for features like avatar stylization, you should migrate to Imagen 3 Subject Customization. This new feature provides improved capabilities for generating consistent subjects.

For more information, see the Subject customization overview.

For more information, see the following pricing pages:

  • Gemini Models Pricing

docs.title: Omit content using a negative prompt
docs.text:
Caution:

Starting on June 24, 2025, Imagen versions 1 and 2 are deprecated. Imagen models imagegeneration@002, imagegeneration@005, and imagegeneration@006 will be removed on September 24, 2025. For more information about migrating to Imagen 3, see Migrate to Imagen 3.

Try Imagen in a Colab

This page describes how to omit content from images generated by Imagen on Vertex AI.

A negative prompt is a description of what you want to omit in generated images. For example, to generate an image of a cityscape at night without any people, you could use the prompt "a rainy city street at night" with a negative prompt of "people". Using a negative prompt helps the model better understand what to exclude.

The following examples show how a negative prompt affects the generated image.

Text prompt only

  • Text prompt: "a pizza"
Images generated with only a text prompt.

Text prompt and negative prompt

  • Text prompt: "a pizza"
  • Negative prompt: "pepperoni"
Images generated with a negative prompt to exclude pepperoni.

The following models support negative prompts:

  • imagen-3.0-capability-001
  • imagen-3.0-fast-generate-001
  • imagen-3.0-generate-001

Important:

Negative prompts are a legacy feature and are not included with Imagen models starting with imagen-3.0-generate-002 and newer.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Negative Prompt: A parameter used to specify elements you want to exclude from a generated image.
  • Imagen: A family of text-to-image diffusion models developed by Google for generating photorealistic images from natural language prompts.

docs.title: Use a negative prompt
docs.text:
You can add a negative prompt using the Google Cloud console or the REST API.

ConsoleREST

The following workflow shows how to use a negative prompt in the Media Studio.

flowchart TD
    A[Go to Media Studio] --> B[Select Imagen]
    B --> C[Configure settings and add negative prompt]
    C --> D[Enter text prompt]
    D --> E[Generate image]

    click A "#go-to-media-studio"
    click B "#select-imagen"
    click C "#configure-settings-and-add-negative-prompt"
    click D "#enter-text-prompt"
    click E "#generate-image"
Use the Google Cloud console

1. Go to Media Studio

In the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI > Media Studio page.

Go to Media Studio

2. Select Imagen

Click Imagen. The Imagen Media Studio image generation page is displayed.

3. Configure settings and add negative prompt

In the Settings panel, adjust the following options:

  • Model: Choose a model from the available options. For more information, see Imagen models.
  • Number of results: Adjust the slider or enter a value between 1 and 4.
  • Negative prompt: In the Negative prompt box, enter a prompt that describes what you don't want generated in the image.

4. Enter text prompt

In the Write your prompt box, enter your text prompt that describes the images to generate. For example, small boat on water in the morning watercolor illustration.

For more information about writing effective prompts, see Prompt and image attribute guide.

5. Generate image

Click send Generate.

To omit content from generated images using the REST API, include the negativePrompt field in the parameters object of your JSON request body.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • LOCATION: Your project's region. For example, us-central1, europe-west2, or asia-northeast3. For a list of available regions, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.
  • MODEL_VERSION: The Imagen model version to use. For more information, see Imagen models.
  • TEXT_PROMPT: The text prompt that guides what images the model generates.
  • NEGATIVE_PROMPT: A negative prompt to help generate the images. For example: "animals", "blurry", "text", or "cropped".
  • IMAGE_COUNT: The number of generated images. Accepted integer values: 1-8 (imagegeneration@002), 1-4 (all other model versions). Default value: 4.

docs.title: HTTP method and URL
docs.text: POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_VERSION:predict

docs.title: Request body
docs.text:
{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "TEXT_PROMPT"
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "negativePrompt": "NEGATIVE_PROMPT",
    "sampleCount": IMAGE_COUNT
  }
}
View all optional parameters

This list shows common optional parameters and isn't meant to be exhaustive. For more information, see the Imagen API reference.

  • addWatermark: (boolean) Optional. Enables a SynthID watermark for generated images. Default: true. You must set this to false to use the seed field.
  • aspectRatio: (string) Optional. Controls the aspect ratio. Supported values: "1:1" (default), "3:4", "4:3", "16:9", "9:16".
  • enhancePrompt: (boolean) Optional. Uses an LLM-based prompt rewriting feature for higher quality images. Default: true.
  • includeRaiReason: (boolean) Optional. Enables the Responsible AI filtered reason code in responses. Default: true.
  • includeSafetyAttributes: (boolean) Optional. Enables rounded Responsible AI scores for a list of safety attributes. Default: false.
  • outputOptions.mimeType: (string) Optional. The MIME type of the image. Supported values include image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, etc.
  • outputOptions.compressionQuality: (integer) Optional. For JPEG output only. Image quality from 0 to 100. Default: 75.
  • personGeneration: (string) Optional. Controls the type of people or face generation. Values: "allow_adult" (default), "dont_allow".
  • safetySetting: (string) Optional. Controls safety filter thresholds. Values: "block_low_and_above", "block_medium_and_above" (default), "block_only_high".
  • seed: (integer) Optional. A non-negative integer to make output images deterministic. Requires "addWatermark": false.
  • storageUri: (string) Optional. A Cloud Storage bucket to store output images (e.g., gs://image-bucket/output/). If not provided, images are returned as base64-encoded bytes.

docs.title: Send the request
docs.text:
Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

To send your request, choose one of these options:

curlPowerShell

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d @request.json \
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_VERSION:predict"

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method POST `
    -Headers $headers `
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `
    -InFile request.json `
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_VERSION:predict" | Select-Object -Expand Content

docs.title: Sample response
docs.text:
The following sample response is for a request with "sampleCount": 2. The response returns two prediction objects, with the generated image bytes base64-encoded.

{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES",
      "mimeType": "image/png"
    },
    {
      "mimeType": "image/png",
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES"
    }
  ]
}

If you use a model that supports prompt enhancement, the response includes an additional prompt field with the enhanced prompt used for generation:

{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "mimeType": "MIME_TYPE",
      "prompt": "ENHANCED_PROMPT_1",
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES_1"
    },
    {
      "mimeType": "MIME_TYPE",
      "prompt": "ENHANCED_PROMPT_2",
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES_2"
    }
  ]
}

Feature Vertex AI SDK for Python REST API Primary Use Case Best for integrating image generation into Python applications and interactive environments like Jupyter notebooks. Best for use with other languages or for direct interaction from the command line or web clients. Ease of Use Higher-level abstraction, simpler to use for common tasks. Requires manual construction of JSON requests and handling of HTTP responses.

PythonREST

docs.title: Replace the background of an image
docs.text:
This page describes how to replace the background of an image using Imagen on Vertex AI. You can either use automatic object segmentation to preserve the main subject while modifying the background or provide your own mask for more precise control over the edited area.

View Imagen for Editing and Customization model card

docs.title: Product image editing example
docs.text:
To see an example of Imagen 3 editing capabilities, you can run the "Imagen 3 Image Editing" Jupyter notebook in one of the following environments:

Open in Colab Open in Colab Enterprise Open in Vertex AI Workbench View on GitHub

docs.title: Choose an editing method
docs.text:
Before you start, decide whether you want Imagen to automatically detect the background or if you want to provide a specific mask to define the editing area.

Feature Automatic Background Detection User-Provided Mask Definition The model automatically identifies and segments the primary subject from the background, creating a mask for editing. You supply a black-and-white mask image where white areas are editable and black areas are preserved. Pros - Fast and easy to use.- No need to create a mask manually. - Provides precise control over the edited area.- Ideal for complex images or specific editing needs. Cons - The automatically generated mask might not be perfect for all images. - Requires you to create or supply a separate mask image. Best for Quickly replacing backgrounds in product photos or images with a clear foreground subject. Detailed editing tasks where accuracy is critical, such as preserving intricate details or editing specific, non-background regions.

The following workflow outlines the general steps to replace an image background.

flowchart TD
    A[Set up your environment] --> B{Choose editing method};
    B -- Automatic Detection --> C[Edit with an automatically detected background mask];
    B -- Manual Mask --> D[Edit with a user-defined mask];
    C --> E[Generate edited image];
    D --> E;

    click A "#before-you-begin"
    click B "#choose-an-editing-method"
    click C "#edit-with-an-automatically-detected-background-mask"
    click D "#edit-with-a-user-defined-mask"
Before you begin

Concepts
  • Mask: A black-and-white image used in image editing to define which areas of a source image should be modified (typically white) and which should be protected from changes (typically black).
  • Object Segmentation: The process of partitioning a digital image into multiple segments (sets of pixels) to simplify or change the representation of an image into something that is more meaningful and easier to analyze.
  • Prompt: A short text description that you provide to a generative model to guide the image generation process.
  • Vertex AI SDK: A set of Python libraries that simplify the process of interacting with the Vertex AI API for training and deploying machine learning models.
  • REST API: A way for different software applications to communicate with each other over the internet using standard HTTP requests.

  1. Set up your project

docs.title: Edit with an automatically detected background mask
docs.text:
Imagen can automatically detect the background of an image, which is useful for modifying a product image's background while preserving the product's appearance. This feature uses technology from Google Product Studio (GPS).

Image generated with the prompt: on a table in a boutique store. Original image source: Irene Kredenets on Unsplash.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Imagen 3Imagen 2

Use the following samples to send a product image editing request using the Imagen 3 model.

ConsoleGen AI SDK for PythonREST

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI > Media Studio page.

    Go to Media Studio

  2. Click Upload. In the displayed file dialog, select a file to upload.

  3. Click Inpaint.
  4. In the Parameters panel, click Product Background.
  5. In the editing toolbar, click background_replaceExtract.
  6. Select one of the mask extraction options:
    • Background elements: detects the background elements and creates a mask around them.
    • wallpaperForeground elements: detects the foreground objects and creates a mask around them.
    • background_replacePeople: detects people and creates a mask around them.
  7. Optional: In the Parameters side panel, adjust the following options:
    • Model: the Imagen model to use
    • Number of results: the number of result to generate
    • Negative prompt: items to avoid generating
  8. In the prompt field, enter a prompt to modify the image.
  9. Click sendGenerate.

Install

pip install --upgrade google-genai

To learn more, see the SDK reference documentation.

Set environment variables

# Replace the `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` values
# with appropriate values for your project.
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=us-central1
export GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=True

Run the code

from google import genai
from google.genai.types import RawReferenceImage, MaskReferenceImage, MaskReferenceConfig, EditImageConfig

client = genai.Client()

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below line
# output_file = "output-image.png"

raw_ref = RawReferenceImage(
    reference_image=Image.from_file(location='test_resources/suitcase.png'), reference_id=0)
mask_ref = MaskReferenceImage(
    reference_id=1,
    reference_image=None,
    config=MaskReferenceConfig(
        mask_mode="MASK_MODE_BACKGROUND",
    ),
)

image = client.models.edit_image(
    model="imagen-3.0-capability-001",
    prompt="A light blue suitcase in front of a window in an airport",
    reference_images=[raw_ref, mask_ref],
    config=EditImageConfig(
        edit_mode="EDIT_MODE_BGSWAP",
    ),
)

image.generated_images[0].image.save(output_file)

print(f"Created output image using {len(image.generated_images[0].image.image_bytes)} bytes")
# Example response:
# Created output image using 1234567 bytes

For more information, see the Edit images API reference.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • LOCATION: Your project's region. For example, us-central1, europe-west2, or asia-northeast3. For a list of available regions, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.
  • TEXT_PROMPT: The text prompt that guides what images the model generates.
  • referenceType: A ReferenceImage provides context for editing. A raw RGB image (REFERENCE_TYPE_RAW) is required. A mask reference image (REFERENCE_TYPE_MASK) is required for masked editing.
  • referenceId: The integer ID of the reference image.
  • B64_BASE_IMAGE: The base image to edit, as a base64-encoded string. Size limit: 10 MB.
  • maskImageConfig.maskMode: Use MASK_MODE_BACKGROUND to automatically mask the background.
  • MASK_DILATION: The percentage of image width to dilate the mask by (float). A value of 0.00 is recommended. Min: 0, max: 1. Default: 0.03.
  • EDIT_STEPS: The number of sampling steps (integer). For product image editing, start at 75.
  • EDIT_IMAGE_COUNT: The number of edited images to generate (integer). Accepted values: 1-4. Default: 4.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagen-3.0-capability-001:predict

Request JSON body:

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "TEXT_PROMPT",
      "referenceImages": [
        {
          "referenceType": "REFERENCE_TYPE_RAW",
          "referenceId": 1,
          "referenceImage": {
            "bytesBase64Encoded": "B64_BASE_IMAGE"
          }
        },
        {
          "referenceType": "REFERENCE_TYPE_MASK",
          "referenceId": 2,
          "maskImageConfig": {
            "maskMode": "MASK_MODE_BACKGROUND",
            "dilation": MASK_DILATION
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "editConfig": {
      "baseSteps": EDIT_STEPS
    },
    "editMode": "EDIT_MODE_BGSWAP",
    "sampleCount": EDIT_IMAGE_COUNT
  }
}

To send your request, choose one of these options:

curl

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \  
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \  
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \  
     -d @request.json \  
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagen-3.0-capability-001:predict"

PowerShell

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token  
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }  

Invoke-WebRequest `  
    -Method POST `  
    -Headers $headers `  
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `  
    -InFile request.json `  
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagen-3.0-capability-001:predict" | Select-Object -Expand Content

Caution

Starting on June 24, 2025, Imagen versions 1 and 2 are deprecated. Imagen models imagegeneration@002, imagegeneration@005, and imagegeneration@006 will be removed on September 24, 2025. For more information about migrating to Imagen 3, see Migrate to Imagen 3.

Use the following samples to send a product image editing request using an older Imagen model.

ConsoleVertex AI SDK for PythonREST

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI > Media Studio page.

    Go to Media Studio

  2. In the lower task panel, click editEdit image.

  3. Click Upload to select your locally stored product image to edit.
  4. In the Parameters panel, select check_boxEnable product style image editing.
  5. In the Prompt field, enter your prompt.
  6. Click Generate.

from vertexai.preview.vision_models import Image, ImageGenerationModel

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines

    base_image=base_img,
    prompt=prompt,
    edit_mode="product-image",

images[0].save(location=output_file, include_generation_parameters=False)

# Optional. View the edited image in a notebook.
# images[0].show()

  • LOCATION: Your project's region. For example, us-central1, europe-west2, or asia-northeast3. For a list of available regions, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.

Request JSON body:

    {
      "prompt": "TEXT_PROMPT",

          "bytesBase64Encoded": "B64_BASE_IMAGE"
      }
    }
  ],

    "editConfig": {
      "editMode": "product-image",

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
Because masks are sometimes incomplete, the model might try to complete the foreground object when small bits are missing at the boundary. As a rare side effect, when the foreground object is already complete, the model may create slight extensions.

A workaround is to segment the model output and then blend it. The following Python snippet demonstrates this workaround:

blended = Image.composite(out_images[0].resize(image_expanded.size), image_expanded, mask_expanded)

docs.title: Responsible AI and usage guidelines for Imagen
docs.text:
Imagen on Vertex AI brings Google's state-of-the-art generative AI capabilities to application developers. As an early-stage technology, Imagen on Vertex AI's evolving capabilities and uses create potential for misapplication, misuse, and unintended or unforeseen consequences. For example, Imagen on Vertex AI could generate output that you don't expect, such as images that are offensive, insensitive, or contextually incorrect.

Given these risks and complexities, Imagen on Vertex AI is designed with Google's AI Principles in mind. However, it is important for developers to understand and test their models to deploy them safely and responsibly. To aid developers, Imagen on Vertex AI has built-in safety filters to help customers block potentially harmful outputs within their use case. See the Safety filters and attributes section for more.

When Imagen on Vertex AI is integrated into a customer's unique use case and context, additional responsible AI considerations and model limitations may need to be considered. We encourage customers to use fairness, interpretability, privacy, and security recommended practices.

View Imagen for Generation model card View Imagen for Editing and Customization model card

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Responsible AI (RAI): A framework for developing, assessing, and deploying AI systems in a safe, ethical, and responsible manner.
  • Safety Filters: Automated mechanisms designed to detect and block potentially harmful content in both input prompts and generated outputs.
  • Safety Attributes: A set of categories (e.g., "Violence", "Sexual") used to score content for potential harm, which can be returned in the API response for user review.
  • Acceptable Use Policy (AUP): A set of rules that define prohibited uses of a service to prevent abuse and ensure legal and ethical compliance.

docs.title: Imagen usage guidelines
docs.text:
Read the following general product attributes and legal considerations before you use Imagen on Vertex AI.

  • Image and text filters and outputs: Images (generated or uploaded) through Imagen on Vertex AI are assessed against safety filters. Imagen aims to filter out content that violates our acceptable use policy (AUP) or additional Generative AI product restrictions. Our generative imagery models are intended to generate original content and not replicate existing content. We've designed our systems to limit the chances of this occurring, and we will continue to improve how these systems function. Like all cloud service providers, Google maintains an Acceptable Use Policy that prohibits customers from using our services in ways that infringe third-party IP rights.
  • Configurable safety filter thresholds: Google blocks model responses that exceed the designated confidence scores for certain safety attributes. To request the ability to modify a safety threshold, contact your Google Cloud account team.
  • Text addition supported on certain model versions: Imagen does not support adding text to images (uploaded or generated) using a text prompt when using the imagegeneration@004 or lower model versions.
  • Report suspected abuse: You can report suspected abuse of Imagen on Vertex AI or any generated output that contains inappropriate material or inaccurate information using the Report suspected abuse on Google Cloud form.
  • Trusted Tester Program opt-out: If you previously opted in to permit Google to use your data to improve pre-GA AI/ML services as part of the Trusted Tester Program terms, you can opt out using the Trusted Tester Program - Opt Out Request form.

docs.title: Safety filters and attributes
docs.text:
Text prompts provided as inputs and images (generated or uploaded) through Imagen on Vertex AI are assessed against a list of safety filters. These filters include harmful categories like violence, sexual, derogatory, and toxic. They aim to block content that violates our Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy or our AI Principles.

If the model responds with an error like "The prompt couldn't be submitted" or if fewer images are returned than requested, it indicates that the input or generated output triggered a safety filter.

It's important to understand the distinction between safety filters and safety attributes: * Safety filters are the internal mechanisms Google uses to block harmful content. You can adjust their sensitivity but cannot see the exact scores that trigger them. * Safety attributes are the safety scores returned to you when you set includeSafetyAttributes to true. These scores are for your information and do not represent all the filters Google applies. For example, we return a score for the "Health" category but do not filter content based on it.

You can choose how aggressively to filter sensitive content by adjusting the safetySetting parameter.

docs.title: Configure safety filters
docs.text:
You can use several parameters to control safety filtering in the image generation models. Some parameters affect the content produced, while others affect how filtering is reported to you.

The following table describes the optional parameters that affect content filtering. For more technical information, see the image generation model API reference.

Parameter Description safetySetting Sets how aggressively to filter for potentially sensitive output content. includeRaiReason Provides a reason code or message when generated images are filtered. personGeneration Allows you more control over the generation of people, faces, and children. disablePersonFace Deprecated. A choice to allow person and face generation or not. Use personGeneration instead. includeSafetyAttributes Returns detailed safety attribute scores for the input prompt, input image (for editing), and all generated images that are not filtered.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Understand filter responses
docs.text:
The API response varies depending on whether the input prompt or the generated output image was filtered.

Filtered Input ResponseFiltered Output with includeRaiReasonFiltered Output with includeSafetyAttributes

If your text prompt or input image is filtered, the API returns a 400 error. The response provides a message indicating that the input violates Google's Responsible AI practices.

{
  "error": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Image generation failed with the following error: The prompt could not be submitted. This prompt contains sensitive words that violate Google's Responsible AI practices. Try rephrasing the prompt. If you think this was an error, send feedback.",
    "status": "INVALID_ARGUMENT",
    "details": [
      {
        "@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.DebugInfo",
        "detail": "[ORIGINAL ERROR] generic::invalid_argument: Image generation failed with the following error: The prompt could not be submitted. This prompt contains sensitive words that violate Google's Responsible AI practices. Try rephrasing the prompt. If you think this was an error, send feedback. [google.rpc.error_details_ext] { message: \"Image generation failed with the following error: The prompt could not be submitted. This prompt contains sensitive words that violate Google\\'s Responsible AI practices. Try rephrasing the prompt. If you think this was an error, send feedback.\" }"
      }
    ]
  }
}

If you set includeRaiReason: true and some generated images are filtered, the predictions array will contain objects for the successful images and raiFilteredReason objects for the filtered ones. The reason may be a descriptive message or a numerical support code, depending on the model version.

Example Response (Descriptive Reason) 

{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "/9j/4AAQSkZJRgABA[...]bdsdgD2PLbZQfW96HEFE/9k=",
      "mimeType": "image/png"
    },
    {
      "raiFilteredReason": "Your current safety filter threshold filtered out 2 generated images. You will not be charged for blocked images. Try rephrasing the prompt. If you think this was an error, send feedback."
    }
  ],
  "deployedModelId": "MODEL_ID"
}

Example Response (Support Code) 

{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "/9j/4AAQSkZJRgABA[...]bdsdgD2PLbZQfW96HEFE/9k=",
      "mimeType": "image/png"
    },
    {
      "raiFilteredReason": "56562880"
    }
  ],
  "deployedModelId": "MODEL_ID"
}

If you set includeSafetyAttributes: true, the response includes safety scores for the input prompt and for each generated image that was not filtered. Filtered images are omitted and their safety attributes are not returned.

{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "/9j/4AAQSkZJRgABA[...]bdsdgD2PLbZQfW96HEFE/9k=",
      "mimeType": "image/png",
      "safetyAttributes": {
        "categories": [
          "Porn",
          "Violence"
        ],
        "scores": [
          0.1,
          0.2
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      "contentType": "Positive Prompt",
      "safetyAttributes": {
        "categories": [
          "Death, Harm & Tragedy",
          "Firearms & Weapons",
          "Hate",
          "Health",
          "Illicit Drugs",
          "Politics",
          "Porn",
          "Religion & Belief",
          "Toxic",
          "Violence",
          "Vulgarity",
          "War & Conflict"
        ],
        "scores": [
          0,
          0,
          0,
          0,
          0,
          0,
          0.2,
          0,
          0.1,
          0,
          0.1,
          0
        ]
      }
    }
  ],
  "deployedModelId": "MODEL_ID"
}

docs.title: Safety filter error codes
docs.text:
When content is filtered, the response may include a support code in the raiFilteredReason field. These codes map to specific harmful categories.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: The following limitations apply to different Imagen capabilities.

docs.title: Image generation and editing
docs.text:
• Bias amplification: Imagen can generate high-quality images, but the content relies on its training data, which can unintentionally include biases that may perpetuate stereotypes or discriminate against certain groups. Careful monitoring and evaluation are necessary to ensure outputs align with your use case.
  • Transparency and disclosure: It can be difficult for users to differentiate between AI-generated and non-AI-generated imagery. When using AI-generated images, clearly disclose that they were created by an AI system to ensure transparency. We apply metadata labeling to AI-generated images to help combat misinformation.
  • Insufficient context: Imagen may lack the contextual understanding required to generate images appropriate for all situations. Check that your generated images align with your chosen context, purpose, and intended audience.
  • Misrepresentation and authenticity: Editing images, especially of people, can result in misrepresentation or manipulation, potentially leading to deceptive content. It is important to use editing features responsibly, without compromising the authenticity of the images. We apply metadata labeling to AI-edited images to help combat misinformation.

docs.title: Visual captioning
docs.text:
• Accuracy and context sensitivity: Visual captioning may struggle with complex or ambiguous images. The generated descriptions may not always capture the complete context or nuance.
  • Ambiguity and subjective interpretations: Images can be open to multiple interpretations. The generated captions may not always align with human understanding or cultural backgrounds.
  • Accessibility considerations: While automated captions can support accessibility, they may not fully replace human-generated alt-text tailored to specific accessibility needs.

docs.title: Visual Question Answering (VQA)
docs.text: • Overconfidence and uncertainty: VQA models may provide answers with unwarranted confidence, even when the correct answer is ambiguous. It is essential to communicate the model's uncertainty rather than conveying a false sense of certainty.

docs.title: Recommended practices
docs.text:
To use this technology safely and responsibly, it is important to consider risks specific to your use case in addition to the built-in technical safeguards. The following workflow outlines our recommended practices.

flowchart TD
    A[Assess security risks] --> B[Mitigate safety risks]
    B --> C[Perform safety testing]
    C --> D[Solicit user feedback and monitor]

click A "#assess-security-risks"
click B "#mitigate-safety-risks"
click C "#perform-safety-testing"
click D "#solicit-user-feedback-and-monitor"
Recommended Practices

1. Assess your application's security risks. Consider how your application could be misused by bad actors. Generative AI introduces new risks, such as generating harmful content, misleading information, or infringing on intellectual property.

2. Consider adjustments to mitigate safety risks. In addition to Imagen's built-in safety filters, consider implementing other mitigations. This could include adding user input restrictions, filtering generated output on the client side, or requiring human review for sensitive workflows.

3. Perform safety testing appropriate to your use case. Test your application to ensure the safety controls are working as expected. Use techniques like red-teaming to probe for vulnerabilities and test the system's response to adversarial inputs.

4. Solicit user feedback and monitor content. Provide a mechanism for your users to report inappropriate content. Continuously monitor application outputs and user feedback to identify and address any emerging safety issues or model limitations.

Concepts

  • JSON (JavaScript Object Notation): A lightweight data-interchange format that is easy for humans to read and write and easy for machines to parse and generate.

docs.title: How to set the prompt language
docs.text:
You can specify the prompt language using the REST API. In Vertex AI Studio, the language is detected automatically.

Vertex AI StudioREST API

In Vertex AI Studio, Imagen automatically detects the language of your prompt from the supported languages. If your prompt is in an unsupported language, Imagen uses the text verbatim, which might result in unexpected output. There is no manual setting to specify the language in the UI.

Important: imagen-3.0-generate-002 doesn't support the text prompt language feature.

You can specify the prompt language by including the language parameter in your JSON request body.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • TEXT_PROMPT: The text prompt that guides what images the model generates.
  • PROMPT_LANGUAGE: The language code that corresponds to your text prompt language.

Supported languages

The following values are supported for the language parameter:

  • auto: Automatic detection (default). If a supported language is detected, the prompt is translated to English. Otherwise, the prompt is used verbatim.
  • en: English
  • es: Spanish
  • fr: French
  • de: German
  • hi: Hindi
  • ja: Japanese
  • ko: Korean
  • pt: Portuguese
  • zh or zh-CN: Chinese (simplified)
  • zh-TW: Chinese (traditional)

Request details

  • HTTP method and URL: 

    POST https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/imagegeneration@005:predict

  • Request JSON body: 

    {
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "सूर्यास्त के समय एक समुद्र तट। उड़ते पक्षी, हवा में लहराते नारियल के पेड़। लोग समुद्र तट पर सैर का आनंद ले रहे हैं।"
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "language": "hi"
  }
}

To send your request, choose one of the following options.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

cURLPowerShell

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

  1. Save the request body in a file named request.json.
  2. Execute the following command in your terminal: 
    curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d @request.json \
     "https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/imagegeneration@005:predict"

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

  1. Save the request body in a file named request.json.
  2. Execute the following command in PowerShell: 
    $cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method POST `
    -Headers $headers `
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `
    -InFile request.json `
    -Uri "https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/imagegeneration@005:predict" | Select-Object -Expand Content

Sample response

The following sample response returns two prediction objects, with the generated image bytes base64-encoded.

{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES",
      "mimeType": "image/png"
    },
    {
      "mimeType": "image/png",
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Style customization
docs.text:
Preview

This product or feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Google Cloud Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA products and features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

Deprecation Notice

Starting on June 24, 2025, Imagen versions 1 and 2 are deprecated. Imagen models imagegeneration@002, imagegeneration@005, and imagegeneration@006 will be removed on September 24, 2025. For more information about migrating to Imagen 3, see Migrate to Imagen 3.

Imagen 3 style customization helps you generate new images that adhere to the style of reference images you provide. By supplying one or more reference images along with a text prompt, you can guide the model to create new visuals that adopt the specified artistic style.

Note: For more information about imagen-3.0-capability-001 model requests, see the imagen-3.0-capability-001 model API reference.

docs.title: Use cases
docs.text:
Imagen 3 offers free-style prompting, which can give the impression that it can do more than it is trained to do. The following sections describe intended use cases for Imagen 3 style customization and provide non-exhaustive examples of unintended use cases.

We recommend using Imagen 3 for the intended use cases, as we've trained the model on those scenarios and expect good results. Conversely, while you can push the model to do things outside of the intended use cases, we don't expect good results.

docs.title: Intended use cases
docs.text:
The following are use cases intended for Imagen 3 style customization:

  • Generate an image from text input that follows the specific style provided by a reference image.
  • Alter a photo of a person.
  • Alter a photo of a person and preserve their facial expression.

docs.title: Examples of unintended use cases
docs.text:
The following is a non-exhaustive list of use cases that Imagen 3 isn't trained to do and for which it might produce poor results:

  • Generate an image from text and a reference image with the intent to control the composition of the generated image from the reference image.
  • Generate an image of a person from a reference image that has a person with a particular facial expression.
  • Place two people in a different scene, preserve their identities, and specify the style of the output image (such as an oil painting) using a reference image.
  • Stylize a photo of a pet and turn it into a drawing while preserving or specifying the composition of the image.
  • Place a product, such as a cookie or a couch, into different scenes with different product angles while following a specific image style (such as photorealistic with specific colors, lighting, or animation).

Concepts

RESTPython

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • LOCATION: Your project's region (for example, us-central1). For a list of available regions, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.
  • TEXT_PROMPT: The text prompt that guides what images the model generates. To use style customization, include the referenceId of the reference image(s) in the format [referenceId]. For example: Generate an image in glowing style [1] based on the following caption: A church in the mountain.

  • STYLE_DESCRIPTION: (Optional) A text description of the reference image you can then use in the prompt field.

from google import genai
from google.genai.types import EditImageConfig, Image, StyleReferenceConfig, StyleReferenceImage

client = genai.Client()

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below line

# Create a style reference image of a neon sign stored in Google Cloud Storage

    reference_id=1,
    reference_image=Image(gcs_uri="gs://cloud-samples-data/generative-ai/image/neon.png"),
    config=StyleReferenceConfig(style_description="neon sign"),

image = client.models.edit_image(
    model="imagen-3.0-capability-001",
    prompt="generate an image of a neon sign [1] with the words: have a great day",
    reference_images=[style_reference_image],
    config=EditImageConfig(
        edit_mode="EDIT_MODE_DEFAULT",
        number_of_images=1,
        seed=1,
        safety_filter_level="BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE",
        person_generation="ALLOW_ADULT",
        output_gcs_uri=output_gcs_uri,

)

# Example response:

print(image.generated_images[0].image.gcs_uri)

docs.title: Use cases
docs.text:
Imagen 3 Customization offers free-style prompting, which can give the impression that it can do more than it is trained to do. The following sections describe intended use cases for Imagen 3 Customization, and non-exhaustive examples of unintended use cases.

We recommend using Imagen 3 Customization for the intended use cases, as we've trained the model on those use cases and expect good results for them. Conversely, while you can push the model to do things outside of the intended use cases, we don't expect good results.

docs.title: Intended use cases
docs.text:
The following are use cases intended for Imagen 3 Customization subject customization:

  • Stylize a photo of a person, with the option to preserve their facial expressions.
  • Place a product, such as a couch or a cookie, into different scenes with different product angles (with low success).
  • Generate variations of a product that doesn't preserve exact details.

docs.title: Examples of unintended use cases
docs.text:
The following is a non-exhaustive list of use cases that Imagen 3 Customization isn't trained to do and produces poor results for:

  • Place two or more people in different scenes while preserving their identities.
  • Place two or more people in different scenes while preserving their identities and specifying the style of the output image using an example image as input for the style.
  • Stylize a photo of two or more people while preserving their identities.
  • Place a pet into different scenes while preserving its identity.
  • Stylize a photo of a pet and turn it into a drawing.
  • Stylize a photo of a pet and turn it into a drawing, while preserving or specifying the style of the image (such as watercolor).
  • Place a pet and a person into a different scene, preserving the identities of both.
  • Stylize a photo of a pet and one or more people and turn it into a drawing.
  • Place two products into different scenes with different product angles.
  • Place a product, such as a cookie or a couch, into different scenes with different product angles, and following a specific image style (such as photorealistic with specific colors, lighting styles, or animation).
  • Place a product into a different scene, while preserving the specific composition of the scene as specified by a control image.
  • Place two products into different scenes with different product angles, using a specific image as input (such as photorealistic with specific colors, lighting styles, or animation).
  • Place two products into different scenes, while preserving the specific composition of the scene as specified by a control image.

    When you use the Google Cloud console to access Google Cloud services and APIs, you don't need to set up authentication.

    To use the REST API samples on this page in a local development environment, you use the credentials you provide to the gcloud CLI.

    After installing the Google Cloud CLI, initialize it by running the following command:

    gcloud init

    If you're using an external identity provider (IdP), you must first sign in to the gcloud CLI with your federated identity.

    For more information, see Authenticate for using REST in the Google Cloud authentication documentation.

docs.title: Perform subject customization
docs.text:
This workflow guides you through the process of generating customized images with Imagen 3.

flowchart TD
    A[Set up your environment] --> B{Choose a subject type}
    B -- Person --> C[Perform person customization]
    B -- Product --> D[Perform product customization]

    click A "#before-you-begin"
    click C "#person-customization"
    click D "#product-customization"

To see an example of Imagen 3 Customization, run the "Imagen 3 Customized Images" Jupyter notebook in one of the following environments:

Open in Colab Open in Colab Enterprise Open in Vertex AI Workbench View on GitHub

You can provide reference images of subject types when you use Imagen 3 Customization. Specifically, few-shot prompting with Imagen 3 Customization supports the following subjects: product, person, and animal companion. The subject you choose affects how you form your generation request.

The prompt you use with Imagen 3 Customization might affect the quality of your generated images. The following sections describe recommended prompt templates and samples to send customization requests.

docs.title: Person customization
docs.text:
The following table describes prompt templates that we recommend as a starting point when writing person customization prompts:

Use case Reference images Prompt template Example Person image stylization with face mesh input Subject image (1)*Facemesh control image (1) Generate an image of SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION [1] with the facemesh from the control image [2]. ${PROMPT} Generate an image of the person [1] with the facemesh from the control image [2]. The person should be looking straight ahead with a neutral expression. The background should be a ... Person image stylization without face mesh input Subject image (1-4) Create an image about SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION [1] to match the description: a portrait of SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION [1] ${PROMPT} Create an image about a woman with short hair[1] to match the description: a portrait of a woman with short hair[1] in 3d-cartoon style with blurred background. A cute and lovely character, smile face, looking at the camera, pastel color tone, high quality, 4k, masterpiece, super details, skin texture, texture mapping, soft shadows, soft realistic lighting, vibrant colors Person image stylization without face mesh input Subject image (1-4) Create a STYLE_DESCRIPTION [2] image about SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION [1] to match the description: a portrait of SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION [1] STYLE_PROMPT Create a 3d-cartoon style [2] image about a woman with short hair [1] to match the description: a portrait of a woman with short hair [1] in 3d-cartoon style with blur background. A Cute and lovely character, smile face. see the camera, pastel color tone, high quality, 4k, masterpiece, super details, skin texture, texture mapping, Soft shadows, soft realistic lighting, vibrant colors Person image stylization with face mesh input Subject image (1-3)*Facemesh control image (1) Create an image about SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION [1] in the pose of the CONTROL_IMAGE [2] to match the description: a portrait of SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION [1] ${PROMPT} Create an image about a woman with short hair [1] in the pose of the control image [2] to match the description: a portrait of a woman with short hair [1] in 3d-cartoon style with blur background. A Cute and lovely character, smile face. See the camera, pastel color tone, high quality, 4k, masterpiece, super details, skin texture, texture mapping, Soft shadows, soft realistic lighting, vibrant colors Person image stylization with face mesh input Subject image (1-3)*Facemesh control image (1) Create a STYLE_DESCRIPTION [3] image about SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION [1] in the pose of the CONTROL_IMAGE [2] to match the description: a portrait of SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION [1] ${PROMPT} Create a 3d-cartoon style [3] image about a woman with short hair [1] in the pose of the control image [2] to match the description: a portrait of a woman with short hair [1] in 3d-cartoon style with blur background. A Cute and lovely character, smile face. See the camera, pastel color tone, high quality, 4k, masterpiece, super details, skin texture, texture mapping, Soft shadows, soft realistic lighting, vibrant colors

We recommend that the face in your reference image has the following properties:

  • Is centered and occupies at least half of the whole image
  • Is rotated in frontal view in all directions (roll, pitch, and yaw)
  • Isn't occluded by objects, such as sunglasses or masks

Use the following samples to send a customization request with person reference images used to guide image generation. You can send this type of request with or without a face mesh control image to further guide image generation.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

RESTPython

For more information about imagen-3.0-capability-001 model requests, see the imagen-3.0-capability-001 model API reference.

This sample shows you how to specify a face mesh control area to guide generation, but you can also omit the control reference object ("referenceType": "REFERENCE_TYPE_CONTROL") and Imagen will automatically detect a face mesh control area.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • LOCATION: Your project's region. For example, us-central1, europe-west2, or asia-northeast3. For a list of available regions, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.
  • TEXT_PROMPT: The text prompt guides what images the model generates. To use Imagen 3 Customization, include the referenceId of the reference image or images you provide in the format [referenceId]. For example:
    • The following text prompt is for a request that has two reference images with "referenceId": 1. Both images have an optional description of "subjectDescription": "man with short hair". Additionally, there is a control face mesh image specified with "referenceId": 2: Create an image about a man with short hair [1] in the pose of control image [2] to match the description: A pencil style sketch of a full-body portrait of a man with short hair [1] with hatch-cross drawing, hatch drawing of portrait with 6B and graphite pencils, white background, pencil drawing, high quality, pencil stroke, looking at camera, natural human eyes
  • "referenceId": The ID of the reference image, or the ID for a series of reference images that correspond to the same subject or style. In this example the two reference images are of the same person, so they share the same referenceId (1) and the control face mesh image has a distinct referenceId (2). The generated image will follow the face structure of the face mesh extracted from the reference image and will improve the face appearance following. Only one face mesh control is supported.
  • BASE64_REFERENCE_IMAGE: A reference image to guide image generation. The image must be specified as a base64-encoded byte string.

  • SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION: Optional. A text description of the reference image you can then use in the prompt field. For example:

    "prompt": "_a full-body portrait of a man with short hair [1] with hatch-cross drawing_",
[...],
"subjectDescription": "man with short hair"

  • IMAGE_COUNT: The number of generated images. Accepted integer values: 1-4. Default value: 4.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagen-3.0-capability-001:predict

Request JSON body:

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "TEXT_PROMPT",
      "referenceImages": [

        {
          "referenceType": "REFERENCE_TYPE_SUBJECT",
          "referenceId": 1,
          "referenceImage": {
            "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_REFERENCE_IMAGE"
          },
          "subjectImageConfig": {
            "subjectDescription": "SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION",
            "subjectType": "SUBJECT_TYPE_PERSON"
          }
        },
        {
          "referenceType": "REFERENCE_TYPE_SUBJECT",
          "referenceId": 1,
          "referenceImage": {
            "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_REFERENCE_IMAGE"
          },
          "subjectImageConfig": {
            "subjectDescription": "SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION",
            "subjectType": "SUBJECT_TYPE_PERSON"
          }
        },{
          "referenceType": "REFERENCE_TYPE_CONTROL",
          "referenceId": 2,
          "referenceImage": {
            "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_REFERENCE_IMAGE"
          },
          "controlImageConfig": {
            "controlType": "CONTROL_TYPE_FACE_MESH",
            "enableControlImageComputation": true
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "sampleCount": IMAGE_COUNT
  }
}

To send your request, choose one of these options:

curl

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login , or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI . You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d @request.json \
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagen-3.0-capability-001:predict"

PowerShell

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login . You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method POST `
    -Headers $headers `
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `
    -InFile request.json `
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagen-3.0-capability-001:predict" | Select-Object -Expand Content

The following sample response is for a request with "sampleCount": 2. The response returns two prediction objects, with the generated image bytes base64-encoded.

{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES",
      "mimeType": "image/png"
    },
    {
      "mimeType": "image/png",
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES"
    }
  ]
}

from google import genai
from google.genai.types import (
    ControlReferenceConfig,
    ControlReferenceImage,
    EditImageConfig,
    Image,
    SubjectReferenceConfig,
    SubjectReferenceImage
)

client = genai.Client()

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below line
# output_gcs_uri = "gs://your-bucket/your-prefix"

# Create subject and control reference images of a photograph stored in Google Cloud Storage
# using https://storage.googleapis.com/cloud-samples-data/generative-ai/image/person.png
subject_reference_image = SubjectReferenceImage(
    reference_id=1,
    reference_image=Image(gcs_uri="gs://cloud-samples-data/generative-ai/image/person.png"),
    config=SubjectReferenceConfig(
        subject_description="a headshot of a woman", subject_type="SUBJECT_TYPE_PERSON"
    ),
)
control_reference_image = ControlReferenceImage(
    reference_id=2,
    reference_image=Image(gcs_uri="gs://cloud-samples-data/generative-ai/image/person.png"),
    config=ControlReferenceConfig(control_type="CONTROL_TYPE_FACE_MESH"),
)

image = client.models.edit_image(
    model="imagen-3.0-capability-001",
    prompt="""
    a portrait of a woman[1] in the pose of the control image[2]in a watercolor style by a professional artist,
    light and low-contrast stokes, bright pastel colors, a warm atmosphere, clean background, grainy paper,
    bold visible brushstrokes, patchy details
    """,
    reference_images=[subject_reference_image, control_reference_image],
    config=EditImageConfig(
        edit_mode="EDIT_MODE_DEFAULT",
        number_of_images=1,
        seed=1,
        safety_filter_level="BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE",
        person_generation="ALLOW_ADULT",
        output_gcs_uri=output_gcs_uri,
    ),
)

# Example response:
# gs://your-bucket/your-prefix
print(image.generated_images[0].image.gcs_uri)

docs.text:
The following table describes prompt templates that we recommend as a starting point when writing product customization prompts:

The woman's hand is well-lit and the focus is sharp on the bottle, with a shallow depth of field blurring the background and emphasizing the product. The lighting is soft and diffused, creating a subtle glow around the bottle and hand. The overall composition is simple and elegant, highlighting the product's luxurious appeal. Use the following samples to send a customization request with product reference images used to guide image generation.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

ConsoleREST

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI > Media Studio page.

    Go to Media Studio

  2. In the Model section of the Parameters pane, select Imagen 3 if not already selected.

  3. Optional. Choose an Aspect ratio other than 1:1 (default).
  4. Optional. Change the Number of results.
  5. Optional. Provide a Negative prompt to guide the model on what to avoid generating.
  6. Optional. Change any Advanced options.
    1. In the Add reference pane, choose the Reference type: Subject - product.
    2. In the Reference images section, click Upload.
    3. Choose a locally-stored image and click Open.
    4. Optional. Provide a Description for the reference image.
    5. Click Done.
    6. Optional. To add more reference images, click Add an image and upload another image.
    7. After you add all your reference images, click Add reference.

    In the text prompt field (Write your prompt...), click Add reference.

    All the reference images you add in that pane have the same reference number. Use this reference number when you add the text prompt.

  8. In the text prompt field (Write your prompt...), add a text prompt that includes the reference number or numbers for the reference images. For example:

    1. bright white room, the product [1] on a glass table
    2. the animal [1] standing on a wide open field with a forest in the distance
    3. a black and white portrait of the person [1] on a city street in film noir style [2]

docs.title: Upscale a generated, edited, or existing image
docs.text: You can use the image upscaling feature of Imagen on Vertex AI to increase the resolution of an image by 2x or 4x without a significant loss in quality. This is useful for improving the detail of generated, edited, or existing images.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • REST API: A REST API (Representational State Transfer Application Programming Interface) is a way for different software applications to communicate with each other over the internet using standard HTTP methods.
  • base64 encoding: A method of converting binary data (like an image) into a text string, allowing it to be easily transmitted in text-based formats like JSON.
  • Cloud Storage URI: A unique identifier for an object stored in Google Cloud Storage, formatted as gs://BUCKET_NAME/OBJECT_NAME.

docs.title: Model availability
docs.text:
Upscaling availability is based on the model version.

Feature imagegeneration@002 imagegeneration@005 imagegeneration@006 Upscaling ✔ Not supported Not supported

docs.title: Ways to upscale an image
docs.text:
You can upscale an image using the Google Cloud console for quick tasks or the REST API for automation and integration.

Method Use Case Google Cloud console Best for quick, one-off tasks and visual confirmation of results. REST API Best for automating upscaling tasks and integrating into applications. Google Cloud consoleREST API

The following workflow outlines the steps to upscale an image using the Google Cloud console.

flowchart TD
    A["Generate or select an image"] --> B["Configure upscaling"]
    B --> C["Export the image"]

click A "#generate-or-select-an-image"
click B "#configure-upscaling"
click C "#export-the-image"
Upscale an image using the Google Cloud console

1. Generate or select an image

  • Follow the generate image with text instructions to generate new images.
  • In the gallery, select the generated or an existing image that you want to upscale.

2. Configure upscaling

  • Click download Upscale/export.
  • Select Upscale images.
  • Choose a value from the Scale factor menu (2x or 4x).

3. Export the image

  • Click download Export to save the upscaled image to your local machine.

Use the following instructions to upscale an image by sending a POST request to the imagegeneration@002 model endpoint.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Before sending the request, replace the following placeholders with your own values:

  • LOCATION: Your project's region. For example, us-central1, europe-west2, or asia-northeast3. For a list of available regions, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.
  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • B64_BASE_IMAGE: The base image to upscale, specified as a base64-encoded byte string. The size limit is 10 MB.
  • IMAGE_SOURCE: The Cloud Storage URI of the image you want to upscale. For example: gs://output-bucket/source-photos/photo.png.
  • UPSCALE_FACTOR: The factor by which the image is upscaled. Available values are x2 or x4.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Make an upscale request
docs.text:
Send a POST request to the model. In the request body, specify "mode": "upscale" and include the upscaleConfig object.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagegeneration@002:predict

Request JSON body:

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "",
      "image": {
        // use one of the following to specify the image to upscale
        "bytesBase64Encoded": "B64_BASE_IMAGE"
        "gcsUri": "IMAGE_SOURCE"
        // end of base image input options
      },
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "sampleCount": 1,
    "mode": "upscale",
    "upscaleConfig": {
      "upscaleFactor": "UPSCALE_FACTOR"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Send the request
docs.text:
To send your request, choose one of the following options.

==== "curl" Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login , or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI . You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named `request.json`, and execute the following command:

```bash
curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \

     -d @request.json \

```

==== "PowerShell" Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login . You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named `request.json`, and execute the following command:

```powershell
$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method POST `
    -Headers $headers `
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `
    -InFile request.json `
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagegeneration@002:predict" | Select-Object -Expand Content

docs.title: Use prompt rewriter
docs.text:
Caution: Starting on June 24, 2025, Imagen versions 1 and 2 are deprecated. Imagen models imagegeneration@002, imagegeneration@005, and imagegeneration@006 will be removed on September 24, 2025. For more information about migrating to Imagen 3, see Migrate to Imagen 3.

Imagen on Vertex AI offers an LLM-based prompt rewriting tool, also known as a prompt rewriter. The prompt rewriter helps you obtain higher-quality output images by adding more detail to your prompt. If you disable the prompt rewriter, the quality of the images and how well the output resembles the prompt that you supplied might be impacted.

This feature is enabled by default for the following model versions:

  • imagen-4.0-generate-preview-06-06 (Preview)
  • imagen-4.0-fast-generate-preview-06-06 (Preview)
  • imagen-4.0-ultra-generate-preview-06-06 (Preview)
  • imagen-3.0-generate-002

The rewritten prompt is delivered in the API response only if the original prompt is fewer than 30 words long.

Try image generation (Vertex AI Studio) Try Imagen in a Colab

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Prompt Rewriter: An LLM-based tool that enhances a short, simple user prompt by adding more detail and descriptive language to generate higher-quality images.
  • Imagen: A family of text-to-image diffusion models developed by Google that generate photorealistic images from natural language text prompts.
  • LLM (Large Language Model): A type of artificial intelligence model trained on vast amounts of text data to understand and generate human-like language.
  • REST API: A standardized way for computer systems to communicate over the internet, allowing you to send requests and receive responses to interact with services like Vertex AI.

docs.title: Use the prompt rewriter
docs.text:
You can use the prompt rewriter through the Google Cloud console or by making a REST API request.

ConsoleREST API

flowchart TD

Steps to use the prompt rewriter in the console

1. Navigate to Imagen in Media Studio

  • In the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI > Media Studio page.

    Go to Media Studio

  • Click Imagen. The Imagen Media Studio image generation page is displayed.

2. Configure generation settings

In the Settings panel, adjust the following options:

  • Model: Choose a model from the available options. For more information, see Imagen models.
  • Number of results: Adjust the slider or enter a value between 1 and 4.
  • Negative prompt: In the box, enter a prompt that describes what you don't want generated in the image.

3. Enhance the prompt

  • In the Write your prompt box, click Help me write. The Enhance my prompt window is displayed.
  • In the Current prompt box, write your prompt, and then click Enhance. The rewritten prompt is displayed in the Enhanced prompt box. You can edit the enhanced prompt or use it as displayed.
  • Click Insert to use the displayed prompt. The prompt is inserted into the Write your prompt box.

4. Generate the image

  • Click send Generate.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • MODEL_VERSION: The image generation model version to use. For more information, see model versions.
  • LOCATION: Your project's region. For example, us-central1, europe-west2, or asia-northeast3. For a list of available regions, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.
  • TEXT_PROMPT: The text prompt that guides what images the model generates. Before images are generated, this base prompt is enhanced with more detail using the prompt rewriter.
  • IMAGE_COUNT: The number of generated images. Accepted integer values: 1-4. Default value: 4.

To enable the prompt rewriter, set the enhancePrompt parameter to true in your request.

      "prompt": "TEXT_PROMPT"
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {

    "enhancePrompt": true
  }
}

docs.text:

This page describes how to verify if an image generated by Imagen on Vertex AI contains a digital watermark.

By default, Imagen on Vertex AI adds a digital watermark to any images generated by a model version that supports this feature. When you generate an image with a watermark, Imagen adds a non-visible digital watermark, called a SynthID, to the image file. You can then check if an image contains this digital watermark.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Imagen: A text-to-image diffusion model that lets you generate and edit high-quality, photorealistic images from natural language prompts.
  • SynthID: A technology that adds a non-visible digital watermark directly into the pixels of an image, making it detectable for identification without compromising image quality.
