docs.title: Use models in Model Garden
docs.text:
Discover, test, tune, and deploy generative AI models by using Model Garden in the Google Cloud console. You can also interact with Model Garden models programmatically by using the Vertex AI SDK for Python, the Google Cloud CLI, or the REST API.

This document guides you through the common lifecycle of using a model from Model Garden, from initial discovery to final cleanup.

The following workflow shows the general steps for using a model from Model Garden.

flowchart TD
    A[Discover and test a model] --> B{Need to customize?};
    B -- Yes --> C[Tune a model];
    B -- No --> D[Deploy a model];
    C --> D;
    D --> E[Manage and clean up resources];

    click A "#discover-and-test-a-model"
    click C "#tune-a-model"
    click D "#deploy-a-model"
    click E "#manage-and-clean-up-resources"

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Model Garden: A central place in Vertex AI to discover, test, tune, and deploy Google-proprietary and select open source models.
  • Model Registry: A central repository for managing the lifecycle of your ML models after they are trained or imported.
  • Endpoint: A service you deploy your model to, which serves online predictions. An endpoint has a unique URI that you send prediction requests to.
  • Tuning: The process of adjusting a pre-trained model's parameters on a specific dataset to improve its performance on a particular task.
Set up your project and environment
  1. In the Google Cloud console, on the project selector page, select or create a Google Cloud project.
  2. Make sure that billing is enabled for your Google Cloud project.
  3. Enable the Vertex AI API.
  4. If you are using the gcloud CLI or the SDK, install and initialize the Google Cloud CLI.

docs.title: Discover and test a model
docs.text:
The first step is to explore Model Garden to find a model suitable for your use case. You can then test it directly in the console using the prompt design interface or review its documentation for code samples.

Steps to discover and test a model

Send test prompts

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Model Garden page.

    Go to Model Garden

  2. Find a supported model that you want to test and click View details.

  3. Click Open prompt design. You're taken to the Prompt design page.
  4. In the Prompt field, enter the prompt that you want to test.
  5. Optional: Configure the model parameters.
  6. Click Submit.

View code samples

Most model cards for task-specific models contain code samples that you can copy and test.

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Model Garden page.
  2. Find a supported model and click its model card to view details.
  3. Click the Documentation tab to find embedded code samples.

docs.title: Tune a model
docs.text:
For some models, you can fine-tune them with your own data to improve their performance on a specific task. Model Garden supports tuning through a guided pipeline or by using a Jupyter notebook for more control.

Method Best For Description Fine-tuning pipeline Users who prefer a guided, UI-based experience for tuning standard models like T5-FLAN or BERT. A structured pipeline in the Google Cloud console that walks you through the tuning process. Notebook Developers who need more flexibility and control over the tuning process and environment. Most open source and fine-tunable models provide a notebook that can be opened in Vertex AI Workbench or Colab. Tune with a fine-tuning pipelineTune in a notebook

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Model Garden page.

    Go to Model Garden

  2. In Search models, enter BERT or T5-FLAN, then click the magnifying glass to search.

  3. Click View details on the T5-FLAN or the BERT model card.
  4. Click Open fine-tuning pipeline. You're taken to the Vertex AI pipelines page.
  5. To start tuning, click Create run.

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Model Garden page.

    Go to Model Garden

  2. Find a supported model that you want to tune and go to its model card.

  3. Click Open notebook.

docs.title: Deploy a model
docs.text:
After you have selected a model, deploy it to a Vertex AI endpoint to serve online predictions. You can deploy models using the Google Cloud console for a guided experience, or programmatically using the Vertex AI SDK, gcloud CLI, or REST API for automation and integration.

Method Best For Key Features Console Quick deployments and users who prefer a graphical interface. Guided, step-by-step UI for configuration and deployment. Vertex AI SDK for Python Integrating model deployment into Python applications and MLOps workflows. High-level, intuitive Python library for managing AI resources. gcloud CLI Scripting, automation, and terminal-based management. Command-line interface for managing Google Cloud resources. REST API Integrating with custom applications or services in any language. Language-agnostic interface for programmatic control over resources.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

ConsoleVertex AI SDK for PythongcloudREST API

You can deploy both open models and partner models through the Google Cloud console.

Deploy an open model

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Model Garden page.

    Go to Model Garden

  2. Find a supported model that you want to deploy, and click its model card.

  3. Click Deploy to open the Deploy model pane.
  4. In the Deploy model pane, specify details for your deployment.
    1. Use or modify the generated model and endpoint names.
    2. Select a location to create your model endpoint in.
    3. Select a machine type to use for each node of your deployment.
    4. To use a Compute Engine reservation, under the Deployment settings section, select Advanced. For the Reservation type field, select a reservation type. The reservation must match your specified machine specs.
      • Automatically use created reservation: Vertex AI automatically selects an allowed reservation with matching properties.
      • Select specific reservations: Vertex AI uses a specific reservation. If there's no capacity, an error is thrown.
      • Don't use (default): Vertex AI uses the general Google Cloud resource pool.
  5. Click Deploy.
Deploy a partner model

Preview

This feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

Before you begin

You must have an agreement with the partner, including terms, licensing, and pricing. To initiate contact, see the partner documentation on their Model Garden model card and click Contact sales. You must deploy on the partner's required machine types.

Note: For self-deploy partner models, if you have sufficient quotas but encounter serving quota issues during deployment, contact your Google Cloud account team for assistance.

Steps

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Model Garden page.

    Go to Model Garden

  2. To find a specific model, enter its name in the Model Garden search box.

  3. To view all models that you can self-deploy, in the Model collections section of the filter pane, select Self-deploy partner models.
  4. Click the name of the model to deploy, which opens its model card.
  5. Click Deploy options.
  6. In the Deploy on Vertex AI pane, configure your deployment such as the location and machine type.
  7. Click Deploy.

After the deployment is complete, you can request predictions by using the SDK or API. Additional instructions are available in the "Documentation" section on the model card.

For more information about setting up the SDK, see the Google Gen AI SDK overview or Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python.

Deploy an open model

1. List deployable models

List the models that you can deploy and record the model ID.

import vertexai
from vertexai.preview import model_garden

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

# List deployable models, optionally list Hugging Face models only or filter by model name.
deployable_models = model_garden.list_deployable_models(list_hf_models=False, model_filter="gemma")
print(deployable_models)
# Example response:
# ['google/gemma2@gemma-2-27b','google/gemma2@gemma-2-27b-it', ...]

2. View deployment specifications

View the machine type, accelerator type, and container image URI for a model.

import vertexai
from vertexai.preview import model_garden

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# model = "google/gemma3@gemma-3-1b-it"
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

# For Hugging Face modelsm the format is the Hugging Face model name, as in
# "meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct".
# Go to https://console.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/model-garden to find all deployable
# model names.

model = model_garden.OpenModel(model)
deploy_options = model.list_deploy_options()
print(deploy_options)
# Example response:
# [
#   dedicated_resources {
#     machine_spec {
#       machine_type: "g2-standard-12"
#       accelerator_type: NVIDIA_L4
#       accelerator_count: 1
#     }
#   }
#   container_spec {
#     ...
#   }
#   ...
# ]

3. Deploy a model to an endpoint

Model Garden uses the default deployment configuration unless you specify additional arguments.

import vertexai
from vertexai.preview import model_garden

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

open_model = model_garden.OpenModel("google/gemma3@gemma-3-12b-it")
endpoint = open_model.deploy(
    machine_type="g2-standard-48",
    accelerator_type="NVIDIA_L4",
    accelerator_count=4,
    accept_eula=True,
)

# Optional. Run predictions on the deployed endoint.
# endpoint.predict(instances=[{"prompt": "What is Generative AI?"}])
Deploy a partner model

Preview

This feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

Note: The values for the machine type, accelerator type, and accelerator count, must all match one of the partner's recommended configurations. View the partner's Model Garden model card to see the recommended configurations.

In your code, replace the placeholders.

from google.cloud import aiplatform

# Replace with your values
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# LOCATION = "us-central1"
# DISPLAY_NAME_MODEL = "my-partner-model"
# PUBLISHER_NAME = "partner-name"
# PUBLISHER_MODEL_NAME = "partner-model-name"
# DISPLAY_NAME_ENDPOINT = "my-partner-endpoint"
# DISPLAY_NAME_DEPLOYED_MODEL = "my-deployed-partner-model"
# MACHINE_TYPE = "g2-standard-4"
# ACCELERATOR_TYPE = "NVIDIA_L4"
# ACCELERATOR_COUNT = 1
# REQUEST_PAYLOAD = {"instances": [...]}

aiplatform.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location=LOCATION)

# Upload a model
model = aiplatform.Model.upload(
    display_name=DISPLAY_NAME_MODEL,
    model_garden_source_model_name = f"publishers/{PUBLISHER_NAME}/models/{PUBLISHER_MODEL_NAME}",
)

# Create endpoint
my_endpoint = aiplatform.Endpoint.create(display_name=DISPLAY_NAME_ENDPOINT)

# Deploy model
model.deploy(
    endpoint=my_endpoint,
    deployed_model_display_name=DISPLAY_NAME_DEPLOYED_MODEL,
    traffic_split={"0": 100},
    machine_type=MACHINE_TYPE,
    accelerator_type=ACCELERATOR_TYPE,
    accelerator_count=ACCELERATOR_COUNT,
    min_replica_count=1,
    max_replica_count=1,
)

# Unary call for predictions
PAYLOAD = REQUEST_PAYLOAD
request = json.dumps(PAYLOAD)
response = my_endpoint.raw_predict(
    body = request,
    headers = {'Content-Type':'application/json'}
)
print(response)

# Streaming call for predictions
PAYLOAD = REQUEST_PAYLOAD
request = json.dumps(PAYLOAD)
for stream_response in my_endpoint.stream_raw_predict(
    body = request,
    headers = {'Content-Type':'application/json'}
):
    print(stream_response)

Before you begin, specify a quota project to run the following commands. For more information, see Set the quota project.

Deploy an open model

1. List deployable models

Run the gcloud ai model-garden models list command to find the model ID to deploy.

gcloud ai model-garden models list

The output shows model IDs and whether they support deployment. To view supported Hugging Face models, add the --can-deploy-hugging-face-models flag.

MODEL_ID                                                                SUPPORTS_DEPLOYMENT
google/gemma2@gemma-2-27b                                               Yes
google/gemma2@gemma-2-27b-it                                            Yes
...

2. View deployment specifications

Run the gcloud ai model-garden models list-deployment-config command to view supported machine types, accelerators, and container URIs.

gcloud ai model-garden models list-deployment-config \
    --model=MODEL_ID

Replace MODEL_ID with the ID from the previous step (e.g., google/gemma@gemma-2b).

3. Deploy a model to an endpoint

Run the gcloud ai model-garden models deploy command. Model Garden uses default settings unless you specify them.

gcloud ai model-garden models deploy \
    --model=MODEL_ID \
    [--machine-type=MACHINE_TYPE] \
    [--accelerator-type=ACCELERATOR_TYPE] \
    [--endpoint-display-name=ENDPOINT_NAME] \
    [--hugging-face-access-token=HF_ACCESS_TOKEN] \
    [--reservation-affinity reservation-affinity-type=any-reservation] \
    [--reservation-affinity reservation-affinity-type=specific-reservation,key="compute.googleapis.com/reservation-name",values=RESERVATION_RESOURCE_NAME] \
    [--asynchronous]

Replace the placeholders: * MODEL_ID: The model ID to deploy. For Hugging Face models, use the URL format (e.g., stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0). * MACHINE_TYPE: The machine type for deployment (e.g., g2-standard-4). * ACCELERATOR_TYPE: The accelerator type (e.g., NVIDIA_L4). * ENDPOINT_NAME: A name for the Vertex AI endpoint. * HF_ACCESS_TOKEN: An access token for gated Hugging Face models. * RESERVATION_RESOURCE_NAME: The name of a specific Compute Engine reservation.

4. View deployment details

Run the gcloud ai endpoints list --list-model-garden-endpoints-only command to see details about your deployment.

gcloud ai endpoints list --list-model-garden-endpoints-only \
    --region=LOCATION_ID

Replace LOCATION_ID with the region where you deployed the model.

You can list all deployable models and then deploy a model with default or custom configurations.

Deploy an open model

1. List models that you can deploy

Make a GET request to list available models. Before using the request data, replace PROJECT_ID and QUERY_PARAMETERS. * To list Model Garden models, use listAllVersions=True&filter=is_deployable(true). * To list Hugging Face models, use alt=json&is_hf_wildcard(true)+AND+labels.VERIFIED_DEPLOYMENT_CONFIG%3DVERIFIED_DEPLOYMENT_SUCCEED&listAllVersions=True.

HTTP method and URL:

GET https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/publishers/*/models?QUERY_PARAMETERS

To send your request, choose one of these options:

curlPowerShell 
curl -X GET \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "x-goog-user-project: PROJECT_ID" \
     "https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/publishers/*/models?QUERY_PARAMETERS"

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred"; "x-goog-user-project" = "PROJECT_ID" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method GET `
    -Headers $headers `
    -Uri "https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/publishers/*/models?QUERY_PARAMETERS" | Select-Object -Expand Content

2. Deploy a model

You can deploy a model from Model Garden, a Hugging Face model, or deploy with custom configurations.

Deploy a model with its default configuration

Before using the request data, replace LOCATION, PROJECT_ID, and MODEL_ID. The MODEL_ID format is publishers/PUBLISHER_NAME/models/MODEL_NAME@MODEL_VERSION.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION:deploy

Request JSON body:

{
  "publisher_model_name": "MODEL_ID",
  "model_config": {
    "accept_eula": "true"
  }
}

To send your request, choose one of these options:

curlPowerShell

Save the request body in a file named request.json, then execute the command:

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d @request.json \
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION:deploy"

Save the request body in a file named request.json, then execute the command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method POST `
    -Headers $headers `
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `
    -InFile request.json `
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION:deploy" | Select-Object -Expand Content
Deploy a Hugging Face model

Before using the request data, replace LOCATION, PROJECT_ID, MODEL_ID (format: PUBLISHER_NAME/MODEL_NAME), and ACCESS_TOKEN (if the model is gated).

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION:deploy

Request JSON body:

{
  "hugging_face_model_id": "MODEL_ID",
  "hugging_face_access_token": "ACCESS_TOKEN",
  "model_config": {
    "accept_eula": "true"
  }
}

To send your request, use the curl or PowerShell commands from the previous section with this request body.

Deploy a model with customizations

Before using the request data, replace the placeholders in the JSON body.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION:deploy

Request JSON body:

{
  "publisher_model_name": "MODEL_ID",
  "deploy_config": {
    "dedicated_resources": {
      "machine_spec": {
        "machine_type": "MACHINE_TYPE",
        "accelerator_type": "ACCELERATOR_TYPE",
        "accelerator_count": ACCELERATOR_COUNT,
        "reservation_affinity": {
          "reservation_affinity_type": "ANY_RESERVATION"
        }
      },
      "spot": "false"
    },
    "fast_tryout_enabled": false
  },
  "model_config": {
    "accept_eula": "true",
    "container_spec": {
      "image_uri": "IMAGE_URI",
      "args": [CONTAINER_ARGS ],
      "ports": [
        {
          "container_port": CONTAINER_PORT
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}

To send your request, use the curl or PowerShell commands from the previous sections with this request body.

Deploy a partner model

Preview

This feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

Note: The values for the machine type, accelerator type, and accelerator count, must all match one of the partner's recommended configurations.

In the sample curl commands, replace the placeholders.

1. Upload a model to your Model Registry

curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapi.com/v1beta1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/models:upload \
-d '{
  "model": {
    "displayName": "DISPLAY_NAME_MODEL",
    "baseModelSource": {
      "modelGardenSource": {
        "publicModelName": f"publishers/PUBLISHER_NAME/models/PUBLISHER_MODEL_NAME",
      }
    }
  }
}'

2. Create an endpoint

curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapi.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/endpoints \
-d '{
  "displayName": "DISPLAY_NAME_ENDPOINT"
}'

3. Deploy the uploaded model to the endpoint

curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapi.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/endpoints/ENDPOINT_ID:deployModel \
-d '{
  "deployedModel": {
    "model": f"projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/models/MODEL_ID",
    "displayName": "DISPLAY_NAME_DEPLOYED_MODEL",
    "dedicatedResources": {
     "machineSpec": {
        "machineType": "MACHINE_TYPE",
        "acceleratorType": "ACCELERATOR_TYPE",
        "acceleratorCount":"ACCELERATOR_COUNT",
     },
     "minReplicaCount": 1,
     "maxReplicaCount": 1
    },
  },
  "trafficSplit": {
    "0": 100
  }
}'

4. Make prediction requests

After the model is deployed, you can make a unary or streaming call for predictions.

  • Sample unary call:

    curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapi.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/endpoints/ENDPOINT_ID:rawPredict \
-d 'REQUEST_PAYLOAD'

  • Sample streaming call:

    curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapi.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/endpoints/ENDPOINT_ID:streamRawPredict \
-d 'REQUEST_PAYLOAD'

docs.title: Manage and clean up resources
docs.text: To avoid incurring unnecessary charges to your Google Cloud account, it's important to clean up the resources you created. This involves undeploying the model from its endpoint, then deleting the endpoint and the model from the Model Registry.

docs.title: View or manage an endpoint
docs.text:
To view and manage your endpoint, go to the Vertex AI Online prediction page.

Go to Online prediction

docs.title: Clean up resources
docs.text:
To stop a deployed model from using resources, you must perform the following steps in order: 1. Undeploy the model from its endpoint. 2. Delete the endpoint. 3. Delete the model from the Model Registry.

ConsoleVertex AI SDK for Pythongcloud Undeploy a model

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Endpoints tab on the Online prediction page.

    Go to Endpoints

  2. In the Region drop-down list, choose the region where your endpoint is located.

  3. Click the endpoint name to open the details page.
  4. On the row for the model, click more_vert Actions, and then select Undeploy model from endpoint.
  5. In the Undeploy model from endpoint dialog, click Undeploy.
Delete an endpoint

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Endpoints tab on the Online prediction page.

    Go to Endpoints

  2. In the Region drop-down list, choose the region your endpoint is located.

  3. At the end of the endpoint's row, click more_vert Actions, and then select Delete endpoint.
  4. In the confirmation prompt, click Confirm.
Delete a model

  1. Go to the Model Registry page from the Vertex AI section in the Google Cloud console.

    Go to the Model Registry page

  2. In the Region drop-down list, choose the region where you deployed your model.

  3. On the row for your model, click more_vert Actions and then select Delete model.
  4. In the confirmation prompt, click Delete.

Replace the placeholders in the code snippets with your PROJECT_ID, LOCATION, ENDPOINT_ID, and MODEL_ID.

Undeploy a model 
from google.cloud import aiplatform

aiplatform.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location=LOCATION)

# To find out which endpoints are available, un-comment the line below:
# endpoints = aiplatform.Endpoint.list()

endpoint = aiplatform.Endpoint(ENDPOINT_ID)
endpoint.undeploy_all()
Delete an endpoint 
from google.cloud import aiplatform

aiplatform.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location=LOCATION)

# To find out which endpoints are available, un-comment the line below:
# endpoints = aiplatform.Endpoint.list()

endpoint = aiplatform.Endpoint(ENDPOINT_ID)
endpoint.delete()
Delete a model 
from google.cloud import aiplatform

aiplatform.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location=LOCATION)

# To find out which models are available in Model Registry, un-comment the line below:
# models = aiplatform.Model.list()

model = aiplatform.Model(MODEL_ID)
model.delete()

Replace the placeholders in the commands with your PROJECT_ID, LOCATION_ID, ENDPOINT_ID, MODEL_ID, and DEPLOYED_MODEL_ID.

Undeploy a model

  1. Find the endpoint ID associated with your deployment.

    gcloud ai endpoints list \
    --project=PROJECT_ID \
    --region=LOCATION_ID

  2. Find the model ID.

    gcloud ai models list \
    --project=PROJECT_ID \
    --region=LOCATION_ID

  3. Get the deployed model ID using the model ID from the previous step.

    gcloud ai models describe MODEL_ID \
    --project=PROJECT_ID \
    --region=LOCATION_ID

    In the output, find the deployedModelId.

  4. Undeploy the model from the endpoint.

    gcloud ai endpoints undeploy-model ENDPOINT_ID \
    --project=PROJECT_ID \
    --region=LOCATION_ID \
    --deployed-model-id=DEPLOYED_MODEL_ID
Delete an endpoint

  1. Get the endpoint ID to delete.

    gcloud ai endpoints list \
    --project=PROJECT_ID \
    --region=LOCATION_ID

  2. Delete the endpoint.

    gcloud ai endpoints delete ENDPOINT_ID \
    --project=PROJECT_ID \
    --region=LOCATION_ID

    When prompted, type y to confirm.

Delete a model

  1. Find the model ID to delete.

    gcloud ai models list \
    --project=PROJECT_ID \
    --region=LOCATION_ID

  2. Delete the model.

    gcloud ai models delete MODEL_ID \
    --project=PROJECT_ID \
    --region=LOCATION_ID

docs.title: Generative AI on Vertex AI inference API errors
docs.text: This guide lists common errors you might encounter when using the Generative AI on Vertex AI inference API. The errors align with the Google Cloud API error model, with specific causes and solutions tailored for generative AI models. For more information on the API itself, see the Model API reference for Generative AI.

docs.title: API errors
docs.text:
The following sections describe common API error codes, their causes, and potential solutions.

400 Bad Request (INVALID_ARGUMENT / FAILED_PRECONDITION)

Cause: The request fails API validation, or you tried to access a model that requires allowlisting or is disallowed by your organization's policy.

Example: The request exceeds the model's input token limit.

Solution: Refer to the Model API reference for Generative AI for details on request parameters, token count, and other parameters.

403 Permission Denied (PERMISSION_DENIED)

Cause: The client does not have sufficient permission to call the API.

Example: A service account does not have permission to access the Cloud Storage bucket that hosts image or video resources.

Solution:

  • Verify that all necessary APIs are enabled and that the service account has the correct permission to access the selected Vertex AI service.
  • Ensure the Vertex AI per-product, per-project service account (P4SA) is granted the necessary permission to access resources referenced in the input.
404 Not Found (NOT_FOUND)

Cause: No valid object is found at the designated URL.

Example: The image file is not found in the specified storage URL.

Solution: Check and fix the file location.

429 Resource Exhausted (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED)

Cause: Depending on the error message, this could be caused by one of the following:

  • API quota has been exceeded.
  • The server is overloaded due to shared capacity.
  • You've reached the daily limit for requests using logprobs.

Example: The Gemini API request rate exceeds the per-minute limit.

Solution:

  • Check your Vertex AI Generative AI quota limits. If needed, request a higher quota.
  • Retry after a few seconds. If the error persists for a prolonged period (hours), contact Vertex AI support.
499 Cancelled (CANCELLED)

Cause: The request was cancelled by the client.

Solution: This error is initiated by the client; no server-side solution is applicable.

500 Internal Server Error (UNKNOWN / INTERNAL)

Cause: A server error occurred due to overload or a dependency failure.

Example: The request is throttled because the service is temporarily overloaded.

Solution: Retry after a few seconds. If the error persists for a prolonged period (hours), contact Vertex AI support.

503 Service Unavailable (UNAVAILABLE)

Cause: The service is temporarily unavailable.

Example: The server is not responding to incoming requests.

Solution: The unavailable status might be temporary. Retry your request after a short delay. If the error persists, contact Vertex AI support.

504 Deadline Exceeded (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED)

Cause: The client set a deadline shorter than the server's default timeout (10 minutes), and the request did not finish within the client-provided deadline.

Solution: Consider increasing the deadline in your client configuration.

docs.title: Handle errors
docs.text:
To minimize errors, consider the following best practices:

  • Avoid traffic spikes: Sudden, large increases in request volume can trigger quota limits or cause server overloading. Distribute your API calls more evenly over time.
  • Implement retry logic carefully: When retrying a failed request, use an exponential backoff strategy. We recommend a minimum delay of one second for the first retry and retrying no more than twice.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues not listed here, refer to the general Vertex AI Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Get batch predictions for Gemini
docs.text:
Batch predictions let you send a large number of multimodal prompts in a single batch request.

For more information about the batch workflow and how to format your input data, see Get batch predictions for Gemini.

docs.title: Supported models
docs.text:
• Gemini 1.5 Pro
  • Gemini 1.5 Flash
  • Gemini 1.0 Pro

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Batch Prediction: A process for sending a large number of inference requests to a model in a single asynchronous job, which is ideal for offline processing of non-real-time data.
  • Cloud Storage: A scalable and durable object storage service for unstructured data, often used to store input files (like JSONL) and receive model outputs.
  • BigQuery: A serverless, highly scalable data warehouse that enables super-fast SQL queries using the processing power of Google's infrastructure, used here as both an input source and output destination.
  • JSONL: A text format for storing structured data where each line is a valid JSON object, commonly used for streaming data and batch inputs.
  • REST API: A standardized architectural style for creating web services that allows different systems to communicate over HTTP, used here for making direct calls to the Vertex AI service.

docs.title: Batch prediction workflow
docs.text:
The following diagram shows the high-level workflow for getting batch predictions.

flowchart TD
    A[Prepare your inputs] --> B[Create a batch prediction job]
    B --> C[Check job status]
    C --> D[Retrieve batch output]

    click A "#prepare-your-inputs"
    click B "#create-a-batch-prediction-job"
    click C "#check-job-status"
    click D "#retrieve-batch-output"

docs.title: Prepare your inputs
docs.text:
Before you can create a batch prediction job, you need to prepare your input data. Inputs can be stored in either Cloud Storage as a JSONL file or in a BigQuery table.

For detailed instructions on how to format your data for different multimodal prompts, see Prepare your batch request inputs.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: The following tables describe the parameters for a batch prediction job request.

docs.title: Request body
docs.text: Parameter Description displayName A name you choose for your job. model The model to use for batch prediction. inputConfig The configuration for your input data source. Gemini batch prediction supports Cloud Storage and BigQuery. outputConfig The configuration for your output location. Cloud Storage and BigQuery are supported.

docs.title: inputConfig
docs.text: Parameter Description instancesFormat The prompt input format. Use jsonl for Cloud Storage or bigquery for BigQuery. gcsSource.uris The input source URI. This is a Cloud Storage location of the JSONL file in the format gs://bucketname/path/to/file.jsonl. bigquerySource.inputUri The input source URI. This is a BigQuery table URI in the format bq://project_id.dataset.table. The region of the input BigQuery dataset must be the same as the Vertex AI batch prediction job.

docs.title: outputConfig
docs.text: Parameter Description predictionsFormat The output format of the prediction. Use jsonl for Cloud Storage or bigquery for BigQuery. gcsDestination.outputUriPrefix The Cloud Storage bucket and directory location, in the format gs://mybucket/path/to/output. bigqueryDestination.outputUri The BigQuery URI of the target output table, in the format bq://project_id.dataset.table. If the table doesn't already exist, it is created for you. The region of the output BigQuery dataset must be the same as the Vertex AI batch prediction job.

docs.title: Create a batch prediction job
docs.text:
You can create a batch prediction job using the REST API or client libraries for various programming languages. Depending on the number of input items you submitted, a batch generation task can take some time to complete.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

RESTGen AI SDK for PythonNode.jsJavaGo

To create a batch prediction job, use the projects.locations.batchPredictionJobs.create method.

Cloud Storage inputBigQuery input

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • LOCATION: A region that supports Gemini models.
  • PROJECT_ID: Your project ID.
  • MODEL_PATH: The publisher model name (e.g., publishers/google/models/gemini-1.5-flash-001) or the tuned endpoint name (e.g., projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/models/MODEL_ID).
  • INPUT_URI: The Cloud Storage location of your JSONL batch prediction input (e.g., gs://bucketname/path/to/file.jsonl).
  • OUTPUT_FORMAT: To output to a BigQuery table, specify bigquery. To output to a Cloud Storage bucket, specify jsonl.
  • DESTINATION: For BigQuery, specify bigqueryDestination. For Cloud Storage, specify gcsDestination.
  • OUTPUT_URI_FIELD_NAME: For BigQuery, specify outputUri. For Cloud Storage, specify outputUriPrefix.
  • OUTPUT_URI: For BigQuery, specify the table location (e.g., bq://myproject.mydataset.output_result). For Cloud Storage, specify the bucket and directory location (e.g., gs://mybucket/path/to/output).

Request JSON body:

{
  "displayName": "my-cloud-storage-batch-prediction-job",
  "model": "MODEL_PATH",
  "inputConfig": {
    "instancesFormat": "jsonl",
    "gcsSource": {
      "uris" : ["INPUT_URI"]
    }
  },
  "outputConfig": {
    "predictionsFormat": "OUTPUT_FORMAT",
    "DESTINATION": {
      "OUTPUT_URI_FIELD_NAME": "OUTPUT_URI"
    }
  }
}

To send your request, choose one of these options:

curl

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \  
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \  
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \  
     -d @request.json \  
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/batchPredictionJobs"

PowerShell

To learn more, see the SDK reference documentation.

  const gcsSource = new aiplatform.GcsSource({
    uris: [inputUri],
  });

  const inputConfig = new aiplatform.BatchPredictionJob.InputConfig({
    gcsSource: gcsSource,
    instancesFormat: 'jsonl',
  });

  const gcsDestination = new aiplatform.GcsDestination({
    outputUriPrefix: outputUri,
  });

  const outputConfig = new aiplatform.BatchPredictionJob.OutputConfig({
    gcsDestination: gcsDestination,
    predictionsFormat: 'jsonl',
  });

  const batchPredictionJob = new aiplatform.BatchPredictionJob({

    model: modelName,
    inputConfig: inputConfig,
    outputConfig: outputConfig,
  });

  const request = {
    parent: parent,

  console.log('Response name: ', response.name);

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "io"
    "time"

    aiplatform "cloud.google.com/go/aiplatform/apiv1"
    aiplatformpb "cloud.google.com/go/aiplatform/apiv1/aiplatformpb"

    "google.golang.org/api/option"
    "google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/structpb"
)

// batchPredictGCS submits a batch prediction job using GCS data source as its input
func batchPredictGCS(w io.Writer, projectID, location string, inputURIs []string, outputURI string) error {
    // location := "us-central1"
    // inputURIs := []string{"gs://cloud-samples-data/batch/prompt_for_batch_gemini_predict.jsonl"}
    // outputURI := "gs://<cloud-bucket-name>/<prefix-name>"
    modelName := "gemini-1.0-pro-001"
    jobName := "batch-predict-gcs-test-001"

    ctx := context.Background()
    apiEndpoint := fmt.Sprintf("%s-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443", location)
    client, err := aiplatform.NewJobClient(ctx, option.WithEndpoint(apiEndpoint))
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("unable to create aiplatform client: %w", err)
    }
    defer client.Close()

    modelParameters, err := structpb.NewValue(map[string]interface{}{
        "temperature":     0.2,
        "maxOutputTokens": 200,
    })
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("unable to convert model parameters to protobuf value: %w", err)
    }

    req := &aiplatformpb.CreateBatchPredictionJobRequest{
        Parent: fmt.Sprintf("projects/%s/locations/%s", projectID, location),
        BatchPredictionJob: &aiplatformpb.BatchPredictionJob{
            DisplayName:     jobName,
            Model:           fmt.Sprintf("publishers/google/models/%s", modelName),
            ModelParameters: modelParameters,
            // Check the API reference for `BatchPredictionJob` for supported input and output formats:
            // https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/reference/rpc/google.cloud.aiplatform.v1#google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.BatchPredictionJob
            InputConfig: &aiplatformpb.BatchPredictionJob_InputConfig{
                Source: &aiplatformpb.BatchPredictionJob_InputConfig_GcsSource{
                    GcsSource: &aiplatformpb.GcsSource{
                        Uris: inputURIs,
                    },
                },
                InstancesFormat: "jsonl",
            },
            OutputConfig: &aiplatformpb.BatchPredictionJob_OutputConfig{
                Destination: &aiplatformpb.BatchPredictionJob_OutputConfig_GcsDestination{
                    GcsDestination: &aiplatformpb.GcsDestination{
                        OutputUriPrefix: outputURI,
                    },
                },
                PredictionsFormat: "jsonl",
            },
        },
    }

    job, err := client.CreateBatchPredictionJob(ctx, req)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    fullJobId := job.GetName()
    fmt.Fprintf(w, "submitted batch predict job for model %q\n", job.GetModel())
    fmt.Fprintf(w, "job id: %q\n", fullJobId)
    fmt.Fprintf(w, "job state: %s\n", job.GetState())
    // Example response:
    // submitted batch predict job for model "publishers/google/models/gemini-1.0-pro-001"
    // job id: "projects/.../locations/.../batchPredictionJobs/1234567890000000000"
    // job state: JOB_STATE_PENDING

    for {
        time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)

        job, err := client.GetBatchPredictionJob(ctx, &aiplatformpb.GetBatchPredictionJobRequest{
            Name: fullJobId,
        })
        if err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("error: couldn't get updated job state: %w", err)
        }

        if job.GetEndTime() != nil {
            fmt.Fprintf(w, "batch predict job finished with state %s\n", job.GetState())
            break
        } else {
            fmt.Fprintf(w, "batch predict job is running... job state is %s\n", job.GetState())
        }
    }

    return nil
}

docs.title: Execute code with the Gemini API
docs.text:
The Gemini API code execution feature enables the model to generate and run Python code and learn iteratively from the results until it arrives at a final output. You can use this code execution capability to build applications that benefit from code-based reasoning and that produce text output. For example, you could use code execution in an application that solves complex equations or processes text.

The Gemini API provides code execution as a tool, similar to function calling. After you add code execution as a tool in your request, the model decides when to use it based on the prompt.

docs.title: Supported models and limitations
docs.text:
The following models support code execution:

  • Gemini 2.5 Pro
  • Gemini 2.5 Flash
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash

Preview

The following models are available in Preview: * Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite * Gemini 2.0 Flash with Live API

Experimental

The following model is available as an Experimental feature: * Vertex AI Model Optimizer

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The feature doesn't support file I/O.
  • Code execution can run for a maximum of 30 seconds before timing out.
Concepts
  • Code Execution Tool: The mechanism in the Gemini API that allows the model to generate and run Python code to solve problems.
  • ExecutableCode: An object containing the code generated by the model that is intended for execution.
  • CodeExecutionResult: An object containing the outcome (for example, success or failure) and output from the executed code.

docs.title: Code execution examples
docs.text:
The following examples show how to submit a query to the model and enable the code execution tool.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

cURLPython 
PROJECT_ID=myproject
REGION=us-central1
MODEL_ID=gemini-2.0-flash-001

curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://${REGION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/${REGION}/publishers/google/models/${MODEL_ID}:generateContent \
  -d '{
    "contents": [{
      "role": "user",
      "parts": [{
        "text": "Calculate 20th fibonacci number. Then find the nearest palindrome to it."
      }]
    }],
    "tools": [{"codeExecution": {}}],
  }'

from google import genai
from google.genai.types import Tool, ToolCodeExecution, GenerateContentConfig

client = genai.Client()
model_id = "gemini-2.0-flash-001"

code_execution_tool = Tool(
    code_execution=ToolCodeExecution()
)
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model=model_id,
    contents="Calculate 20th fibonacci number. Then find the nearest palindrome to it.",
    config=GenerateContentConfig(
        tools=[code_execution_tool],
        temperature=0,
    ),
)
for part in response.candidates[0].content.parts:
    if part.executable_code:
        print(part.executable_code)
    if part.code_execution_result:
        print(part.code_execution_result)
# Example response:
# code='...' language='PYTHON'
# outcome='OUTCOME_OK' output='The 20th Fibonacci number is: 6765\n'
# code='...' language='PYTHON'
# outcome='OUTCOME_OK' output='Lower Palindrome: 6666\nHigher Palindrome: 6776\nNearest Palindrome to 6765: 6776\n'

docs.title: CodeExecution
docs.text: A tool that executes code generated by the model and automatically returns the result to the model.

docs.title: Part
docs.text: Field Description executable_code Optional: ExecutableCode. Code generated by the model to be executed. code_execution_result Optional: CodeExecutionResult. Result of executing the ExecutableCode.

docs.title: ExecutableCode
docs.text: Field Description language Required: string (enum). The programming language for the generated code. Supported: PYTHON. code Required: string. The code to be executed.

docs.title: CodeExecutionResult
docs.text:
| Field | Description - | | outcome | Required: string (enum). The outcome of the code execution. Possible outcomes:

  • OUTCOME_OK: Code execution completed successfully.
  • OUTCOME_FAILED: Code execution finished but with a failure. stderr should contain the reason.
  • OUTCOME_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED: Code execution ran for too long and was canceled. There might be a partial output.
| | output | Required: string. Contains stdout when code execution is successful, or stderr or another description otherwise. - |

docs.title: CountTokens API
docs.text:
The CountTokens API calculates the number of input tokens before sending a request to the Gemini API.

Use the CountTokens API to prevent requests from exceeding the model context window and to estimate potential costs based on billable characters or tokens.

The CountTokens API can use the same contents parameter as Gemini API inference requests.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Token: A token is the smallest unit of text that a language model processes, which can be a word, part of a word, or punctuation.
  • Context Window: The context window is the maximum number of tokens that a model can consider at one time when generating a response.
  • MIME Type: A MIME (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions) type is a standard that indicates the nature and format of a document, file, or assortment of bytes.
  • System Instruction: A system instruction is a set of directions given to the model to guide its behavior and responses during a conversation.
  • Function Declaration: A function declaration provides the model with a structured description of a function it can call, including its name, parameters, and purpose.

docs.title: Supported models
docs.text:
• Gemini 2.5 Pro
  • Gemini 2.5 Flash
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash with image generation (Preview)
  • Vertex AI Model Optimizer (Experimental)

docs.title: Request body parameters
docs.text: The request body for countTokens contains a contents object, which is an array of Content objects.

docs.title: Content
docs.text:
A Content object consists of a role and a list of parts.

Parameter Type Description role Optional: string The identity of the entity that creates the message. Set the string to one of the following:
  • user: Indicates the message is sent by a real person.
  • model: Indicates the message is generated by the model. This is used for multi-turn conversations.
For non-multi-turn conversations, this field can be left blank or unset. parts Part[] A list of ordered parts that make up a single message. Different parts may have different IANA MIME types.

docs.title: Part
docs.text:
A data type containing media that is part of a multi-part Content message.

Parameter Type Description text Optional: string A text prompt or code snippet. inline_data Optional: Blob Inline data in raw bytes. file_data Optional: FileData Data stored in a file.

docs.title: Blob
docs.text:
A content blob. If possible, send this as text rather than raw bytes.

Parameter Type Description mime_type string IANA MIME type of the data. data bytes Raw bytes.

docs.title: FileData
docs.text:
URI-based data.

Parameter Type Description mime_type string IANA MIME type of the data. file_uri string The Cloud Storage URI to the file storing the data.

docs.title: system_instruction
docs.text:
This field is for user-provided system_instructions. It is the same as contents but with limited support of content types.

Parameter Type Description role string The role for the system instruction. This field is required, but its value is ignored by the model. parts Part Text-only instructions that users want to pass to the model.

docs.title: Count tokens from a text prompt
docs.text:
This example counts the tokens of a single text prompt.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

RESTGoogle AI SDK for PythonGoogle AI SDK for GoGoogle AI SDK for Node.jsGoogle AI SDK for Java

To get the token count and the number of billable characters for a prompt by using the Vertex AI API, send a POST request to the publisher model endpoint.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • LOCATION: The region to process the request. ??? "Click to expand a partial list of available regions" * us-central1 * us-west4 * northamerica-northeast1 * us-east4 * us-west1 * asia-northeast3 * asia-southeast1 * asia-northeast1
  • PROJECT_ID: Your project ID.
  • MODEL_ID: The model ID of the multimodal model that you want to use.
  • ROLE: The role in a conversation associated with the content. Specifying a role is required even in single-turn use cases. Acceptable values include:
    • USER: Specifies content that's sent by you.
  • TEXT: The text instructions to include in the prompt.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:countTokens

Request JSON body:

{
  "contents": [{
    "role": "ROLE",
    "parts": [{
      "text": "TEXT"
    }]
  }]
}

To send your request, choose one of these options:

curl

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \  
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \  
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \  
     -d @request.json \  
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:countTokens"

PowerShell

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token  
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }  

Invoke-WebRequest `  
    -Method POST `  
    -Headers $headers `  
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `  
    -InFile request.json `  
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:countTokens" | Select-Object -Expand Content

You should receive a JSON response similar to the following.

Response

{
  "totalTokens": 31,
  "totalBillableCharacters": 96,
  "promptTokensDetails": [
    {
      "modality": "TEXT",
      "tokenCount": 31
    }
  ]
}

client = genai.Client(http_options=HttpOptions(api_version="v1"))

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "io"

    genai "google.golang.org/genai"
)

// countWithTxt shows how to count tokens with text input.
func countWithTxt(w io.Writer) error {
    ctx := context.Background()

    client, err := genai.NewClient(ctx, &genai.ClientConfig{
        HTTPOptions: genai.HTTPOptions{APIVersion: "v1"},
    })
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to create genai client: %w", err)
    }

    modelName := "gemini-2.0-flash-001"
    contents := []*genai.Content{
        {Parts: []*genai.Part{
            {Text: "What's the highest mountain in Africa?"},
        }},
    }

    resp, err := client.Models.CountTokens(ctx, modelName, contents, nil)
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate content: %w", err)
    }

    fmt.Fprintf(w, "Total: %d\nCached: %d\n", resp.TotalTokens, resp.CachedContentTokenCount)

    // Example response:
    // Total: 9
    // Cached: 0

    return nil
}

public class CountTokensWithText {

  public static void main(String[] args) {
    // TODO(developer): Replace these variables before running the sample.

  public static Optional<Integer> countTokens(String modelId) {

docs.title: Count tokens from a media prompt
docs.text:
This example counts the tokens of a prompt that uses various media types.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

RESTGoogle AI SDK for PythonGoogle AI SDK for GoGoogle AI SDK for Node.jsGoogle AI SDK for Java

To get the token count and the number of billable characters for a prompt by using the Vertex AI API, send a POST request to the publisher model endpoint.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • LOCATION: The region to process the request. ??? "Click to expand a partial list of available regions" * us-central1 * us-west4 * northamerica-northeast1 * us-east4 * us-west1 * asia-northeast3 * asia-southeast1 * asia-northeast1
  • PROJECT_ID: Your project ID.
  • MODEL_ID: The model ID of the multimodal model that you want to use.
  • ROLE: The role in a conversation associated with the content. Specifying a role is required even in single-turn use cases. Acceptable values include:
    • USER: Specifies content that's sent by you.
  • TEXT: The text instructions to include in the prompt.
  • FILE_URI: The URI or URL of the file to include in the prompt. Acceptable values include:
    • Cloud Storage bucket URI: The object must either be publicly readable or reside in the same Google Cloud project that's sending the request. For gemini-2.0-flash and gemini-2.0-flash-lite, the size limit is 2 GB.
    • HTTP URL: The file URL must be publicly readable. You can specify one video file, one audio file, and up to 10 image files per request. Audio files, video files, and documents can't exceed 15 MB.
    • YouTube video URL: The YouTube video must be either owned by the account that you used to sign in to the Google Cloud console or is public. Only one YouTube video URL is supported per request.
  • MIME_TYPE: The media type of the file specified in the data or fileUri fields. ??? "Click to expand MIME types" * application/pdf * audio/mpeg * audio/mp3 * audio/wav * image/png * image/jpeg * image/webp * text/plain * video/mov * video/mpeg * video/mp4 * video/mpg * video/avi * video/wmv * video/mpegps * video/flv

docs.title: Gen AI evaluation service API
docs.text:
The Gen AI evaluation service lets you evaluate your large language models (LLMs) across several metrics with your own criteria. You can provide inference-time inputs, LLM responses, and additional parameters, and the Gen AI evaluation service returns metrics specific to the evaluation task.

Metrics include model-based metrics, such as PointwiseMetric and PairwiseMetric, and in-memory computed metrics, such as rouge, bleu, and tool function-call metrics. PointwiseMetric and PairwiseMetric are generic model-based metrics that you can customize with your own criteria. Because the service takes the prediction results directly from models as input, the evaluation service can perform both inference and subsequent evaluation on all models supported by Vertex AI.

For more information on evaluating a model, see Gen AI evaluation service overview.

Concepts
  • Pointwise Metric: Evaluates a single model response based on a given prompt, context, and instructions.
  • Pairwise Metric: Compares two model responses to determine which one is better according to the evaluation criteria.
  • ROUGE (Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation): A metric for evaluating automatic summarization by comparing an automatically produced summary against a reference summary.
  • BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy): A metric for evaluating the quality of text which has been machine-translated from one natural language to another.
  • COMET (Cross-lingual Optimized Metric for Evaluation of Translation): A neural framework for training multilingual machine translation evaluation models.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
The following are limitations of the evaluation service:

  • The evaluation service may have a propagation delay in your first call.
  • Most model-based metrics consume gemini-1.0-pro quota because the Gen AI evaluation service leverages gemini-1.0-pro as the underlying judge model to compute these model-based metrics.
  • Some model-based metrics, such as MetricX and COMET, use different machine learning models, so they don't consume gemini-1.0-pro quota.

Preview

MetricX and COMET will not be charged during Preview. At GA, the pricing will be the same as all pointwise model-based metrics.

docs.title: API Request Structure
docs.text:
You can send an evaluation call to the evaluateInstances endpoint using curl or the Python client libraries.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

cURLPython 
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://${LOCATION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/${LOCATION}:evaluateInstances \
  -d '{
    "pointwise_metric_input" : {
      "metric_spec" : {
        ...
      },
      "instance": {
        ...
      },
    }
  }'

import json

from google import auth
from google.api_core import exceptions
from google.auth.transport import requests as google_auth_requests

creds, _ = auth.default(
    scopes=['https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform'])

data = {
  # Metric input data, e.g., "pointwise_metric_input": { ... }
}

uri = f'https://${LOCATION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/${LOCATION}:evaluateInstances'
result = google_auth_requests.AuthorizedSession(creds).post(uri, json=data)

print(json.dumps(result.json(), indent=2))

docs.title: Evaluation Metrics
docs.text:
The evaluation service provides a variety of metrics to assess different aspects of model performance. Use the following table to choose the best metric for your use case.

Metric Category Metric Name Use Case Computed Metrics exact_match Assess if the prediction matches the reference exactly. bleu Compute BLEU score by comparing the prediction against a reference, typically for translation quality. rouge Compute ROUGE scores for summarization quality by comparing the prediction against a reference. Model-Based Pointwise Metrics fluency Assess a single response's grammatical correctness and readability. coherence Assess if a single response is logical and easy to follow. safety Assess a single response's level of safety. groundedness Assess if a response is based only on information provided in the context. fulfillment Assess how completely a response fulfills the instructions in a prompt. summarization_quality Assess the overall quality of a summary. summarization_helpfulness Assess if a summary contains the necessary details to substitute the original text. summarization_verbosity Assess if a summary is succinct. question_answering_quality Assess the overall ability to answer questions based on a given context. question_answering_relevance Assess if a response provides relevant information to answer a question. question_answering_helpfulness Assess if a response provides key details when answering a question. question_answering_correctness Assess if a response correctly answers a question. pointwise_metric Define a custom metric to evaluate a single response using a prompt template. comet Evaluate translation quality using the COMET model. metricx Evaluate translation quality using the MetricX model. Model-Based Pairwise Metrics pairwise_summarization_quality Compare two responses to determine which provides a better quality summary. pairwise_question_answering_quality Compare two responses to determine which provides a better quality answer. pairwise_metric Define a custom metric to compare two responses using a prompt template. Tool Call Metrics tool_call_valid Assess if a response predicts a valid tool call. tool_name_match Assess if a response predicts a tool call with the correct tool name. tool_parameter_key_match Assess if a response predicts a tool call with the correct parameter names. tool_parameter_kv_match Assess if a response predicts a tool call with the correct parameter names and values.

docs.title: Metric Details
docs.text:
Expand the following sections to view the specific input and output formats for each metric.

Exact Match

Input (ExactMatchInput) 

{
  "exact_match_input": {
    "metric_spec": {},
    "instances": [
      {
        "prediction": string,
        "reference": string
      }
    ]
  }
}
| Parameter | Description | |---|---| | metric_spec | Optional: ExactMatchSpec. Metric spec, defining the metric's behavior. | | instances | Optional: ExactMatchInstance[]. Evaluation input, consisting of LLM response and reference. | | instances.prediction | Optional: string. LLM response. | | instances.reference | Optional: string. Golden LLM response for reference. |

Result (ExactMatchResults) 

{
  "exact_match_results": {
    "exact_match_metric_values": [
      {
        "score": float
      }
    ]
  }
}
| Field | Description | |---|---| | exact_match_metric_values | ExactMatchMetricValue[]. Evaluation results per instance input. | | exact_match_metric_values.score | float. 1 for an exact match, 0 otherwise. |

BLEU

Input (BleuInput) 

{
  "bleu_input": {
    "metric_spec": {
      "use_effective_order": bool
    },
    "instances": [
      {
        "prediction": string,
        "reference": string
      }
    ]
  }
}
| Parameter | Description | |---|---| | metric_spec | Optional: BleuSpec. Metric spec, defining the metric's behavior. | | metric_spec.use_effective_order | Optional: bool. Whether to take into account n-gram orders without any match. | | instances | Optional: BleuInstance[]. Evaluation input, consisting of LLM response and reference. | | instances.prediction | Optional: string. LLM response. | | instances.reference | Optional: string. Golden LLM response for reference. |

Result (BleuResults) 

{
  "bleu_results": {
    "bleu_metric_values": [
      {
        "score": float
      }
    ]
  }
}
| Field | Description | |---|---| | bleu_metric_values | BleuMetricValue[]. Evaluation results per instance input. | | bleu_metric_values.score | float. Score between [0, 1], where higher scores mean the prediction is more like the reference. |

ROUGE

Input (RougeInput) 

{
  "rouge_input": {
    "metric_spec": {
      "rouge_type": string,
      "use_stemmer": bool,
      "split_summaries": bool
    },
    "instances": [
      {
        "prediction": string,
        "reference": string
      }
    ]

docs.title: Evaluate an output
docs.text:
The following example demonstrates how to evaluate the output of an LLM using a variety of pointwise metrics.

PythonGo 
import pandas as pd

import vertexai
from vertexai.preview.evaluation import EvalTask, MetricPromptTemplateExamples

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below line
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

eval_dataset = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "instruction": [
            "Summarize the text in one sentence.",
            "Summarize the text such that a five-year-old can understand.",
        ],
        "context": [
            """As part of a comprehensive initiative to tackle urban congestion and foster
            sustainable urban living, a major city has revealed ambitious plans for an
            extensive overhaul of its public transportation system. The project aims not
            only to improve the efficiency and reliability of public transit but also to
            reduce the city\'s carbon footprint and promote eco-friendly commuting options.
            City officials anticipate that this strategic investment will enhance
            accessibility for residents and visitors alike, ushering in a new era of
            efficient, environmentally conscious urban transportation.""",
            """A team of archaeologists has unearthed ancient artifacts shedding light on a
            previously unknown civilization. The findings challenge existing historical
            narratives and provide valuable insights into human history.""",
        ],
        "response": [
            "A major city is revamping its public transportation system to fight congestion, reduce emissions, and make getting around greener and easier.",
            "Some people who dig for old things found some very special tools and objects that tell us about people who lived a long, long time ago! What they found is like a new puzzle piece that helps us understand how people used to live.",
        ],
    }
)

eval_task = EvalTask(
    dataset=eval_dataset,
    metrics=[
        MetricPromptTemplateExamples.Pointwise.SUMMARIZATION_QUALITY,
        MetricPromptTemplateExamples.Pointwise.GROUNDEDNESS,
        MetricPromptTemplateExamples.Pointwise.VERBOSITY,
        MetricPromptTemplateExamples.Pointwise.INSTRUCTION_FOLLOWING,
    ],
)

prompt_template = (
    "Instruction: {instruction}. Article: {context}. Summary: {response}"
)
result = eval_task.evaluate(prompt_template=prompt_template)

print("Summary Metrics:\n")

for key, value in result.summary_metrics.items():
    print(f"{key}: \t{value}")

print("\n\nMetrics Table:\n")
print(result.metrics_table)
# Example response:

# row_count:      2

import (
    context_pkg "context"
    "fmt"
    "io"

    aiplatform "cloud.google.com/go/aiplatform/apiv1beta1"
    aiplatformpb "cloud.google.com/go/aiplatform/apiv1beta1/aiplatformpb"
    "google.golang.org/api/option"
)

// evaluateModelResponse evaluates the output of an LLM for groundedness, i.e., how well
// the model response connects with verifiable sources of information
func evaluateModelResponse(w io.Writer, projectID, location string) error {
    // location = "us-central1"
    ctx := context_pkg.Background()
    apiEndpoint := fmt.Sprintf("%s-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443", location)
    client, err := aiplatform.NewEvaluationClient(ctx, option.WithEndpoint(apiEndpoint))

    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("unable to create aiplatform client: %w", err)
    }
    defer client.Close()

    // evaluate the pre-generated model response against the reference (ground truth)
    responseToEvaluate := `
The city is undertaking a major project to revamp its public transportation system.
This initiative is designed to improve efficiency, reduce carbon emissions, and promote
eco-friendly commuting. The city expects that this investment will enhance accessibility
and usher in a new era of sustainable urban transportation.
`
    reference := `
As part of a comprehensive initiative to tackle urban congestion and foster
sustainable urban living, a major city has revealed ambitious plans for an
extensive overhaul of its public transportation system. The project aims not
only to improve the efficiency and reliability of public transit but also to
reduce the city\'s carbon footprint and promote eco-friendly commuting options.
City officials anticipate that this strategic investment will enhance
accessibility for residents and visitors alike, ushering in a new era of
efficient, environmentally conscious urban transportation.
`
    req := aiplatformpb.EvaluateInstancesRequest{
        Location: fmt.Sprintf("projects/%s/locations/%s", projectID, location),
        // Check the API reference for a full list of supported metric inputs:
        // https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/reference/rpc/google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1#evaluateinstancesrequest
        MetricInputs: &aiplatformpb.EvaluateInstancesRequest_GroundednessInput{
            GroundednessInput: &aiplatformpb.GroundednessInput{
                MetricSpec: &aiplatformpb.GroundednessSpec{},
                Instance: &aiplatformpb.GroundednessInstance{
                    Context:    &reference,
                    Prediction: &responseToEvaluate,
                },
            },
        },
    }

    resp, err := client.EvaluateInstances(ctx, &req)
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("evaluateInstances failed: %v", err)
    }

    results := resp.GetGroundednessResult()
    fmt.Fprintf(w, "score: %.2f\n", results.GetScore())
    fmt.Fprintf(w, "confidence: %.2f\n", results.GetConfidence())
    fmt.Fprintf(w, "explanation:\n%s\n", results.GetExplanation())
    // Example response:
    // score: 1.00
    // confidence: 1.00
    // explanation:
    // STEP 1: All aspects of the response are found in the context.
    // The response accurately summarizes the city's plan to overhaul its public transportation system, highlighting the goals of ...
    // STEP 2: According to the rubric, the response is scored 1 because all aspects of the response are attributable to the context.

    return nil
}

docs.title: Function calling reference
docs.text:
Function calling improves the ability of a large language model (LLM) to provide relevant and contextual answers.

You can provide custom functions to a generative AI model with the Function Calling API. The model doesn't directly invoke these functions. Instead, it generates structured data output that specifies the function name and suggested arguments. This output enables the calling of external APIs or information systems such as databases, customer relationship management systems, and document repositories. The resulting API output can then be provided back to the LLM to improve the quality of its response.

For more conceptual documentation on function calling, see Function calling.

Concepts
  • Function Calling: A feature that allows a large language model (LLM) to request the invocation of external tools or functions during a conversation.
  • FunctionDeclaration: A definition of a custom function's signature, including its name, parameters, and a description of what it does, which the model uses to understand how to call it.
  • Schema: A structured definition, typically in JSON Schema format, that describes the expected data types and format for a function's parameters and response.
  • OpenAPI 3.0: A standard, language-agnostic specification for describing RESTful APIs, which can be used to define the schema for function declarations.

docs.title: Supported models
docs.text:
• Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite > Preview
  • Gemini 2.5 Flash with Live API native audio > Preview
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash with Live API > Preview

  • Gemini 2.5 Pro

Limitations:

docs.title: Parameter list
docs.text: This section describes the parameters for a function call request.

docs.title: FunctionDeclaration
docs.text:
Defines a function that the model can generate JSON inputs for based on OpenAPI 3.0 specifications.

Parameter Type Description name string The name of the function to call. Must start with a letter or an underscore. Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain underscores, dots, or dashes, with a maximum length of 64. description Optional: string The description and purpose of the function. The model uses this to decide how and whether to call the function. For the best results, we recommend that you include a description. parameters Optional: Schema Describes the parameters of the function in the OpenAPI JSON Schema Object format: OpenAPI 3.0 specification. response Optional: Schema Describes the output from the function in the OpenAPI JSON Schema Object format: OpenAPI 3.0 specification.

For more information, see Function calling.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
Defines the format of the input and output data in a function call based on the OpenAPI 3.0 Schema specification.

Parameter Type Description type string Enum. The type of the data. Must be one of: STRING, INTEGER, BOOLEAN, NUMBER, ARRAY, OBJECT. description Optional: string Description of the data. enum Optional: string[] Possible values of the element of primitive type with enum format. items Optional: Schema[] Schema of the elements of Type.ARRAY. properties Optional: Schema Schema of the properties of Type.OBJECT. required Optional: string[] Required properties of Type.OBJECT. nullable Optional: bool Indicates if the value may be null.

docs.title: FunctionCallingConfig
docs.text:
The FunctionCallingConfig controls the behavior of the model and determines what type of function to call.

Parameter Type Description mode Optional: enum/string[]
  • AUTO: Default model behavior. The model can make predictions in either a function call form or a natural language response form. The model decides which form to use based on the context.
  • NONE: The model doesn't make any predictions in the form of function calls.
  • ANY: The model is constrained to always predict a function call. If allowed_function_names is not provided, the model picks from all of the available function declarations. If allowed_function_names is provided, the model picks from the set of allowed functions.
allowed_function_names Optional: string[] Function names to call. Only set when the mode is ANY. Function names should match [FunctionDeclaration.name]. With mode set to ANY, the model will predict a function call from the set of function names provided.

docs.title: functionCall
docs.text:
A predicted functionCall returned from the model that contains a string representing the functionDeclaration.name and a structured JSON object containing the parameters and their values.

Parameter Type Description name string The name of the function to call. args Struct The function parameters and values in JSON object format. See Function calling for parameter details.

docs.title: functionResponse
docs.text:
The resulting output from a FunctionCall that contains a string representing the FunctionDeclaration.name. Also contains a structured JSON object with the output from the function (and uses it as context for the model). This should contain the result of a FunctionCall made based on model prediction.

Parameter Type Description name string The name of the function to call. response Struct The function response in JSON object format.

docs.title: Send a function declaration
docs.text:
The following examples show how to send a query and a function declaration to the model.

Vertex AI API (REST)Vertex AI API (Python)Vertex AI API (Node.js)Vertex AI API (Java)Vertex AI API (Go)OpenAI API (REST)OpenAI API (Python)

The following curl command demonstrates how to send a prompt and a function declaration to the model.

Before using the request data, make the following replacements: * myproject: Your project ID. * us-central1: The location of your project. * gemini-2.5-flash: The model ID to use.

PROJECT_ID=myproject
LOCATION=us-central1
MODEL_ID=gemini-2.5-flash

curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://"${LOCATION}"-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/"${PROJECT_ID}"/locations/"${LOCATION}"/publishers/google/models/"${MODEL_ID}":generateContent \
  -d '{
    "contents": [{
      "role": "user",
      "parts": [{
        "text": "What is the weather in Boston?"
      }]
    }],
    "tools": [{
      "functionDeclarations": [
        {
          "name": "get_current_weather",
          "description": "Get the current weather in a given location",
          "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
              "location": {
                "type": "string",
                "description": "The city and state, e.g. San Francisco, CA or a zip code e.g. 95616"
              }
            },
            "required": [
              "location"
            ]
          }
        }
      ]
    }]
  }'

from google import genai
from google.genai.types import GenerateContentConfig, HttpOptions

def get_current_weather(location: str) -> str:
    """Example method. Returns the current weather.

    Args:
        location: The city and state, e.g. San Francisco, CA
    """
    weather_map: dict[str, str] = {
        "Boston, MA": "snowing",
        "San Francisco, CA": "foggy",
        "Seattle, WA": "raining",
        "Austin, TX": "hot",
        "Chicago, IL": "windy",
    }
    return weather_map.get(location, "unknown")

client = genai.Client(http_options=HttpOptions(api_version="v1"))
model_id = "gemini-2.0-flash-001"

response = client.models.generate_content(
    model=model_id,
