docs.title: Manage encryption with CMEK
docs.text:
By default, all user data within RagManagedDb is encrypted using a Google-owned and Google-managed encryption key. If you require more control over your encryption keys, Vertex AI RAG Engine supports customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK). With CMEK, you can use your own cryptographic keys, managed within Cloud Key Management Service (KMS), to protect your RAG corpus data.

For information on CMEK limitations for RAG corpora, see CMEK limitations for Vertex AI RAG Engine.

Set up your KMS key and grant permissions

Before you can create a CMEK-enabled RAG corpus, you must set up a cryptographic key in Cloud KMS and grant the Vertex AI RAG Engine service agent permission to use it. To perform these steps, your user account needs the Cloud KMS Admin role (roles/cloudkms.admin).

1. Enable the Cloud KMS API

  1. In the Google Cloud console, select your project.
  2. In the search bar, type "Key Management" and select the Key Management service.
  3. If the API isn't enabled, click Enable.

2. Create your KMS key ring and key

  1. In the Key Management section, click Create Key Ring.
    • Key ring name: Enter a unique name (e.g., rag-engine-cmek-keys).
    • Location type: Select Region.
    • Location: Choose a region (e.g., us-central1). This should match the region of your RAG Engine resources.
  2. Click Create.
  3. After the key ring is created, click Create Key.
    • Key name: Enter a unique name (e.g., my-rag-corpus-key).
    • Protection level: Choose Software or HSM.
    • Purpose: Select Symmetric encrypt/decrypt.
    • Key material source: Select Generated key.
    • Rotation period: (Optional but recommended) Configure a key rotation schedule.
  4. Click Create.

3. Copy the key resource name

  1. After the key is created, navigate to its details page.
  2. Locate the resource name, which has the format projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/locations/YOUR_REGION/keyRings/YOUR_KEY_RING_NAME/cryptoKeys/YOUR_KEY_NAME/cryptoKeyVersions/1.
  3. Copy the resource name and remove the version number at the end (/cryptoKeyVersions/VERSION_NUMBER). The correctly formatted name is projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/locations/YOUR_REGION/keyRings/YOUR_KEY_RING_NAME/cryptoKeys/YOUR_KEY_NAME.

4. Grant permissions to the Vertex AI RAG Engine service agent

  1. Navigate to the IAM & Admin > IAM page in the Google Cloud console.
  2. Enable the Include Google-provided role grants checkbox.
  3. In the filter bar, search for the Vertex AI RAG Engine service agent, which follows the pattern service-YOUR_PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-vertex-rag.iam.gserviceaccount.com.
  4. Go back to the Key Management service, select your key ring, and then select your key.
  5. In the key's details page, go to the Permissions tab and click Add Principal.
  6. In the New principals field, enter the service agent's email address.
  7. In the Select a role drop-down, select Cloud KMS CryptoKey Encrypter/Decrypter (roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter).
  8. Click Save.

docs.text:

docs.title: Use Vertex AI Search as a retrieval backend using Vertex AI RAG Engine
docs.text:
This page introduces Vertex AI Search integration with the Vertex AI RAG Engine.

Vertex AI Search provides a solution for retrieving and managing data within your Vertex AI RAG applications. By using Vertex AI Search as your retrieval backend, you can improve performance, scalability, and ease of integration.

  • Enhanced performance and scalability: Vertex AI Search is designed to handle large volumes of data with exceptionally low latency. This translates to faster response times and improved performance for your RAG applications, especially when dealing with complex or extensive knowledge bases.
  • Simplified data management: Import your data from various sources, such as websites, BigQuery datasets, and Cloud Storage buckets, that can streamline your data ingestion process.
  • Seamless integration: Vertex AI provides built-in integration with Vertex AI Search, which lets you select Vertex AI Search as the corpus backend for your RAG application. This simplifies the integration process and helps to ensure optimal compatibility between components.
  • Improved LLM output quality: The retrieval capabilities of Vertex AI Search help ensure your RAG application retrieves the most relevant information from your corpus, which leads to more accurate and informative LLM-generated outputs.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Before you begin

Concepts

  • Vertex AI RAG Engine: A tool that enhances generative AI models by retrieving information from specified knowledge bases to provide more factual and relevant answers.
  • Vertex AI Search: A managed service that provides Google-quality search capabilities on your own data for use in applications.
  • RAG Corpus: A collection of documents or data that the RAG Engine uses as a knowledge base for retrieving information.
  • Large Language Model (LLM): A type of artificial intelligence model trained on vast amounts of text data to understand and generate human-like language.

Prerequisites

To use Vertex AI Search as a retrieval backend, you must first configure it. For detailed instructions, see the Vertex AI Search documentation.

  1. Create a search data store.
  2. Create a search application.

Security

Note

The VPC-SC security controls and CMEK are supported by Vertex AI RAG Engine. Data residency and AXT security controls aren't supported.

Try the notebook tutorial

docs.title: Use Vertex AI Vector Search with Vertex AI RAG Engine
docs.text:
The VPC-SC security controls and CMEK are supported by Vertex AI RAG Engine. Data residency and AXT security controls aren't supported.

This page shows you how to connect your Vertex AI RAG Engine to Vertex AI Vector Search.

To see a complete example, you can run the "RAG Engine with Vector Search" Jupyter notebook in one of the following environments:

Open in Colab Open in Colab Enterprise Open in Vertex AI Workbench View on GitHub

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): A technique that enhances large language model (LLM) responses by first retrieving relevant information from an external knowledge base and providing it as context to the LLM.
  • Vertex AI RAG Engine: A managed service that orchestrates the RAG workflow, connecting language models with your data sources to deliver more factual and relevant answers.
  • Vertex AI Vector Search: A high-performance service for finding the most semantically similar items to a given query from a large dataset of vectors.
  • Embeddings: Numerical vector representations of data like text or images, where similar items are located closer to each other in the vector space.
  • Vector Search Index: A data structure in Vector Search that organizes vectors to enable fast and efficient similarity searches.
Prerequisites

Set up the Vertex AI SDK

To learn how to install or update the Vertex AI SDK for Python, see Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python. For more information, see the Vertex AI SDK for Python API reference documentation.

Authenticate to Vertex AI

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Connect RAG Engine to Vertex AI Vector Search

docs.title: Step 1: Set up Vertex AI Vector Search
docs.text: Vertex AI Vector Search is built on the same technology that powers Google Search, YouTube, and Google Play. To integrate with RAG Engine, you need to set up an empty Vector Search index first.

docs.title: Create a Vector Search index
docs.text:
To be compatible with your RAG Corpus, the Vector Search index must meet the following criteria:

  1. IndexUpdateMethod must be STREAM_UPDATE.
  2. The distance measure type must be DOT_PRODUCT_DISTANCE or COSINE_DISTANCE.
  3. The vector dimension must be consistent with the embedding model you plan to use in the RAG corpus.
Python 
def vector_search_create_streaming_index(
    project: str, location: str, display_name: str, gcs_uri: Optional[str] = None
) -> aiplatform.MatchingEngineIndex:
    """Create a vector search index.

    Args:
        project (str): Required. Project ID
        location (str): Required. The region name
        display_name (str): Required. The index display name
        gcs_uri (str): Optional. The Google Cloud Storage uri for index content

    Returns:
        The created MatchingEngineIndex.
    """
    # Initialize the Vertex AI client
    aiplatform.init(project=project, location=location)

    # Create Index
    index = aiplatform.MatchingEngineIndex.create_tree_ah_index(
        display_name=display_name,
        contents_delta_uri=gcs_uri,
        description="Matching Engine Index",
        dimensions=100,
        approximate_neighbors_count=150,
        leaf_node_embedding_count=500,
        leaf_nodes_to_search_percent=7,
        index_update_method="STREAM_UPDATE",  # Options: STREAM_UPDATE, BATCH_UPDATE
        distance_measure_type=aiplatform.matching_engine.matching_engine_index_config.DistanceMeasureType.DOT_PRODUCT_DISTANCE,
    )

    return index

docs.title: Create a Vector Search index endpoint
docs.text:
Vertex AI RAG Engine supports public endpoints.

Python 
def vector_search_create_index_endpoint(
    project: str, location: str, display_name: str
) -> None:
    """Create a vector search index endpoint.

    Args:
        project (str): Required. Project ID
        location (str): Required. The region name
        display_name (str): Required. The index endpoint display name
    """
    # Initialize the Vertex AI client
    aiplatform.init(project=project, location=location)

    # Create Index Endpoint
    index_endpoint = aiplatform.MatchingEngineIndexEndpoint.create(
        display_name=display_name,
        public_endpoint_enabled=True,
        description="Matching Engine Index Endpoint",
    )

    print(index_endpoint.name)

docs.title: Deploy an index to an index endpoint
docs.text:
Before you can perform a nearest neighbor search, you must deploy the index to an index endpoint.

Python 
def vector_search_deploy_index(
    project: str,
    location: str,
    index_name: str,
    index_endpoint_name: str,
    deployed_index_id: str,
) -> None:
    """Deploy a vector search index to a vector search index endpoint.

    Args:
        project (str): Required. Project ID
        location (str): Required. The region name
        index_name (str): Required. The index to update. A fully-qualified index
          resource name or a index ID.  Example:
          "projects/123/locations/us-central1/indexes/my_index_id" or
          "my_index_id".
        index_endpoint_name (str): Required. Index endpoint to deploy the index
          to.
        deployed_index_id (str): Required. The user specified ID of the
          DeployedIndex.
    """
    # Initialize the Vertex AI client
    aiplatform.init(project=project, location=location)

    # Create the index instance from an existing index
    index = aiplatform.MatchingEngineIndex(index_name=index_name)

    # Create the index endpoint instance from an existing endpoint.
    index_endpoint = aiplatform.MatchingEngineIndexEndpoint(
        index_endpoint_name=index_endpoint_name
    )

    # Deploy Index to Endpoint
    index_endpoint = index_endpoint.deploy_index(
        index=index, deployed_index_id=deployed_index_id
    )

    print(index_endpoint.deployed_indexes)

If it's the first time you're deploying an index to an index endpoint, it takes approximately 30 minutes to build and initiate the backend. Subsequent deployments are much faster. To see the status of the index deployment, go to the Vector Search Console, select the Index endpoints tab, and choose your index endpoint.

Go to the Vector Search Console

Identify the resource name of your index and index endpoint, which have the following formats:

  • projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/${LOCATION_ID}/indexes/${INDEX_ID}
  • projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/${LOCATION_ID}/indexEndpoints/${INDEX_ENDPOINT_ID}

docs.title: Step 2: Use Vector Search in a RAG application
docs.text: After the Vector Search instance is set up, follow these steps to use it as the vector database for your RAG application.

docs.title: Create a RAG corpus
docs.text:
When you create the RAG corpus, specify the full INDEX_ENDPOINT_NAME and INDEX_NAME. The RAG corpus is automatically associated with the Vector Search index. If validation requirements aren't met, the request is rejected.

PythonREST 
from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# vector_search_index_name = "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/{LOCATION}/indexes/{INDEX_ID}"
# vector_search_index_endpoint_name = "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/{LOCATION}/indexEndpoints/{INDEX_ENDPOINT_ID}"
# display_name = "test_corpus"
# description = "Corpus Description"

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

# Configure embedding model (Optional)
embedding_model_config = rag.RagEmbeddingModelConfig(
    vertex_prediction_endpoint=rag.VertexPredictionEndpoint(
        publisher_model="publishers/google/models/text-embedding-005"
    )
)

# Configure Vector DB
vector_db = rag.VertexVectorSearch(
    index=vector_search_index_name, index_endpoint=vector_search_index_endpoint_name
)

corpus = rag.create_corpus(
    display_name=display_name,
    description=description,
    backend_config=rag.RagVectorDbConfig(
        rag_embedding_model_config=embedding_model_config,
        vector_db=vector_db,
    ),
)
print(corpus)

# RagCorpus(name='projects/1234567890/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/1234567890',
# display_name='test_corpus', description='Corpus Description', embedding_model_config=...
# ...

docs.title: Import files
docs.text:
Use the ImportRagFiles API to import files from Cloud Storage or Google Drive. The files are chunked, embedded, and stored in the Vector Search index.

PythonREST 
from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# corpus_name = "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/{rag_corpus_id}"
# paths = ["https://drive.google.com/file/123", "gs://my_bucket/my_files_dir"]  # Supports Google Cloud Storage and Google Drive Links

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

response = rag.import_files(
    corpus_name=corpus_name,
    paths=paths,
    transformation_config=rag.TransformationConfig(
        rag.ChunkingConfig(chunk_size=512, chunk_overlap=100)
    ),
    import_result_sink="gs://sample-existing-folder/sample_import_result_unique.ndjson",  # Optional, this has to be an existing storage bucket folder, and file name has to be unique (non-existent).
    max_embedding_requests_per_min=900,  # Optional
)
print(f"Imported {response.imported_rag_files_count} files.")
# Example response:
# Imported 2 files.

# TODO(developer): Update and uncomment the following lines:
# RAG_CORPUS_ID = "your-rag-corpus-id"
#
# Google Cloud Storage bucket/file location.
# For example, "gs://rag-fos-test/"
# GCS_URIS= "your-gcs-uris"

# Call ImportRagFiles API to embed files and store in the BigQuery table
curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/${RAG_CORPUS_ID}/ragFiles:import \
-d '{
  "import_rag_files_config": {
    "gcs_source": {
      "uris": '\""${GCS_URIS}"\"'
    },
    "rag_file_chunking_config": {
      "chunk_size": 512
    }
  }
}'

# Call ListRagFiles API to verify the files are imported successfully
curl -X GET \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/${RAG_CORPUS_ID}/ragFiles

docs.title: Generate content
docs.text:
To generate content using Gemini models, call the Vertex AI GenerateContent API. By specifying the RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE in the request, the API automatically retrieves data from the Vector Search index to augment the generation.

PythonREST 
from vertexai import rag
from vertexai.generative_models import GenerativeModel, Tool
import vertexai

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# corpus_name = "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/{rag_corpus_id}"

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

rag_retrieval_tool = Tool.from_retrieval(
    retrieval=rag.Retrieval(
        source=rag.VertexRagStore(
            rag_resources=[
                rag.RagResource(
                    rag_corpus=corpus_name,
                    # Optional: supply IDs from `rag.list_files()`.
                    # rag_file_ids=["rag-file-1", "rag-file-2", ...],
                )
            ],
            rag_retrieval_config=rag.RagRetrievalConfig(
                top_k=10,
                filter=rag.utils.resources.Filter(vector_distance_threshold=0.5),
            ),
        ),
    )
)

rag_model = GenerativeModel(
    model_name="gemini-2.0-flash-001", tools=[rag_retrieval_tool]
)
response = rag_model.generate_content("Why is the sky blue?")
print(response.text)
# Example response:
#   The sky appears blue due to a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering.
#   Sunlight, which contains all colors of the rainbow, is scattered
#   by the tiny particles in the Earth's atmosphere....
#   ...

# TODO(developer): Update and uncomment the following lines:
# MODEL_ID=gemini-2.0-flash
# GENERATE_CONTENT_PROMPT="your-generate-content-prompt"

# GenerateContent with contexts retrieved from the FeatureStoreOnline index
curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json"  https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/${MODEL_ID}:generateContent \
-d '{
  "contents": {
    "role": "user",
    "parts": {
      "text": '\""${GENERATE_CONTENT_PROMPT}"\"'
    }
  },
  "tools": {
    "retrieval": {
      "vertex_rag_store": {
        "rag_resources": {
            "rag_corpus": '\""${RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE}"\"',
          },
        "similarity_top_k": 8,
        "vector_distance_threshold": 0.32
      }
    }
  }
}'

docs.title: Use a Weaviate database with Vertex AI RAG Engine
docs.text:
Preview

Some of the RAG features are Preview offerings, subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" of the Google Cloud Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA products and features may have limited support, and changes to Pre-GA products and features may not be compatible with other Pre-GA versions. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

Further, by using the Gemini API on Vertex AI, you agree to the Generative AI Preview terms and conditions (Preview Terms).

The VPC-SC security controls and CMEK are supported by Vertex AI RAG Engine. Data residency and AXT security controls aren't supported.

This page shows you how to connect your RAG Engine corpus to your Weaviate database. You can use your Weaviate database instance, which is an open-source database, with RAG Engine to index and conduct a vector-based similarity search.

To see an example of using RAG Engine with Weaviate, you can also follow along with the "RAG Engine with Weaviate" Jupyter notebook in one of the following environments:

Open in Colab Open in Colab Enterprise Open in Vertex AI Workbench View on GitHub

A similarity search finds pieces of text that are similar to your query, which requires the use of an embedding model. The embedding model produces vector data for each piece of text being compared. The similarity search is used to retrieve semantic contexts for grounding to return the most accurate content from your LLM.

With RAG Engine, you can continue to use your fully-managed vector database instance, which you are responsible for provisioning. RAG Engine uses the vector database for storage, index management, and search.

Create a Weaviate collection

Create a secret in Secret Manager

These samples show how to create a secret and add your Weaviate API key as a new version.

ConsoleREST APIPython
  1. Go to the Secret Manager page. Go to Secret Manager
  2. Click + Create Secret.
  3. Enter a Name for your secret (e.g., weaviate-api-key).
  4. In the Secret value field, enter your Weaviate API key.
  5. Click Create secret.
# TODO(developer): Update the variables.
SECRET_NAME="MyWeaviateApiKeySecret"
WEAVIATE_API_KEY="example-api-key"

# Create a secret in SecretManager.
curl "https://secretmanager.googleapis.com/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/secrets?secretId=${SECRET_NAME}" \
    --request "POST" \
    --header "authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
    --header "content-type: application/json" \
    --data "{\"replication\": {\"automatic\": {}}}"

# Encode your WEAVIATE_API_KEY using base 64.
SECRET_DATA=$(echo ${WEAVIATE_API_KEY} | base64)

# Create a new version of your secret which uses SECRET_DATA as payload
curl "https://secretmanager.googleapis.com/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/secrets/${SECRET_NAME}:addVersion" \
    --request "POST" \
    --header "authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
    --header "content-type: application/json" \
    --data "{\"payload\": {\"data\": \"${SECRET_DATA}\"}}"

# Import the Secret Manager client library.
from google.cloud import secretmanager
from typing import Optional
import google_crc32c  # type: ignore


def create_secret(
    project_id: str, secret_id: str
) -> secretmanager.Secret:
    """
    Create a new secret with the given name.
    """
    client = secretmanager.SecretManagerServiceClient()
    parent = f"projects/{project_id}"
    response = client.create_secret(
        request={
            "parent": parent,
            "secret_id": secret_id,
            "secret": {"replication": {"automatic": {}}},
        }
    )
    print(f"Created secret: {response.name}")
    return response

def add_secret_version(
    project_id: str, secret_id: str, payload: str
) -> secretmanager.SecretVersion:
    """
    Add a new secret version to the given secret with the provided payload.
    """
    client = secretmanager.SecretManagerServiceClient()
    parent = client.secret_path(project_id, secret_id)
    payload_bytes = payload.encode("UTF-8")
    crc32c = google_crc32c.Checksum()
    crc32c.update(payload_bytes)
    response = client.add_secret_version(
        request={
            "parent": parent,
            "payload": {
                "data": payload_bytes,
                "data_crc32c": int(crc32c.hexdigest(), 16),
            },
        }
    )
    print(f"Added secret version: {response.name}")
    return response

docs.title: Step 2: Create a RAG corpus
docs.text:
Expand to see corpus creation steps and code

Create a RAG corpus and set the Weaviate instance as its vector database. When calling the CreateRagCorpus or UpdateRagCorpus APIs, you must specify the Weaviate configuration.

  • rag_vector_db_config.weaviate: Contains all Weaviate configuration fields.
  • weaviate.http_endpoint: The Weaviate endpoint. This is immutable once set.
  • weaviate.collection_name: The name of your Weaviate collection. This is immutable once set.
  • api_auth.api_key_config.api_key_secret_version: The resource name of the secret version in Secret Manager containing your Weaviate API key. This is mutable.

First-time corpus creation

If you are creating a RAG corpus for the first time in a project, the RAG Engine service account might not exist yet.

  1. Create a RAG corpus with an empty Weaviate configuration to trigger the creation of the service account (service-{project-number}@gcp-sa-vertex-rag.iam.gserviceaccount.com).
  2. Grant this new service account the Secret Manager Secret Accessor role as described in the "Before you begin" section.
  3. Call the UpdateRagCorpus API to update the corpus with your Weaviate endpoint, collection name, and API key secret version.

Subsequent corpus creation

If the service account already exists, you can create the RAG corpus with the full Weaviate configuration in a single CreateRagCorpus API call.

REST APIPython

docs.title: Step 4: Retrieve context and generate content
docs.text:
Expand to see retrieval and generation steps

Once your files are indexed, you can retrieve relevant contexts for a query and use them to ground a generative model.

Retrieve context

Search the RAG corpus to find information relevant to a user's query.

REST APIPython 
# Before using, replace the following:
# PROJECT_ID: Your project ID.
# LOCATION: The region to process the request (e.g., us-central1).
# RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE: The resource name of the RagCorpus (e.g., projects/{project}/locations/{location}/ragCorpora/{rag_corpus}).
# TEXT: The query text.

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d '{
         "parent": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION",
         "retrieval_query": {
           "text": "TEXT"
         },
         "vertex_rag_store": {
           "rag_resources": [{
             "rag_corpus": "RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE"
           }]
         }
       }' \
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION:retrieveContexts"

from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# corpus_name = "projects/[PROJECT_ID]/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/[rag_corpus_id]"

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

response = rag.retrieval_query(
    rag_resources=[
        rag.RagResource(
            rag_corpus=corpus_name,
            # Optional: supply IDs from `rag.list_files()`.
            # rag_file_ids=["rag-file-1", "rag-file-2", ...],
        )
    ],
    text="Why is the sky blue?",
    similarity_top_k=10,
    vector_distance_threshold=0.5,
)
print(response)
# Example response:
# contexts {
#   contexts {
#     source_uri: "gs://your-bucket-name/file.txt"
#     text: "....
#   ....

Generate content

Use the retrieved context to ground a generative model's response.

REST APIPython 
# Before using, replace the following:
# PROJECT_ID: Your project ID.
# LOCATION: The region to process the request (e.g., us-central1).
# MODEL_ID: The LLM model for content generation (e.g., gemini-1.0-pro).
# INPUT_PROMPT: The text prompt for the LLM.
# RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE: The resource name of the RagCorpus.

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d '{
         "contents": {
           "role": "user",
           "parts": {
             "text": "INPUT_PROMPT"
           }
         },
         "tools": [{
           "retrieval": {
             "vertex_rag_store": {
               "rag_resources": [{
                 "rag_corpus": "RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE"
               }]
             }
           }
         }]
       }' \
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:generateContent"

from vertexai import rag
from vertexai.generative_models import GenerativeModel, Tool
import vertexai

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# corpus_name = "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/{rag_corpus_id}"

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

rag_retrieval_tool = Tool.from_retrieval(
    retrieval=rag.Retrieval(
        source=rag.VertexRagStore(
            rag_resources=[
                rag.RagResource(
                    rag_corpus=corpus_name,
                    # Optional: supply IDs from `rag.list_files()`.
                    # rag_file_ids=["rag-file-1", "rag-file-2", ...],
                )
            ],
        ),
    )
)

rag_model = GenerativeModel(
    model_name="gemini-1.0-pro", tools=[rag_retrieval_tool]
)
response = rag_model.generate_content("Why is the sky blue?")
print(response.text)
# Example response:
#   The sky appears blue due to a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering.
#   Sunlight, which contains all colors of the rainbow, is scattered
#   by the tiny particles in the Earth's atmosphere....
#   ...

Use hybrid search

Hybrid search, which combines semantic (dense vector) and keyword (sparse vector) searches, is supported with a Weaviate database to improve the relevance of search results. You can enable it by setting the retrieval_strategy during a retrieval query. You can also adjust the weight between dense and sparse vector similarity.

Python 
from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# corpus_name = "projects/[PROJECT_ID]/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/[rag_corpus_id]"

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

response = rag.retrieval_query(
    rag_resources=[
        rag.RagResource(
            rag_corpus=corpus_name,
        )
    ],
    text="Why is the sky blue?",
    retrieval_strategy="hybrid", # Enable hybrid search
    hybrid_alpha=0.75, # Optional: weight for dense vectors (0.0 to 1.0)
)
print(response)

docs.title: Vector database choices in Vertex AI RAG Engine
docs.text:
Preview

This product or feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA products and features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

The following vector database options are in Preview: RagManagedDb, Vertex AI Feature Store, and Weaviate.

This page introduces the vector databases supported by Vertex AI RAG Engine and helps you choose the best option for your application.

Vector databases are essential for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) applications. They store and query vector embeddings, which are numerical representations of your data (such as documents or images). By using vector embeddings, RAG systems can efficiently find the most semantically relevant information from a large knowledge base to answer complex queries. This enhances the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) by grounding their responses in your specific data, leading to more accurate and relevant answers.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): A technique that enhances large language model (LLM) responses by retrieving relevant information from an external knowledge base.
  • Vector database: A specialized database designed to store, manage, and search high-dimensional vector embeddings efficiently.
  • Vector embedding: A numerical representation of data (like text or images) in a multi-dimensional space, where similar items are located closer to each other.
  • K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN): An exact search algorithm that finds the absolute closest data points to a query vector, offering perfect recall at the cost of higher latency.
  • Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN): A search algorithm that finds data points that are close, but not guaranteed to be the absolute closest, to a query vector, trading some accuracy for significant speed improvements.
  • Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK): A security feature that allows you to use your own cryptographic keys to protect your data in Google Cloud services.

Security

Vertex AI RAG Engine supports VPC Service Controls and CMEK. Data residency and AXT security controls are not supported.

docs.title: Vector database options
docs.text:
Vertex AI RAG Engine provides several options for your vector database. You can use the default, fully managed RagManagedDb for a streamlined experience, or integrate with other vector databases like Vector Search, Vertex AI Feature Store, Weaviate, or Pinecone. If you use an external vector database, you are responsible for managing its lifecycle and scalability.

Use the following table to compare the available vector database options and decide which one best suits your needs.

  • Low provisioning and maintenance overhead.
  • Using with chat bots.

docs.title: Vertex AI GenAI API Reference
docs.text: This document provides a reference for the REST resources and methods available in the Vertex AI Generative AI API. You can use these endpoints to interact with Vertex AI's generative models and related services directly via HTTP requests.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
This section provides essential concepts and information you need before using the API.

Concepts
  • REST API: A standardized architecture for creating web services that allows different systems to communicate over the internet using standard HTTP methods.
  • Discovery Document: A machine-readable specification that describes a REST API, enabling the automated creation of client libraries and tools.
  • Service Endpoint: The base URL that specifies the network address of an API service. All API request URIs are relative to this endpoint.
  • RagCorpus: A collection of documents used for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), which helps ground model responses in specific information.
  • TuningJob: A process to customize or fine-tune a foundation model using your own dataset to improve its performance on specific tasks.

docs.title: Service Information
docs.text:
To call this service, we recommend that you use the Google-provided client libraries. If your application needs to use your own libraries to call this service, use the following information when you make the API requests.

Discovery Document

A Discovery Document is a machine-readable specification for describing and consuming REST APIs. It is used to build client libraries, IDE plugins, and other tools that interact with Google APIs. This service provides the following discovery documents:

  • https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/$discovery/rest?version=v1
  • https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/$discovery/rest?version=v1beta1

Service Endpoint

A service endpoint is a base URL that specifies the network address of an API service. This service has the following service endpoint, and all URIs below are relative to it:

  • https://aiplatform.googleapis.com

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with API requests or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide for Vertex AI.

docs.title: Method: publishers.models.countTokens
docs.text: Performs a token count in express mode.

docs.title: HTTP request
docs.text: POST https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/{model}:countTokens

docs.title: Path parameters
docs.text: • model (string): Required. The name of the model requested to perform token counting. Format: /publishers/google/models/*

docs.title: Request body
docs.text:
The request body is a JSON object with the following fields:

  • model (string): Optional. The name of the publisher model requested to serve the prediction. Format: publishers/*/models/*
  • instances[] (value Value format): Optional. The instances that are the input to the token counting call. The schema is identical to the prediction schema of the underlying model.
  • contents[] (object Content): Optional. Input content.
  • tools[] (object Tool): Optional. A list of Tools the model may use to generate the next response. A Tool is a piece of code that enables the system to interact with external systems to perform an action, or set of actions, outside of the knowledge and scope of the model.
  • systemInstruction (object Content): Optional. The user-provided system instructions for the model. Note: only text should be used in parts, and content in each part will be in a separate paragraph.
  • generationConfig (object GenerationConfig): Optional. Generation config that the model will use to generate the response.

docs.title: Response body
docs.text: If successful, the response body contains a JSON object of type CountTokensResponse.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
The following is a sample request and response for counting tokens in the text "why is the sky blue?".

RequestResponse 
curl -X POST \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    "https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/publishers/google/models/gemini-1.5-flash-001:countTokens" -d \
    $'{
      "contents": {
        "role": "user",
        "parts": { "text": "why is the sky blue?" }
      }
    }'

{
  "totalTokens": 6,
  "totalBillableCharacters": 20
}

docs.title: HTTP request

docs.title: Path parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description model string Required. The fully qualified name of the publisher model to use, in the format publishers/google/models/*.

docs.title: Request body
docs.text:
The request body is a JSON object with the following fields:

  • contents (object (Content)[]): Required. The content of the current conversation with the model. For single-turn queries, this is a single instance. For multi-turn queries, this is a repeated field that contains conversation history and the latest request.
  • tools (object (Tool)[]): Optional. A list of Tools the model may use to generate the next response. A Tool is a piece of code that enables the system to interact with external systems to perform an action, or set of actions, outside of the knowledge and scope of the model.
  • toolConfig (object (ToolConfig)): Optional. Tool configuration for any Tool specified in the request.
  • labels (map (key: string, value: string)): Optional. The labels with user-defined metadata for the request, used for billing and reporting.
    • Label keys and values can be no longer than 63 characters (Unicode codepoints) and can only contain lowercase letters, numeric characters, underscores, and dashes. International characters are allowed.
    • Label values are optional.
    • Label keys must start with a letter.
  • safetySettings (object (SafetySetting)[]): Optional. Per-request settings for blocking unsafe content. This is enforced on GenerateContentResponse.candidates.
  • generationConfig (object (GenerationConfig)): Optional. Generation configuration for the model.
  • systemInstruction (object (Content)): Optional. The user-provided system instructions for the model. Note: Only text should be used in parts, and content in each part will be in a separate paragraph.

docs.title: Method: publishers.models.streamGenerateContent
docs.text:
Generates content from a multimodal model in a streaming fashion.

Concepts
  • Content: The user-provided instructions for the model, which can include text, images, or other media.
  • Tool: A piece of code that enables the model to interact with external systems to perform an action, such as calling another API or accessing a database.
  • ToolConfig: Configuration settings that are shared across all tools provided in a request.
  • SafetySetting: Per-request settings used to block potentially unsafe content from being generated.
  • GenerationConfig: Parameters that control the model's content generation process, such as temperature, top-K, and maximum output tokens.
  • System Instruction: High-level directives provided by the user to guide the model's behavior, tone, and responses throughout the conversation.

docs.text: POST https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/{model}:streamGenerateContent

docs.title: Path parameters
docs.text: • model (string): Required. The fully qualified name of the publisher model to use. The format is publishers/google/models/<MODEL_NAME>.

The request body contains data with the following structure:

  • contents[] (object (Content)): Required. The content of the current conversation with the model. For single-turn queries, this is a single instance. For multi-turn queries, this is a repeated field that contains the conversation history plus the latest request.
  • tools[] (object (Tool)): Optional. A list of Tools the model may use to generate the next response. A Tool is a piece of code that enables the system to interact with external systems to perform an action, or set of actions, outside of the knowledge and scope of the model.

  • labels (map (key: string, value: string)): Optional. The labels with user-defined metadata for the request, used for billing and reporting only.
    • Label keys and values can be no longer than 63 characters (Unicode codepoints) and can only contain lowercase letters, numeric characters, underscores, and dashes.
    • International characters are allowed.

  • systemInstruction (object (Content)): Optional. The user-provided system instructions for the model. Note: only text should be used in parts, and content in each part will be in a separate paragraph.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
The publishers.models resource provides methods to interact with the models. The following table compares the available methods to help you choose the right one for your use case.

Method Description Use Case countTokens Performs token counting on your input. Best for estimating the number of tokens in a prompt to understand potential billing costs before generating content. generateContent Generates a non-streaming response from the model based on multimodal inputs. Ideal for single-turn requests where the entire response is needed at once, such as summarizing a document or answering a question. streamGenerateContent Generates a streaming response from the model based on multimodal inputs. Use for interactive or real-time applications, like chatbots, where you want to display the response as it's being generated.

  • Tool: A piece of code that enables the model to interact with external systems to perform actions beyond its inherent knowledge.

docs.title: Dynamic shared quota (DSQ)
docs.text:
Dynamic shared quota (DSQ) provides a flexible way to manage your pay-as-you-go (PayGo) usage for generative AI models on Vertex AI. With DSQ, there are no predefined quota limits on your project. Instead, you get access to a large, shared pool of resources that are dynamically allocated based on real-time availability and demand.

This model allows your workloads to burst and consume more resources when available, adapting to your needs without requiring you to manage specific quota limits or submit quota increase requests (QIR).

docs.title: DSQ vs. Provisioned Throughput
docs.text:
Vertex AI offers two main ways to manage throughput for generative AI models. The following table compares the benefits of the pay-as-you-go model, which uses DSQ, with the provisioned throughput model.

Feature Dynamic Shared Quota (Pay-as-you-go) Provisioned Throughput Cost Model Pay only for what you use. Fixed hourly rate for reserved, dedicated throughput. Throughput Varies based on shared resource availability and overall demand. Throughput is not guaranteed. Stable, predictable, and guaranteed throughput. Best for Development, testing, and applications with variable or bursty traffic patterns. Production-critical applications requiring high availability and consistent, predictable performance. Availability Access is subject to contention in a shared pool. You might receive 429 errors during peak demand. Dedicated resources ensure high availability and eliminate 429 resource exhaustion errors.

To learn more about reserving dedicated throughput for your production workloads, see Provisioned throughput.

docs.title: How DSQ works
docs.text:
DSQ adapts to your traffic patterns by providing access to a shared pool of capacity. Your project's access to resources is not capped by a predefined limit but is determined by the overall capacity of the shared pool and the current demand from all customers.

To ensure a fair and stable experience for all users, DSQ uses a dynamic prioritization approach, especially during periods of high demand:

  • Flexibility for Bursts: The system is designed to accommodate bursts in traffic, allowing your workloads to scale up when resources are available.
  • Dynamic Prioritization: To protect overall system stability, unusually large and rapid spikes in traffic from a single project might be managed with a different priority than more consistent, steady traffic. This ensures that broad user activity is protected from transient, extreme spikes.

Gemini requests with multi-modal inputs are also subject to the corresponding system rate limits for image, audio, video, and document processing.

docs.title: Supported models
docs.text:
The following models and their supervised fine-tuned versions support DSQ.

Preview

The following models are in Preview: * Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite * Gemini 2.0 Flash with Live API * Gemini 2.0 Flash with image generation

Current Gemini models

  • Gemini 2.5 Pro
  • Gemini 2.5 Flash
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite

Legacy Gemini models

  • Gemini 1.5 Pro
  • Gemini 1.5 Flash

docs.title: Handle resource exhaustion (429) errors
docs.text:
When using DSQ, a 429 (Resource Exhausted) error does not mean you have hit a specific quota limit on your project. Instead, it indicates that the shared resource pool for a specific model in a region is temporarily experiencing extremely high demand from many users at once.

This is a temporary state of contention for resources, not a fixed limit on your project. Because availability in this dynamic environment can change quickly, we recommend implementing client-side retry mechanisms with exponential backoff to handle these errors.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

For more tactics on handling 429 errors, see Error code 429.

docs.title: Provisioned Throughput overview
docs.text:
This page explains what Provisioned Throughput is and when to use it compared to the pay-as-you-go consumption model.

Concepts
  • Provisioned Throughput: A fixed-cost, fixed-term subscription that reserves dedicated processing capacity (throughput) for a specific generative AI model, ensuring stable and predictable performance.
  • Pay-as-you-go (On-demand): A flexible consumption model where you pay for generative AI model usage based on the number of requests you send, using a shared pool of resources.
  • Throughput: A measure of the rate at which a model can process requests, typically measured in tokens per second or characters per second, depending on the model.

docs.title: Consumption models
docs.text:
Vertex AI offers two consumption models for using supported generative AI models: Provisioned Throughput and pay-as-you-go. Provisioned Throughput reserves throughput for a fixed cost, while the pay-as-you-go model, also known as on-demand, bills you based on usage.

To help you choose the right model for your workload, the following table compares the key features of each option.

Feature Provisioned Throughput Pay-as-you-go (On-demand) Cost Model Fixed-cost, fixed-term subscription (e.g., weekly, monthly). Per-request pricing based on input and output characters or tokens. Performance Reserved, stable, and predictable throughput for your dedicated use. Throughput is dynamic and depends on shared capacity and overall demand. Best for Production applications with consistent, high-throughput needs, such as real-time chatbots and agents. Development, testing, or applications with variable, unpredictable, or low traffic. Cost Predictability High. Costs are deterministic and fixed for the subscription term, with control over overages. Low. Costs vary directly with usage and can be unpredictable.

docs.title: When to use Provisioned Throughput
docs.text:
You should consider using Provisioned Throughput if your use case aligns with the following requirements:

  • Real-time production applications: You are building applications like chatbots and agents that require consistent performance.
  • High throughput needs: Your critical workloads consistently require high throughput.
  • Predictable user experience: You want to provide a consistent and predictable experience for your application's users.
  • Deterministic costs: You want to manage generative AI costs by paying a fixed price with control over potential overages.

To reserve your throughput, you must specify the model and the available locations where the model runs.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
• Learn about supported models that can be used with Provisioned Throughput.
  • Understand how to troubleshoot on-demand quota errors.

docs.title: Google Gen AI SDK
docs.text:
The Google Gen AI SDK provides a unified interface to Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 2.0 models through both the Gemini Developer API and the Gemini API on Vertex AI. With a few exceptions, code that runs on one platform will run on both. This means that you can prototype an application using the Gemini Developer API and then migrate the application to Vertex AI without rewriting your code.

To learn more about the differences between the Gemini Developer API and Gemini on Vertex AI, see Migrate from the Gemini Developer API to the Gemini API in Vertex AI.

Concepts
  • Gemini Developer API: A free-of-charge API suitable for prototyping and development, accessible via API keys.
  • Gemini API on Vertex AI: A fully-managed, enterprise-ready API integrated with Google Cloud services, offering features like data governance and security.

Set environment variables to use the Gen AI SDK with Vertex AI:

export GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=True

Quickstart

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "io"

    "google.golang.org/genai"
)

// generateWithText shows how to generate text using a text prompt.
func generateWithText(w io.Writer) error {
    ctx := context.Background()

    client, err := genai.NewClient(ctx, &genai.ClientConfig{
        HTTPOptions: genai.HTTPOptions{APIVersion: "v1"},
    })
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to create genai client: %w", err)
    }

    resp, err := client.Models.GenerateContent(ctx,
        "gemini-2.0-flash-001",
        genai.Text("How does AI work?"),
        nil,
    )
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate content: %w", err)
    }

    respText, err := resp.Text()
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to convert model response to text: %w", err)
    }
    fmt.Fprintln(w, respText)
    // Example response:
    // That's a great question! Understanding how AI works can feel like ...
    // ...
    // **1. The Foundation: Data and Algorithms**
    // ...

    return nil
}

import {GoogleGenAI} from '@google/genai';

const GEMINI_API_KEY = process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY;
const GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT = process.env.GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT;
const GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION = process.env.GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION;
const GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI = process.env.GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI;

async function generateContentFromMLDev() {
  const ai = new GoogleGenAI({vertexai: false, apiKey: GEMINI_API_KEY});
  const response = await ai.models.generateContent({
    model: 'gemini-2.0-flash',
    contents: 'why is the sky blue?',
  });
  console.debug(response.text);
}

async function generateContentFromVertexAI() {
  const ai = new GoogleGenAI({
    vertexai: true,
    project: GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT,
    location: GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION,
  });
  const response = await ai.models.generateContent({
    model: 'gemini-2.0-flash',
    contents: 'why is the sky blue?',
  });
  console.debug(response.text);
}

async function main() {
  if (GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI) {
    await generateContentFromVertexAI().catch((e) =>
      console.error('got error', e),
    );
  } else {
    await generateContentFromMLDev().catch((e) =>
      console.error('got error', e),
    );
  }
}

main();

/**
 * Usage:
 *
 * <p>1a. If you are using Vertex AI, setup ADC to get credentials:
 * https://cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/provide-credentials-adc#google-idp
 *
 * <p>Then set Project, Location, and USE_VERTEXAI flag as environment variables:
 *
 * <p>export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=YOUR_PROJECT
 *
 * <p>export GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=YOUR_LOCATION
 *
 * <p>export GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=true
 *
 * <p>1b. If you are using Gemini Developer API, set an API key environment variable. You can find a
 * list of available API keys here: https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey
 *
 * <p>export GOOGLE_API_KEY=YOUR_API_KEY
 *
 * <p>2. Compile the java package and run the sample code.
 *
 * <p>mvn clean compile exec:java -Dexec.mainClass="com.google.genai.examples.GenerateContent"
 * -Dexec.args="YOUR_MODEL_ID"
 */
package com.google.genai.examples;

import com.google.genai.Client;
import com.google.genai.types.GenerateContentResponse;

/** An example of using the Unified Gen AI Java SDK to generate content. */
public final class GenerateContent {
  public static void main(String[] args) {
    String modelId = "gemini-2.0-flash-001";
    if (args.length != 0) {
      modelId = args[0];
    }

    // Instantiate the client. The client by default uses the Gemini Developer API. It gets the API
    // key from the environment variable `GOOGLE_API_KEY`. Vertex AI API can be used by setting the
    // environment variables `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, as well as setting
    // `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI` to "true".
    //
    // Note: Some services are only available in a specific API backend (Gemini or Vertex), you will
    // get a `UnsupportedOperationException` if you try to use a service that is not available in
    // the backend you are using.
    Client client = new Client();

    if (client.vertexAI()) {
      System.out.println("Using Vertex AI");
    } else {
      System.out.println("Using Gemini Developer API");
    }

    GenerateContentResponse response =
        client.models.generateContent(modelId, "What is your name?", null);

    // Gets the text string from the response by the quick accessor method `text()`.
    System.out.println("Unary response: " + response.text());
  }

  private GenerateContent() {}
}

docs.title: Convert speech to text
docs.text:
This page shows you how to convert speech to text on Google Cloud. You can use the Vertex AI Studio for quick, simple transcriptions or the Speech-to-Text API for more advanced features and larger files.

To learn how to convert text to speech, see Convert text to speech.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Chirp: A universal speech model developed by Google that can transcribe audio in over 100 languages.
  • Linear PCM WAV: An uncompressed audio format where audio samples are stored in a linear sequence; WAV is the file container format.

docs.title: Choose a speech-to-text tool
docs.text:
Vertex AI provides two main ways to convert speech to text. The following table compares Vertex AI Studio with the Speech-to-Text API to help you decide which is right for your use case.

Feature Vertex AI Studio Speech-to-Text API Best for Quick tests, simple UI-based transcription, and evaluating the Chirp model. Production applications, transcribing long audio files, and accessing advanced features like speaker diarization. Input Method UI-based file upload. Programmatic requests using client libraries or REST/gRPC APIs. Audio Length Up to 60 seconds. Up to 8 hours for synchronous and batch recognition. File Size Limit Up to 10 MB. Up to 8 GB (for batch recognition in Cloud Storage). Supported Formats 16-bit linear PCM WAV only. Supports multiple formats including WAV, FLAC, MP3, and more. Advanced Features Basic transcription with the Chirp model. Speaker diarization, automatic punctuation, word-level confidence scores, and model adaptation.

docs.title: Convert speech to text using Vertex AI Studio
docs.text:
The following workflow outlines the steps to transcribe a short audio file using the Vertex AI Studio console.

flowchart TD
    A["Navigate to the Speech-to-Text tool"] --> B["Configure and submit the transcription job"];
    B --> C["Review the output"];

    click A "#navigate-to-the-speech-to-text-tool"
    click B "#configure-and-submit-the-transcription-job"
    click C "#review-the-output"
Transcribe an audio file

1. Navigate to the Speech-to-Text tool

In the Vertex AI section of the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI Studio page and open the Speech tool.

Go to Vertex AI Studio

  1. From the Vertex AI Studio dashboard, click Speech in the Multimodal section.
  2. Click Generate speech.
  3. Select the Speech-to-text tab.

2. Configure and submit the transcription job

  1. In the Speech section, click Browse to select the local audio file you want to convert to text. The file must be a 16-bit linear PCM WAV file, with a maximum duration of 60 seconds or size of 10 MB.
  2. In the Language selector box, select the language of the speech in the audio file.
  3. Click Submit.

3. Review the output

After you submit, the transcribed text appears in the Text box.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Steps to convert text to speech
docs.text:
Steps to convert text to speech

1. Open the Text-to-Speech tool

In Vertex AI Studio, navigate to the text-to-speech tool:

  1. Click Generate speech.
  2. Select the Text-to-speech tab.

2. Configure generation parameters

Configure the settings for your speech generation:

  • Text: Enter the text that you want to convert to speech.
  • Voice: Select a voice for the generated speech.
  • Speed: Use the slider or text field to set the speaking rate. A value of 1 is the normal speaking rate, and a value of 4 is four times the normal rate.

3. Submit and generate audio

Click Submit to generate the audio from your text.

4. Review and download the audio

After the audio is generated:

  • To listen to the speech, in the Speech section, click the play_arrow Play button.
  • To download the audio file in .wav format, click download Download.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.text:
• Vertex AI Studio only synthesizes audio with Text-to-Speech voices.

docs.title: Vertex AI in express mode overview
docs.text:
Preview

This feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

Vertex AI in express mode is the fastest way to start building generative AI applications on Google Cloud. Signing up in express mode is quick and easy, and it doesn't require entering any billing information. After you sign up, you can access and use Google Cloud APIs in just a few steps.

To learn more about Vertex AI in express mode, see Google Cloud express mode FAQs.

Concepts
  • API Key: A unique string used to authenticate requests to an API without needing a Google Cloud project.
  • Quota: A limit on the amount of a particular Google Cloud resource that you can use.
  • Vertex AI Studio: A Google Cloud console UI for prototyping and testing generative AI models.
  • Project: The base-level organizing entity for creating and using Google Cloud services.
  • Organization: The root node of the Google Cloud resource hierarchy, to which projects and billing accounts belong.

docs.title: Express mode eligibility
docs.text:
Vertex AI in express mode is separate from, and not available through, the Google Cloud Free Program. If you are in the Google Cloud Free Program, see the other quickstarts in the Get Started section to start using Generative AI on Vertex AI.

Vertex AI is available in express mode for developers that click the Try Vertex AI Studio free button and sign up using a @gmail.com Google Account. Accounts used previously to access Google Cloud are ineligible for express mode and are not shown the Try Vertex AI Studio free button. For example, if you used your Google Account to create a Google Cloud free trial account, you are not eligible to sign up in express mode with that same Google Account.

docs.title: Key features and limitations
docs.text:
Upon completing your sign-up in express mode, you get access to core Vertex AI Studio features, an API key, and a 90-day trial period. During the trial, you can use the supported Vertex AI APIs for free up to their quotas. You can increase your quota limits at any time by enabling billing.

The following table summarizes the key differences between using Vertex AI in express mode, with billing enabled, and the standard Vertex AI experience.

Item Vertex AI express mode Vertex AI express mode with billing Vertex AI (standard) Time limit 90 days Unlimited Unlimited Available services Basic Generative AI on Vertex AI services Expanded Vertex AI services and select Google Cloud services All Google Cloud services, including Vertex AI Data sources Google Drive Google Drive, web files, YouTube video URLs All data sources available in Google Cloud Quota Free tier quotas Standard quotas. See Rate limits. Standard quotas. See Rate limits. Service Level Agreement (SLA) None Vertex AI SLA Vertex AI SLA Authentication API Key API Key Project ID and location

docs.title: Available models and rate limits
docs.text:
You can try out several models in express mode, including the Gemini family of models. The following table lists the models that are available in express mode, along with their rate limits:

Model category Available models Requests per minute Discontinuation date Gemini gemini-1.5-pro 30 June 17, 2026 gemini-1.5-flash 30 June 17, 2026 gemini-1.5-flash-lite-preview-06-17 30 gemini-1.5-flash-preview-05-20 30 July 15, 2025 gemini-1.5-flash-preview-04-17 30 July 15, 2025 gemini-1.5-pro-preview-05-06 30 July 15, 2025 gemini-1.0-flash-001 30 February 5, 2026 gemini-1.0-flash-lite-001 30 February 25, 2026

For Gemini 1.0 models, the Multimodal Live API isn't available in the Console in express mode. To use the Multimodal Live API in express mode, use the Vertex AI API or the Google Gen AI SDK.

docs.title: Get started with express mode
docs.text:
You can start sending requests from your application to Vertex AI APIs in three steps. This workflow shows how to test a prompt in Vertex AI Studio, get the equivalent code, and use your API key to run it in your application.

flowchart LR

    B --> C[Authenticate with API key]

click B "#get-code"

Get started with express mode

1. Try features in Vertex AI Studio

Use Vertex AI Studio in express mode to quickly try Vertex AI features. For example, in the Google Cloud console in express mode, select Vertex AI > Freeform and use the Freeform page to create and optimize multimodal prompts using a variety of Gemini models.

2. Get code

On the Freeform page, click code Get code. A panel opens showing code that programmatically sends the same requests that you implemented in the UI. You can get the code for a programming language or as a cURL command. You can use Google Colab to try the Python code.

3. Authenticate with your API key

In the Google Cloud console in express mode, click menu Menu and select API Keys, and then copy your key into your code where it says "YOUR_API_KEY".

Python example

  • google-genai on PyPI

docs.title: Manage your express mode environment
docs.text: The following sections describe how to manage your API keys, quotas, and billing settings in express mode.

docs.title: View and manage API keys
docs.text:

To learn more about the best practices for managing API keys, see Best practices for managing API keys.

Steps to view and manage API keys

  1. Go to the Vertex AI Studio Overview page in express mode.

    Go to Vertex AI Studio

  2. In the Google Cloud console in express mode, click menu Menu.

  3. Select API Keys. The API Keys page opens, where you can manage your API keys.

docs.title: View quotas
docs.text:

Steps to view quotas

    Go to Vertex AI Studio

docs.title: Enable billing
docs.text:
You can increase your quotas and remove the 90-day limit by enabling billing. After enabling billing, you pay only for what you use. You can also save your prompts and access additional settings in the console that are grayed out when billing isn't enabled.

Steps to enable billing

    Go to Vertex AI Studio

  2. In the Google Cloud console in express mode, click menu Menu.

docs.title: Graduate to the full Google Cloud experience
docs.text:
You can start using all the capabilities and services available in Google Cloud in your project by graduating from express mode.

Steps to graduate from express mode

  1. Go to the Vertex AI Studio Overview page in express mode.

    Go to Vertex AI Studio

  2. In the Google Cloud console in express mode, click menu Menu.

  3. Select Billing.

  4. In the Access all Google Cloud section, click Learn more and get started.

After you graduate from express mode, specify your project ID and location instead of your API key when you call the REST API endpoints. For example: https://{location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{projectid}/locations/{location}/publishers/google/models/{model}:streamGenerateContent

docs.title: How express mode differs from standard Vertex AI
docs.text:
Vertex AI in express mode provides a subset of the features for Generative AI on Vertex AI. For details on the available API endpoints in express mode, see the Vertex AI in express mode REST API reference.

In addition, customers in Google Cloud typically use organizations and projects to work with resources. When using Vertex AI in express mode, you don't need to worry about organizations or projects. However, you might see them mentioned in some of the Google Cloud documentation. You can still use the documentation, but ignore concepts and instructions that refer to organizations and projects. In addition, the location you selected when signing up in express mode is used throughout your experience.

When calling REST API endpoints, you must use the format specific to express mode and provide your API key.

Endpoint Type URL Format Standard endpoint URL https://{location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{project}/locations/{location}/publishers/google/models/{model}:streamGenerateContent Endpoint URL in express mode https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/publishers/google/models/{model}:streamGenerateContent?key={API_KEY}

Vertex AI in express mode lets you quickly try out core generative AI features available on Vertex AI. This tutorial shows you how to use the Vertex AI API in express mode to install the necessary SDK and send different types of requests to the Gemini API.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Express mode: A streamlined method for accessing Vertex AI's generative AI features using an API key for quick setup and experimentation.
  • Google Gen AI SDK: A software development kit (SDK) that enables developers to use Google's generative AI models in their applications.
  • Streaming request: An API request that returns the response in smaller chunks as it is being generated, reducing perceived latency.
  • Non-streaming request: An API request that returns the complete response in a single chunk after all processing is finished.
  • Function calling: A feature that allows a large language model to request a specific, predefined function or tool to be executed to retrieve real-time or external information.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: • To follow this tutorial, you need an API key for express mode. For instructions, see Vertex AI in express mode overview.

docs.title: Interactive Tutorial
docs.text:
You can also follow this tutorial in an interactive Jupyter notebook environment.

Open in Colab Open in Colab Enterprise Open in Vertex AI Workbench View on GitHub

docs.title: Tutorial Workflow
docs.text:
This tutorial follows a three-step process. The following diagram shows the high-level workflow you will follow to send a request to the Gemini API using express mode.

flowchart TD
    A["Step 1: Install and initialize the SDK"] --> B["Step 2: Send a request to the Gemini API"]
    B --> C["Step 3: Clean up"]

    click A "#install-and-initialize-the-sdk"
    click B "#send-a-request-to-the-gemini-api"
    click C "#clean-up"
Tutorial: Use the Vertex AI API in express mode

Step 1: Install and initialize the Google Gen AI SDK

The Google Gen AI SDK lets you use Google generative AI models to build AI-powered applications. When using Vertex AI in express mode, you install and initialize the google-genai package to authenticate with your API key.

Install the SDK

Run the following commands to install the package. If you're using Colab, ignore any dependency conflicts and restart the runtime after installation.

# Developer TODO: If you're using Colab, uncomment the following lines:
# from google.colab import auth
# auth.authenticate_user()

!pip install google-genai

!pip install --force-reinstall -qq "numpy<2.0"

Initialize the client

Configure the client with your API key to authenticate your requests.

from google import genai
from google.genai import types

# Developer TODO: Replace YOUR_API_KEY with your API key.
API_KEY = "YOUR_API_KEY"

client = genai.Client(
    vertexai=True, api_key=API_KEY
)

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Step 2: Send a request to the Gemini API

You can send requests to the Gemini for Google Cloud API in several ways depending on your needs. The primary methods are streaming and non-streaming requests.

Request Type Description When to Use Streaming Returns the response in chunks as it's being processed. Ideal for interactive applications (like chatbots) where users expect immediate feedback. Non-streaming Returns the entire response in one block after the request is fully processed. Suitable for offline or batch processing tasks where latency is not a primary concern. Function Calling The model requests a specific tool to be executed to get more information. Use when the model needs to interact with external APIs or retrieve real-time data to answer a prompt.

Select a tab to view the code for each request type.

Streaming requestNon-streaming requestFunction calling request

To send a streaming request, set stream=True and process the response in chunks as they arrive. This approach reduces the perceived latency for the user.

from google import genai
from google.genai import types

def generate():
  client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, api_key=YOUR_API_KEY)

  config=types.GenerateContentConfig(
      temperature=0,
      top_p=0.95,
      top_k=20,
      candidate_count=1,
      seed=5,
      max_output_tokens=100,
      stop_sequences=["STOP!"],
      presence_penalty=0.0,
      frequency_penalty=0.0,
      safety_settings=[
          types.SafetySetting(
              category="HARM_CATEGORY_HATE_SPEECH",
              threshold="BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH",
          )
      ],
  )
  for chunk in client.models.generate_content_stream(
    model="gemini-2.0-flash-001",
    contents="Explain bubble sort to me",
    config=config,
  ):
    print(chunk.text)

generate()

A non-streaming request waits for the entire response to be generated before returning it. The following code sample sends a non-streaming request to the gemini-2.0-flash-001 model and shows how to configure basic request parameters and safety settings.

from google import genai
from google.genai import types

def generate():
  client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, api_key=YOUR_API_KEY)

  config=types.GenerateContentConfig(
      temperature=0,
      top_p=0.95,
      top_k=20,
      candidate_count=1,
      seed=5,
      max_output_tokens=100,
      stop_sequences=["STOP!"],
      presence_penalty=0.0,
      frequency_penalty=0.0,
      safety_settings=[
          types.SafetySetting(
              category="HARM_CATEGORY_HATE_SPEECH",
              threshold="BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH",
          )
      ],
  )
  response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.0-flash-001",
    contents="Explain bubble sort to me",
    config=config,
  )
  print(response.text)

generate()

Function calling allows the model to request that you call an external tool or API. The following code sample declares a function, passes it as a tool, and then receives a function call in the response. After receiving the function call, you invoke the function, get the result, and pass the result back to the model.

function_response_parts = [
    {
        'function_response': {
            'name': 'get_current_weather',
            'response': {
                'name': 'get_current_weather',
                'content': {'weather': 'super nice'},
            },
        },
    },
]
manual_function_calling_contents = [
    {'role': 'user', 'parts': [{'text': 'What is the weather in Boston?'}]},
    {
        'role': 'model',
        'parts': [{
            'function_call': {
                'name': 'get_current_weather',
                'args': {'location': 'Boston'},
            }
        }],
    },
    {'role': 'user', 'parts': function_response_parts},
]
function_declarations = [{
    'name': 'get_current_weather',
    'description': 'Get the current weather in a city',
    'parameters': {
        'type': 'OBJECT',
        'properties': {
            'location': {
                'type': 'STRING',
                'description': 'The location to get the weather for',
            },
            'unit': {
                'type': 'STRING',
                'enum': ['C', 'F'],
            },
        },
    },
}]

response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.0-flash-001",
    contents=manual_function_calling_contents,
    config=dict(tools=[{'function_declarations': function_declarations}]),
)
print(response.text)

Step 3: Clean up

This tutorial does not create any Google Cloud resources, so no cleanup is needed to avoid charges.

docs.title: Endpoint format comparison

Unlike the standard REST resource endpoints on Google Cloud, endpoints that are available when using Vertex AI in express mode use the global endpoint aiplatform.googleapis.com and don't include projects or locations.

  • Standard Vertex AI endpoint format: https://{location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{project}/locations/{location}/{model}:generateContent
  • Endpoint format for Vertex AI in express mode: https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/{model}:generateContent

docs.title: Choose an API version
docs.text:
The Vertex AI in express mode API has two versions: v1 (General Availability) and v1beta1 (Beta). Before you start, choose the version that best fits your use case.

Version Stability Features Recommendation v1 (GA) Stable, production-ready APIs. A comprehensive set of proven features. Recommended for most production applications that require stability. v1beta1 (Beta) Subject to change; not recommended for production. Includes new and experimental features not yet in v1. Use for development and testing to try the latest capabilities.

docs.title: Tutorial: Vertex AI Studio in express mode
docs.text:
Preview

This feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the . Pre-GA features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the .

Vertex AI in express mode lets you quickly try out core generative AI features that are available on Vertex AI. This quickstart shows you how to perform the following tasks in Vertex AI Studio in express mode:

  • View and try a list of sample prompts.
  • Create and save your own prompts.
  • Design a chatbot and get the code.
Concepts
  • Express mode: A simplified interface in Vertex AI for quickly trying core generative AI features.
  • Prompt: An instruction or question given to a generative AI model to elicit a specific response.
  • Chatbot: A program designed to simulate conversation with human users.
View and try a sample prompt

To view and try a sample prompt in Vertex AI Studio, follow these steps:

  1. In the Vertex AI section of the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI Studio page.

    Go to Vertex AI Studio

  2. In the navigation pane, click Prompt Gallery.

  3. On the Prompt Gallery page, click Image to filter for prompt samples that include images.

  4. Click the sample prompt card titled Extract text from images. The prompt opens in the prompt editor.

  5. In the Prompt box, click the submit button to submit the prompt.

A response similar to the following is returned in the Response box:

the best dreams HAPPEN when you are awake
Create and save your own prompt

To create and save a prompt in Vertex AI Studio, follow these steps. Note that you need billing enabled to save prompts.

  1. In the Vertex AI section of the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI Studio page.

    Go to Vertex AI Studio

  2. In the navigation pane, click Create prompt.

  3. In the Prompt text field, enter a text prompt. For example:

what is a good name for a flower shop that specializes in selling bouquets of dried flowers?
  1. In the Prompt box, click the submit button to submit the prompt.

A response similar to the following is returned in the Response box:

Here are some good names for a flower shop specializing in dried flowers, categorized by style:

Elegant & Romantic:

* Everlasting Bloom
* The Dried Flower Garden
* Bloom & Branch
...

  1. Click Save.

  2. In the Save prompt dialog, enter a name for your prompt.

  3. Click Save.

  4. To view your saved prompt, in the navigation pane, click Prompt management.

Design a chatbot and get the code

To design a chatbot in Vertex AI Studio and get the code for it, follow these steps:

  1. In the Vertex AI section of the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI Studio page.

    Go to Vertex AI Studio

  2. In the navigation pane, click Create prompt.

  3. In the System instructions text field, enter the following instructions:

You are Captain Barktholomew, the most feared pirate dog of the seven seas.
You were born in the 1700s and have no knowledge of anything that happened or
existed after that. Only talk about topics that a pirate dog captain would be
interested in.
  1. In the prompt text field, enter a message. For example:
Hello! Do you like computers?
  1. Send the message by clicking the submit button or pressing Enter.

A response similar to the following is returned based on the system instructions you provided:

Ahoy there, matey! What in Neptune's name be ye talkin' about? "Computers"?
Sounds like a fancy landlubber word! A pirate dog like me ain't interested in
fancy contraptions. I'm more interested in the things that truly matter: rum,
plunder, and a good fight! Now, tell me, do ye have any gold doubloons to
spare? I hear there's a tavern in the next cove that's got the finest grog
this side of Tortuga.
  1. Click Build with code > Get code.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

  1. In the Get code pane that opens, get the code for your chatbot by selecting your preferred programming language.
