docs.title: Quickstart: Deploy your Vertex AI Studio prompt as a web application
docs.text:
Preview

This feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

In Vertex AI Studio, you can design and test prompts by comparing results from different configurations and models. After engineering your prompt, you can deploy it as a web application hosted on Cloud Run. This allows you to share your prompt with collaborators or users outside of the Google Cloud console for testing.

In this quickstart, you will learn how to:

  • Create a prompt that uses variables.
  • Deploy your prompt as a web application.
  • Monitor the deployment and test the application.
  • Update and re-deploy your prompt.
  • Test prompt submissions with multimodal content like images and videos.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Set up your environment and permissions

Concepts

Concepts
  • Prompt Variable: A placeholder in a prompt that allows users to dynamically insert different values, making the prompt reusable for various inputs.
  • Cloud Run: A managed compute platform that enables you to run containers that are invocable via requests or events.
  • Artifact Registry: A single place for your organization to manage container images and language packages.
  • Cloud Build: A service that executes your builds on Google Cloud's infrastructure.
  • Service Account: A special type of Google account intended to represent a non-human user that needs to authenticate and be authorized to access data in Google APIs.

Prerequisites

Before starting this quickstart, ensure you have the following:

  1. A Google Cloud project with billing enabled.
  2. The Vertex AI API enabled.

If you have never used Vertex AI Studio, you can follow the Vertex AI Studio quickstart or take the Google Cloud Skills Boost course to learn the basics.

Additional permissions required

To deploy your prompt, you need additional permissions beyond those required for general Vertex AI Studio use.

Action Required Permissions Purpose Enable additional APIs serviceusage.services.enable Enable the Cloud Run Admin, Artifact Registry, Cloud Build, and Cloud Logging APIs. Grant permissions to service accounts resourcemanager.projects.setIamPolicy Grant the Compute Engine default service account the Vertex AI Service Agent and Cloud Build Service Account roles. Deploy specific permissions storage.buckets.createrun.services.createartifactregistry.repositories.createrun.services.setIamPolicy These permissions are required to upload source code to Cloud Storage, create a Cloud Run service, create an Artifact Registry repository for the container image, and make the service publicly accessible.

If you are the project owner, you can follow the guided steps in Vertex AI Studio. If you are not the project owner, ask your administrator to perform the first two actions and grant you the Editor (roles/editor) and Cloud Run Admin (roles/run.admin) roles.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

This diagram shows the high-level workflow for deploying your prompt as a web application.

flowchart TD
    A["Step 1: Create a prompt with variables"] --> B["Step 2: Deploy the prompt as a web app"]
    B --> C["Step 3: Monitor the deployment"]
    C --> D["Step 4: Update and re-deploy the prompt"]
    D --> E["Step 5: Test with multimodal content"]

    click A "#create-a-prompt-with-prompt-variables"
    click B "#deploy-your-prompt-as-a-web-application"
    click C "#monitor-the-deployment-status"
    click D "#update-and-re-deploy-your-prompt"
    click E "#test-with-multimodal-content"

docs.title: Deploy and test your prompt
docs.text:
Steps to deploy and test your prompt

Step 1: Create a prompt with prompt variables

  1. Navigate to the Create prompt page in Vertex AI Studio.
  2. In the prompt input box, click Add variable.
  3. In the Manage prompt variables dialog, enter a variable name, provide a default value, and click Apply.

The "Manage prompt variables" dialog.

  1. Compose your prompt using the variable you created. You can also adjust other parameters, such as enabling Grounding with Google Search and setting the system instructions to "Always get current weather from the web".

Step 2: Deploy your prompt as a web application

  1. Click the Build with code button in the top right corner, then select Deploy as app.

Deploying the prompt as an app.

Save the prompt

A dialog appears prompting you to save the prompt, which is required for deployment. The deployment dialog opens automatically after the prompt is saved.

Saving the prompt before deployment.

Note: Saving your prompt in a region for the first time can take 2-3 minutes. A warning box appears after 1 minute. This is a one-time operation; subsequent saves in the same project and region will be much faster.

Enable APIs and grant permissions

If this is your first deployment, you will be prompted to enable the required APIs. Click Enable required APIs.

After the APIs are enabled, the Create a web app dialog appears. All deployed applications allow public access. Don't include sensitive or personally identifiable information (PII) in your prompt.

  1. Check the I understand this app will be deployed publicly checkbox.
  2. Click Create app.
  3. If prompted, click Grant all to grant the required roles to the service account.

Note: If you lack the necessary permissions, ask your project administrator for assistance. See the additional permissions required for details.

Deployment starts

Vertex AI Studio packages the web application's source code into a ZIP file and uploads it to a Cloud Storage bucket. The Manage web app dialog appears, showing deployment information such as the application name, status, and last deployment time.

The "Manage web app" dialog.

Step 3: Monitor the deployment status

Deployment takes 2-3 minutes. You can monitor the status in the Manage web app dialog or through the notification bell in the Google Cloud console.

When deployment is complete, the status changes to Ready, and an Open button appears.

The application is ready to open.

Access control and secret key

Your web application is deployed with unauthenticated access enabled. To provide basic protection, the application requires a secret key in the URL. You can find this key in the Secret Key column of the Manage web app dialog. When you open the app from Vertex AI Studio, the key is appended automatically.

Open and test the web application

  1. Click Open in the Manage web app dialog. The application opens in a new tab with the secret key appended to the URL (?key=SECRET_KEY).
  2. Enter a value for the prompt variable and click Submit. The results appear on the right.

Submitting a prompt and viewing results in the web app.

Note: Cloud Run is serverless, so the application container may shut down after a period of inactivity. If the app is slow to load or a submission fails, refreshing the page usually resolves the issue.

Step 4: Update and re-deploy your prompt

  1. Edit your prompt in Vertex AI Studio (for example, by turning it into a conversation).
  2. Click the Build with code button and select Manage app.
  3. In the Manage web app dialog, click Update app.
  4. A confirmation dialog appears. Click Confirm to proceed. Redeploying will overwrite any changes made directly to the source code in Cloud Run.

After the update is complete, open the web application again. You will see the updated UI.

The updated application with a conversation UI.

Step 5: Test with multimodal content

The web application supports multimodal inputs like images, videos, and documents, depending on the selected model. For details, see Model variations and multimodal support.

  1. Click the clip icon in the conversation input box to insert a file.
  2. Interact with the model using the provided input.

Interacting with the model using an image.

docs.title: Advanced customization and management
docs.text:
Edit the web application source code

To customize the web application, you can edit its source code directly in Cloud Run.

  1. Open the Manage web app dialog, click the more_vert icon for your app, and select Open source code editor.
  2. In the Cloud Run source code page, click Edit source.
  3. After making your changes, click Save and redeploy.

Note: Cloud Run does not have built-in version control. Re-deploying from Vertex AI Studio will overwrite any changes made in the Cloud Run editor. To save a version of your code, click Download ZIP before re-deploying.

Manage public access for the web application

Turn off public access

  1. In the Manage Web App dialog, click the pencil icon in the Access Control column. This opens the Cloud Run security page.
  2. Select Require authentication and click Save.

Your web application will no longer be publicly accessible and will show an "Error: Forbidden" page.

Turn on public access again

To restore public access, return to the Cloud Run security page and select Allow unauthenticated invocations.

For more details, see Authentication in Cloud Run.

Set up local access for development

If you have turned off public access, you can set up a local proxy to access the application for development.

  1. Open Cloud Shell by clicking the terminal icon in the Google Cloud console.
  2. In the Manage web app dialog, click the more_vert icon and select Set up local access via Cloud Shell.
  3. A command is added to your Cloud Shell. Press Enter to run it.
  4. Click the preview link provided in the Cloud Shell output to access your application locally. This link only works while the gcloud command is running.

Accessing the application via a local proxy in Cloud Shell.

docs.title: Troubleshoot common issues
docs.text:
Authentication error: No secret key

If you see an error indicating a missing secret key, the key was not appended to the URL. Open the web application from the Manage web app dialog in Vertex AI Studio, which appends the key automatically. Alternatively, copy the key from the dialog and manually append it to the URL in the format ?key=SECRET_KEY.

Error message for a missing secret key.

Authentication error: Invalid secret key

This error means the secret key in the URL is incorrect. Each prompt has a unique key. Ensure you are using the correct key for the specific prompt by opening the application from the Manage web app dialog.

Error message for an invalid secret key.

Error 400: Invalid argument - empty input

This error occurs if the prompt variables have values but the chat input box is empty. To fix this, type any non-empty content into the chat box and resubmit.

Error message for an empty chat input.

Error 400: Invalid argument - unsupported mimeType

This error occurs if you upload a file type that the selected model does not support. You must use a file type compatible with the model. For details, see the documentation for multimodal support for each model.

Error message for an unsupported file type.

docs.title: Quickstart: Generate text using the Vertex AI Gemini API
docs.text:
To see an example of getting started with Gemini, you can run the "Intro to Gemini 2.0 Flash" Jupyter notebook in one of the following environments:

Open in Colab Open in Colab Enterprise Open in Vertex AI Workbench View on GitHub

In this quickstart, you learn how to send multimodal requests to the Vertex AI Gemini API and view the responses. You will complete the following tasks:

  • Send a text-only prompt.
  • Send a prompt that includes text and an image.
  • Send a prompt that includes text and a video file.

You can complete this quickstart by using a programming language SDK in your local environment or by sending requests using the REST API.

This tutorial follows the workflow below:

flowchart TD
    A[Set up your environment] --> B[Send a text prompt]
    B --> C[Send a prompt and an image]
    C --> D[Send a prompt and a video]

    click A "#before-you-begin"
    click B "#send-a-text-prompt"
    click C "#send-a-prompt-and-an-image"
    click D "#send-a-prompt-and-a-video"
Before you begin

Concepts
  • Vertex AI Gemini API: A service that provides access to Google's Gemini family of large multimodal models.
  • Multimodal: The ability to process information from and work with multiple types of data, such as text, images, and video, simultaneously.
  • Prompt: The input (which can include text, images, and video) that you send to a generative model to elicit a specific response.
  • SDK (Software Development Kit): A collection of pre-packaged code and tools that simplify the process of interacting with an API in a specific programming language.
  • REST API: A standardized way for applications to communicate over the web, allowing you to send requests to the Gemini API using standard HTTP methods.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Set up your Google Cloud project
docs.text:
1. Sign in to your Google Cloud account. If you're new to Google Cloud, create an account to evaluate how our products perform in real-world scenarios. New customers also get $300 in free credits to run, test, and deploy workloads.

  2. In the Google Cloud console, on the project selector page, select or create a Google Cloud project.

    Note: If you don't plan to keep the resources that you create in this procedure, create a project instead of selecting an existing project. After you finish these steps, you can delete the project, removing all resources associated with the project.

    Go to project selector

  3. Make sure that billing is enabled for your Google Cloud project.

  4. Enable the Vertex AI API.

    Enable the API

docs.title: Set up the Google Cloud CLI
docs.text:
On your local machine, set up and authenticate with the Google Cloud CLI. The Vertex AI Gemini API uses Identity and Access Management (IAM) for access control.

  1. Install and initialize the Google Cloud CLI.

  2. If you previously installed the gcloud CLI, ensure your components are updated:

    gcloud components update

  3. Authenticate with the gcloud CLI to generate local Application Default Credentials (ADC):

    gcloud auth application-default login

For more information, see Set up Application Default Credentials.

Note: To avoid providing your project ID and region in every command, you can use gcloud config set to configure defaults.

docs.title: Choose your method and install the required tools
docs.text:
You can interact with the Gemini API using the Google AI SDKs, the Vertex AI SDKs, or the REST API.

Method Description Use Case Google AI SDKs for Gemini A newer set of SDKs designed for Gemini, offering a more idiomatic and streamlined experience. They can be configured to use the Vertex AI backend. Recommended for new projects focused on Gemini. Provides a simpler interface for generative features. Vertex AI SDKs The traditional SDKs for the entire Vertex AI platform, providing comprehensive access to all Vertex AI services, including Gemini. Best for projects that are already using other Vertex AI services or require tight integration with the broader Vertex AI ecosystem. REST API Direct HTTP requests to the Vertex AI endpoint. Offers language-agnostic access but requires manual handling of authentication and request/response bodies. Useful for environments where an SDK is not available or for quick testing with tools like curl.

Select a tab below to see the installation and setup instructions for your chosen method.

Python (Google AI SDK)Go (Google AI SDK)Node.js (Google AI SDK)Java (Google AI SDK)Node.js (Vertex AI SDK)Java (Vertex AI SDK)C# (Vertex AI SDK)REST

Install and update the Google AI SDK for Python:

pip install --upgrade google-genai

Install and update the Google AI SDK for Go:

go get google.golang.org/genai

Install and update the Google AI SDK for Node.js:

npm install @google/genai

Add the following Maven dependency to your pom.xml:

<dependencies>
  <dependency>
    <groupId>com.google.genai</groupId>
    <artifactId>google-genai</artifactId>
    <version>0.7.0</version>
  </dependency>
</dependencies>

Before trying this sample, follow the Node.js setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart. For more information, see the Vertex AI Node.js API reference documentation.

Before trying this sample, follow the Java setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart. For more information, see the Vertex AI Java API reference documentation.

Install the Google.Cloud.AIPlatform.V1 package from NuGet. For example, right-click your project in Visual Studio and choose Manage NuGet Packages....

  1. Configure your environment variables. Replace PROJECT_ID with your Google Cloud project ID.

    MODEL_ID="gemini-2.0-flash-001"
PROJECT_ID="PROJECT_ID"

  2. Use the gcloud CLI to provision the endpoint:

    gcloud beta services identity create --service=aiplatform.googleapis.com --project=${PROJECT_ID}

docs.title: Send a text prompt
docs.text:
Use the following code to send a text prompt to the Vertex AI Gemini API. This sample returns a list of possible names for a specialty flower store.

Python (Google AI SDK)Go (Google AI SDK)Node.js (Google AI SDK)Java (Google AI SDK)C# (Vertex AI SDK)REST

Set environment variables to use the Google AI SDK with Vertex AI:

# Replace the `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` values
# with appropriate values for your project.
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global
export GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=True

Run the following code:

from google import genai
from google.genai.types import HttpOptions

client = genai.Client(http_options=HttpOptions(api_version="v1"))
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.0-flash-001",
    contents="How does AI work?",
)
print(response.text)
# Example response:
# Okay, let's break down how AI works. It's a broad field, so I'll focus on the ...
#
# Here's a simplified overview:
# ...

# with appropriate values for your project.
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global
export GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=True

Run the following code:

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "io"

    "google.golang.org/genai"
)

// generateWithText shows how to generate text using a text prompt.
func generateWithText(w io.Writer) error {
    ctx := context.Background()

    client, err := genai.NewClient(ctx, &genai.ClientConfig{
        HTTPOptions: genai.HTTPOptions{APIVersion: "v1"},
    })
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to create genai client: %w", err)
    }

    resp, err := client.Models.GenerateContent(ctx,
        "gemini-2.0-flash-001",
        genai.Text("How does AI work?"),
        nil,
    )
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate content: %w", err)
    }

    respText, err := resp.Text()
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to convert model response to text: %w", err)
    }
    fmt.Fprintln(w, respText)
    // Example response:
    // That's a great question! Understanding how AI works can feel like ...
    // ...
    // **1. The Foundation: Data and Algorithms**
    // ...

    return nil
}

import com.google.genai.Client;
import com.google.genai.types.Content;
import com.google.genai.types.GenerateContentResponse;
import com.google.genai.types.HttpOptions;
import com.google.genai.types.Part;

public class GenerateContentWithText {

  public static void main(String[] args) {
    // TODO(developer): Replace these variables before running the sample.
    String modelId = "gemini-2.0-flash";
    generateContent(modelId);
  }

  public static String generateContent(String modelId) {
    // Initialize client that will be used to send requests. This client only needs to be created
    // once, and can be reused for multiple requests.
    try (Client client = Client.builder()
        .httpOptions(HttpOptions.builder().apiVersion("v1").build())
        .build()) {

      GenerateContentResponse response =
          client.models.generateContent(modelId, Content.fromParts(
                  Part.fromText("How does AI work?")),
              null);

      System.out.print(response.text());
      // Example response:
      // Okay, let's break down how AI works. It's a broad field, so I'll focus on the ...
      //
      // Here's a simplified overview:
      // ...
      return response.text();
    }
  }
}

Create a C# file (.cs), copy the following code into it, and replace your-project-id with your Google Cloud project ID.

using Google.Cloud.AIPlatform.V1;
using System;
using System.Threading.Tasks;

public class TextInputSample
{
    public async Task<string> TextInput(
        string projectId = "your-project-id",
        string location = "us-central1",
        string publisher = "google",
        string model = "gemini-2.0-flash-001")
    {

        var predictionServiceClient = new PredictionServiceClientBuilder
        {
            Endpoint = $"{location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com"
        }.Build();
        string prompt = @"What's a good name for a flower shop that specializes in selling bouquets of dried flowers?";

        var generateContentRequest = new GenerateContentRequest
        {
            Model = $"projects/{projectId}/locations/{location}/publishers/{publisher}/models/{model}",
            Contents =
            {
                new Content
                {
                    Role = "USER",
                    Parts =
                    {
                        new Part { Text = prompt }
                    }
                }
            }
        };

        GenerateContentResponse response = await predictionServiceClient.GenerateContentAsync(generateContentRequest);

        string responseText = response.Candidates[0].Content.Parts[0].Text;
        Console.WriteLine(responseText);

        return responseText;
    }
}

Run the following curl command:

curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/global/publishers/google/models/${MODEL_ID}:generateContent -d \
$'{
  "contents": {
    "role": "user",
    "parts": [
      {
        "text": "What\'s a good name for a flower shop that specializes in selling bouquets of dried flowers?"
      }
    ]
  }
}'

import com.google.cloud.vertexai.VertexAI;
import com.google.cloud.vertexai.api.GenerateContentResponse;
import com.google.cloud.vertexai.generativeai.ContentMaker;
import com.google.cloud.vertexai.generativeai.GenerativeModel;
import com.google.cloud.vertexai.generativeai.PartMaker;
import java.io.IOException;

public class Quickstart {

  public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
    // TODO(developer): Replace these variables before running the sample.
    String projectId = "your-google-cloud-project-id";
    String location = "us-central1";
    String modelName = "gemini-2.0-flash-001";

    String output = quickstart(projectId, location, modelName);
    System.out.println(output);
  }

  // Analyzes the provided Multimodal input.
  public static String quickstart(String projectId, String location, String modelName)
      throws IOException {
    // Initialize client that will be used to send requests. This client only needs
    // to be created once, and can be reused for multiple requests.
    try (VertexAI vertexAI = new VertexAI(projectId, location)) {
      String imageUri = "gs://generativeai-downloads/images/scones.jpg";

      GenerativeModel model = new GenerativeModel(modelName, vertexAI);
      GenerateContentResponse response = model.generateContent(ContentMaker.fromMultiModalData(
          PartMaker.fromMimeTypeAndData("image/png", imageUri),
          "What's in this photo"
      ));

      return response.toString();
    }
  }
}

using Google.Api.Gax.Grpc;
using Google.Cloud.AIPlatform.V1;
using System.Text;
using System.Threading.Tasks;

public class GeminiQuickstart
{
    public async Task<string> GenerateContent(
        string projectId = "your-project-id",
        string location = "us-central1",
        string publisher = "google",
        string model = "gemini-2.0-flash-001"
    )
    {
        // Create client
        var predictionServiceClient = new PredictionServiceClientBuilder
        {
            Endpoint = $"{location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com"
        }.Build();

        // Initialize content request
        var generateContentRequest = new GenerateContentRequest
        {
            Model = $"projects/{projectId}/locations/{location}/publishers/{publisher}/models/{model}",
            GenerationConfig = new GenerationConfig
            {
                Temperature = 0.4f,
                TopP = 1,
                TopK = 32,
                MaxOutputTokens = 2048
            },
            Contents =
            {
                new Content
                {
                    Role = "USER",
                    Parts =
                    {
                        new Part { Text = "What's in this photo?" },
                        new Part { FileData = new() { MimeType = "image/png", FileUri = "gs://generativeai-downloads/images/scones.jpg" } }
                    }
                }
            }
        };

        // Make the request, returning a streaming response
        using PredictionServiceClient.StreamGenerateContentStream response = predictionServiceClient.StreamGenerateContent(generateContentRequest);

        StringBuilder fullText = new();

        // Read streaming responses from server until complete
        AsyncResponseStream<GenerateContentResponse> responseStream = response.GetResponseStream();
        await foreach (GenerateContentResponse responseItem in responseStream)
        {
            fullText.Append(responseItem.Candidates[0].Content.Parts[0].Text);
        }

        return fullText.ToString();
    }
}

async function analyze_video_with_audio(projectId = 'PROJECT_ID') {
  const vertexAI = new VertexAI({project: projectId, location: 'us-central1'});

  const generativeModel = vertexAI.getGenerativeModel({
    model: 'gemini-2.0-flash-001',
  });

  const filePart = {
    file_data: {
      file_uri: 'gs://cloud-samples-data/generative-ai/video/pixel8.mp4',
      mime_type: 'video/mp4',
    },
  };
  const textPart = {
    text: `
    Provide a description of the video.
    The description should also contain anything important which people say in the video.`,
  };

  const request = {
    contents: [{role: 'user', parts: [filePart, textPart]}],
  };

  const resp = await generativeModel.generateContent(request);
  const contentResponse = await resp.response;
  console.log(JSON.stringify(contentResponse));
}

public class VideoInputWithAudio {

  public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
    // TODO(developer): Replace these variables before running the sample.

  // Analyzes the given video input, including its audio track.
  public static String videoAudioInput(String projectId, String location, String modelName)
      throws IOException {
    // Initialize client that will be used to send requests. This client only needs
    // to be created once, and can be reused for multiple requests.
    try (VertexAI vertexAI = new VertexAI(projectId, location)) {
      String videoUri = "gs://cloud-samples-data/generative-ai/video/pixel8.mp4";

      GenerativeModel model = new GenerativeModel(modelName, vertexAI);

          ));

      String output = ResponseHandler.getText(response);
      System.out.println(output);

      return output;
    }
  }
}

using Google.Cloud.AIPlatform.V1;

The description should also contain anything important which people say in the video.";

        var generateContentRequest = new GenerateContentRequest
        {

            Contents =

                new Content
                {
                    Role = "USER",
                    Parts =
                    {

        GenerateContentResponse response = await predictionServiceClient.GenerateContentAsync(generateContentRequest);

        string responseText = response.Candidates[0].Content.Parts[0].Text;
        Console.WriteLine(responseText);

        return responseText;
    }
}

docs.title: Quickstart: Send text prompts to Gemini using Vertex AI Studio
docs.text:
You can use Vertex AI Studio to design, test, and manage prompts for Google's Gemini large language models (LLMs) and supported third-party models.

In this quickstart, you use sample prompts from the generative AI prompt gallery to test the Gemini model. You will learn how to:

  • Send a text summarization prompt.
  • Send a code generation prompt.
  • View the code used to generate the responses.

docs.title: What is a prompt?
docs.text:
A prompt is a natural language request sent to a language model to elicit a response. A prompt can include questions, instructions, contextual information, and examples.

For example, to generate a list of marketing slogans for a new coffee shop, you could use the following prompt:

"Generate five short and catchy marketing slogans for a new coffee shop called 'The Daily Grind'."

After the model receives the prompt, it generates a response, such as text, code, or images.

docs.title: Available models in Vertex AI Studio
docs.text:
Vertex AI Studio gives you access to Google's Gemini models and popular third-party models.

Note

When you use a third-party model for the first time, Vertex AI prompts you to accept the provider's terms and conditions. You must do this once for each third-party provider to start using their models.

The following table provides a high-level comparison of the models available:

Model Provider Key Features Best For Google (Gemini) State-of-the-art multimodal models with strong reasoning, text, code, and chat generation capabilities. Deeply integrated with the Google Cloud ecosystem. General-purpose tasks, complex reasoning, multimodal applications (text, image, audio, video), and leveraging Google Cloud services. Anthropic (Claude) Models designed with a focus on safety, helpfulness, and constitutional AI principles. Strong in conversational and text-processing tasks. Applications requiring high levels of safety, detailed instruction-following, and thoughtful, nuanced responses. Meta (Llama) High-performing open models that are popular in the open-source community. Known for strong performance in text and code generation. Development and research, fine-tuning for specific tasks, and applications where model transparency is important.

docs.title: Step 4: Configure Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP)
docs.text:
In this step, you configure Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) to create a centralized authorization layer for your app deployed in Cloud Run. This process involves configuring an OAuth consent screen, creating credentials, enabling IAP on the load balancer, and assigning user access.

This section provides a high-level overview of the steps to configure IAP.

flowchart TD
    A[Configure the OAuth consent screen] --> B[Create OAuth access credentials]
    B --> C[Enable IAP on the load balancer]
    C --> D[Set up and use IAP]

click A "#configure-the-oauth-consent-screen"
click B "#create-oauth-access-credentials"
click C "#enable-iap-on-the-load-balancer"
click D "#set-up-and-use-iap"

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP): A Google Cloud service that uses identity and context to guard access to your applications and VMs running on Google Cloud.
  • OAuth consent screen: A prompt that informs users which application is requesting access to their data and what kind of data it's asking to access.
  • OAuth client ID: A unique identifier used to authenticate an application when it requests access to a user's data using the OAuth 2.0 protocol.

docs.title: Steps to configure IAP
docs.text:
Configure Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP)

1. Configure the OAuth consent screen

The OAuth consent screen defines what is displayed to users and app reviewers and registers your app so you can publish it later.

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the OAuth consent screen.

    Go to OAuth consent screen

  2. Select a user type for your app. For this tutorial, we recommend selecting External.

    User Type Description Internal Only members of your Google Cloud organization can make authorization requests to the app. External Any user with a Google Account can make authorization requests.

  3. Click Create.

  4. In the Authorized domains section, click Add domain, and specify the domain name used during certificate creation.

  5. In the Developer contact information section, enter your email address.

  6. Click Save and Continue.

  7. On the Scopes page, click Save and Continue.

  8. Optional: If you selected External as the user type, add test users on the Test users page:

    1. Click Add users.
    2. Enter your email address and any other authorized test users, and then click Save and continue.

  9. Review your app registration summary. To make changes, click Edit. If the app registration looks correct, click Back to dashboard.

2. Create OAuth access credentials

You need an OAuth client ID to allow your application to call the required APIs.

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to Credentials.

    Go to Credentials

  2. Click Create credentials and then select OAuth client ID.

  3. In the Application type list, select Web application.

  4. In the Name field, enter gemini-streamlit-app.

  5. In the Authorized JavaScript origins section, click Add URI and then enter the following URI. Replace DOMAIN_NAME with the domain name used during certificate creation.

    https://DOMAIN_NAME

  6. Click Create. The Oauth client created screen appears, displaying your Client ID and Client secret.

  7. Copy the Client ID and Client secret. You'll need these details in the next step.

3. Enable IAP on the load balancer

Use the OAuth client ID and secret to enable IAP on the load balancer you created for your app.

  1. In the Google Cloud console, activate Cloud Shell.

    Activate Cloud Shell

    At the bottom of the Google Cloud console, a Cloud Shell session starts and displays a command-line prompt. Cloud Shell is a shell environment with the Google Cloud CLI already installed and with values already set for your current project. It can take a few seconds for the session to initialize.

  2. In the Cloud Shell terminal, run the following command. Replace CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET with the OAuth credentials you created in the previous step.

    gcloud compute backend-services update gemini-streamlit-app-backend \
      --iap=enabled,oauth2-client-id=CLIENT_ID,oauth2-client-secret=CLIENT_SECRET \
      --global

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

4. Set up and use IAP

Secure your app by creating principals who can access your app and then turning on IAP.

Caution: When IAP is turned off, a resource is accessible to anyone with the URL. Ensure that IAP is turned on so that the resource is accessible only by the configured principals.

  1. Go to the Identity-Aware Proxy page.

    Go to the Identity-Aware Proxy page

  2. Select your project.

  3. Select the checkbox next to gemini-streamlit-app-backend.

  4. Click Add principal.

  5. In the New principals field, enter the email addresses of groups or individuals to grant them access to your app. Ensure that you include a Google Account that you have access to. A principal can be any of the following:

    • Google Account
    • Google Group
    • Service account
    • Google Workspace domain

  6. In the Role list, select Cloud IAP > IAP-secured Web App User.

  7. Click Save.

  8. On the Identity-Aware Proxy page, under Applications, click the IAP toggle to the on position in the row corresponding to the gemini-streamlit-app-backend resource.

  9. In the Turn on IAP window that appears, select the checkbox to acknowledge that you've read the configuration requirements and configured your backend accordingly.

  10. Click Turn on. After you turn on IAP, it requires login credentials for all connections to your load balancer. Only accounts with the IAP-Secured Web App User role on the project are granted access.

docs.title: Step 2: Create a Cloud Run service
docs.text:
In this step, you create a Cloud Run service to deploy the app from the repository that you forked in the previous step. You also set up an automatic Cloud Build trigger, so that the app is built and deployed to Google Cloud whenever you push a new commit to the repository.

This guide walks you through the following procedures:

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Cloud Run: A managed compute platform that enables you to run stateless containers that are invocable via web requests or Pub/Sub events.
  • Cloud Build: A service that executes your builds on Google Cloud's infrastructure.
  • Continuous Deployment (CD): An automated process that builds, tests, and deploys code changes to a production environment.
  • Dockerfile: A text document that contains all the commands a user could call on the command line to assemble an image.

docs.title: Create and configure the Cloud Run service
docs.text:
Step-by-step guide to creating the service

Create a Cloud Run service with continuous build

  1. In the Google Cloud console, navigate to Cloud Run.

    Go to Cloud Run

  2. Click Create service.

  3. Select Continuously deploy from a repository.

  4. Click Set up with Cloud Build.

  5. In the Repository list, select the forked GitHub repository that you created for your app.

    If your repository isn't listed, click Manage connected repositories. While completing this step, do the following, if prompted: * Authenticate to GitHub. * Install Cloud Build on your GitHub account.

  6. If you're selecting a repository for the first time for use with Cloud Build in your project, select the checkbox to agree to the terms of use policy.

  7. Click Next.

  8. In the Build configuration section, enter the following details:

    • Branch: The default branch is ^main$. Don't update this.
    • Build type: Click Dockerfile.

    • Source location: Enter the following:

      /gemini/sample-apps/gemini-streamlit-cloudrun/Dockerfile

  9. Click Save.

  10. On the Create service page, enter the following details in the Configure section:

    • Service name: Enter gemini-streamlit-cloudrun.
    • Authentication: Click Allow unauthenticated invocations.
    • Service autoscaling: Set the Minimum number of instances to 1.

  11. Click Container(s), volumes, networking, security.

  12. In the Revision autoscaling section, enter the following:

    • Minimum number of instances: Enter 1.
    • Maximum number of instances: Enter 3.

  13. Click Create.

  14. Optional: To test the app deployment to Cloud Run, do the following:

    1. On the Services page in Cloud Run, click the service name.

      Go to the Services page

    2. On the Service details page, click the URL displayed next to the service name.

Set up an automatic Cloud Build trigger

  1. Navigate to the Triggers page in Cloud Build.

    Go to the Triggers page

  2. Click the name of your new trigger.

  3. Under Source, click to expand Show included and ignored files filters.

  4. In the Included files filter box, enter gemini-streamlit-cloudrun/**.

  5. Click Save.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Tip: If you want to manually build the Cloud Run service again, go to the Triggers page and click Run.

docs.title: Step 3: Create a load balancer
docs.text: In this step, you create a Global external Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic to backend instances hosted on Cloud Run. In the load balancer configuration, you define routing rules, which determine how the load balancer directs traffic based on the request's host and path.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Concepts
  • Application Load Balancer: A proxy-based Layer 7 load balancer that enables you to run and scale your services behind a single IP address.
  • Serverless Network Endpoint Group (NEG): A backend for a load balancer that points to a serverless service like Cloud Run, App Engine, or Cloud Functions.
  • URL map: A configuration resource that defines routing rules for directing incoming requests to specific backend services based on the request's host and path.
  • Google-managed SSL certificate: A free, auto-renewing SSL certificate that Google provisions and manages for your domains for use with Google Cloud load balancers.

Prerequisites

To complete this step, you must have a valid domain name and a self-managed certificate.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
The following diagram shows the workflow for creating the load balancer and updating your DNS records.

flowchart TD
    A[Configure the frontend] --> B[Configure the backend]
    B --> C[Configure routing rules]
    C --> D[Review and finalize]
    D --> E[Update DNS records]

click A "#configure-the-frontend"
click B "#configure-the-backend"
click C "#configure-routing-rules"
click D "#review-and-finalize"
click E "#update-dns-records"
Create and configure the load balancer

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Load balancing page.

    Go to Load balancing

  2. Click Create load balancer.

  3. In the Type of load balancer section, select Application Load Balancer (HTTP/HTTPS), and then click Next.
  4. In the Public facing or internal section, select Public facing (external), and then click Next.
  5. In the Global or single region deployment section, select Best for global workloads, and then click Next.
  6. In the Load balancer generation section, select Global external Application Load Balancer, and then click Next.
  7. Click Configure.
  8. For Load Balancer name, enter gemini-streamlit-app-lb.
  9. Configure the load balancer by completing the Frontend configuration, Backend configuration, and Routing rules sections.

Frontend Configuration

  1. Specify the following Frontend configuration:
    • Name: Enter gemini-streamlit-app-frontend.
    • Protocol: Select HTTPS (includes HTTP/2 and HTTP/3).
    • Network Service Tier: Set the IP address by reserving a new external static IP address. While reserving the new IP address, specify genai-app-ip as the Name.
    • Certificate: To create a new Google-managed certificate, perform the following steps:
      1. Click Create a new certificate.
      2. Specify the following details:
        • Name: Enter my-genai-app-certificate.
        • Create mode: Click Create Google-managed certificate.
        • Domains: Enter the domain name for provisioning the certificate.
      3. Click Create. For more information about Google-managed SSL certificates, see Use Google-managed SSL certificates.
    • Select the Enable HTTP to HTTPS redirect checkbox.
  2. Click Done.
  3. Click Backend configuration to configure the backend.

Backend configuration

  1. Click the Backend services & backend buckets list and then click Create backend service. Enter the following details:
    • Name: Enter gemini-streamlit-app-backend.
    • Backend type: Click Serverless network endpoint group.
    • Backends: On the New Backend card, perform the following steps:
      1. Click the Serverless network endpoint groups list, and then click Create serverless network endpoint group.
      2. Enter the following details:
        • Name: Enter streamlit-app-neg.
        • Region: Select us-central1.
        • Serverless network endpoint group type: Select Cloud Run.
        • Select service: Select the gemini-streamlit-cloudrun Cloud Run service.
      3. Click Create.
      4. Click Done.
  2. Clear the Enable Cloud CDN checkbox.
  3. In the Policy name box, enter default-security-policy-gemini-app-backend.
  4. Click Create, and then click OK.
  5. Click Routing rules to configure the routing rules.

Routing rules

  1. Click Advanced host and path rule.
  2. In the Host and path rules section, click (Default) Route traffic to backend "" for any unmatched hosts, and then enter the following details:
    • Action: Select Route traffic to a single backend.
    • Backend: Select gemini-streamlit-app-backend. Note: This rule handles the traffic for any unmatched host.
  3. Click Done.
  4. Click Add host and path rule to add a new rule.
  5. Under New host and path rule, enter the following details:

  1. Click Done.

docs.title: Step 1: Set up your project and source repository
docs.text:
In this step, you set up your Google Cloud project and Python environment in Cloud Shell, enable the required APIs, and assign the Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles that you need to complete the tutorial. You also set up a GitHub repository containing the app source files by forking and cloning the GoogleCloudPlatform/generative-ai repository. After completing these steps, you verify the setup by running and testing the app locally in Cloud Shell.

This document guides you through the following high-level steps:

flowchart TD
    A[Before you begin] --> B[Set up the source repository]
    B --> C[Set up the environment and dependencies]
    C --> D[Test the app locally]

click A "#before-you-begin"
click B "#set-up-the-source-repository"
click C "#set-up-the-environment-and-dependencies"
click D "#test-the-app-locally"
Concepts
  • Vertex AI: A unified platform for building, deploying, and scaling machine learning models.
  • Cloud Run: A managed compute platform that enables you to run stateless containers that are invocable via web requests or Pub/Sub events.
  • IAM (Identity and Access Management): The service that lets you grant granular access to specific Google Cloud resources and prevents unwanted access to other resources.
  • Artifact Registry: A universal repository manager for storing and managing container images and language packages.
  • Cloud Shell: An interactive shell environment for Google Cloud that provides command-line access to your resources directly from your browser.
Before you begin

  1. Sign in to your Google Cloud account. If you're new to Google Cloud, create an account to evaluate how our products perform in real-world scenarios. New customers also get $300 in free credits to run, test, and deploy workloads.

  2. Select or create a Google Cloud project. In the Google Cloud console, on the project selector page, select or create a Google Cloud project.

    Note: If you don't plan to keep the resources that you create in this procedure, create a project instead of selecting an existing project. After you finish these steps, you can delete the project, removing all resources associated with the project.

    Go to project selector

  3. Enable billing for your project. Make sure that billing is enabled for your Google Cloud project.

  4. Enable the required APIs. Enable the Vertex AI, Compute Engine, Artifact Registry, Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP), Cloud Run Admin, Cloud Build, Identity and Access Management (IAM) API, and Gemini for Google Cloud APIs.

    Enable the APIs

  5. Grant IAM roles. Make sure that you have the following roles on the project:

    • Vertex AI User
    • Cloud Build Editor
    • Cloud Run Admin
    • Artifact Registry Admin
    • Compute Load Balancer Admin
    • Service Account User
    • IAP Policy Admin
    • OAuth Config Editor
    • Service Usage Admin
    How to check for and grant roles

    Check for the roles

    1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the IAM page.

      Go to IAM

    2. Select the project.

    3. In the Principal column, find all rows that identify you or a group that you're included in. To learn which groups you're included in, contact your administrator.
    4. For all rows that specify or include you, check the Role column to see whether the list of roles includes the required roles.

    Grant the roles

    1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the IAM page.

      Go to IAM

    2. Select the project.

    3. Click person_add Grant access.
    4. In the New principals field, enter your user identifier (typically your Google Account email address).
    5. In the Select a role list, select a role.
    6. To grant additional roles, click add Add another role and add each additional role.
    7. Click Save.
Set up your environment and test the app

Set up the source repository

  1. In GitHub, fork the GoogleCloudPlatform/generative-ai repository. For more information, see Fork a repo.

    Fork the repository in GitHub

  2. In the Google Cloud console, activate Cloud Shell.

    Activate Cloud Shell

    At the bottom of the Google Cloud console, a Cloud Shell session starts and displays a command-line prompt. Cloud Shell is a shell environment with the Google Cloud CLI already installed and with values already set for your current project. It can take a few seconds for the session to initialize.

  3. In the Cloud Shell terminal, clone your forked repository and change to the app directory.

    cd
git clone https://github.com/GIT_USER_NAME/FORK_NAME/
cd FORK_NAME/gemini/sample-apps/gemini-streamlit-cloudrun

    Replace the following:

    • GIT_USER_NAME: Your GitHub username.
    • FORK_NAME: The name of the forked repository you created in GitHub.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Set up the environment and dependencies

  1. In the Cloud Shell terminal, run the following commands to set up a virtual environment and install dependencies:

    python3 -m venv gemini-streamlit
source gemini-streamlit/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

  2. Run the following commands to set the environment variables for Vertex AI initialization:

    export GCP_PROJECT=$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
export GCP_REGION='us-central1'

Test the app locally

  1. From the Cloud Shell terminal, run the app with the following command:

    streamlit run app.py \
  --browser.serverAddress=localhost \
  --server.enableCORS=false \
  --server.enableXsrfProtection=false \
  --server.port 8080

  2. To preview the app, in the Cloud Shell taskbar, click Web Preview, and then select Preview on port 8080. For more information, see Preview web apps.

docs.title: Secure a generative AI app by using IAP
docs.text:
This tutorial shows you how to deploy a generative AI application built with Streamlit to Cloud Run and secure it with Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP). IAP provides a central authorization layer for applications, allowing you to enforce access control policies at the application level rather than relying on network-level firewalls.

The application you deploy makes calls to the Gemini API.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Deploy a generative AI Streamlit app to Cloud Run.
  • Configure an external Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic.
  • Secure the application using Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP).
  • Automate builds and deployments using a Cloud Build trigger.

docs.text: For translation tasks, Generative AI on Vertex AI offers a choice between general-purpose Gemini models and two specialized translation models from the Cloud Translation API. Understanding the strengths of each model helps you select the right one for your use case.

Set up your project and environment

  2. Make sure that billing is enabled for your Google Cloud project.
  3. Enable the Vertex AI API.
  4. Set up authentication for a local development environment.
Concepts
  • Translation LLM: A large language model from Google that is specialized for high-quality translation tasks.
  • Neural Machine Translation (NMT): A model that uses neural networks to translate text, optimized for speed and real-time applications.
  • Gemini: A family of multimodal models from Google that can understand and generate text, images, and other types of information, including translations.
  • Temperature: A parameter that controls the randomness of the model's output; lower values result in more predictable text, while higher values produce more creative text.
  • Top-K: A parameter that limits the model's selection of the next token to the K most likely tokens.
  • Top-P: A parameter that selects the next token from a group of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds a certain threshold (P).

RESTPythonNode.js

Before you begin

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_NUMBER_OR_ID: The numeric or alphanumeric ID of your Google Cloud project.
  • LOCATION: The location to process the request. ??? "View a partial list of available regions" * us-central1 * us-west4 * northamerica-northeast1 * us-east4 * us-west1 * asia-northeast3 * asia-southeast1 * asia-northeast1
  • MODEL_ID: The ID of the model, such as gemini-1.0-pro-002.
  • SOURCE_LANGUAGE_CODE: The language of the input text.
  • TARGET_LANGUAGE_CODE: The target language to translate the input text to.
  • SOURCE_TEXT: The text to translate.
View parameter definitions
  • TEMPERATURE: The temperature is used for sampling during response generation, which occurs when topP and topK are applied. Temperature controls the degree of randomness in token selection. Lower temperatures are good for prompts that require a less open-ended or creative response, while higher temperatures can lead to more diverse or creative results. A temperature of 0 means that the highest probability tokens are always selected. In this case, responses for a given prompt are mostly deterministic, but a small amount of variation is still possible. If the model returns a response that's too generic, too short, or the model gives a fallback response, try increasing the temperature.
  • TOP_P: Top-P changes how the model selects tokens for output. Tokens are selected from the most probable to least probable until the sum of their probabilities equals the top-P value. For example, if tokens A, B, and C have a probability of 0.3, 0.2, and 0.1 and the top-P value is 0.5, then the model will select either A or B as the next token by using temperature and excludes C as a candidate. Specify a lower value for less random responses and a higher value for more random responses.
  • TOP_K: Top-K changes how the model selects tokens for output. A top-K of 1 means the next selected token is the most probable among all tokens in the model's vocabulary (also called greedy decoding), while a top-K of 3 means that the next token is selected from among the three most probable tokens by using temperature. For each token selection step, the top-K tokens with the highest probabilities are sampled. Then tokens are further filtered based on top-P with the final token selected using temperature sampling. Specify a lower value for less random responses and a higher value for more random responses.
  • MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS: Maximum number of tokens that can be generated in the response. A token is approximately four characters. 100 tokens correspond to roughly 60-80 words. Specify a lower value for shorter responses and a higher value for potentially longer responses.
  • SAFETY_CATEGORY: The safety category to configure a threshold for. ??? "View safety categories" * HARM_CATEGORY_SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT * HARM_CATEGORY_HATE_SPEECH * HARM_CATEGORY_HARASSMENT * HARM_CATEGORY_DANGEROUS_CONTENT
  • THRESHOLD: The threshold for blocking responses that could belong to the specified safety category based on probability. ??? "View blocking thresholds" * BLOCK_NONE * BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH * BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE (default) * BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE blocks the most while BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH blocks the least.

HTTP method and URL:

      "parts": [

      ]
    }
  ],
  "generation_config": {
    "temperature": TEMPERATURE,
    "topP": TOP_P,
    "topK": TOP_K,
    "candidateCount": 1,
    "maxOutputTokens": MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS
  },

    {

from vertexai.generative_models import [GenerativeModel](https://cloud.google.com/python/docs/reference/vertexai/latest/vertexai.preview.generative_models.GenerativeModel.html), [Part](https://cloud.google.com/python/docs/reference/vertexai/latest/vertexai.preview.generative_models.Part.html), [FinishReason](https://cloud.google.com/python/docs/reference/vertexai/latest/vertexai.preview.generative_models.FinishReason.html)

      ["""SOURCE_LANGUAGE_CODE: TEXT
TARGET_LANGUAGE_CODE:"""],

import os

# Import the Google Cloud Translation library.
from google.cloud import [translate](https://cloud.google.com/python/docs/reference/translate/latest/google.cloud.translate_v2.client.Client.html)_v3

PROJECT_ID = os.environ.get("GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT")


def translate_text(
    text: str = "YOUR_TEXT_TO_TRANSLATE",
    source_language_code: str = "en-US",
    target_language_code: str = "fr",
) -> translate_v3.TranslationServiceClient:
    """Translate Text from a Source language to a Target language.
    Args:
        text: The content to translate.
        source_language_code: The code of the source language.
        target_language_code: The code of the target language.
            For example: "fr" for French, "es" for Spanish, etc.
            Find available languages and codes here:
            https://cloud.google.com/translate/docs/languages#neural_machine_translation_model
    """

    # Initialize Translation client.
    client = translate_v3.TranslationServiceClient()
    parent = f"projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/global"

    # MIME type of the content to translate.
    # Supported MIME types:
    # https://cloud.google.com/translate/docs/supported-formats
    mime_type = "text/plain"

    # Translate text from the source to the target language.
    response = [client](https://cloud.google.com/python/docs/reference/translate/latest/google.cloud.translate_v2.client.html).[translate_text](https://cloud.google.com/python/docs/reference/translate/latest/google.cloud.translate_v3.services.translation_service.TranslationServiceClient.html#google_cloud_translate_v3_services_translation_service_TranslationServiceClient_translate_text)(
        contents=[text],
        parent=parent,
        mime_type=mime_type,
        source_language_code=source_language_code,
        target_language_code=target_language_code,
    )

    # Display the translation for the text.
    # For example, for "Hello! How are you doing today?":
    # Translated text: Bonjour comment vas-tu aujourd'hui?
    for translation in response.translations:
        print(f"Translated text: {translation.translated_text}")

    return response

docs.title: Customize translations with the Translation LLM
docs.text:
You can customize responses from the Translation LLM by providing your own example translations. This feature, also known as adaptive translation, is only available for the Translation LLM.

You can request customized translations through the Vertex AI Studio or the API. The console supports custom translations by uploading a file with examples (TMX or TSV), while the API supports providing up to five example sentence pairs inline with the request.

Data requirements

If you provide example translations in a file for the Google Cloud console, the examples must be written as segment pairs in a TMX or TSV file. Each pair includes a source language segment and its translated counterpart. For more information, see Prepare example translations in the Cloud Translation documentation.

To get the most accurate results, include specific examples from a wide variety of scenarios. You must include at least five sentence pairs but no more than 10,000 pairs. Also, a segment pair can be at most a total of 512 characters.

ConsoleAPI Customize translations using Vertex AI Studio

  1. In the Vertex AI section of the Google Cloud console, go to the Translate text page in Vertex AI Studio.

    Go to Vertex AI Studio

  2. In the Run settings pane, configure your translation settings.

    • In the Model field, select Translation LLM.
    • To change the temperature, expand Advanced.

  3. Click Add examples.

    • Select a local file or a file from Cloud Storage. Vertex AI Studio determines the source and target languages from your file.
    • Select the number of examples for the model to use before generating a response. The number of examples you select counts toward the input character limit per request of 3,000.

  4. In the input field, enter the text to translate.

  5. Click Submit. Vertex AI automatically selects your specified number of reference sentences that are most similar to your input. The translation model identifies patterns from your examples and then applies those patterns when generating a response. The output limit per request is 3,000 characters. Any text beyond this limit is dropped.

  6. To get the code or curl command that demonstrate how to request translations, click code Get code.

To request custom translations via the API, include up to five reference sentence pairs in your translation request. The translation model uses all of them to identify patterns from your examples and then applies those patterns when generating a response.

RESTPythonNode.js

Before you begin

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_NUMBER_OR_ID: The numeric or alphanumeric ID of your Google Cloud project.
  • LOCATION: The location where you want to run this operation. For example, us-central1.
  • REFERENCE_SOURCE: A sentence in the source language that is part of a reference sentence pair.
  • REFERENCE_TARGET: A sentence in the target language that is part of a reference sentence pair.
  • SOURCE_LANGUAGE: The language code of the input text.
  • TARGET_LANGUAGE: The target language to translate the input text to.
  • SOURCE_TEXT: Text in the source language to translate.
  • MIME_TYPE (Optional): The format of the source text, such as text/html or text/plain. By default, the MIME type is set to text/plain.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/translate-llm:predict

Request JSON body:

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "reference_sentence_config": {
        "reference_sentence_pair_lists": [
          {
            "reference_sentence_pairs": [
              {
                "source_sentence": "REFERENCE_SOURCE_1_1",
                "target_sentence": "REFERENCE_TARGET_1_1"
              },
              {
                "source_sentence": "REFERENCE_SOURCE_1_2",
                "target_sentence": "REFERENCE_SOURCE_1_2"
              }
            ]
          }
        ],
        "source_language_code": "SOURCE_LANGUAGE_CODE",
        "target_language_code": "TARGET_LANGUAGE_CODE"
      },
      "content": [
        "SOURCE_TEXT"
      ],
      "mimeType": "MIME_TYPE"
    }
  ]
}

Before trying this sample, follow the Python setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Python API reference documentation.

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

from google.cloud import aiplatform
from google.protobuf.json_format import MessageToDict

def translate():
  # Create a client
  client_options = {"api_endpoint": "LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com"}
  client = aiplatform.gapic.PredictionServiceClient(client_options=client_options)

  # Initialize the request
  endpoint_id = f"projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/translate-llm"
  instances=[{
      "reference_sentence_config": {
        "reference_sentence_pair_lists": [{
          "reference_sentence_pairs": [{
            "source_sentence": 'SAMPLE_REFERENCE_SOURCE_1',
            "target_sentence": 'SAMPLE_REFERENCE_TARGET_1'
          },
          {
            "source_sentence": 'SAMPLE_REFERENCE_SOURCE_2',
            "target_sentence": 'SAMPLE_REFERENCE_TARGET_2'
          }]
        }],
        "source_language_code": 'SOURCE_LANGUAGE_CODE',
        "target_language_code": 'TARGET_LANGUAGE_CODE'
      },
      "content": ["SOURCE_TEXT"]
  }]
  # Make the request
  response = client.[predict](https://cloud.google.com/python/docs/reference/aiplatform/latest/google.cloud.aiplatform_v1.services.prediction_service.PredictionServiceClient.html)(
      endpoint=endpoint_id, instances=instances,
  )
  # Handle the response
  print(response)

  # The predictions are a google.protobuf.Value representation of the model's predictions.
  predictions = MessageToDict(response._pb)['predictions']
  for prediction in predictions:
      print(prediction['translations'])

            }]
          }],
          "source_language_code": 'SOURCE_LANGUAGE_CODE',

  const [response] = await endpoint.predict(request)

You can also use the Cloud Translation API to create a dataset and import your example sentence pairs. When you use the Cloud Translation API to request translations, you can include your dataset to customize responses. The dataset persists and can be reused with multiple translation requests. For more information, see Request adaptive translations in the Cloud Translation documentation.

docs.text:
This section shows you how to generate a video from an image and a text prompt.

The following workflow diagram provides a high-level overview of the steps:

flowchart TD
    A[Set up your environment] --> B{Choose generation method};
    B -- Console --> C[Generate video in the Console];
    B -- REST API --> D[Generate video with the REST API];

| Sample input | Sample output | | :--- | :--- | | 1. Input image¹ ![Input PNG file of a crocheted elephant](../images/ITV_elephant_base2.png) 2. Text prompt: `the elephant moves around naturally` | ![Output video of a crocheted elephant](../images/ITV_elephant_output.gif) | ¹ Image generated using Imagen on Vertex AI from the prompt: A Crochet elephant in intricate patterns walking on the savanna.

You can generate videos using the Google Cloud console for a graphical interface, or programmatically using the REST API or the Python SDK.

Method Best for Google Cloud console Quickly experimenting with prompts and model settings without writing any code. REST API Integrating video generation into your applications using standard web requests. Python SDK A streamlined, high-level programmatic experience for Python developers. ConsoleREST APIPython SDK

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI Studio > Media Studio page.

Media Studio

  1. Click Video.
  2. Optional: In the Settings pane, configure the following settings:
    • Model: Choose a model from the available options.
    • Aspect ratio: Choose either 16:9 or 9:16. Note: The 9:16 aspect ratio isn't supported by veo-3.0-generate-preview.
    • Number of results: Adjust the slider or enter a value between 1 and 4.
    • Video length: Select a length between 5 seconds and 8 seconds.
    • Output directory: Click Browse to create or select a Cloud Storage bucket to store output files.
  3. Optional: In the Safety section, select one of the following Person generation settings:
    • Allow (Adults only): Default value. Generate adult people or faces only. Don't generate youth or children people or faces.
    • Don't allow: Don't generate people or faces.
  4. Optional: In the Advanced options section, enter a Seed value for randomizing video generation.
  5. In the Write your prompt box, click upload Upload.
  6. Choose a local image to upload and click Select.
  7. In the Write your prompt box, enter your text prompt that describes the videos to generate.
  8. Click send Generate.

The following samples show how to send a video generation request. This request begins a long-running operation. For more information, see the Veo API reference.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Step 1: Send a video generation request

Use the following command to send a video generation request. This request begins a long-running operation and returns an operation name.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • MODEL_ID: The model ID to use. Available values:
    • veo-2.0-generate-001 (GA)
    • veo-3.0-generate-preview (Preview)
  • TEXT_PROMPT: The text prompt used to guide video generation.
  • INPUT_IMAGE: Base64-encoded bytes string representing the input image. To ensure quality, the input image should be 720p or higher (1280 x 720 pixels) and have a 16:9 or 9:16 aspect ratio. Images of other aspect ratios or sizes may be resized or centrally cropped during the upload process.
  • MIME_TYPE: The MIME type of the input image. Supported MIME types: image/jpeg or image/png.
  • OUTPUT_STORAGE_URI: Optional: The Cloud Storage bucket to store the output videos. If not provided, video bytes are returned in the response. For example: gs://video-bucket/output/.
  • RESPONSE_COUNT: The number of video files you want to generate. Accepted integer values: 1-4.
  • DURATION: The length of video files that you want to generate. Accepted integer values are 5-8.
  • Additional optional parameters: Use the following optional variables in the "parameters": {} object.
    • ASPECT_RATIO: (string) Defines the aspect ratio of the generated videos. Values: 16:9 (default, landscape) or 9:16 (portrait).
    • NEGATIVE_PROMPT: (string) A text string that describes what you want to discourage the model from generating.
    • PERSON_SAFETY_SETTING: (string) The safety setting that controls whether people or face generation is allowed. Values: allow_adult (default) or disallow.
    • SEED_NUMBER: (uint32) A number to make generated videos deterministic. Specifying a seed number guides the model to produce the same videos. Values: 0 - 4294967295.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:predictLongRunning

Request JSON body:

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "TEXT_PROMPT",
      "image": {
        "bytesBase64Encoded": "INPUT_IMAGE",
        "mimeType": "MIME_TYPE"
      }
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "storageUri": "OUTPUT_STORAGE_URI",
    "sampleCount": RESPONSE_COUNT
  }
}

To send your request, choose one of these options:

curl

     "https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:predictLongRunning"

{

}
Step 2: Check the operation status

After you start a video generation job, it might take some time to complete. You can use the operation name returned from the previous step to check the status of the job.

GET https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/OPERATION_NAME

curl

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `

Install the SDK

Run the Python code

Set environment variables to use the Gen AI SDK with Vertex AI:

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below line

while not operation.done:
    time.sleep(15)

if operation.response:

docs.text:
You can use Veo on Vertex AI to generate new videos from a text prompt. Supported interfaces include the Google Cloud console, the REST API, and the Python SDK.

For more information about writing effective text prompts for video generation, see the Veo prompt guide.

This document walks you through the following high-level steps:

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Complete the following prerequisites Concepts
  • Veo: A generative AI model that creates video content from text and image inputs.
  • Prompt: A natural language text description that you provide as input to guide the video generation process.
  • Long-running operation: An asynchronous task, such as video generation, that runs in the background and can be polled for its status.
  • Seed: An optional number used to make video generation deterministic, ensuring the same output for the same prompt.
  • Cloud Storage: A Google Cloud service for storing and accessing data objects, such as the generated video files.

  1. Set up your Google Cloud project

    Sign in to your Google Cloud account. If you're new to Google Cloud, create an account to evaluate how our products perform in real-world scenarios. New customers also get $300 in free credits to run, test, and deploy workloads.

    In the Google Cloud console, on the project selector page, select or create a Google Cloud project.

    Note: If you don't plan to keep the resources that you create in this procedure, create a project instead of selecting an existing project. After you finish these steps, you can delete the project, removing all resources associated with the project.
